history.note: CLOSED the voice-call-handler test breakage — ALL 83 tests across the 9 voice-call-handler*.test.ts files now green (the prior triage counted 8 across 3 files; running all 9 files surfaced ~32). Every fix was a STALE TEST DOUBLE / STALE ASSERTION / TEST-TIMING issue — production voice-call-handler.ts is UNCHANGED (git diff empty). The earlier 'merged heldTurnText blob' hypothesis was WRONG; the real root causes, found by instrumenting the actual audit/spoken trail: (1) The test tenants omit voiceTier, so the handler defaults to 'starter' (voice-call-handler.ts:1831 `tenant.voiceTier ?? 'starter'`) whose allowedActions EXCLUDE confirm/list/pay/lookup-practitioner → the dialog's out-of-scope gate (dialog.ts:1799) TRANSFERS on turn 1 before verification. Fixed: register with voiceTier:'pro' (e6/e7/e9/provenance/comms). (2) The inline StubIdentityCheck.checkSecondFactor returned a bare boolean, but the #38 interface now returns { matched, factor } — so result.matched was undefined → the 2nd factor NEVER verified → no verified dispatch. Fixed in all six stubs (voice-call-handler.test.ts, -e6/-e9/-provenance/-comms). (3) provenance's driveVerifiedTurn emitted list_upcoming as the turn-1 jump-the-gun intent but expected book — the PHI-gate auto-resume (which is what actually dispatches) fired the wrong intent; verification turns don't consume the LLM queue so turn-4's re-emit got a stale text response. Fixed: the jump-the-gun intent IS the target intent (mirrors e6). (4) persona (5 tests): the two-voice compliance greeting (commit 24149aa7) INTENTIONALLY overrides persona wording — ttsCalls[0] is now the male disclosure voice, and agentName/greetingTemplate are dropped (dialog.ts:738 emitGreeting aiDisclosure branch). Those tests validate the persona greeting path, so they now run with CERNIA_VOICE_AI_DISCLOSURE=0 (the disclosure greeting is covered separately in packages/voice-agent/src/dialog.test.ts:1619). (5) e7 disambiguation follow-up: the caller's 'Sarah' pick was dropped by the barge-in echo filter (isLikelyEcho: the agent's prompt lists 'Dr. Sarah Smith' so a one-word 'Sarah' overlaps 100% while bargeIn.isSpeaking). Real callers answer AFTER the prompt; added a deterministic drainSpeech(stream) helper (pumps setImmediate until stream.record.outboundFrames stops growing → synthesis done → isSpeaking cleared) before delivering the answer. Verified: @cernia/api typecheck clean; full voice-call-handler suite 83/83 green; production code untouched.

Voice hardening — SERIALIZED intent dispatch (concurrent-flow race). The handler's onIntent fired `void registry.handle(...)` per intent, so two flow-opening intents emitted in ONE turn (LLM emits book+reschedule together, or both auto-resume after verification) dispatched CONCURRENTLY and both passed the existing `deferredFlowIntents` `flowActive()` guard before either set `activeBookingFlow` (startBookingFlow only assigns it AFTER an await) — starting two deterministic flows at once and double-prompting the caller. Extracted a pure FIFO serializer apps/api/src/serial-dispatch.ts (createSerialRunner: runs each intent one-at-a-time, in order, next never starts until the previous settles; rejection-isolated) + apps/api/src/serial-dispatch.test.ts (3 tests: serial+in-order, rejection isolation, max-concurrency=1). apps/api/src/voice-call-handler.ts now dispatches intents through it, so the first flow registers before the second is handled and the goal-stack defers it correctly. apps/api typecheck clean, lint clean, serial-dispatch 3/3; the voice-call-handler suites show IDENTICAL failure counts to baseline (8 pre-existing carry-forward across 3 files, git-stash-verified — zero new regressions).

Coverage vs a 37-checkpoint rubric: sonnet 88% / medgemma:27b 83.5% / qwen3-vl 77% / medgemma:4b 75.5% / qwen3-scribe 73%. Latency 5.3s / 443.5s / 65.6s / 13.9s / 23.2s. Every draft proven to have invoked the claimed model by joining llm_audit_events.response_hash to an Ollama-side logging proxy's sha256(content) - time-window attribution was tried and REJECTED (back-to-back runs cross-claim wire rows). Two findings for consumers of this path: (a) the currently configured default OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen3-scribe is the WEAKEST model measured on completeness, and is a re-tag of qwen3-vl:8b-instruct (identical weights blob, no SYSTEM prompt, no ADAPTER; only num_ctx 8192 differs - a latent truncation risk on long visits); (b) the most complete model is the least faithful - claude-sonnet-4 reproducibly invented a medication concentration and a numeric anatomical identifier that is WRONG for the site named. No production default changed by this eval (recommendation only).

CLOSURE PASS — two outcomes. (1) FIXED HERE: the text-channel booking-silence bug (surfaced by the text-only harness 2026-06-19) is closed. Root cause was as filed — the text hardcoded handler in apps/api/src/text-dialog-routes.ts fell through to a bare `state.pendingIntents.push({kind: intent.kind})` for every non-pay-balance/transfer/end-call action, so a turn that emitted ONLY an intent returned {messages: [], intents: [{kind: "book-appointment"}]} and the caller got silence; voice masked it because the orchestrator narrates with TTS prompts, text has no narration layer. Fix: a TEXT_ACTION_ACK map (19 action kinds → a fixed, non-PHI channel-appropriate line) plus applyActionAcks(state), invoked in POST /text-dialog/:id/message AFTER the dialog turn and after the in-flight intent dispatches settle. It fires ONLY when the turn produced no agent text at all (stream.peekAgentText().length === 0), so a model that did speak is never doubled up, and it adds at most ONE line even when a turn emits several actions. transfer-to-human and end-call are deliberately excluded — both close the stream and the client branches on ended/transferTo, so a trailing utterance would mislead. Every ack string is a fixed literal that interpolates nothing off the intent (no appointment times, names, or medications), keeping the backstop out of the PHI path. Tests: 8 new cases in apps/api/src/text-dialog-routes.test.ts under "action-only turns are never silent" — the book-appointment regression itself, 4 parameterised action kinds, a no-double-up case, a one-line-for-many-actions case, and a stays-silent-for-transfer case. (2) NARROWED: the nightly --live canary bullet. Its "the workflow is dormant (dispatch-only)" premise was stale — .github/workflows/voice-agent-eval-live.yml has had `schedule: cron "0 4 * * *"` and `gh run list` shows nightly executions going back weeks; the cost-control ask is also already implemented (--max-spend-usd circuit breaker, default $2, skipped-vs-failed distinction, report-only + scorecard artifact + auto-issue). The ONE thing genuinely still missing is the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY repo secret, verified absent by `gh secret list` (only MIRROR_DEPLOY_KEY). Separately noted, not re-filed: those nightly runs have been RED at the "Build voice-agent-evals" step with TS2307 (@cernia/design-tokens, @cernia/speech), which is the backwards-pnpm-ellipsis bug fixed repo-wide by #770 / commit 003d06c2 — that landed 2026-08-03 16:50 EDT, AFTER the 06:53 UTC nightly, so the first nightly eligible to get past the build step is 2026-08-04. history.note: R10 part 1 COMPLETE — admin-side escalation-number validation. PATCH /api/voice-agent/policy (apps/api/src/voice-agent-admin-routes.ts) previously merged + upserted the policy body with NO validation, so a tenant could enable the 'transfer' intent with an empty/garbage escalationPhone → the agent would try to hand callers to a dead line. Now the merged policy is validated: any non-empty escalationPhone must be E.164 (isE164) → 400; and if enabledIntents includes 'transfer', a valid escalationPhone is REQUIRED → 400 with a clear field+detail. Pairs with the call-time callback fallback (R10 part 2, below): config-time prevention + run-time safety net. 3 new tests in voice-agent-admin-routes.test.ts (transfer+empty→400 & not persisted, non-E164→400, transfer+valid E.164→200); full file 15/15. apps/api typecheck clean; changed region lint-clean (one pre-existing carry-forward assertion on an untouched persona line). R10 hardening — a FAILED transfer never drops the caller silently. The transfer-to-human path attempted the live carrier redirect (telephony.redirectToHuman) but, when a live-redirect backend was configured yet the caller was NOT bridged (escalation number missing, or the redirect threw), it fell through to terminate()+stream.close() — dead air. Added apps/api/src/voice-call-handler.ts fallbackToCallbackAfterFailedTransfer(): captures a callback Task via appointmentManager.requestCallback for a verified caller (reason 'general-question'), speaks an acknowledgment either way (the line is never dead), waits (bounded) for it to play, and logs a visible voice.call.transfer phase:'callback-fallback' audit row {ok, taskId?}. Gated on `canLiveRedirect && !bridgedToHuman` so tests / legacy deploys without a live-redirect backend keep the existing close-and-drop (finalResponse still drives a TwiML transfer at the webhook) — zero behaviour change there. remaining: [storagebacked-scheduler-pr-20260711] SCHEDULED WORKFLOWS FIRE EXACTLY ONCE ACROSS PODS — CLOSED 2026-08-07, and NOT the way the residue asked for. The gap was real: WorkflowScheduler.tick looped in-memory entries with an in-memory lastFiredMinute and no cross-pod identity, so N pods produced N runs per minute for every schedule registered through $schedule. THE BRIEF SAID LEADER-ELECT THE TICK. THAT WAS REFUSED, ON MEASUREMENT, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE INTERESTING PART: the boot scan shipped 2026-08-06 RELEASES its registrations when it loses ITS election, so scanned schedules live only on the scan leader. A second independent election on the tick makes the tick leader a different pod on any given round, and those crons then stop firing while every log line stays green. Sharing one lock key does not fix it either — pg_try_advisory_lock is taken per round, so the scan winner and the tick winner remain independent draws. That is a SILENCE bug, strictly worse than the duplication being fixed, and precisely the failure the boot scan was built to end. SHIPPED INSTEAD, and it needs no leader to be correct: a deterministic run id, scheduleRunId(workflowId, minuteKey) -> `sched-{workflowId}-{YYYYMMDDTHHmm}`, passed as WorkflowTriggerContext.executionId and used as the WorkflowExecution resource id — so the resources (tenant_id, id) PRIMARY KEY IS the ON CONFLICT. No migration, and the claim row IS the run record, which makes "exactly one run" a countable row rather than bookkeeping. The id uses `-` not `:` because it becomes a FHIR logical id ([A-Za-z0-9-.]{1,64}), and an over-long workflow id falls back to a sha256 form rather than truncating, since truncation would let two workflows sharing a 40-char prefix collide and silently suppress one. A lost insert becomes DuplicateExecutionError, counted as `deduplicated` and logged at INFO — on a healthy 3-pod deployment 2 pods report this every minute, so alerting on workflow failures must not page for it. Fail-toward-FIRING throughout, as instructed: no leader injected -> this pod leads; elector throws -> fire anyway and warn; no storage adapter -> no dedupe, everything runs; any error not POSITIVELY a duplicate-id conflict is reported failed rather than swallowed as "already done". ScheduleTickLeader + AdvisoryLockScheduleTickLeader ship as an OPT-IN seam, tested on real Postgres, DELIBERATELY UNWIRED, with the boot-scan hazard written on the interface. Evidence is two pools over ONE schema (two fixtures would mint separate schemas and pass by construction): two pods + one due schedule -> exactly 1 WorkflowExecution row, control stripped -> 2; a HANDOVER case where a pod fires then dies and a survivor with no memory ticks the same minute; per-minute and PER-TENANT claim scoping (a global key would have silenced tenant B while every "exactly one" assertion stayed green). 299 executor tests (was 273), gates 80/80, ratchet 371. THE TEST WAS VACUOUS ON ITS FIRST DRAFT AND THE AGENT CAUGHT IT: the snapshot-extraction recipe it borrowed takes only CREATE TABLE, and pg_dump emits primary keys as separate ALTER TABLE statements — so `resources` had NO primary key, two pods inserted two rows with the same id, the dedupe tests failed loudly and the falsifying controls passed for entirely the wrong reason. Fixed by extracting constraints too, plus a positive control asserting the fixture really carries the (tenant_id, id) PRIMARY KEY. Same class found in InMemoryStorage.create, which silently overwrote on a repeated id and would have green-lit the dedupe with the feature DELETED. WHAT REMAINS is behavioural, not a gap: (a) a run that FAILS mid-flight is no longer retried by a sibling pod within the same minute, because the claim row already exists — it ran and failed visibly, and next minute is a new claim; (b) clock skew >60s between pods yields different minute keys and a duplicate fire, degrading to today's behaviour and never to silence; (c) wiring AdvisoryLockScheduleTickLeader requires changing the boot scan's release-on-yield ownership first, which is a separate decision recorded in both module headers.

[delete-workflows-id-schedule] DELETE /admin/workflows/:id/$schedule 400s WHEN A CLIENT SENDS content-type: application/json WITH NO BODY — found 2026-08-06 by the live boot smoke, which is precisely what a live smoke is for; no unit test would have surfaced it. The request is rejected by the body parser BEFORE reaching the handler, so the route code is not at fault and neither is its RBAC. A correct-HTTP call (no content-type on a bodyless DELETE) works, and unregistration is proven end to end. This is server-wide body-parsing behaviour rather than anything specific to this route, which is why it was recorded as an ASSERTED CONSTRAINT in verify-cron-scan.mts (B5) rather than papered over at the route. IT MATTERS BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS CLIENT GETS IT WRONG: most HTTP libraries set a JSON content-type by default on every verb, so an admin UI wired the natural way will fail to unschedule a workflow and report a 400 the operator cannot act on. WHAT IS LEFT is a decision about where to fix it: either the Fastify body-parser config accepts an empty JSON body platform-wide (one place, affects every route, needs care that it does not turn a genuinely malformed body into a silent empty object), or every admin client is required to omit the header on bodyless DELETEs (no code change, but it is folklore unless documented). Not chosen here because the blast radius of the first option reaches every route in apps/api.

Compute and storage went from unmeasurable to MEASURED: @cernia/finops has its first runtime caller, ComputeProbe has a real in-process meter, migration 352 stops the ledger recording 0 for every sub-cent infra row, and cost_ledger holds real rows on a live stack for the first time since migration 067. The rollup is now MULTI-POD CORRECT: a durable window watermark (migration 356) means a restart cannot re-meter the storage level into a ledger that has no key to deduplicate on, and the storage half is leader-elected on an advisory lock so N pods no longer multiply storage cost by N — both proven against real Postgres with the guard-removed control arm. The two vendor rate tables are collapsed into one (the gateway’s), with the LLM rows derived from MODEL_RATES so they cannot drift again; @cernia/finops keeps only the internal compute/storage rates it has to measure. A NOTE is still unpriced overall, and honestly so: no per-note allocation basis for compute/storage has been chosen, which is a pricing decision rather than a code gap.

(a) PostgresCostLedgerStore.summarize() is a SQL GROUP BY (packages/o4-cost-tracking-budgets/src/postgres-cost-ledger-store.ts): at most one row per (model, provider) pair instead of an unbounded SELECT * summed in JS, so the check no longer costs more every day of the billing period. Gated by summarize-sql-equivalence.test.ts, which runs the OLD JS aggregate over the same real-Postgres rows and demands the two agree — hand-written expected numbers would have encoded my reading of the unpriced/widened semantics, and that reading was exactly what could be wrong. (b) THE CHECK IS OFF THE REQUEST PATH. checkBudget stays SYNCHRONOUS and reads a TTL cache, refreshing behind it — "check asynchronously, enforce on the next call", which is the shape the budget-manager.ts header asked for. apps/api/src/llm-budget-source.ts reads the cap from o4_llm_budgets and SUMS the spend from the ledger; nothing accumulates a running total, deliberately, because a counter can drift from the rows it claims to summarise and there is no way to notice. THE WRITE HALF WAS ALSO MISSING and is now done: POST /admin/llm/budget used to call gateway.setBudget() and answer 204, which wrote to one process Map. It now persists FIRST via PostgresLlmBudgetWriter and answers 503 budget-not-persisted if the write fails, because a 204 followed by no enforcement anywhere else is the state this whole change exists to remove. With no writer configured (db-less boot) it answers 200 {scope:"process-local"} and says so. The test that covered this was named "...and persists" and asserted 204 — it asserted the defect. Proof: 16 unit tests (packages/o1-llm-gateway/src/multipod-budget.test.ts) whose FIRST TWO reproduce the old behaviour so the rest are not asserting against a bug that was never there, plus 10 real-Postgres tests (apps/api/src/llm-budget-source.integration.test.ts) ending in a SECOND CostStore that shares nothing but the database refusing a call it never served. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT. (i) It is EVENTUALLY consistent by design: cross-pod convergence lags by up to the TTL (30s default) and the FIRST call for a tenant on a cold pod is not enforced. Both are bounded and both are stated in the code; the previous behaviour was unbounded and silent. Tightening either means blocking the LLM path on a query. (ii) CLOSED 2026-08-06 — $report reads the DURABLE ledger (apps/api/src/llm-spend-source.ts + CostStore.buildDurableReport). It AWAITS rather than caching, deliberately: unlike checkBudget this is an admin endpoint, not the LLM request path. An INCOMPLETE window emits totalCostUSDLowerBound INSTEAD OF totalCostUSD, so a caller that reads the plain field and ignores complete gets undefined — visibly missing — rather than a floor that reads as a figure. An unreadable ledger 503s rather than falling back, because a pod-local number under the platform-wide label is the original defect wearing the fix badge. Db-less boot answers scope:process-local. RESIDUE: byPurpose and totalTokens are ABSENT rather than zeroed, because summarize() groups by (model, provider) only; closing that needs a GROUP BY on the tags purposeOfUse key plus token SUMs inside @cernia/o4-cost-tracking-budgets. (iii) CLOSED 2026-08-06 — cross-pod rate limiting via IDurableRateLimitSource + RedisLlmRateLimitSource. checkRateLimit STAYS SYNCHRONOUS (its only call site, api.ts, was outside the writable set, and it runs on every LLM turn including live voice), so it follows the budget seam: cached read plus local delta, refresh behind. A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from RedisCallerRateLimiter, documented at both ends: that limiter GET-mutate-SET race is bounded at limit+1 because its read and write are one step of one call; here the read is a background refresh and the write happens later in record(), so read-modify-write across that gap loses updates and UNDER-counts — the exact defect being closed. So it is one atomic INCR against a window-keyed counter. THE COST, stated rather than hidden: a FIXED window, so a boundary-straddling burst can admit 2x the rate in one window-length. 2x bounded and stated beats Nx unbounded and silent. A corrupt counter THROWS rather than returning 0, because a 0 would lift the limit for as long as the bad value sat there. RESIDUE: nothing primes the counter at boot, so the first check on a cold pod counts locally and converges within the TTL; and NEITHER seam has been exercised against a real Redis or a genuinely multi-pod deployment — all proof is unit/route-level with fakes. (iv) the alert THRESHOLD from the durable source is derived (the platform default warning level, 75%) because o4_llm_budgets has no threshold column; a per-tenant threshold set through the route is still process-local. (v) the per-tier overrun policy from (c).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT: (a) NO RATE IS INVOICE-RECONCILED. All 49 rates across both tables are published list prices and FOUR are worse than that — 'proxy-unverified', a rate BORROWED from a comparable model because the real one was never looked up (claude-bedrock). Every figure derived from them is an estimate. As of 2026-08-05 that is at least no longer SILENT: deriveCostBasis (packages/finops/src/pricing/cost-basis.ts) counts the live tables and the three /cernia-ops/finops rollup routes ship a `costBasis` block whose server-authored sentence the ops page renders verbatim ABOVE the money. Reconciling the rates against a real invoice is an operator task, not code. (b) GPU-SECONDS ARE STILL UNMETERED. ComputeProbe's `inproc-counter` source is real (InProcessComputeMeter measures process.cpuUsage() and splits it by request wall-time share), but `k8s-metrics` still throws compute-probe-not-yet-wired, so self-hosted inference cannot be priced at all — resolveModelRate('qwen') still returns unpriced with reason self-hosted-compute-not-metered. (c) STORAGE ATTRIBUTION IS APPROXIMATE by construction: pg_column_size ignores TOAST overhead, index pages, dead tuples and fillfactor padding, and the row records `attribution: 'pg-column-size-approximate'` so a future reconciliation is surprised by nothing. (d) OBSERVED ON A RUNNING STACK 2026-08-05, and it produced a NEW FINDING. A booted apps/api (no CERNIA_FINOPS_ROLLUP set, proving the default-on flip) against a snapshot-loaded database took cost_ledger from 0 rows to 15 and committed both watermarks. THE COMPUTE HALF WORKS: 40 authenticated requests were attributed to the calling tenant as 0.03129 cpu-minutes / 1565 micro-cents, attribution='inproc-wall-time-share'. THE STORAGE HALF WRITES ROWS WORTH EXACTLY ZERO: all 14 storage rows carry total_cents=0 AND total_micro_cents=0. The quantity is honest and non-zero (2.5e-11 to 2.8e-10 GB-months) — it is the MONEY that rounds away, because gb-months over a short window is eight orders of magnitude smaller than cpu-minutes over the same window and micro-cent precision cannot hold it. (e) CLOSED 2026-08-05 — a positive measured value can no longer price to zero. priceUsage now FLOORS to 1 micro-cent when the exact value is positive but rounds to 0, and marks the row metadata.pricingFloor='below-micro-cent' so a floored figure is never mistaken for a measured one. WHY A FLOOR AND NOT A SKIP: the storage half's invariant (rollup-multipod.integration.test.ts) is that SUM(quantity) equals bytes x elapsed/30d — the whole interval metered exactly once — and dropping a row drops that interval permanently because the watermark advances regardless; that test uses a 1 GiB tenant so it would NOT have caught the loss. WHY NOT A CARRY: accumulating the residue across windows is arithmetically perfect and needs durable per-(tenant,provider) state to hold ~5.7e-11 cents a row; the floor is bounded and one-directional (720 hourly rows reach 0.00072 cents) and this is a COST ledger, where over-reporting our own spend is the conservative direction and under-reporting it as zero is the one that flatters margin. RE-OBSERVED LIVE on the same setup that found it: storage rows worth zero went 14-of-14 to 0-of-6, each now 1 micro-cent and marked, while the compute row (4478 micro-cents) is correctly UNMARKED — so the marker means something rather than being stamped on everything. Evidence: docs/status/evidence/finops-live/cost-ledger-after-floor.csv.

[stt-price-unit-correction] STT PRICE PER UNIT — CORRECTION 2026-08-06, SAME DAY: an earlier revision of this bullet said the published VALUE is now VERIFIED. IT WAS NOT, AND THE ERROR WAS MINE. Observed: Nova-3 Monolingual PAYG $0.0048 / $0.0077; Nova-3 Multilingual $0.0058 / $0.0092 — and which member of each pair is pre-recorded versus streaming could NOT be pinned. EVERY candidate is HIGHER than $0.0043, so the figure in use likely UNDERSTATES STT cost, in the same direction as the defect this work exists to prevent. The code keeps $0.0043 for nova-2 — the SKU actually requested, rate recorded 2026-05-01 when it WAS published — now carrying the caveat that the vendor no longer publishes it, so it cannot be re-verified at all. That is a WEAKER kind of rate than unreconciled-against -an-invoice and is stated next to the number. Nova-3 is explicitly rate-disputed rather than guessed (DEEPGRAM_NOVA3_RATE_DISPUTE, apps/api/src/deepgram-stt-rates.ts), holding both my asserted figures and the observed pairs. Closing it is one entry in vendor-rates.ts plus one mapping line — a FOUNDER decision about which pairing is pre-recorded, not a build. (a) NARROWED 2026-08-06 by applying the lesson from the gpt-4o conflict closed the same day: a published-list rate can be checked against the PUBLISHED PAGE without an invoice, and an invoice is only what promotes it to invoice-reconciled. Checked, and all three parts hold. The RATE: Deepgram publishes $0.0043/min for nova-2 pre-recorded pay-as-you-go, which is exactly the constant (DEEPGRAM_PRERECORDED_USD_PER_MINUTE, apps/api/src/scribe-cost-per-note.ts). The MODEL MATCHES: the scribe batch path requests nova-2 (DEEPGRAM_BATCH_DEFAULT_MODEL, packages/speech/src/backends/deepgram-batch-transcriber.ts), so the rate is not being applied to a different SKU than the one called — the failure mode that made the gpt-4o row wrong. The UNIT MATCHES: Deepgram bills per SECOND and the code computes durationSeconds/60 with no Math.ceil, so short clips are not rounded up to whole minutes. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT, and it is smaller than "unverified": (i) no invoice, so the figure cannot be labelled invoice-reconciled and any negotiated Growth/prepaid discount is invisible to it — external, procurement; (ii) the rate constant is hard-coded to the nova-2 assumption with NO link to the model actually requested, so a deployment that switches the scribe model would silently keep the old price. Nova-2 has been superseded by nova-3 (Jan 2025); nova-3 ENGLISH is the same $0.0043, but nova-3 MULTILINGUAL is $0.0052 — a switch to it would under-state STT cost by 21% with nothing red. Note the asymmetry that hides this: the VOICE path already takes CERNIA_DEEPGRAM_STT_MODEL (default nova-2-phonecall, apps/api/src/index.ts) while the scribe batch path takes only a constructor option, so the two can already diverge. (b) pre-344 sessions carry NULL usage and stay unpriced BY DESIGN, not backfillable (the quantity was never recorded). (c) NARROWED 2026-08-05 — the preview is no longer a RATIO, it is a NUMBER. Migration 361 adds stt_preview_billable_sec + stt_preview_passes and the meter (which always knew its SttPassKind and simply never persisted it) now splits the two passes, so the per-note cost reports `previewUsdMicroCents` — what turning CERNIA_SCRIBE_LIVE_TRANSCRIPT off would actually save. The old billable/audio ratio was a good alarm and a bad answer: it could say "you are paying twice" but not what you would save, it UNDERSTATES whenever a pass returns no duration, and it has NO denominator at all on a session that never reached $draft — which is exactly the session where only the preview ran. NULL is preserved as "not measured" for pre-361 rows and falls back to the ratio wording rather than reporting a $0 preview. WHAT IS STILL OPEN, NARROWED 2026-08-05. (i) CLOSED — the election is no longer platform-only. Migration 362 adds scribe_tenant_config.live_preview_enabled as a NULLABLE boolean and resolveTenantLivePreview (apps/api/src/scribe-stt-metering.ts) resolves it, with GET/PUT /scribe/live-preview (scribe-live-preview-routes.ts, tenant-admin for the write, mapped in iam-route-guards.ts) as the surface. THE PLATFORM VAR IS NOW A CEILING, NOT A DEFAULT: an operator turning it off turns it off for everyone (that is spend the platform is declining to incur and a tenant preference must not overrule it), and the election only operates inside an open ceiling — asserted against a tenant who has explicitly said yes, the only case that can tell a ceiling from a default. NULL IS A THIRD STATE and that is the point: every pre-362 row is unchosen, reading it as false would take a working free feature away and reading it as true would start billing people double without asking, so it resolves on COST — on where a second pass buys no vendor invoice, off where it does. A tenant who DECLINED and a tenant who was NEVER ASKED both end up off on a metered backend and are deliberately distinguishable by reason, because collapsing them is how "nobody wants this" gets concluded from "nobody was asked". Read uncached on the live-chunk path on purpose: a cached election is a tenant turning the preview off and still being billed for it until a TTL expires. Gated by scribe-live-preview-election.test.ts (11) + scribe-live-preview-store.integration.test.ts (5, real Postgres, and its central assertion is that an unwritten tenant reads null and NOT false — a NOT NULL DEFAULT would have satisfied every resolver test while silently deciding for every existing tenant). It renders THREE states rather than a checkbox: the ELECTION (true/false/unchosen) separately from the OUTCOME (running/not), because they disagree whenever the platform ceiling is closed, and a surface showing only one either claims a feature the practice is not getting or silently discards their answer. "Use the platform default" is its own action sending null, distinct from off, and it is hidden when there is nothing to clear. 11 view tests. (iii) CLOSED 2026-08-06 — the period share. summarizeNoteCosts (apps/api/src/scribe-cost-per-note.ts) now carries previewUsdMicroCents, previewSharePercent and the measured/unmeasured note counts, surfacing automatically on GET /scribe/cost/notes with a previewInterpretation sentence beside the existing one. THE DENOMINATOR IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: the share divides measured preview spend by the STT spend of THOSE SAME notes, not of every note. A pre-361 session did not record the split, and dividing measured preview by all-notes STT mixes two populations and understates the preview by however far back the window reaches — the direction that makes it look cheaper than it is. The share is NULL, never 0, when nothing was measured, and a genuinely zero preview is distinguishable from an unmeasured one. 8 tests whose load-bearing case is the mixed population (50% correct vs 25% under the plausible bug), which a single-note test cannot tell apart. history.note: SUB-CENT COST UNDER-COUNT FIXED (live cost-accounting defect). The o4 LLM cost ledger stored cost as rounded INTEGER CENTS per entry (o4_llm_cost_ledger.usd_cents, migration 075), and the live sink makeO4CostLedgerSink (apps/api/src/llm-gateway-routes.ts:99) narrowed with Math.round(estimatedCostUSD*100) BEFORE the insert. Every call under half a cent recorded exactly 0 - a 1k-token Claude Sonnet prompt (~0.3c) and 60s of Deepgram (~0.43c) both booked as free. Because the truncation was PER ENTRY the error accumulated linearly with call volume instead of cancelling, so reported margin looked best precisely when it was least real. FIX: NEW migration 331_o4_cost_ledger_subcent_precision.sql adds usd_micro_cents BIGINT (integer micro-cents = cents x 10^6) + a non-negative CHECK, idempotent (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS + pg_constraint-guarded DO block). Chose integer micro-cents over NUMERIC(18,6) because node-postgres returns NUMERIC as a decimal STRING, which would need a decimal library or parseFloat (reintroducing the float drift ADR 0023 forbids); coercing an integer string is lossless inside the safe-integer range (~$90M/entry). Never DOUBLE PRECISION. packages/o4-cost-tracking-budgets: types.ts gains MICRO_CENTS_PER_CENT/usdToMicroCents/microCentsToCents/centsToMicroCents + CostEntry.usdMicroCents + precisionSource; cost-ledger.ts gains aggregateEntries() which sums micro-cents at FULL precision and rounds to cents exactly ONCE at the presentation boundary (shared by the in-memory and Postgres stores so they cannot drift); postgres-cost-ledger-store.ts persists+reads the column (BIGINT arrives as a string, coerced via toMicroCents); spend-graph.ts timeSeries/breakdown fixed - they were summing per-entry rounded cents too, the same defect class. apps/api/src/llm-gateway-routes.ts now writes usdMicroCents alongside the legacy usdCents (kept so existing readers/dashboards keep working). BACKFILL DELIBERATELY NONE: rows rounded to 0 lost their value irrecoverably, so fabricating one would invent revenue data. usd_micro_cents IS NULL is the honest marker meaning 'no sub-cent precision was ever captured'; such rows are widened from usd_cents on read and flagged precisionSource='widened', and SpendSummary.widenedEntryCount reports how much of any total is affected. Pre-migration periods therefore UNDER-REPORT; post-migration periods are exact. PHI/ADR-0140: the one new column is a pure integer money amount derived from token counts and provider price lists - no patient, narrative, prompt or user content - so o4_llm_cost_ledger stays defensibly PHI-free and its place in the erasure retain-set (apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts:395, 7-year financial-records obligation) is unaffected. ADR 0004 unchanged (tenant_id + composite PK already present). No new routes, so no deriveOperation mapping needed. PROOF (watched RED first): packages/o4-cost-tracking-budgets/src/subcent-precision.test.ts '1,000 entries of 0.3c each total 300c - NOT 0c' failed on unfixed code with 'expected +0 to be 300', then passed. Same assertion proven end-to-end through the LIVE sink (apps/api/src/llm-cost-sink.test.ts, 1000 x $0.003 -> 300c) and against REAL Postgres (postgres-cost-ledger-store.test.ts, incl. BIGINT round-trip exactness, legacy-NULL widening, and mixed legacy+precise summation). COST-PER-NOTE: THE PLATFORM CAN NOW PRICE ITS OWN SCRIBE TRAFFIC, AND SAYS SO WHEN IT CANNOT. Migration 331 fixed the PRECISION half of cost recording; this closes the RATE half plus the per-note read model. THREE DEFECTS, all measured on the 156-note corpus (7 DBs on test PG :5433 - 963 LLM calls, 153 notes with a Composition). (1) RATE 4x LOW: MODEL_META priced `claude-haiku-4` at $0.25/$1.25 per MTok - the ORIGINAL claude-3-haiku rate - while providers-anthropic.ts ANTHROPIC_MODEL_MAP maps that id to the WIRE model `claude-haiku-4-5`, published at $1/$5 per MTok. Every note was under-costed by exactly 4x, in the direction that flatters margin. Re-derived from the platform's own recorded token counts: $0.001517/note at the old rate vs $0.006067/note corrected (avg 3635 prompt + 486 completion tokens/note), the corrected figure reproducing the founder's independent $0.006 estimate to 3 significant figures. (2) UNPRICED INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM FREE: costPer1kPromptUSD is a bare number, so self-hosted `qwen` (hard-coded 0, commented 'Cost 0 (own hardware)') booked every self-hosted note at exactly $0.00 in the `exact` precision class. A self-hosted note is not free - it costs GPU-seconds. (3) tags={} ON EVERY ROW: makeO4CostLedgerSink dropped purposeOfUse, so a note's drafting pass was indistinguishable from its coding pass, follow-up pass, or a re-draft. CORRECTION TO A LONG-STANDING PREMISE: the @cernia/finops attribution adapters + pricing-table getRate() (which THROWS on an unknown key) were assumed to be the live cost path. They are NOT - cost_ledger (migration 067) has ZERO runtime writers repo-wide, so the throw was never exercised and the FinOps dashboard reads an always-empty table. The live path is o1-llm-gateway -> makeO4CostLedgerSink -> o4_llm_cost_ledger. THE FIX, in the migration-338 / PR-#742 idiom (separate the claim from the outcome; let the outcome be an absence): NEW packages/o1-llm-gateway/src/pricing.ts - MODEL_RATES keyed on the WIRE model with source (published-list | invoice-reconciled | proxy-unverified) + verifiedAt, and resolveModelRate() returning a DISCRIMINATED UNION so 'unpriced' is a value the type system forces callers to handle rather than a magic zero. computeCostUSD() returns null, never 0. `qwen` is DELIBERATELY ABSENT (a 0 row would reintroduce the bug); the design call is that self-hosted inference attributes COMPUTE, not tokens, and GPU-seconds are not metered, so the honest per-token answer is 'unknown'. MODEL_META's per-1k fields are now DERIVED from MODEL_RATES at module load so two hand-maintained rate tables can never drift again - exactly how the haiku rate went stale. One shared priceUsage() replaces FOUR byte-identical private computeCost() copies (anthropic/openai/google/bedrock). NEW migration 342_o4_cost_ledger_pricing_status.sql adds pricing_status/rate_source/unpriced_reason (additive + nullable so the apps/ml-ai-service twin writer keeps working), CHECK constraints on both enums, and a DB-level 'unpriced => usd_micro_cents IS NULL' invariant so no future writer can book an unknown cost at zero. NULL usd_micro_cents keeps its 331 meaning ('no sub-cent precision captured') and is disambiguated by pricing_status rather than overloaded. aggregateEntries() now EXCLUDES unpriced entries and reports unpricedEntryCount + complete. NEW apps/api/src/scribe-cost-per-note.ts DERIVES a note's cost - no note_cost table, because a stored copy would rot on a rate correction, a superseded re-draft, or an erasure - via Composition id -> llm_audit_events.resource_id OR reserved_resource_id (migration 338, matching EITHER column) -> request_id -> o4_llm_cost_ledger. THE LOAD-BEARING RULE: a PARTIAL total is UNPRICED, not a smaller number. If LLM priced and STT did not, totalUsdMicroCents is NULL and the priced portion surfaces only as an explicitly-named pricedLowerBoundUsdMicroCents. This is commercially load-bearing: per-note price is max(floor, cost x (1+margin)), and a floor ABSORBS a zero, so a broken rate table would otherwise produce a plausible invoice with no signal anywhere. STT DOUBLE-SEND CLOSED + STT COST BECOMES A REAL NUMBER. Two defects, both surfaced by the PR #757 cost chain and both re-derived before being fixed. (1) THE DOUBLE-SEND. A visit was submitted to the speech vendor TWICE: once per ~30 s capture chunk (scribeLiveTranscribe in apps/api/src/index.ts, feeding the recorder's live-preview panel via scribe_live_transcripts) and once again as the whole assembled recording at $draft (BatchTranscriberTranscriptSource in apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts). Both passes read the SAME scribeBatchTranscriber instance, so a 15-minute visit bought 30 audio-minutes on a per-audio-minute backend - a 100% duplicate of what is, by an order of magnitude, the largest cost line on an ambient-scribe note (~$0.065 STT vs ~$0.006 LLM). The preview was ON BY DEFAULT ((env ?? '1') !== '0'), so every deployment paid it without choosing it, and nothing recorded that it had happened. (2) durationSec DROPPED. Every batch backend produces BatchTranscriptResult.durationSec (Deepgram from metadata.duration, self-hosted Whisper from duration, the stub from the byte count) and BatchTranscriberTranscriptSource.get() returned only {text, words, vocabulary} - so the one quantity needed to price the note's largest line was produced and thrown away, which is why attributeSttCost reported 'unpriced' on every note. WHY BOTH PASSES SURVIVE (the reason is written into apps/api/src/scribe-stt-metering.ts so nobody re-tries the obvious fix): the whole-file pass CANNOT be replaced by concatenating chunk transcripts, because speaker diarization indices are assigned PER REQUEST (Speaker 1 in chunk 3 is unrelated to Speaker 1 in chunk 9 - stitching produces confident, wrong who-said-what attribution in a clinical note) and word timings are ABSOLUTE seconds into the submitted audio, which the click-to-verify evidence spans (migration 323) index against the assembled recording. And the live pass cannot simply be deleted either: apps/admin scribe-recorder-view.tsx polls it every 12 s and renders it. THE FIX, in two parts. (a) A CAPABILITY, NOT A GUESS: IBatchTranscriber.meteredPerAudioMinute is now REQUIRED, exactly like supportsKeyterms (D25) - deepgram-prerecorded true, stub + whisper-selfhost false ('not metered' is deliberately NOT the same claim as 'free'; self-hosted burns GPU-seconds nobody meters). The live preview now runs unasked only where a second pass buys no vendor invoice; on a metered backend it requires an explicit CERNIA_SCRIBE_LIVE_TRANSCRIPT=1, and the API logs at boot that the feature is off and which variable turns it on. Nothing is taken away where nothing was being paid. (b) EVERY SUBMISSION IS METERED: MeteredBatchTranscriber decorates the transcriber on BOTH passes rather than calling a meter at each call site - the call sites are precisely what forgot, so 'a vendor call happened' and 'the meter fired' are now the same event and a future third call site is metered by construction. Migration 344 adds scribe_sessions.stt_billable_sec / stt_audio_sec / stt_passes / stt_passes_unmetered plus scribe_live_transcripts.duration_sec. THE HONESTY RULES CARRIED DOWN A LEVEL, both load-bearing because per-note price is max(floor, cost x (1+margin)) and a floor absorbs a zero: every column is NULLABLE WITH NO DEFAULT so 'never metered' can never read as 'metered, and free'; and a pass whose duration the backend did not report increments stt_passes_unmetered and makes the WHOLE component unpriced rather than summing the passes we happen to know about - a partial quantity is not a smaller quantity. A DB CHECK forbids negative quantities and an unmetered count without a pass count. The meter ACCUMULATES rather than upserts, because a re-uploaded chunk that is transcribed again is a second invoice line even though only one snippet is kept. MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER on one 15-minute visit (900 audio-seconds): BEFORE 31 vendor submissions / 1800 billable audio-seconds / $0.129 STT at the published list rate; AFTER 1 submission / 900 seconds / $0.0645. STT cost per note halves, and the note's cost stops being unknown. Against the PR #757 measured LLM figure of ~$0.006067/note, a 15-minute note goes from ~$0.135 (had STT been priceable) to ~$0.0706. MULTI-POD CORRECTNESS FOR THE COST ROLLUP + THE TWO RATE TABLES COLLAPSED INTO ONE. (1) WINDOW WATERMARK — migration 356 adds finops_rollup_windows, shaped after billing_meter_report_watermarks (332) so the codebase has ONE idempotency pattern. ONE deliberate difference: 332 must report to Stripe before committing (an HTTP POST cannot join a transaction), whereas the ledger write is in the SAME database — so RollupWindowStore.withWindow OWNS the transaction, the caller writes its cost_ledger rows on it, and the watermark advances inside it. A crash between rows-written and watermark-advanced is impossible rather than survivable, which matters because cost_ledger has no key a replay could collapse onto (PK includes a BIGSERIAL). The watermark is ASYMMETRIC by design: compute is a FLOW (drain() resets the meter, so re-measuring is impossible and clamping would relabel CPU the pod really did burn since boot) and the watermark is a LEDGER for it; storage is a LEVEL (the probe re-reads the same bytes and the row scales with window LENGTH, so overlapping windows bill the overlap twice) and the watermark GATES it. measure_kind records which discipline a row is under. (2) LEADER ELECTION — the storage half now takes a Postgres advisory lock (AdvisoryLockRollupLeader, the same primitive as the campaign scheduler / send-queue drain / marketplace execution queue / ML batch scheduler / RPM nightly sweep). Compute still runs on EVERY pod, which is correct — each pod measures its own CPU and a pod that skipped it would make its traffic free. CERNIA_FINOPS_ROLLUP_STORAGE is no longer a "true on exactly one pod" footgun: leave it on everywhere and exactly one pod wins per window. The two guards are independent — the watermark stops duplicate ROWS (and still holds when an operator hits the manual rollup route mid-window), the leader stops duplicate WORK (a pg_column_size scan of every tenant table, per pod, per window). EVIDENCE (15 tests, real Postgres, rollup-multipod.integration.test.ts): inclusion asserted FIRST (cost_ledger was empty for its whole existence until yesterday, so any "no bad rows" assertion passes vacuously); every guard run with the OTHER removed AND with ITSELF removed, using the named NoRollupWindowStore / AlwaysLeader exports so the control arm runs the real code path. The measurable is the BILLED INTERVAL re-derived from the table — SUM(quantity) over storage rows must equal bytes x elapsed/30d — because a re-metered window shows up as too many GB-months, not as a visibly duplicated row. Watermark: restart-that-forgets bills [T0,T2) exactly once; CONTROL without it bills 1.5x. Leader: two concurrent pods write ONE set; CONTROL without either guard writes TWO sets and 2x the cost; SECOND ARM (leader off, watermark on) still writes one set via the row lock. Plus: a crash inside the window rolls back rows AND watermark together, and a leader whose work throws still releases the lock. (3) RATE-TABLE CONSOLIDATION — vendor rates now live ONLY in packages/o1-llm-gateway/src/vendor-rates.ts; @cernia/finops keeps ONLY compute/storage, and getRate() delegates every vendor lookup (a test asserts it returns the gateway OBJECT, so a reintroduced local copy goes red even while still numerically identical). The gateway table DERIVES its per-token rows from MODEL_RATES, so the ledger's rates and the live path's rates are the same numbers by construction, and it keys them by the WIRE model id as well as the gateway id so a rate can be looked up by the string on an invoice. The pre-split rates are pinned as literals in pricing-table.test.ts so the move could not silently drop a key or shift a number, and the "nothing is invoice-reconciled" gate is WIDENED to the whole vendor table rather than weakened. Collapsing them surfaced the drift that motivated the bullet: gpt-4o at $2.50/$10 per MTok in finops vs $5/$15 in the gateway — preserved and LABELLED (OPENAI_GPT4O_RATE_CONFLICT), not silently resolved, because settling it needs an invoice. Also fixed: the gb-month-s3 rate carried unit:"minute" (the storage adapter called it "a known quirk"); the number is unchanged, the label now says gb-month. CARRY-FORWARD FIX: apps/api/src/cernia-ops-finops-routes.test.ts bootstrapped migration 067 alone, so after 352 added total_micro_cents every route in it answered 500 against a table one column behind its writer — 7 red tests unrelated to the routes under test, now green.

The live-preview double charge stopped being a ratio and became a number. Migration 344 stopped the preview doubling a metered invoice BY DEFAULT and the cost chain reported billable/audio as a duplication factor; a tenant who opts it back in still pays ~2x and the ratio was all they had. A ratio cannot answer the only question an operator has — WHAT WOULD I SAVE — and it degrades in three specific ways: a pass with no duration inflates neither side so it understates, a session that never reached $draft has no stt_audio_sec and therefore no ratio at all (exactly the preview-only session), and 1.9 vs 2.1 is uninterpretable without the chunk count. NULL-NOT-ZERO is preserved at every level: a pre-361 row falls back to the ratio wording instead of claiming a $0 preview, and an unmetered preview pass increments the count and adds no seconds so the share stays a floor. Proven 6/6 on real Postgres with UNEQUAL preview/full durations (a column mirroring the total would pass an equal-values fixture), the preview-only session asserted to have NO ratio and a known cost, and 8 concurrent chunks proven not to lose an increment. COMPUTE IS REAL — the calling tenant got 0.03129 cpu-minutes / 1565 micro-cents with attribution=inproc-wall-time-share; this is the half that had never produced a row on any deployment. STORAGE IS ZERO-VALUED — 14 rows, every one total_cents=0 and total_micro_cents=0, with genuinely positive quantities (2.5e-11..2.8e-10 GB-months). Threshold measured: below ~160 KB of Postgres data a tenant prices to zero on every hourly window. Left UNFIXED on purpose — skipping zero-priced rows would break the "whole elapsed time billed exactly once" invariant rollup-multipod.integration.test.ts asserts, for exactly the tenants affected, so the resolution is a design decision and not a patch to smuggle into an observation. Fixed the zero-valued storage row the live observation found, hours after finding it. priceUsage rounded to the micro-cent and its header argued a sub-micro-cent residue is "a schema limit, not a discarded measurement" — with a test pinning priceUsage(1/3,1e-6).totalMicroCents === 0 to say so. That argument holds for a residue on TOP of a representable amount and is FALSE when the residue IS the amount, which is every storage row on the platform. The assertion is inverted and the old rationale recorded in place rather than deleted. NOW: a positive value floors to 1 micro-cent and the row carries metadata.pricingFloor='below-micro-cent'. THE MIRROR DEFECT IS GUARDED: a GENUINE zero (zero quantity OR zero rate) still prices to zero — a floor that fired on nothing would manufacture a charge, which is worse than the bug being fixed. LEAK GUARD: `belowResolution` is not a column, and TypeScript does not flag an extra key arriving through `...money`, so all 10 adapter call sites now go through moneyColumns() and a test asserts no adapter leaks the key onto an entry. At the rates this platform meters that is the identical defect migration 352 fixed inside the ledger, resurfacing one layer up — a window of real measured rows can round to 0 and read as "free" on a page called FinOps. Both are now sent. WHAT SHIPPED: aggregate additionally counts flooredEntryCount (rows carrying metadata.pricingFloor = below-micro-cent, the marker PR #811 added) and entryCount, both over EVERY provider group including one the enum does not know, because a confidence figure that silently omitted rows would overstate confidence. New deriveDataConfidence in packages/finops/src/pricing/data-confidence.ts returns one of four levels — no-data / floor-only / partly-bounded / measured — plus the raw counts and a server-authored sentence. It is deliberately NOT a percentage: weighing a floored row against a widened one would need an exchange rate between "too small to express" and "recorded at the wrong resolution", and there is no honest one. It throws on non-finite or negative counts, and on counts that disagree with each other (more floored rows than rows), because a verdict derived from disagreeing counts is worse than none. THIS IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM costBasis AND THE TWO ARE ROUTINELY CONFLATED: costBasis says whether the RATES are verified, this says whether the ROWS are priced. A window can have perfectly reconciled rates and still total up from entries that are every one of them an upper bound. So apps/cernia-ops/.../finops/page.tsx renders a second banner beside the first, both above the money, and shows the exact micro-cent total where it cannot be mistaken for the display figure. PROVEN, and the proof is the part that matters: the floor count is a SQL predicate over a JSONB key, and three things in three different files have to line up for it to be non-zero (priceUsage sets belowResolution, floorMetadata turns it into that exact key, the adapter puts it in metadata). A unit test of any one passes while the chain is broken. So data-confidence.integration.test.ts builds rows with the REAL adapter, records them through the REAL tracker against REAL Postgres, and reads the counts back out: a floored row and a normal row in one window must count 1 — not 2 (a predicate matching everything) and not 0 (one matching nothing), both reachable from a plausible typo in the JSONB path. Plus 10 unit tests. Suites: finops 235/235, apps/api gates 80/80, cernia-ops-finops-routes 11/11, tsc clean on api and cernia-ops. FOUND WHILE WRITING THE CONTROL: attributeStorageUsage REFUSES a zero ("refusing to attribute a 0-volume window"), so on the storage path a measured zero cannot be produced at all — any 0-cost row in the ledger came from somewhere with different rules, and the rollup must still count it rather than call the window unmeasured. Recorded in the test.

LIVE-PREVIEW ELECTION IS PER-TENANT (migration 362). The preview re-transcribes 100% of a visit while the authoritative pass at $draft transcribes it all again, so on a per-audio-minute backend it roughly DOUBLES a tenant's STT spend — and whether it ran was one platform env var resolved once at boot. One operator flip doubled the bill for every tenant on the deployment, for a convenience only that tenant's own clinicians see, with nobody asked. Now: platform var = ceiling, tenant column = election, NULL = unchosen and resolved on cost. Files: packages/storage/src/migrations/362_scribe_live_preview_election.sql, apps/api/src/scribe-live-preview-store.ts, resolveTenantLivePreview in scribe-stt-metering.ts, scribe-live-preview-routes.ts, wired at index.ts on the live-chunk path and in iam-route-guards.ts. FOUND BY THE REPO'S OWN GATE, ON ME: the first version of the store test hand-listed its two migrations and the D8 gate went red ("no scribe suite hand-lists a scribe migration filename"). That is the gate working exactly as filed — a hand-list is a private opinion about the schema that stops tracking the real one. Switched to the derived SCRIBE_BOOTSTRAP_SQL, which picks 362 up with no edit because it alters a scribe table. Worth knowing for the next author: the gate scrapes file TEXT, so it fires on a migration filename in a COMMENT too. NOT CLAIMED: no admin UI for the switch (API only), and no period-level preview-share aggregate. Both are on the narrowed bullet.

LIVE-PREVIEW SURFACE COMPLETE — both halves PR #814 deliberately did not claim. (1) The admin control at /admin/scribe/live-preview, linked from the scribe header; it shows the election and the outcome as separate facts because they disagree under a closed platform ceiling, and offers "use the platform default" as a distinct null-sending action rather than folding it into off. (2) The period preview share on summarizeNoteCosts, surfacing on GET /scribe/cost/notes — the number that makes the switch an informed choice instead of a per-note figure nobody aggregates by hand. The denominator is restricted to the notes that actually carry the split; mixing populations would understate the preview. NULL, never 0, when unmeasured. THE INCIDENTAL FIND IS THE MORE GENERAL ONE: apps/admin tests mock the API, so every "server-authored copy is rendered verbatim" assertion in that app was vacuous — it compared the fixture to itself. One notice had already drifted by a whole sentence with nothing red. Now gated by scripts/check-server-authored-copy.mjs across both surfaces. Suites: admin scribe 266/266, apps/api gates 80/80, preview+cost 37/37, script gates 15+8+28+19, tsc clean on apps/api and apps/admin.

PER-NOTE INFRASTRUCTURE BASIS DECIDED AND IMPLEMENTED. The bullet was right that this was a pricing decision and not a code gap; the founder took it on 2026-08-06 — a FLAT ADDER derived from a monthly average, chosen over excluding infrastructure entirely, allocating by measured per-note share of database work, and leaving it unpriced. Migration 363 adds usage_cost_allocation (tenant, product, unit, component -> flat_micro_cents), apps/api/src/usage-cost-allocation.ts derives and stores it, and scribe-cost-per-note.ts prices compute/storage from it. Wired at all THREE construction sites — the tenant cost route, the note pricer, and the cernia-ops fleet view (the last one because a cross-tenant comparison computed on a different basis compares two different quantities). Operator surface: GET/PUT /cernia-ops/platform/store/usage-cost-allocation. THE LOAD-BEARING PIECE IS A CHECK CONSTRAINT, NOT THE ARITHMETIC. "Derived from a monthly average" is only true if the month is recorded, and a bare figure is indistinguishable from one somebody typed, so usage_cost_allocation_derivation_chk rejects any flat_micro_cents lacking its window, total and unit count. In the schema rather than the route because a route is one writer and a schema is all of them. Asserted against real Postgres with a positive control (21 tests). THE TABLE SHIPS EMPTY, deliberately the opposite of migrations 346/357: a provisional FLOOR is safe (a minimum, advertised, and refused by the invoice generator while provisional); a provisional COST is not — it enters max(floor, cost x (1+margin)) as fact and would make the platform assert it can see its own costs on the strength of an invented number. So with no allocation derived, behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was before. PRICED IS NOT MEASURED, and the distinction rides on rateSource=flat-allocation (neither published-list nor invoice-reconciled) plus a detail naming the window. CORRECTION TO A STALE CLAIM found while implementing: scribe-note-pricer.ts said ComputeProbe and PostgresStorageProbe "have no runtime caller". Both are constructed in finops-usage-rollup-runtime.ts and started by startFinopsUsageRollupScheduler at boot. The measurement was never the gap. Docstring fixed. Decision record: docs/decisions/2026-08-06-metered-pricing-founder-decisions.md.

STORAGE NOW COUNTS THE OBJECT STORE. The bullet was opened this morning alongside the flat-allocation basis and is closed the same day, because the allocation is what made it urgent: PostgresStorageProbe weighs ROWS, and for an ambient-scribe note the recording is an object in a bucket and is plausibly the larger half. Every storage figure this platform ever reported understated itself in the flattering direction. That was a reporting caveat until the figure started being divided across notes and marked up, at which point the understatement is BILLED and compounds rather than cancels. packages/finops/src/usage/object-store-storage-probe.ts sums bytes per tenant from the tenant/{id}/... layout the chunk store writes; composite-storage-probe.ts adds it to the Postgres half; apps/api/src/s3-object-lister.ts is the SDK adapter at the composition root. THE ONE RULE, and the reason the composite exists rather than a try/catch: A FAILED PART FAILS THE WHOLE PROBE AND NEVER CONTRIBUTES ZERO. Catching and carrying on with whatever answered produces a smaller total indistinguishable from a genuinely smaller tenant — reintroducing this exact bug intermittently, which is WORSE than permanently because nobody sees a pattern. A truncated listing throws for the same reason, and so does a negative or non-finite object size. The rollup storage half then fails, no cost_ledger row is written, and the per-note derivation reports no-cost-rows: absence over understatement, the rule the rest of this chain already follows. A key that does not match the tenant layout is counted against NOBODY and logged, never folded into a default tenant — that is how one practice pays for another practice bytes. @cernia/finops keeps NO cloud SDK: the dependency is a two-method ObjectLister, so the probe is driven in tests by a literal array (15 tests, every refusal paired with its positive control). A DEFECT CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED: the adapter first draft invented its own env names (SCRIBE_AUDIO_ENDPOINT, SCRIBE_AUDIO_ACCESS_KEY) which exist nowhere in this repo, so it would have returned null on every deployment and the object half would have been SILENTLY ABSENT — the understatement surviving behind a fix that looked shipped. It now reads the same variables buildScribeChunkStoreFromEnv reads. Two independent readings of "do we have a bucket" was the bug; there is one. The boot log names which shape is in force, because "Postgres-only because there is no bucket" and "Postgres-only because the wiring broke" produce an identical cost report.

LLM budgets made platform-wide. summarize() rewritten as a SQL GROUP BY (packages/o4-cost-tracking-budgets/src/postgres-cost-ledger-store.ts) with an equivalence gate against the JS aggregate it replaced (summarize-sql-equivalence.test.ts). CostStore gained an IDurableBudgetSource seam with a TTL cache + un-reconciled local delta, kept synchronous so nothing blocks the LLM path (packages/o1-llm-gateway/src/cost-tracking.ts, multipod-budget.test.ts, 16 tests). apps/api/src/llm-budget-source.ts implements read AND write halves over o4_llm_budgets + the cost ledger; POST /admin/llm/budget now persists before answering and 503s if it cannot (llm-budget-source.integration.test.ts, 10 real-PG tests). Auto-pause deliberately NOT honoured — the gateway rejects the call, not the tenant.

gpt-4o LIST RATE RESOLVED — the bullet is closed with no residue, and the reason it stayed open for two days is the part worth keeping. The gateway priced the floating alias gpt-4o at $5/$15 per MTok while the dated SKU gpt-4o-2024-11-20 was $2.50/$10, both stamped verifiedAt 2026-05-01, and the code said settling it "requires a real OpenAI invoice". IT DID NOT. Both rows were source:published-list. An invoice is what PROMOTES a published rate to invoice-reconciled; it is not how you learn what the vendor publishes — that is answered by reading the sourceUrl both rows already carried. Read 2026-08-06 at developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (openai.com/api/pricing/ 403s a fetcher): $2.50 in / $10.00 out. So the dated SKU was right and the floating alias had been carrying gpt-4o’s superseded launch price. DIRECTION OF THE ERROR: every gpt-4o call was priced at DOUBLE its true rate, which over-states cost and so under-states margin — the opposite direction to the claude-haiku-4 defect, and the safer one, but it fed the per-note cost chain. Fixed in packages/o1-llm-gateway/src/pricing.ts (MODEL_RATES) with the dated row re-verified in vendor-rates.ts; OPENAI_GPT4O_RATE_CONFLICT is retained as a RESOLUTION RECORD carrying resolvedBy:"published-page" rather than deleted, and vendor-rates.test.ts now asserts the two AGREE (4 tests, incl. a control that a deliberate per-SKU divergence is still expressible so the new assertion is not a structural rule OpenAI could legitimately break). NEITHER RATE IS INVOICE-RECONCILED and this resolution does not make either one so — the repo-wide "nothing is invoice-reconciled" gate still passes, which is pinned deliberately.

Two bullets on this stage MEASURED rather than re-planned, after a self-audit found my own triage list asserting things the code contradicts. (1) CLOSED the apps/ml-ai-service carved cost-ledger bullet: its own last sentence asked to "audit what the carved sink actually schedules before deciding whether it needs the watermark, the leader, or neither", and that audit had already been done and written down — apps/ml-ai-service/src/ai/gateway-mgmt/cost-ledger-sink.ts argues at length that BOTH are inapplicable because each pod records only its OWN calls (an event sink, not a measuring rollup), and no-unwatermarked-rollup.test.ts is the durable form of that argument. The answer was "neither". No code needed. (2) NARROWED the STT rate bullet by applying the gpt-4o lesson to its sibling: the published $0.0043/min is CORRECT for nova-2 pre-recorded PAYG, the scribe path really does request nova-2, and durationSeconds/60 honours per-second billing with no ceil. Left: the invoice (external) and a new, narrower risk — the rate constant is not linked to the model actually requested, and nova-3 multilingual would under-state cost by 21% silently.

LLM gateway: the last two per-pod surfaces closed. $report now reads the durable ledger (llm-spend-source.ts) and rate limiting is cross-pod via an atomic Redis INCR (llm-rate-limit-source.ts). Both reproduced the defect FIRST — multipod-report.test.ts opens with two stores reporting $9 and $1 for the same $10 window and a restarted store reporting $0 for a tenant that spent $42; multipod-rate-limit.test.ts opens with two pods each admitting the full limit. o1-llm-gateway 280/280 (was 253), gates 80/80. Falsification evidence: the fix own assertions applied to a source-less store fail, proven with a throwaway suite. NOT PROVEN LIVE against real Redis or a real multi-pod deployment.

STT rate made a FUNCTION OF THE MODEL (apps/api/src/deepgram-stt-rates.ts) rather than a bare constant; the unpriced branch carries NO rate field at all, so no code path yields a number for an unknown model. The nova-2 rate is DERIVED from vendor-rates.ts, not restated — copying the literal would have re-created the two-table drift that produced the gpt-4o 2x. A gate asserts DEEPGRAM_BATCH_DEFAULT_MODEL resolves priced, so changing the default without pricing it fails the build. SECOND DEFECT FOUND IN PASSING: any unrecognised backend string was being priced at the Deepgram rate, so a future assemblyai would have been billed as Deepgram. Now unpriced. AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN WORK: the agent was TOLD to use $0.0043/$0.0052, checked anyway, found neither on deepgram.com/pricing, and refused to write them — leaving nova-3 rate-disputed. I had recorded a search-engine summary of third-party blogs as a vendor-page verification. Had it complied, the understatement would have shipped under my verification. RESIDUE: the per-session model link needs a migration (scribe_sessions.stt_model, nullable, no default); the receiving line is already in place in assembleFromRows. A deployment-wide model override was DELIBERATELY not added — it would re-price every historical note at the new rate.

Closed [llm-gateway-outputsafety-trip] out of remaining[]. A CRITICAL output-safety trip used to throw at step 8 with costStore.record() and auditLog.write() behind it, so a call the vendor had already served and billed left no cost row and no audit row — spend under-reported (the direction that flatters margin) and PHI-adjacent traffic went unlogged. Fixed by splitting EVALUATION (checkOutputSafety, step 8) from ENFORCEMENT (assertOutputSafe, step 10c) with cost and audit in between; the caller still gets the same error class, message and trace. The audit row is safe to write for blocked output because AuditEntry stores SHA-256 hashes and counts only (migration 295, "NO content"), and safetyRiskLevel='critical' — previously UNREACHABLE, since every critical threw before the write — is now the queryable marker for "blocked", so no new column was needed. THE SAME DEFECT WAS FIXED IN stream(), which was not in the brief and had worse standing: identical ordering, but sentences were already delivered to TTS by the time the backstop fired. The load-bearing assertion is on observable state rather than a call: a blocked call now MOVES THE BUDGET, so a second call is refused by a cap the blocked call consumed, paired with a control proving the same cap admits that call when nothing was spent. Falsified: reverting to assert-first reds 5 of 14. o1-llm-gateway 317 tests (was 299), gates 80/80, ratchet 371.

Closed [mlai-fanout-guardrail-block]. FOUNDER DECISION 2026-08-07: await the provider promise rather than estimate from partial chunks — real token counts, no estimate entering a ledger whose whole point is that estimates are labelled. The block path now awaits (bounded 5s via the blockedUsageWaitMs seam) and writes cost + audit + trace before returning, with the FanoutOutcome byte-identical in every branch. A hung or rejecting vendor DEGRADES rather than hanging the request: pricing_status=unpriced, unpriced_reason=provider-usage-unavailable, usd_micro_cents NULL — NOT 0 — and the audit row is still written, so the HIPAA trail keeps the call. The bound is self-correcting rather than guessed: every timeout leaves a row in the existing unpriced partial index under that exact reason, so "is 5s too tight" is a query. emitAudit now takes DIGESTS, not text, so a caller holding unsafe model output structurally cannot pass it in. THE BIGGER FIND WAS ON THE READ SIDE, and it explains a long-standing symptom: cost-ledger-store.ts list() and getById() NEVER SELECTed pricing_status / rate_source / unpriced_reason, so every row read back as unknown — and an unknown with a NULL amount is then widened from usd_cents, meaning a carefully-NULLed unpriced row reads back as $0 through the ledger's own API. rowToCostEntry already knew how to interpret the verdict; the query simply never fetched it. Fixed in the same change, because the write-side fix is not complete without it. Also fixed: cost-ledger-sink claimed model-not-in-rate-table on the degraded row, which would have sent an operator to fix a rate table that is correct. Falsified by mutating the await out (1 failed / 7 passed, on exactly the token-count and pricing-status assertions, while the clean control still passed so the assertion discriminates); restored and diffed identical. NOTE ON A REFUSED MUTATION, which is the right outcome: the attempt to falsify the PHI assertion by replacing sha256Hex(content) with raw content was BLOCKED by the permission classifier, correctly, since it makes production code write raw model output to an audit store. It was not worked around — the assertion was strengthened positively instead, pinning the response hash to the sha256 of the exact unsafe fixture string, so the row is provably ABOUT the unsafe output while containing none of it.

Closed the last two clauses of llm-gateway-trace-coverage: the o6 bridge stops hardcoding parameters and system prompt (one shared mapper, both hosts), and stream() traces success AND failure — shipped together, because rejection-only emits were the reason it was deferred. stream() now mints its own requestId so cost/audit/trace share a join key. A test caught traces recording stream:false for streamed calls; `streaming` is now a required argument.

stages.name: Telehealth & remote patient monitoring
stages.rationale: RPM (remote patient monitoring) is the Q-wave's reimbursable feature: device ingestion + care-plan generation + adherence tracking. Telehealth visits via WebRTC are the synchronous-care complement. Both built, neither runs.

No WebRTC signaling endpoint in apps/api, no device webhook routes, no care-plan generation cron, no visit-summary UI.

stages.name: Caregiver delegation & identity federation
stages.rationale: Allows a patient's family/caregiver to act on their behalf (proxy), JIT-grant temporary access to a covering provider, SAML/OIDC federation for hospital-network SSO, and break-glass emergency access. Compliance-load-bearing for any enterprise pilot.

baseline.summary: g-d1-caregiver-proxy, g-d2-delegation, g-d3-jit-access, g-d4-access-review-attestation, g-d5-saml-oidc-federation, g-d6-break-glass all shipped. Existing auth flow doesn't consult any of them; no SAML/OIDC providers configured in apps/api boot path.

current.summary: Caregiver-federation backend complete, and BOTH SSO protocols (OIDC + SAML 2.0) are now wired end-to-end at apps/api boot with full session mint. OIDC: TenantSsoFactory (index.ts step 10i.1) with KmsBackedJwtIssuer + FHIR-User provisioner/lookup + Redis/InMemory state store + FetchOidcHttpClient + tenant-secret ClientSecretResolver. SAML 2.0: TenantSamlProviderFactory (index.ts step 10i.2) builds the hardened in-repo SamlIdentityProvider per tenant — real XML-DSig with XSW guards + RSA/ECDSA-SHA2 algorithm allowlist + replay cache + InResponseTo binding, JIT provisioning, role resolution, and session mint via the SAME jwtIssuer.sign path OIDC uses (byte-identical sessions). Routes: GET /metadata, GET /login (SP-initiated), POST /acs (full session). The earlier node-saml validator detour was removed in favour of this single canonical path. SSO routes still 503 for tenants with no enabled IdP connection, so wiring only widens what works. No SAML handshake work remains deferred (multi-pod InResponseTo store shares the OidcStateStore horizontal-scale follow-up; IdP-initiated SSO is a per-connection opt-in).

Negative paths: tampered assertion → 401 saml-verification-failed; unsolicited (no InResponseTo) → 401. THREE genuine bugs surfaced by driving the full server (the in-process saml-routes.test.ts registers only the saml plugin, no global RBAC hook, so it missed all three): (1) CRITICAL — /api/auth/saml/* + /api/auth/sso/* were NOT in the unauth allowlist (permitAllForUnauthenticatedRoutes), so the global RBAC hook 401-gated SP-initiated SSO login: SSO was unreachable for unauthenticated users.
