Deliberately NO stub verifier — that is exactly the bug class just fixed in the Stripe webhook path. Deps @node-saml/node-saml@^5.1.0 + xml-crypto@^6.1.2 added to apps/api. ADR-0127: @cernia/api typecheck=0, new-file lint=0, build=0, 7/7 tests. Remaining (now narrowed in `deferred`): the Fastify ACS route + boot wiring + JIT claim mapping.

Shipped PostgresProxyStore (apps/api/src/caregiver-proxy-store.ts) + migration 049_caregiver_proxy_relationships. Implements ProxyStore from @cernia/g-d1-caregiver-proxy with tenant-scoped CRUD: grant, revoke (legal-kind admin-only enforcement preserved), findById, listForCaregiver, listForPatient, sweepExpired (CTE-based bulk flip of active rows whose expires_at is past). 12 pg-mem unit tests cover happy path, kind-specific default expiry, legal-kind admin requirement, double-revoke protection, tenant isolation across all reads, sweepExpired CTE correctness. JIT request store + break-glass invocation log remain on InMemory (separate stores, same refactor pattern).

Caught + closed wiring gap: caregiverFederationRoutes was constructing a fresh InMemoryProxyStore (the PostgresProxyStore shipped earlier was sitting unused). Refactored buildCaregiverFederationRuntime to accept opts.proxyStore + apps/api boot now passes new PostgresProxyStore({ db, tenantId: CERNIA_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID ?? "platform" }). Routes are now backed by persistent storage.

Shipped JIT approve/deny + break-glass review endpoints with persistent stores. Migration 050 (jit_access_requests + break_glass_invocations). PostgresJitAccessStore + PostgresBreakGlassStore in apps/api with full tenant scoping. Routes updated: $request + $invoke now persist on ok results; new POST /access/jit/:id/$approve, /$deny, /access/break-glass/:id/$review; new GET /access/jit/pending + /access/break-glass/pending-review for the future admin UI. 7 pg-mem unit tests cover round-trip persistence across the engine state machines (request→approve, request→deny, invoke→review, listing filters, tenant isolation).

Shipped g-d2 user-to-user delegation end-to-end. Migration 051_access_delegations + PostgresAccessDelegationStore + routes mounted in caregiver-federation-routes: POST /access/delegation/$create + /:id/$accept + /:id/$reject + /:id/$revoke, GET /by-delegator/:id + /by-delegatee/:id. Engine state-machine guard rails preserved (only valid transitions persist; 409 invalid-state otherwise). 503 not-configured fallback when store unset. Wired in apps/api boot.

Shipped g-d4 access-review attestation end-to-end. Migration 052 (review_campaigns + attestation_items, two tables). PostgresAttestationStore handles both. 7 new routes: POST /access/attestation/campaigns/$create + /:id/items/$add + /:id/$close, POST /access/attestation/items/:id/$decide, GET /campaigns/:id/summary + /campaigns/:id/items, GET /items/by-reviewer/:id. All engine state-machine guard rails preserved (only-open campaigns accept new items; only-pending items accept decisions; closeCampaign emits itemsToRevoke for the unreviewed sweep).

Shipped admin UI for delegations + attestations. apps/admin/src/lib/caregiver-federation-api.ts (typed client) + 2 new pages: /admin/access/delegations (list by delegator OR delegatee, create form, accept/reject/revoke actions, state-machine-aware buttons) + /admin/access/attestations (campaign create form, per-reviewer pending queue, attest/revoke decisions with optional note). Sidebar gets a new "Access" nav group with both entries. The 17 caregiver-federation endpoints shipped earlier are now reachable from the tenant admin UI.

Shipped g-d5 IdP connection config layer: migration 053_idp_connections (per-tenant SAML 2.0 + OIDC configs, protocol-discriminated columns, JSONB attribute/group mappings), PostgresIdpConnectionStore (multi-tenant; tenantId per call). Tenant-admin CRUD routes mounted: GET/POST /admin/idp-connections, GET/PATCH/DELETE /admin/idp-connections/:id. Validation runs g-d5 engine.validateConnection() on insert; 422 with structured ConfigIssue list on failure. Admin role required for write; all reads tenant-scoped. 11 pg-mem tests cover OIDC + SAML round-trip, validation rejections, tenant isolation across every read/write, idempotent delete. The SAML/OIDC HANDSHAKE itself (AuthnRequest signing, SAMLResponse verification, ACS callback, session bridge) is the remaining piece — needs samlify/passport-saml in @cernia/auth-providers + login route changes.

Shipped TenantSsoFactory (apps/api/src/sso-tenant-factory.ts) — closes the g-d5 → auth-providers translation layer. Per-tenant OidcIdentityProvider construction on demand: reads active OIDC connection from PostgresIdpConnectionStore, resolves clientSecretRef via injected ClientSecretResolver (TenantSecretResolver in prod), maps g-d5 AttributeMapping → auth-providers claimMapping, strips .well-known suffix from discoveryUrl to derive issuer. Built-in cache keyed by (tenantId, connectionId); invalidate(tenantId) drops on admin toggle. 10 pg-mem tests cover happy path, no-enabled error, multi-enabled disambiguation, SAML-rejection, cache hit, cache invalidation, client-secret resolution, issuer derivation, attribute-mapping translation. Remaining for full handshake closure: Fastify routes wiring start + callback into Cernia URL space (needs JwtIssuer + UserProvisioner + persistent OidcStateStore wired in apps/api boot); SAML protocol implementation (needs samlify/passport-saml).

Shipped final piece of g-d5 OIDC chain: ssoRoutes (apps/api/src/sso-routes.ts) mounting GET /api/auth/sso/:tenantId/start + /callback. Routes default to 503 sso-not-configured until apps/api boot wires JwtIssuer + UserProvisioner + UserLookup + OidcStateStore + OidcHttpClient + ClientSecretResolver (clean stub in index.ts with explicit TODO inventory). 6 route tests cover the 503 path + a working happy path via a stub factory (302 redirect on /start, 200 authenticated payload with trusted user fields on /callback, 400 on idp-rejected / invalid-callback). Total caregiver-federation tests now 46 passing across 5 suites.

Wired the OIDC SSO route deps at apps/api boot — closed the last actionable caregiver-federation deferral (the SSO-boot-wiring bullet). New apps/api/src/sso-user-store.ts ships FhirUserProvisioner + FhirUserLookup over the same tenant-scoped StorageAdapter the FHIR server uses: create() JIT-provisions a FHIR User (authProvider=oidc, status=active), findByExternal() dedups by externalIdentifier (paged auth-provider search + in-memory filter — User has no external-identifier search param yet; dedicated param is a future optimization), resolveRoles() reads active RoleBindings→Role names mirroring iam-route-guards' resolver, loadMfaCredentials() returns null (IdP owns MFA). Safe-by-default: JIT users get NO RoleBindings (least privilege); a shared bounded userId→tenantId index recovers tenant for the tenant-less resolveRoles call (always preceded by find/create in the OIDC flow). index.ts step 10i.1 now builds TenantSsoFactory with KmsBackedJwtIssuer + RedisOidcStateStore (REDIS_HOST-gated, else InMemory) + FetchOidcHttpClient + ClientSecretResolver over tenantSecrets.resolver (connection clientSecretRef doubles as the secret provider key) + the new provisioner/lookup; SSO registration moved after the tenant-secret runtime so the resolver is available. Routes still 503 for tenants with no enabled IdP connection — wiring only widens what works. 13 new adapter unit tests; existing 6 sso-route tests still green. @cernia/api typecheck + build clean. Remaining: SAML 2.0 handshake only.

stages.name: SaaS billing & marketplace
stages.rationale: Enterprise invoicing, ASC 606 revenue recognition, SaaS metrics (MRR/ARR/churn), contract auto-renewal, discount-approval workflow, marketplace checkout, tax compliance. The commercial back-end for selling Cernia at scale.

baseline.summary: marketplace, x1a-tax-compliance, x1b-asc-606-revenue-recognition, x1c-saas-metrics-computation, x2a-enterprise-invoicing, x2b-contract-auto-renewal, x3c-discount-approval-workflow, j1c-sandbox-tenant-lifecycle, j1d-marketplace-checkout all shipped. No marketplace UI in apps/*. No invoice generation job. No tax engine wired into payment paths.

current.summary: Comprehensive Stripe COMPLETE (S1-S8): native subscriptions w/ proration+trial conversion, embedded Payment Element, Billing Meters metered usage, dunning + Smart Retries, single reconciling webhook endpoint, refunds + admin surfacing, gated full-lifecycle test-mode harness, go-live runbook. Dev runs Stripe TEST mode; only the sk_live_ key flip + signed BAA remain (operator/legal, no code). v1-clinical-launch U17 (2026-07-14): closed an audited security gap — ambient-scribe and telehealth-visits (KTD16) now have product rows + createRequireProduct()/checker-backed route gates, closing the window where any tenant on any tier could reach those paid routes unentitled. 2026-07-29: closed a latent ~15.5x metered over-report — the nightly flush and the on-demand $report-metered route sent the cumulative month-to-date total to a SUMMING Stripe meter under a month-constant idempotency key, which only dedupes for 24h. Both now send the increment since a durable per-(tenant, period, metric) watermark (migration 332). Latent, never live: no production tenants at the time. 2026-07-31: the ambient scribe became PURCHASABLE — storefront entry + an operator-configured price (migration 341 gives catalog_prices the fixed-fee/allowance/overage triple plus a tenant_id for negotiated rates), an enforced ADR-0035 tier floor, and both the apps/admin and apps/cernia-ops surfaces. Live RED-then-GREEN 23/23 with settlement through the real Stripe-webhook cascade. NOTE the price triple is DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing meters scribe usage yet, so the store states terms the billing chain does not enforce (tracked in remaining). 2026-07-31 (later): the scribe got its REAL price and the ops editor stopped looking broken. $29.99 per CLINICIAN per month (catalog-seed.ts LIST_PRICES + PRODUCT_TERMS quantityUnit), annual on the platform-wide 10%-off ladder = $323.89/yr, and NO included allowance and NO per-note rate — every note is billed individually and the founder has not set that rate yet. The ops price route now writes BOTH cadence rows from one call (explicit annualPriceCents, else annualFromMonthly), which closes the gap where an operator published a price and the annual-by-default storefront answered "price not configured". Also shipped: the per-unit billing POLICY as operator configuration (migration 343 product_usage_pricing) plus the resolver for max(floor, cost x (1 + margin)) that reports WHY the floor applied — separating "cost measured and genuinely below floor" (healthy) from "cost could not be priced at all" (a defect), so a floor cannot silently rescue a blind cost chain. Both numbers ship UNSET; unset resolves to unbillable, never to zero. Proven live over the wire RED-then-GREEN across all four cadence x scope combinations with a cross-tenant isolation control (docs/status/evidence/scribe-pricing/). 2026-08-04: per-unit pricing stopped being a one-product feature and the metering plane got the producers it never had. Migration 357 seeds floor+margin for voice-minute/sms/email (all provenance='seeded-default', floors lifted verbatim from the storefront's own advertised rates), metered-usage-pricer.ts generalises the scribe's shape, and voice-minute-usage.ts is the FIRST thing ever to write a voice usage event - the IVoiceCallMeter seam had been called at every call-end since Wave-E with nothing wired to it, which also meant the per-tenant voice-minutes budget gate summed an empty ledger and could never fire. SMS now bills SEGMENTS rather than one unit per message (a silent ~3x under-recovery on long reminders). Proven on real Postgres 16/16, with inclusion asserted BEFORE idempotence and a falsifying control for each guard.

remaining: [deferred-postga-launch-blocker] Deferred (post-GA, NOT a launch blocker): ML-model marketplace (P3-C) clinical-review dual-control queue before publish — the -A vertical publishes directly; a physician/compliance review gate is a future enhancement (apps/api/src/ml-marketplace-routes.ts).

[auth-plans-deferred-items] Auth Plans 3 + 4 — DEFERRED ITEMS only (core shipped 2026-06-11; Google self-serve signup JIT-promote verified LIVE 2026-06-14, see history): social login cross-tenant chooser, Apple provider; adaptive/risk-based auth, trust-this-device + refresh tokens, password-reset UI, per-tenant MFA-policy enforcement UI, full auth-event audit pipeline. Real OAuth creds = procurement (Google/Microsoft client IDs). Real SMS creds (Twilio) + email SMTP (Google Workspace) code-side shipped 2026-06-11; external remaining = toll-free verification / A2P 10DLC registration (SMS) and App Password + SPF/DKIM/DMARC DNS (email).

[release-t5-publisher-verification] Release 3 / T5 — publisher verification is VENDOR-BLOCKED on two of four backends, not stubbed. NARROWED 2026-08-03: the real backends shipped (apps/api/src/publisher-verifier-backends.ts, wired at index.ts:3959 — the dev stub is now reachable ONLY under isDevLoginEnabled(), for dev/E2E auto-verify). Domain control is a real DNS-TXT probe (`cernia-verification=<tenantId>`, fail-closed on NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL) and OAuth2 resolves the tenant's linked social_identities to an allow-listed issuer; both need no vendor. REMAINING: verifyEin / verifyDuns format-validate and then return an honest false, because the IRS exposes no EIN-match API and Dun & Bradstreet DUNS lookup is a paid product. UNBLOCKER: a commercial D&B (or equivalent) subscription, injected through the existing `EinDunsProvider` seam (publisher-verifier-backends.ts:86) — no other code change. Note the FSM requires oauth2 AND (ein OR duns), so today no publisher can reach 'verified' without an operator override.

[release-t5-publisher-onboarding] Release 3 / T5 — publisher onboarding has a UI, but in apps/developer, not apps/admin. NARROWED 2026-08-03: apps/developer/src/app/publish/page.tsx already does GET+POST /admin/marketplace/publisher with 404→unverified / 402→upgrade handling and a status badge, and the cernia-ops review queue shipped 2026-06-13 (apps/cernia-ops/.../platform/publishers/page.tsx). So this is a surface-PLACEMENT question, not a missing feature: does a tenant admin onboard as a publisher from apps/admin, or is the developer portal the intended (and only) home for it? PRODUCT DECIDED 2026-08-07 (founder): PUBLISHER ONBOARDING STAYS IN THE DEVELOPER PORTAL. The competing reading was CLAUDE.md invariant 3 — tenant-scoped self-serve belongs in apps/admin — which would have made the developer page a near-verbatim port with admin session-claim auth swapped in for the localStorage token. The founder judged publishing a genuinely distinct PERSONA rather than another tenant-admin task, so no port and no duplication. WHAT THIS OWES, and it is the reason this is not simply closed: invariant 3 now has a real exception, and an invariant with an undocumented exception stops being an invariant — the next agent reading CLAUDE.md will either "fix" this by porting it, or will cite it as precedent for putting the next cross-persona surface wherever is convenient. The exception must be WRITTEN INTO CLAUDE.md beside the invariant, naming publisher onboarding, the persona argument, and the date. Until that is written this bullet stays open, because the decision is not durable until the rule that contradicts it acknowledges it.

[entitlement-lifecycle-residuals-after] Entitlement lifecycle — residuals after the 2026-07-29 cancellation fix. NARROWED 2026-08-03: (b) is CLOSED — `resyncStaleVoiceTiers` (apps/api/src/voice-tier-sync.ts) now runs nightly right after the period-end revocation sweep (saas-nightly-batches.ts, job 'voice-tier-resync'), recomputing voice_tier from live entitlements for every tenant with a voice config and logging each correction. Proven on real Postgres by reproducing the drift first (voice-tier-sync.test.ts, 4 new cases incl. cross-tenant isolation). ALL THREE RESIDUALS CLOSED 2026-08-06, and all three were verified still true before building (none was stale). (a) A cancellation carrying current_period_end=null still writes NO expiry and only warns — that fallback is deliberate and stays, because never falling back to immediate revocation is the right direction. What was missing was that nothing SURFACED it, so a tenant silently kept every purchased product. Now derived on read: GET /cernia-ops/platform/entitlements/unsupported lists tenants holding an ACTIVE PERPETUAL grant their current billing state does not support, as subscription-cancelled or tier-floor, each row carrying the paid-through date off their own subscription row as the suggested expiry. DERIVE-ON-READ WAS CHOSEN OVER AN ALERT EMITTER, following the /cernia-ops/platform/incidents precedent, for two reasons worth keeping: an alert records only the failure we ANTICIPATED, whereas the query also catches an unwired seam, a failed store write, and a cancellation event that never arrived; and it is self-healing, since a row leaves the list the instant expires_at is set, with no acknowledge step to forget. It also needed no new wiring, which mattered because index.ts was outside the writable set — a new seam in billing-routes.ts would have been unwireable and therefore dead in production. (c) The cernia-ops UI exists, and the honest answer to the hashing tension is recorded IN THE MARKUP so the next operator does not file it as a rendering bug: a one-click "expire this row" button on the matrix is IMPOSSIBLE AND SHOULD STAY IMPOSSIBLE, because a matrix row carries only a salted hash and the only ways to get that button are to un-hash the read (restoring the customer roster) or add a hash-to-id lookup (the same roster with an extra step). Instead the WORKLIST rows carry raw ids and get the affordance the matrix cannot have — "Prepare expiry" fills the form including the paid-through date, and the operator commits explicitly. A tenant not on the worklist can still be expired by typing the id, which is the abuse/fraud path and SHOULD require deliberately naming the customer. THE SETTLED RULE, now written into all three files: read-only aggregates hash because nothing acts on the identifier; write worklists do not, because a hash cannot become a WHERE clause. Neither new surface carries displayName. (d) A subscription DOWNGRADE now narrows entitlements. The root cause is that packages/billing stripe-backend.ts folds all four customer.subscription.* kinds into one branch emitting no line items and no price ids, and billing-routes.ts had no subscription.updated entitlement handling at all. Item price ids are now read off the already-signature-verified payload (the technique the cernia_cart block already uses), reverse-resolved to a tier via catalog_prices, and every perpetual grant whose registry minTier the new tier fails is expired AT current_period_end. THE RULE AND WHY: the platform already decided who may HOLD these products (ambient-scribe starter+, pro growth+) and validateCart applied that floor at purchase, so the floor was a gate you walked through once — this applies it on the way down. Deliberately NOT "expire everything", since an enterprise-to-growth move must not revoke phone-agent, which has no floor. Deliberately END-OF-PERIOD, matching the settled cancellation rule; the honest cost is that a tenant dropping to a no-BAA tier keeps a PHI-touching product until the period ends, and the operator has the immediate-cutoff primitive (expire with a past date) when compliance requires it. There is no explicit up/down comparison because the floor check IS the rule, so upgrades and renewals no-op by construction. Anything unresolvable — no price ids, no catalog row, two tiers at once, no current_period_end — leaves the tenant FULLY ENTITLED: over-serving is the tolerated failure here, wrongly revoking is not. 20 new tests, cernia-ops 278 (was 268), gates 80/80, ratchet 371. Mutation-proven in four ways, and the FOURTH ONE INITIALLY PASSED: gutting the worklist tenant-id cell still satisfied toContain(TENANT) because the row data-testid also contains the id, so the assertion was passing on an attribute rather than the cell. Tightened to match the cell markup; the mutation now fails. Two absence assertions were likewise found vacuously true on an empty result and given inclusion-first partners. WHAT REMAINS, all newly surfaced by this work and none of it blocking: (i) when someone widens subscriptionSync in packages/billing to capture the price set properly, parseSubscriptionPriceIds in billing-routes.ts should be DELETED in favour of it rather than left as a second reader of the same fact; (ii) a Stripe-portal downgrade does NOT mirror the new tier into the local subscriptions row, so the local tier goes stale and QUOTAS stay at the richer plan — a different blast radius from entitlements, which are correct without it because Stripe is the source of truth and the operation converges on repeat; (iii) NO PUSH CHANNEL, deliberately — the condition reaches an operator surface but pages nobody, because a push means the alerts table, which is a TENANT-facing delivery queue, and writing there risks emailing the tenant that we failed to revoke their access. The right shape is a nightly job asserting the worklist is empty, which needs index.ts.

[store-pricing-connected-endtoend] Store pricing - CONNECTED end-to-end as of 2026-08-04: producers resolve a per-unit price (apps/api/src/metered-usage-pricer.ts, scribe-note-pricer.ts) AND an invoice line now reads it (apps/api/src/metered-invoice-lines.ts, invoice-generation.ts, migration 358). REMAINING: (a) ARMING IS UNBLOCKED AND THE DECISION IS TAKEN (founder, 2026-08-06: arm it once prices are operator-set — migration 364 satisfies that for all four platform products). What is left is not a decision and not code: setting CERNIA_METERED_INVOICE_LINES=1 on a live deployment, which is an environment change outside this repo. The flag is now documented in apps/api/.env.example with its preconditions and both safety properties. Arming with a wrong price is NOT dangerous — the generator still refuses seeded-default lines, so it would bill nothing rather than bill wrongly. The path ships behind CERNIA_METERED_INVOICE_LINES, default OFF, and with it off every billable group is recorded as a hold with reason 'not-armed' rather than dropped. Arming now needs ONE operator decision, not two: real operator-set rates (see the seeded-price bullet below). The PRE-CUTOVER verdict is SETTLED AND ENFORCED (founder, 2026-08-05: forgo the backlog). Migration 360 adds a single-row metered_billing_cutover; invoice-generation.ts calls ensureMeteredBillingCutover() the first time an armed sweep runs, and planMeteredInvoiceLines() bills nothing recorded before that instant. Deliberately an INSTANT and not a seeded watermark: a missing watermark row is ALSO what a brand-new (product, unit, rate) group looks like, so treating absence as backlog would forgive a tenant's first-ever SMS forever. Armed with no cutover recorded it FAILS CLOSED (bills nothing) rather than falling back to the whole ledger; unarmed it still reports the FULL ledger as held, so forgoing the backlog for BILLING does not hide it from the 'what is unbillable' answer. (b) HELD USAGE — NARROWED 2026-08-06, and this bullet was PARTLY STALE. Measured rather than assumed: planMeteredInvoiceLines reads `since = armed ? (cutover ?? UNREACHABLE_FUTURE) : undefined`, so EVERY hold accrued before arming is already disposed of — forgone, by the founder's 2026-08-05 cutover ruling. The open case is only holds accrued AFTER arming (a price later cleared, a newly seeded product), which is much narrower than what this bullet claimed. Usage priced off a seed is held indefinitely: the event carries the price resolved when it happened, and re-pricing it at a later operator-set rate would bill a customer at a number they were never quoted. Deciding to bill it retroactively (at which rate?) or write it off is an operator call and there is no surface for it yet. The amount is visible - GET /admin/billing/metered-holds and the metered_usage_holds table - but nothing can act on it. (c) EVERY unit of all four products still reports basis='cost-unpriced' and healthy=false, because nothing measures per-unit cost: for the scribe because ComputeProbe/PostgresStorageProbe have no runtime caller, and for voice/sms/email because there is no per-unit vendor cost ledger at all (Twilio voice, Twilio SMS and the SMTP provider bill us in aggregate and are reconciled against nothing). The floor is charged 100% of the time everywhere and the margin is inert. DELIBERATELY NOT A HOLD REASON: it is true of every line, so gating on it would withhold every dollar the platform earns while telling an operator nothing they can act on. (d) NO OPERATOR UI for holds beyond the JSON route - apps/admin has no panel and apps/cernia-ops has no cross-tenant fleet view of withheld revenue (the per-tenant route deliberately does not aggregate other practices). (e) apps/billing-service carries its own carved copy of the invoicing plane and has NOT been given migration 358, the metered reader, or the hold surface - cross-service follow-up, deliberately not fixed across the boundary. (f) packages/billing/src/invoicing/invoice-generator.ts, which earlier revisions of this bullet named as the file to change, has NO production caller at all (grep across apps/ and packages/ returns only its own tests and the index re-export); the invoices this platform writes come from apps/api/src/invoice-generation.ts into enterprise_invoices. Its tier-overage logic is correct for what it covers and was left alone; a pointer comment now says so at the top of the file.

[perunit-prices-longer-provisional] Per-unit prices are NO LONGER PROVISIONAL — the founder ratified all four on 2026-08-06 (migration 364) and metered revenue is flowing; what remains is that the COSTS beneath them are unreconciled (see below). This bullet is kept for the cost caveat, not the price decision. Historical context follows: four products were seeded provisional, not one. Migration 346 seeded the scribe (10c floor / 40% margin); migration 357 seeded voice-minute (35c/minute), sms (3c/SEGMENT) and email (1c/message), all at 40%. provenance='seeded-default' marks every such row, the ops price editor renders a warning banner from it, and the value rides onto each billing_usage_events line as policyProvenance. NOBODY HAS DECIDED ANY OF THESE NUMBERS. The scribe's derive from a measured $0.0706/note against vendor rates that are published list and have never been reconciled against an invoice we paid; the other three are simply the storefront's own advertised overage rates re-used as floors, so the policy could not disagree with the copy. A SPECIFIC FOUNDER CORRECTION 2026-08-07 — THIS CLAUSE WAS STALE AND IS REWRITTEN. It described the storefront and the biller DISAGREEING about the unit: catalog-seed.ts advertising "$0.03 per SMS" per MESSAGE while migration 357 billed per SEGMENT, so a three-segment reminder billed 9c against a card implying 3c. THE DRIFT IS CLOSED AND GUARDED. catalog-seed.ts no longer carries the unit only in a code comment; catalog-seed.metered-unit-parity.test.ts (5/5, real Postgres) reads BOTH sides back FROM THE DATABASE after migrations + seed — catalog_prices, what the practice is SHOWN, against product_usage_pricing, what resolvePerUnitCharge BILLS — and fails if they name different units. Reading the database rather than the TypeScript constants is the load-bearing part: a comparison of two constants in one file would pass while the seeded rows drifted. That test states its own scope precisely and correctly: "Whether that rate is right is a founder decision and this test takes no view on it. What it forbids is the two halves DISAGREEING about the unit." WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT is therefore the PRICE, not a mismatch — the founder setting real floors and margins in apps/cernia-ops. Recorded here because the stale version of this clause was used to put a live-billing-defect question to the founder on 2026-08-07, and the founder correctly answered that it had already been fixed. Closing all of this means the founder setting real floors + margins in apps/cernia-ops (Platform -> Store -> product -> terms panel), which stamps provenance='operator-set' and drops the banner. Until then any revenue figure derived from a per-unit price is an estimate on top of an estimate. RAISED IN SEVERITY 2026-08-04: this is no longer only a reporting caveat. The invoice generator now REFUSES to bill any line whose price carries provenance='seeded-default' (apps/api/src/metered-invoice-lines.ts), so while these four rows remain seeded, metered revenue is WITHHELD rather than mis-stated. That is the deliberate choice - a placeholder rate on a real customer invoice is a billing dispute, not a rounding error - but it means the founder setting these numbers is now the gate on metered revenue itself, not just on its accuracy. The withheld amount is countable at GET /admin/billing/metered-holds and in the metered_usage_holds table. NARROWED 2026-08-05 (the AMBIGUITY, not the decision): the storefront no longer hides the unit. Every metered catalog row now declares what its rate is a rate ON — LIST_PRICES.metered carries { rateCents, unit } and seeds catalog_prices.usage_unit ('segment'/'minute'/'message'), and the card renders '$0.03 per segment' where it used to render '$0.03 metered' and never say per what. NO RATE CHANGED. catalog-seed.metered-unit-parity.test.ts (real PG) now asserts the ADVERTISED unit equals the BILLED unit (product_usage_pricing.usage_unit) for every metered product, with a falsifying control, so the two halves cannot silently disagree again — whichever way the founder resolves the 3c-per-message-vs-9c-per-3-segments question, the copy follows the policy. RESOLVED 2026-08-06 (founder). Both halves. (i) THE FOUR PRICES ARE RATIFIED AS-IS — offered confirm-all / confirm-scribe-only / supply-different-numbers / hold-until-reconciled, the founder chose confirm all four. Migration 364 flips provenance seeded-default -> operator-set for the four platform rows. NO NUMBER CHANGES; the diff is a label, and the effect (metered revenue stops being withheld) is much larger than the change. The WHERE matches the exact seeded values AND seeded-default AND tenant_id='' — a ratification of SPECIFIC NUMBERS, not a blanket relabel, so a row an operator already changed and any tenant-negotiated row are untouched (asserted both directions, 8 tests, real PG). [meteredflush-enumeration-residuals-after] METERED-FLUSH RESIDUALS — (c) AND (f) CLOSED IN CODE AND WIRED 2026-08-07. (c) CUSTOMERS WERE BEING OVERBILLED FOR AIRTIME, always in the same direction, and the mechanism was worse than the bullet said: Twilio's CallDuration was not merely losing a race, it was being THROWN AWAY. markEnded is guarded on `ended_at IS NULL`, so in exactly the case needing correction the carrier figure hit the guard and vanished; the only other consumer was a log-only audit emitter. THERE WAS NO DURABLE CARRIER FIGURE ANYWHERE, which is why a new table was genuinely needed (migration 365). The orchestrator measures from RING START while the carrier bills CONNECTED time, so a long ring rounded an extra minute on via ceil(seconds/60). THE CARRIER IS NOW AUTHORITATIVE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: downward-only was rejected because a media socket that dies mid-call ends our clock early while the carrier keeps counting, so downward-only would mean the platform silently eats real airtime. The asymmetry is NOT on the sign of the delta — it is on whether the correction crosses an invoice watermark. THE TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE SWALLOWED EVERY CREDIT: metered-invoice-lines computes deltaUnits = observed - billed and `continue`s on <= 0 ("it can only suppress, never re-bill") — correct for replay, exactly wrong for a credit, since a downward correction on invoiced units pushes the ledger below the watermark and the line is skipped while the customer keeps the overcharge. So the pass does not rely on the invoicer noticing: it records disposition=credit-note-required with owed_cents, surfaced by a partial index and drained via settled_at. NOT an automatic refund — a credit note against a paid invoice is an accounting act with tax consequences. Idempotent on two pre-existing layers. (f) EMAIL SUPPRESSION IS DURABLE (migration 366) and consulted before sending. The previous sink only logged, so a bounced or complained-about address was mailed again. ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING and is why the wiring sits inside the metering decorator: metering bills only a status:'sent' result, so a suppressed send must be refused BEFORE metering sees it or the tenant is billed for an email we deliberately did not send. A suppression-store outage only warns, because refusing the bounce webhook makes the provider retry and we lose the bounce entirely. Load-bearing assertions are SUM over billing_usage_events, never a helper return: 41s ring + 25s connect bills 2 min before / 1 min after; the ceil boundary goes 70c -> 35c; the SAME 10s ring in a minute's interior is correctly left alone; a ring-only never-answered call nets to 0; a second sweep reports examined:0 with the figure and row count unchanged. WHAT REMAINS: (a) NO OPERATOR SURFACE for the credit-note-required worklist or the suppression list — per CLAUDE.md invariant 3 that is half-shipped (tenant-scoped read for apps/admin, cross-tenant money-owed aggregate for apps/cernia-ops); (b) NO BACKFILL of historical calls, since the pass only sees calls carrying a carrier observation and nothing wrote observations before this change — the overbilling already invoiced is NOT corrected by this; (c) no per-provider bounce verifiers, no SMS opt-out list, and suppression is deliberately per-tenant rather than global, because a cross-tenant list would be an oracle about another practice's patients — the consequence is that an UNCORRELATED bounce is still not suppressed.

[phitouching-product-carries-tier] TIER RESTRICTIONS WRITTEN AS PROSE — CLOSED for telehealth-visits 2026-08-07, and the fix is NOT where the bullet said it would be. Built as a RE-RUNNABLE RECONCILE PASS, not a data migration, for two reasons worth keeping: a migration writes raw SQL and is therefore a SECOND WRITER past the append-only history in PostgresProductCatalogStore (the J06 defect this repo already fixed on the operator path), and a migration runs ONCE whereas a floor is a standing rule later operator, marketplace and dev grants must also meet. Falsified by removing the floor: 24 failed / 79 passed, with the positive controls staying GREEN, which is what makes them controls. Silent revenue leak CLOSED — the nightly metered-usage flush never visited store-purchase tenants. `runMeteredFlushSweep` (apps/api/src/saas-nightly-batches.ts) fanned out over `enumerateSubscriptionTenants` (apps/api/src/saas-subscription-store.ts), i.e. `SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id FROM saas_subscriptions`. The store checkout grant path (apps/api/src/store-checkout-routes.ts + the `checkout.session.completed` fan-out in apps/api/src/billing-routes.ts) calls PostgresProductCatalogStore.grantProduct, which writes `product_entitlements` and touches `saas_subscriptions` NOWHERE — so a practice that bought a product through the store had usage recorded into `billing_usage_events` and NEVER flushed to Stripe. No meter event, no invoice line, ever, while the sweep logged success. Closes docs/prds/metering-pricing-cost-chain.md R6a (risk 8.12). FIX: NEW `enumerateBillableTenants` (apps/api/src/saas-subscription-store.ts) — one SQL `SELECT tenant_id FROM saas_subscriptions UNION SELECT tenant_id FROM product_entitlements ORDER BY 1`; `runMeteredFlushSweep` is its ONLY caller. DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE PRD: R6a says to CHANGE `enumerateSubscriptionTenants` to the union. We did not — it has six other callers in saas-nightly-batches.ts (metrics :321, auto-renewal :469, expiry :542, renewal-alert schedule :616, invoice generation :1106, pricing reconcile :1292) and every one immediately opens a PostgresSubscriptionStore and reads `saas_subscriptions` ROWS, so subscription-only is the semantics they want; widening it would also make runSaasMetricsSweep persist zero-MRR/ARR snapshots for store-only tenants and corrupt the FinOps trend. DELIBERATE: NO `status` filter on product_entitlements. Cancellation here is not a status change — the Stripe path calls scheduleExpiryForPerpetualGrants, which sets `expires_at` and leaves status='active' — so hasActive()-style filtering would DROP a tenant who cancelled mid-month while still holding un-flushed usage from the period they DID pay for, a new leak of the same shape. The sweep only DELIVERS already-recorded usage and cannot fabricate a charge, so over-inclusion costs one empty rollup query per tenant per night while under-inclusion silently loses revenue. REVENUE LEAK CLOSED — cancellation now expires purchased product entitlements. THE DEFECT: the grant half of the Stripe flow (checkout.session.completed → opts.productCatalog.grantProduct, apps/api/src/billing-routes.ts) passes NO expiresAt, so every purchased entitlement row was written expires_at=NULL (perpetual) — and the ungrant half was never written at all. PostgresProductCatalogStore.revokeProduct (apps/api/src/product-catalog-store.ts) had ZERO production callers repo-wide; the only thing that ever removed a product_entitlements row was tenant erasure (apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts). Tier downgrade (packages/billing/src/lifecycle/tier-downgrade.ts) removes only TIER-INCLUDED products and explicitly "never silently revokes licenses". Net: a tenant who cancelled kept ambient-scribe (and every other purchased product) FOREVER. THE FIX (founder decision 2026-07-29): access works until the end of the period they already paid for, then stops — NOT immediate revocation (a clinician must never lose scribe access mid-visit, and we do not claw back time already paid for). (1) apps/api/src/product-catalog-store.ts: new scheduleExpiryForPerpetualGrants(expiresAt) sets expires_at on every ACTIVE + PERPETUAL (expires_at IS NULL) entitlement the tenant holds, returning the changed product ids; plus scheduleExpiry(productId, expiresAt) for the operator path. Restricting the write to NULL rows makes it idempotent under Stripe redelivery AND means it can only ever SHORTEN access, never extend it, and never claws back a product carrying its own paid term. NO SWEEPER IS NEEDED — hasActive() already evaluates status=active AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now) at READ time on every gated request. (2) apps/api/src/billing-routes.ts: new customer.subscription.deleted block sets expires_at from the event’s current_period_end (already carried on result.subscriptionSync by packages/billing/src/backends/stripe-backend.ts — no change needed there). Tenant is taken from the LOCAL subscription row via readByStripeSubscriptionId in preference to cernia_tenant_id metadata (ADR 0004), mismatch logged. Every failure is logged and swallowed so the Stripe ack is never rejected (a non-2xx makes Stripe retry forever). A null current_period_end deliberately does NOT fall back to now() — that would be the immediate revocation this change exists to avoid; it warns and defers to the operator route. (3) ProductGrantStore seam extended with an OPTIONAL scheduleExpiryForPerpetualGrants so existing doubles/partial wirings still compile. (4) apps/api/src/index.ts: seam WIRED to PostgresProductCatalogStore — without this the fix would be dead code, i.e. the very defect being fixed. Deliberately no syncVoiceTierFromEntitlements() call at cancel time: rows stay active until expires_at passes, so the derived voice_tier is still correct for the rest of the paid period. (5) apps/api/src/cernia-ops-entitlements-routes.ts: new POST /cernia-ops/platform/entitlements/expire (operator escape hatch for when the webhook could not set the expiry, or an immediate abuse/fraud cut-off via a past date) — requireSuperAdmin + sendPhiSafe, tenant-filtered UPDATE, ACTIVE rows only. DELIBERATELY NOT added to deriveOperation: on /cernia-ops/* the rule INVERTS (mapping it onto a type a tenant-admin’s *:admin covers would turn the hook into an allow-then-deny), and iam-route-guards.repo-coverage.test.ts excludes OPERATOR_PREFIX for exactly that reason — gate re-run green 8/8. Path uses a plain “expire” segment, not “”, to dodge the %24-vs-$ route-encoding footgun this repo has shipped before. TESTS: apps/api/src/billing-routes.test.ts +10 webhook cases (paid-period survival then cut-off, all-products fan-out, idempotent redelivery, cancel→re-purchase restores entitlement, cross-tenant isolation, store failure still ACKs 200, null current_period_end writes nothing, past_due is NOT a cancellation, unknown-subscription metadata fallback, unwired seam); apps/api/src/product-catalog-store.test.ts +15 real-Postgres cases; apps/api/src/cernia-ops-entitlements-routes.test.ts +6 real-Postgres route cases. FALSIFIED before shipping (ADR-0127): deleting the scheduleExpiryForPerpetualGrants call turned 7 webhook tests red naming the expiry date, while the three negative-control tests correctly stayed green; removing the “expires_at IS NULL” guard from the real SQL turned the idempotency + “no claw-back” tests red (a redelivery would have extended access by a year). VERIFICATION: @cernia/api typecheck clean; lint 66 errors on both baseline and branch (zero new); billing-routes 75/75; ops-entitlements 13/13; product-catalog-store 31 pass + 1 PRE-EXISTING failure (the seedProducts closed-set list is stale vs PRODUCT_REGISTRY, which has gained ml-studio/rpm/telehealth-video — fails identically on baseline github/main, proven via git stash -u).

THE AMBIENT SCRIBE BECAME PURCHASABLE. THE DEFECT (journeys.json findings[51], measured live on J01 run 2): GET /admin/store/catalog answered 200 listing phone-agent, digital-assistant, voice-language-spanish, patient-portal, api-webhooks, voice-minute, sms and email — and neither ambient-scribe nor ambient-scribe-pro. product-registry.ts carried storefront:false on both, and catalog-seed.ts LIST_PRICES had no row for either, so POST /admin/store/checkout answered 409 "ambient-scribe: unknown product". The product was gated, entitleable and UNSELLABLE: the only paths in were /dev/checkout-grant or an operator action. The 402 body meanwhile told the practice to "Purchase or contact your admin" for something with no purchase path. THE PRICE SOURCE (founder requirement): the price is NOT a literal in catalog-seed.ts. The "$149/provider/mo" on the registry entry stays a comment; an operator publishes a price through PATCH /cernia-ops/platform/store/price — super-admin only, because that route can set an OVERAGE RATE and a tenant admin who could reach it would set their own to zero (PRD R4a). Until an operator does, the catalog returns price:null + unavailable.reason="price-not-configured" and offers no checkout. There is NO default anywhere on the path, and resolveProductPrice returns null rather than inventing one. THE SHAPE COULD NOT BE EXPRESSED, SO 341 ADDS IT: catalog_prices had a single unit_amount, while every Cernia product is "a fixed fee that includes an allowance, then an overage rate" — phone-agent is documented as "$199/mo (200 voice min incl, $0.35/min over)" with the 200 living in a // comment and the $0.35 in an unrelated product:voice-minute:metered row that nothing joins to it. Per founder decision D3 (PRD docs/prds/metering-pricing-cost-chain.md R1a), migration 341 adds included_quantity / overage_rate_cents / usage_unit / quantity_unit beside unit_amount (REUSED as the fixed fee — every reader already treats it as the recurring amount). No pricing-mode enum: pure metered is (0,0,X), a flat contract is (negotiated, unlimited, n/a), and unlimited is an explicit NULL overage rate rather than a magic large number. PER-TENANT OVERRIDE + NEW ISOLATION (PRD R2a): 341 also adds tenant_id (empty string = the platform list price) and widens UNIQUE to (tenant_id,item_type,item_id,cadence) — under migration 257’s key, writing one practice’s negotiated rate would have overwritten the list price for everybody. Resolution is tenant row then platform row, first match wins; an override replaces the triple WHOLE, because a partial merge would let a negotiated fee silently inherit the list allowance and bill overage nobody agreed to. This is NEW isolation rather than preserved isolation — before 341 the table had no tenant dimension at all — so it was made structural: every PostgresCatalogPriceStore method that predates 341 is PINNED to the platform sentinel, and the tenant-aware reads are separate methods taking a required tenant id. No method returns unscoped rows, so forgetting the filter is not something a caller can do. TIER FLOOR (ADR 0035): ambient-scribe carried the comment "sandbox tier excluded (no BAA)" and NOTHING enforced it — validateCart had no floor, and a sandbox tenant was stopped only incidentally, by the absence of a price row. Publishing a price removes that accident, so ProductDef.minTier became code (starter+ for the scribe, growth+ for pro), enforced in the aggregator (card renders tier-locked, no button) AND in validateCart (409), because a cart is a JSON body a tenant admin can POST directly and hiding the card is not a control. BOTH SURFACES (CLAUDE.md): apps/admin renders the whole price ("$149.00/mo / clinician — Includes 500 notes, then $0.25 per note") plus the named unavailable reason; apps/cernia-ops price-editor.tsx gains the terms fields + a tenant field (blank = list price, the safe default — a mistyped tenant id writes a row nobody reads, whereas defaulting to a current tenant would turn a list-price edit into a single-customer discount). LIVE EVIDENCE, intent channel only: RED at github/main 9e1ef20f reproduces the exact eight-product list (docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/store-scribe-red.json); GREEN 23/23 (store-scribe-green.json) across two stacks over one database. Both stacks port-to-DB pairing-checked by writing THROUGH the port and requiring the row PRESENT in the queried database and ABSENT from the decoy database apps/api/.env names. SETTLEMENT RODE THE REAL CASCADE, not /dev/checkout-grant: a signed checkout.session.completed delivered to POST /billing/webhook/stripe, HMAC-verified by StripeBillingBackend, then the billing-routes.ts cart fan-out to productCatalog.grantProduct + provisioningOrchestrator.enqueue. The resulting entitlement row carries grant_ref="cs_<session>_ambient-scribe" rather than a "dev-checkout:" ref, which is what tells the two paths apart. A TAMPERED signature was refused 401 in the same step, so the signed 200 means something. The Stripe-hosted payment page itself is an external gate this run cannot drive; both Cernia-side legs are real. CONTROLS: the practice that purchased reaches /scribe/sessions; a practice that did not is still refused 402 product-not-entitled (the gate was not widened); Harborview saw its negotiated $99/2,000 notes/$0.10 while Meridian saw the $149/500/$0.25 list price (ADR 0004); a tenant admin was refused on the price route; a sandbox practice was refused 409 on a direct cart POST. SCREENS: docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/screens/store-scribe-0{1..6}*.png. BONUS DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED by driving the operator screen rather than only the wire: apps/cernia-ops/src/lib/store-api.ts setProductPrice never sent the X-Cernia-Ops-CSRF double-submit header, so EVERY price write from a real signed-in operator 403d. The editor has been non-functional for as long as it has existed. No unit test could see it — they all inject a fake fetch that ignores headers. Predates this change; fixed here by echoing cernia_ops_csrf the way ops-fetch.ts already does, then re-driven through the form: $179/clinician/750 notes/$0.30 landed in Postgres, and the practice’s negotiated row was untouched by that list-price edit. VERIFICATION: @cernia/api, @cernia/admin and @cernia/cernia-ops-portal typecheck clean; new apps/api/src/product-price-resolver.test.ts covers 13 real-Postgres cases including both migration CHECK constraints and the cross-tenant control; storefront-catalog 19/19 including an assertion that NO dollar sign reaches an unpriced card.

THE OPS PRICE EDITOR LOOKED BROKEN, AND THE SCRIBE GOT ITS REAL PRICE. THE DEFECT (this stage's own remaining bullet, and reproduced on the wire against github/main before the fix — docs/status/evidence/scribe-pricing/cadence-red.json): PATCH /cernia-ops/platform/store/price wrote one row, `product:<id>:monthly`. The storefront opens on ANNUAL (apps/admin/src/app/admin/store/page.tsx useState('annual')) and store-catalog-aggregator.ts looks a price up by EXACT cadence, so an operator published $29.99 and a tenant admin opening the store was told "Pricing for this product has not been published yet" until they toggled to Monthly. The RED run measured it: two catalog_prices rows, both monthly; C2 and C4 (annual, platform and negotiated) came back unavailable.reason="price-not-configured" with HTTP 200. Nothing caught it because the prior journey (store-scribe-journey.mts) reads ?cadence=monthly on every call and every unit test in apps/cernia-ops/src/lib/store-api.test.ts injects a fake fetch. THE FIX: one call now writes BOTH cadences — an explicit annualPriceCents when the operator states a negotiated annual rate, annualFromMonthly(monthly) (the platform-wide 10%-off ladder in catalog-seed.ts) when they leave it blank, so a blank field can no longer produce a MISSING annual price. Row ids carry both the tenant and the cadence, so a negotiated rate cannot overwrite the list price and the annual row cannot overwrite the monthly one. THE PRICE (founder decision, 2026-07-31): ambient-scribe is $29.99 PER CLINICIAN per month — 2_999 in catalog-seed.ts LIST_PRICES with quantityUnit 'clinician' in the new PRODUCT_TERMS map, so the card reads "$29.99/mo / clinician" and not a flat practice-wide fee — annual $323.89, and NO included allowance and NO overage rate, because every note is billed individually and the per-note rate is cost-plus-margin off a number the founder has deliberately not set yet. The "$149/provider/mo" comment in product-registry.ts was a demo placeholder that had already been quoted as authoritative in docs/prds/metering-pricing-cost-chain.md D2; it is corrected in place. THE PER-UNIT POLICY (same founder decision): a note must never be billed at zero, so per_unit_price = max(floor_price, measured_cost x (1 + margin)). Both inputs are OPERATOR CONFIGURATION, not constants — migration 343 product_usage_pricing (one row per tenant+product+unit, tenant_id '' = the platform default, the same keying catalog_prices uses so a negotiated policy cannot overwrite the default), PATCH/GET /cernia-ops/platform/store/usage-pricing (super-admin — a practice that could reach it would set its own floor to zero), and two more fields in the ops price editor. Both ship UNSET, and unset resolves to `unresolvable`, never to zero. THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: a floor silently rescues a broken cost chain. If the cost pipeline reports $0.00 because it cannot price a model — which is the live condition today, o4_llm_cost_ledger.usd_cents is 0 on all 454 rows in journey_a because the pricing table does not know claude-haiku-4 — the floor kicks in, the invoice looks right, and nobody learns the platform is blind to its own costs. So apps/api/src/per-unit-price-resolver.ts returns TWO independent verdicts per charge: `basis` (cost-plus-margin | cost-below-floor | cost-unpriced) and `costConfidence` (measured | zero-indeterminate | unpriced). Same money, different diagnosis, and they never collapse. A priced zero is billable but never called healthy, because free self-hosted inference and a blind cost chain are the same integer from there — the producer is the only thing that can tell them apart, and that seam is left explicitly for the cost-chain work. ALSO FIXED IN PASSING: the price route conflicted on the surrogate `id` rather than migration 341's real unique key (tenant_id, item_type, item_id, cadence). A row for the same tuple created under a different id — by an older seed, by dev:stripe-bootstrap, by a fixture — missed the id target, hit the unique index anyway, and answered the operator with a 500 instead of a price update. Surfaced by test S11, which prices a product whose seeded row is keyed `cp-pa-monthly`. PROOF: over the wire against real Postgres, RED then GREEN, all four cadence x scope combinations — platform x monthly $29.99, platform x annual $323.89, negotiated x monthly $19.99, negotiated x annual $215.89 — plus an ADR-0004 control (a second growth practice reads the LIST price in both cadences and never the negotiated one) and a check that no card states a per-note rate. Port/DB pairing proven by a write THROUGH the port found in scribe_price and absent from the decoy. Screens driven in a real browser: the ops editor writing the price with a live operator cookie + CSRF, and the tenant storefront rendering $323.89/yr / clinician on its default cadence and $29.99/mo / clinician on the toggle, with ambient-scribe-pro still honestly unpriced. Artifacts: docs/status/evidence/scribe-pricing/ (cadence-red.json, cadence-green.json, ops-price-editor-saved.png, store-card-annual.png, store-card-monthly.png); runner apps/api/scripts/store-price-cadence-journey.mts.

THE AMBIENT SCRIBE BECAME PURCHASABLE ON A USAGE BASIS, AND 'TEMPORARY' BECAME A COLUMN INSTEAD OF A COMMENT. Founder instruction: 'We can set it later in ops portal. Just use temporary floor price. Even the margin % can be set later.' Two things were missing: migration 343's floor_price_cents + margin_ppm shipped UNSET (so resolvePerUnitCharge answered `unresolvable` for every note), and NOTHING CALLED THE RESOLVER — PR #758 shipped it explicitly as an empty seam. Both are now closed.  (1) THE SEED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A CONSTANT. NEW migration 346_usage_pricing_provenance_scribe_seed.sql seeds the platform default at floor 10c / margin 400000ppm (40%) for (tenant_id='', ambient-scribe, note). There is NO number in TypeScript anywhere — the resolver still reads only the database, so an operator write beats the seed by construction rather than by convention. The seed is `ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT product_usage_pricing_tenant_product_unit_key DO NOTHING` on migration 343's REAL unique key (not the surrogate `id` — that is the #758 bug one table over), which makes seeding FIRST-write-wins: a redeploy, a restore or a manual re-apply cannot walk an operator's number back. Every statement in the file is guarded, so the whole migration is re-runnable.  (2) PROVENANCE, so a placeholder can never be read as a decision. NEW column product_usage_pricing.provenance ('seeded-default' | 'operator-set', CHECK-constrained). Its DEFAULT is the CAUTIOUS direction — 'seeded-default' — so a future writer that forgets to set it produces a row labelled provisional (a badge an operator clears by re-saving) rather than one that presents a machine-written number as a human decision; rows that existed before the migration are backfilled to 'operator-set' because the ops PATCH route was their only ever writer. PostgresUsagePricingStore.upsert now stamps 'operator-set' UNCONDITIONALLY (not a parameter), so a caller can neither save a number and leave it labelled a seed nor pass itself off as one. The value travels: GET /cernia-ops/platform/store/usage-pricing returns provenance + a server-authored `caveat` string, the ops price editor prefills the stored policy and renders a 'Seeded default' warning from it, and resolvePerUnitCharge carries `policyProvenance` onto the charge so a BILL LINE priced off the seed says so. THE THREE VERDICTS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT COLLAPSED: `basis` (which arm of the max won), `costConfidence` (was the cost input believable), `policyProvenance` (did a human choose the policy) — a seeded policy over a measured cost and an operator policy over a blind cost chain are different problems with different fixes, and both produce a plausible number.  (3) THE RESOLVER GOT ITS FIRST PRODUCTION CALLER. NEW apps/api/src/scribe-note-pricer.ts: session -> ScribeCostPerNoteStore.bySession (NEW method; the session is the note's durable identity and exists at draft time, whereas composition_ref does not) -> measuredCostFromNoteCost -> PostgresUsagePricingStore.resolveForTenant -> resolvePerUnitCharge -> UsageMeter.record, wired into POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$draft fail-soft (the Composition is already persisted; an unmetered note is recoverable revenue, a lost note is not) and idempotent on the SESSION id (a redraft is not a second sale, so the price is a snapshot taken at first draft). It reuses the SAME @cernia/billing recorder as the voice-persona meter, so the invoicing flush rolls it into a tenant bill line with no second pipeline. THE JUDGEMENT IT REFUSES TO FUDGE: `compute` and `storage` are `not-attributed-per-note` on every note, so assembleNoteCost marks EVERY note unpriced and every note therefore bills the floor with basis='cost-unpriced', healthy=false. Summing pricedLowerBound and calling it the cost would have produced a confident number that is too small in the direction that flatters margin AND flipped basis to 'cost-below-floor' — i.e. the platform asserting it can see its own costs at the exact moment it cannot. Not done; the honest reading rides on the bill line and clears itself when the probes get a runtime caller.  (4) TWO LATENT DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED ON THE WAY. (a) PARTIAL UPDATE: the PATCH route's contract said 'omitting a field leaves whatever is stored alone' but the SQL assigned both columns unconditionally, so saving only a floor NULLed the margin — and a half-set policy is `unresolvable`, so the product went un-billable the moment anyone tried to price it. Harmless while both shipped unset; a live un-sale once they are seeded. Now three-state (number sets / null clears / undefined leaves alone) and the response READS THE ROW BACK rather than echoing the request. (b) WRITE-ONLY EDITOR: the ops price panel never read the stored policy, so the floor/margin boxes rendered blank whatever was stored — an operator could not see the seeded numbers they were being asked to replace, and could 'save' believing they had confirmed a price they had never seen. It now prefills on open. (c) A note with NO cost components at all was reported `priced` with total 0 by assembleNoteCost (nothing blocked completeness because there was nothing to block it), i.e. 'measured, and free'; the producer now refuses it.  LIVE PROOF (intent channel, real apps/api on :8123 against real Postgres scribe_seed on :5433). PORT IDENTITY PROVEN BEFORE TRUSTING ANY RESPONSE: a marker policy written THROUGH the API (product 'port-identity-probe-8123', floor 4242) was read back FROM scribe_seed and is ABSENT from the decoy scribe_price (count 0). PURCHASE TO PRICED NOTE: GET /admin/store/catalog renders the scribe card at $29.99/clinician/mo state='available' (after the tenant is moved to growth — the ADR-0035 starter floor is enforced); entitlement granted and visible on GET /admin/entitlements + product_entitlements; POST /scribe/sessions -> /consent -> POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$draft -> 201 with a real Composition AND a `usage` block reporting centsPerUnit=10, basis='cost-unpriced', costConfidence='unpriced', healthy=false, policySource='platform', policyProvenance='seeded-default'; the durable charge landed in billing_usage_events as kind='feature-use', featureId='ambient-scribe', idempotency_key='scribe-note:<sessionId>', with basis/healthy/blockedBy/policyProvenance/centsPerUnit in the body metadata.  THREE CONTROLS, ALL LIVE: (i) OVERRIDE BEATS SEED — PATCH 18c/55% through the ops route moved the row to 18/550000/'operator-set' and the GET's `caveat` went null; (ii) RE-SEED DOES NOT CLOBBER — re-running migration 346 verbatim against the live DB printed `INSERT 0 0`, left 18/550000/'operator-set' intact and produced no duplicate platform row; (iii) UNPRICED STILL SAYS UNPRICED — the note charged the floor and reported basis='cost-unpriced', never 'cost-below-floor'. A SECOND note drafted after the override billed 18c stamped 'operator-set' while the first stayed at 10c 'seeded-default', and a REDRAFT of the first added no second line (one row per idempotency key).  NOT PROVEN LIVE, stated plainly: no LLM provider on this stack is usable (OPENAI_API_KEY returns 429 billing_not_active, no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, no Ollama), so the drafting call was served by a local OpenAI-compatible STUB behind the gateway's supported self-hosted `ollama` provider. That substitutes the MODEL ONLY — HTTP $draft, the Composition write, llm_audit_events, o4_llm_cost_ledger, the pricer and billing_usage_events are all the real path — and the note text is not clinically meaningful and is not claimed to be. STT did not run either (a persisted transcript was reused, which is the normal U6 path), so no Deepgram invoice was incurred or observed. POST /admin/store/checkout could not create a session ('missing-price: no price id for product:ambient-scribe:monthly') because stripe:sync-prices has never run here — an external Stripe gate; settlement was driven through POST /dev/checkout-grant, the documented stand-in, which writes the same product_entitlements row via the same PostgresProductCatalogStore.grantProduct.
