VOICE TIER NO LONGER OUTLIVES THE ENTITLEMENT. Closes entitlement-lifecycle residual (b). THE DEFECT: every entitlement CHANGE calls syncVoiceTierFromEntitlements, so voice_tier is right at write time — but an entitlement also ends by simply having expires_at pass, with no event at all, which is the normal end of a cancelled subscription. Cancellation deliberately does not flip the tier (index.ts:3637 documents why: at that instant the tenant is still entitled for the period they paid for), and nothing runs when the date arrives. Access stays correct because hasActive honours expires_at at read time; the DERIVED column has no such guard, so voice_tier could sit at pro indefinitely and any consumer reading the column instead of calling resolveVoiceTierForTenant gets a Pro ceiling for free. THE FIX: resyncStaleVoiceTiers (apps/api/src/voice-tier-sync.ts) recomputes the tier from live entitlements for every tenant with a voice config and corrects drift, wired into the nightly tick immediately after runPeriodEndRevocationSweep (the sweep that makes rows go stale), job voice-tier-resync, per-tenant try/catch. It recomputes rather than assuming a direction, so it repairs the opposite drift (a grant whose sync failed) with no special case. PROVEN on real Postgres by reproducing the drift first: grant, sync, backdate the expiry, assert the entitlement is gone while the column still says pro, then assert the sweep corrects it — plus a cross-tenant isolation control where only the lapsed tenant is touched. apps/api/src/voice-tier-sync.test.ts 10/10.

PER-UNIT PRICING GENERALISED PAST THE SCRIBE, AND THE METERING PLANE GOT ITS MISSING PRODUCERS (BU7). (1) POLICY: migration 357 (packages/storage/src/migrations/357_metered_product_usage_pricing_seed.sql) seeds product_usage_pricing for the other three metered products - voice-minute/minute 35c, sms/SEGMENT 3c, email/message 1c, all margin 400000ppm - so they stop resolving unresolvable/floor-not-configured, i.e. unbillable. Every floor is LIFTED VERBATIM from LIST_PRICES.metered in catalog-seed.ts (the rates the storefront already advertises) rather than invented, and every row carries provenance='seeded-default' exactly as migration 346 did: nobody has decided these numbers, the ops editor renders its warning banner off the column, and the value rides onto each bill line as policyProvenance. (2) THE SHAPE: apps/api/src/metered-usage-pricer.ts generalises scribe-note-pricer.ts (product+unit as parameters instead of constants) so voice/SMS/email price through the same resolver as notes. It DIVERGES from the scribe in one documented way: the scribe records nothing when a policy is unresolvable, but a call has already connected and a segment has already left the carrier, so units are ALWAYS recorded and the pricing failure is stamped as pricingOutcome='unresolvable' - dropping the event would also blind the voice budget gate, which is a safety property, not a revenue one. (3) VOICE - A PRODUCER THAT NEVER EXISTED: apps/api/src/voice-minute-usage.ts. The IVoiceCallMeter seam has been called by InboundCallSession.terminate() since Wave-E and voiceCallMeter was NEVER passed in index.ts, so no deployment has ever written a voice usage event. Bigger than the lost revenue: voice-budget-checker.ts sums that same ledger to decide whether to ANSWER a call, so usedMinutes was structurally 0 for every tenant and the per-tenant voice-minutes cap has never been capable of firing. Now wired at BOTH call-end observers (the TS orchestrator's seam and the Pipecat BFF's callSession.record adapter in index.ts - the Pipecat one is the live PSTN path, so wiring only the seam would have missed every real call), idempotent on voice-call:<callSid> so both reporting the same call bills once. sumVoiceMinutesUsed now also counts feature-use/voice-minute (units are already billed minutes; the legacy voice-call arm is kept). (4) SMS/EMAIL - THE TRACKED CLAIM WAS WRONG, THE UNIT WAS THE REAL BUG: a producer DID exist (apps/api/src/metered-notification-backend.ts, wired at index.ts:1687/1704 and pointed at the real meter at index.ts:3244), so 'nothing emits a usage event for sms/email' was not true. What WAS true: MessageUsageInput.units existed from day one with a comment saying a multi-segment SMS may bill >1, and nothing ever passed it - every SMS billed ONE unit regardless of length while the carrier charged per segment, under-recovering ~3x on exactly the long reminders a busy practice sends most. SMS now meters countSmsSegments(body) (packages/billing/src/metering/sms-segments.ts: GSM-7/UCS-2, 160/153 and 70/67, extension chars at 2 septets, surrogate pairs as 2 code units) and both channels now carry the resolved price. Idempotency also FLIPPED to prefer the caller's key over the provider message id - a retry that reaches the provider twice gets a new provider id, so the old key double-billed the same reminder. (5) apps/api/src/cernia-ops-store-routes.ts: the tenant-scoped GET /cernia-ops/platform/store/usage-pricing hardcoded the literal 'note' as the usage unit, so asking about voice-minute for a practice answered source='none' about a unit that does not exist for that product and an operator would set a duplicate. Units are now discovered from the product's platform rows, with an optional ?usageUnit= to narrow. EVIDENCE: apps/api/src/metered-usage-producers.integration.test.ts, 16/16 on real Postgres, structured INCLUSION -> IDEMPOTENCE -> FALSIFYING CONTROL because the obvious 'no duplicate rows' assertion passes vacuously against a table that has never held one of these rows. Both controls are real: four call-end reports under a per-OBSERVATION key produce FOUR bill lines against one 2-minute call, and a retry keyed on the provider id bills TWICE. Counts are re-derived by SELECT from billing_usage_events, never from what a producer returned. Also fixed a PRE-EXISTING red: metered-flush-sweep-enumeration.integration.test.ts called runMeteredFlushSweep with 6 args after migration 332 added a required watermark parameter, so the nowFn stub landed in the watermark slot, nowFn defaulted to Date.now(), the sweep aggregated the wrong calendar month and reported nothing - red since 2026-07-29 and not a type error. Now 4/4.

A RESOLVED PER-UNIT PRICE REACHED AN INVOICE LINE FOR THE FIRST TIME - AND A PLACEHOLDER ONE STILL CANNOT. Two waves built a pricing chain that ended in mid-air: every producer stamped centsPerUnit/basis/policyProvenance onto the usage event and NOTHING read it, so metered usage produced revenue on paper and none on a bill. (0) THE TRACKED GAP NAMED THE WRONG FILE, in good faith. It pointed at packages/billing/src/invoicing/invoice-generator.ts; that function has NO production caller (grep across apps/ and packages/ returns its own tests and the index re-export, nothing else). The invoices this platform actually writes come from apps/api/src/invoice-generation.ts into enterprise_invoices (migration 137), driven by runInvoiceGenerationSweep in saas-nightly-batches.ts, and that generator billed exactly ONE line: the subscription's prorated ARR. Changing the named file would have produced a green diff, a plausible test and zero cents of metered revenue. Its tier-overage logic is NOT wrong - it bills capacity a plan includes at a rate that is a property of the tier - it simply cannot express a product sold BY THE UNIT at a price resolved per event. Left untouched, with a pointer comment at the top so the next reader does not fix it either. (1) THE READER: NEW apps/api/src/metered-invoice-lines.ts sums billing_usage_events per (product, unit, RATE, provenance, outcome) for the products that have a product_usage_pricing policy, and turns each group into one invoice line. Wired through NEW generateInvoiceWithMeteredUsage in invoice-generation.ts and into the nightly sweep. Scope is deliberate: only the four per-unit products; resource writes / workflow runs / exports are billed by the tier path and are NOT reported as unbillable. (2) THE REFUSAL, WHICH IS THE POINT. No invoice line is ever produced from a price stamped provenance='seeded-default' - which is EVERY price today (migrations 346/357 seeded them so the products could be sold before the founder settled the numbers). Three options were on the table and the choice is argued in the module header: refusing the whole INVOICE was rejected because it converts a pricing-config gap into a total revenue outage, taking the seat licence with it; a held/draft LINE was rejected because @cernia/x2a-enterprise-invoicing has no per-line hold state and a line the customer can see but must not pay is a support call. Chosen: refuse the LINE, keep the invoice, and make the refusal a NUMBER. (3) THE MIRROR-IMAGE FAILURE, WHICH IS THE WORSE ONE. Silently dropping unbillable usage under-bills and looks identical to a quiet month. So NEW table metered_usage_holds (migration 358) carries one row per (tenant, product, unit, reason) with the units and - where a rate exists - the cents NOT billed, rewritten in full on every sweep (a LEVEL, not a ledger, so a cleared hold stops alarming). Reasons: seeded-default-price, price-unresolvable, price-missing, non-integer-units, not-armed. withheld_cents is NULL rather than 0 when no rate was resolvable at all, because summing 'no rate' as zero says 'this is costing us nothing'. NEW GET /admin/billing/metered-holds (apps/api/src/billing-metered-holds-routes.ts) reads it back per tenant and returns totalWithheldCents PLUS unknownValueGroups, so the total cannot quietly understate. basis='cost-unpriced' / healthy=false is deliberately NOT a hold reason: it is true of 100% of units of all four products, so gating on it would withhold every dollar the platform earns while surfacing nothing actionable. (4) IDEMPOTENCY IS A QUANTITY, NOT A WINDOW. NEW table metered_invoice_watermarks keyed (tenant, product, unit, CENTS_PER_UNIT): billable_now = all units ever recorded at this rate - billed_units. A time window was rejected for two reasons: runInvoiceGenerationSweep invoices the CURRENT period, so the invoice for [Aug 1, Sep 1) is written on the night of Aug 1 before a single August event exists - a period-scoped line would bill ~nothing every month and look correct - and a window silently DROPS late usage. cents_per_unit is in the PRIMARY KEY so a mid-cycle rate change opens a second row and the invoice carries two honest lines rather than one averaged fiction. Shaped after billing_meter_report_watermarks (mig 332) per its own precedent, with ONE documented difference: no inflight column, because the side effect here is an INSERT into enterprise_invoices in the SAME database, so the claim, the invoice and the watermark advance run in ONE transaction and a crash between them is impossible rather than merely survivable. Two pods racing the sweep serialise on the row lock; the invoice-number constraint catches the same race one layer up. (5) PRECISION. The single rounding in this chain is resolvePerUnitCharge's per-unit Math.round; from there down everything is integer and a line total is an exact product. No second rounding was added. total_micro_cents (mig 352) is not used here because nothing downstream of the resolver is sub-cent - and a bucket whose accumulated units are NOT integral is HELD ('non-integer-units') rather than rounded into the bill. (6) DEFAULT OFF. CERNIA_METERED_INVOICE_LINES gates only the ATTACHMENT of lines; the measurement and the hold snapshot always run, so 'what is unbillable right now' answers correctly in both states and billable-but-unarmed usage is recorded as a hold rather than dropped. Also NEW: a to_regclass availability probe run ONCE per sweep OUTSIDE the transaction - because the metered plan runs inside the invoice transaction, a missing relation would roll back the INVOICE and turn a pricing-table problem into a billing outage; the sweep falls back to subscription-only and reports meteredAvailable=false rather than swallowing it. EVIDENCE (real Postgres 127.0.0.1:5433; every amount re-derived by hand from the persisted enterprise_invoices.invoice document and from metered_invoice_watermarks, never from a return value). NEW apps/api/src/metered-invoice-lines.integration.test.ts 19/19, ordered INCLUSION FIRST because 'no bad line reached an invoice' passes vacuously against a generator that produces no metered lines at all and would have passed on main yesterday: 42 operator-priced notes at 12c became ONE line with quantity 42 x unitPriceCents 12 = totalCents 504 and subtotal 120000+504; three (product, rate) groups became three lines totalling exactly 399c with no averaging; a neighbouring tenant's 99 notes stayed off the bill. THE CONTROL ARM: the SAME 40 notes billed 400c when provenance='operator-set' and produced ZERO lines when provenance='seeded-default', with the invoice still written at the subscription amount and a hold row reading units=40 / withheld_cents=400. FALSIFIERS: deleting the watermark by hand DOES re-bill the same 250c (so 'no second line' is the watermark working, not an empty query), and a late-arriving event whose occurred_at precedes the first invoice is picked up by the next one (which a time window would have dropped). Extended apps/api/src/invoice-generation-sweep.integration.test.ts (2/2) proves both arms through runInvoiceGenerationSweep itself - the production entry point - with tenant A billed 360c and tenant B refused and held at 300c in ONE sweep, and a second sweep adding no second cent. NEW apps/api/src/billing-metered-holds-routes.test.ts 3/3 (real PG): the total EXCLUDES the null-valued group and reports unknownValueGroups=1, cross-tenant holds are invisible, no tenant claim = 401. ADR-0127: @cernia/billing typecheck 0 / test 597 passed + 11 skipped / build 0; @cernia/api typecheck 0 / build 0; lint 63 errors = the documented carry-forward baseline EXACTLY, with ZERO in any touched file. Related suites re-run green: erasure-cascade 10, erasure-cascade.completeness 14, saas-nightly-metered-flush 6, saas-nightly-wedged-watermark 5, metered-usage-producers 16, invoice-generation 5. ADR-0140 gate OK, 278 tenant-scoped tables all classified; migration 358 declares metered_invoice_watermarks = RETAIN and metered_usage_holds = RETAIN, agreeing with ADR_0140_SCOPED_OUT in apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts - the same rationale already recorded there for billing_meter_report_watermarks: delete the watermark and the next sweep re-bills an erased tenant's entire history against a usage ledger that is itself retained. NOT PROVEN, stated plainly: no live invoice has been generated against a real customer, because the gate is OFF and every price is still a seed. What IS proven is that the mechanism bills correctly when a human has set the rate, and refuses when nobody has.

COMMS SPEND STOPPED BEING ATTRIBUTED TO NOBODY, AND A BOUNCE BECAME AN OBSERVABLE EVENT WITH A WAY TO CREDIT IT (policy off). (1) THE 'platform' STRING. apps/api/src/otp-senders.ts built every verification SMS with a hardcoded tenantId 'platform' and called the Twilio adapter DIRECTLY, around createMeteredNotificationBackend - so OTP produced real carrier spend and zero usage events. Twilio Verify (apps/api/src/signup-phone-verifier.ts) was worse: it POSTs the Verify REST API and never touches a notification backend at all. The string itself was the deeper problem - on a single-tenant deployment CERNIA_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID IS a real tenant id, so 'genuinely platform-borne' and 'we lost track of whose this was' were indistinguishable. FIX: migration 359 comms_spend_attribution, classified RETAIN alongside billing_usage_events (financial record; no recipient, no hash of one, no body - the ERASE-classified notification_delivery_log DOES hold a recipient hash, which is exactly why the two sit on opposite lists). Its CHECK forbids a row that names both a tenant and a reason, or neither, so the ambiguous middle is not expressible. UnattributedSpendReason has exactly two values, kept APART on purpose: 'pre-signup-verification' is acquisition cost and benign; 'tenant-unknown-at-send' is lost attribution and a bug report. packages/auth-providers/src/otp/otp-service.ts now forwards tenantId + purpose to the sender as OtpSendContext - not new information: both were already in issueOtp's input and were simply dropped before reaching the sender. The resolver checks PURPOSE BEFORE TENANT (apps/api/src/notification-spend-attribution.ts) because charging a single-tenant customer for a stranger's signup attempt would be a billing error. Tenant-attributed OTP meters through recordMessageUsage with the SEGMENT count; unattributable OTP records units with metered=false. (2) THE BOUNCE. Two complete bounce pipelines existed and NEITHER was on a route - grep -r w3-deliverability apps/api/src returned one hit, a COMMENT in metered-notification-backend.ts explaining that 'delivered' was therefore not an observable signal and metering on it would be metering on nothing. apps/api/src/notification-bounce-routes.ts mounts them at POST /webhooks/bounce/:provider with an HMAC over the RAW body (content-type parser encapsulated to the plugin, so the blast radius of a signature check is not every route on the server), 503 fail-closed on a deployment with no CERNIA_BOUNCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and the prefix added to the registerRbacHook unauth allow-list - the exact shape that once charged Stripe purchases and never granted them. It classifies (unwrapping SendGrid's array batching, which w3's own handler map does and a naive mount would 400 on), drives w3 suppression policy, CORRELATES via comms_spend_attribution.provider_message_id, and writes the outcome to notification_delivery_log so the existing admin observability page shows a bounce beside the send. (3) THE REVERSAL. apps/api/src/notification-usage-reversal.ts writes a COMPENSATING ENTRY - negative units, idempotencyKey 'reverse:<original>', metadata.reverses - and never mutates or deletes the original, because an invoice a tenant disputes has to be reconstructable ('we billed you on the 3rd and credited it on the 5th' is defensible; 'there is no record of that send' is not). It writes through the STORE, not the UsageMeter, because createEventRecorder.validateInput rejects units<=0 and that validator is CORRECT - a reversal is the one legitimate negative, so it gets a narrow, loudly-named path instead of a weakened guard every caller inherits. The aggregator sums with no sign assumption, so the credit nets the charge to zero without the aggregator needing to know reversals exist. (4) CREDITING IS OFF, AND IS NOT AN ENGINEERING DECISION. apps/api/src/notification-bounce-credit-policy.ts states both cases (the ESP bills us on ACCEPTANCE, so crediting means the platform absorbs a tenant's stale contact list and removes the only economic pressure toward the list hygiene that protects every other tenant's shared sending reputation - against a tenant reasonably expecting not to pay for mail nobody received). An ENUM, not a boolean, because 'some of them' is the likely answer and a boolean would need re-plumbing the moment it is. Soft/blocked/auth/content are never creditable under any setting. EVIDENCE, live on a booted apps/api + fully migrated Postgres, 2026-08-04: signed bounce -> 200 through the global RBAC hook; bad signature -> 401 from the ROUTE ('invalid-signature'); a non-allow-listed sibling path -> the RBAC hook's own 401 ('Authorization header is required'), which is the falsifying control proving the allow-list entry is what let the first one through. Policy off -> correlated:true, 'policy-off', 1 usage row. Policy on -> 'reversed', 2 rows netting 0 with the original units still 1; redelivery -> 'already-reversed', still 2 rows. Suites: notification-spend-attribution.integration.test.ts 17/17, notification-usage-reversal.integration.test.ts 12/12, notification-bounce-routes.integration.test.ts 15/15, all on real Postgres.

Made the metered storefront state its unit, and gated the two halves against drift. catalog-seed.ts LIST_PRICES.metered rows became { rateCents, unit } and now seed catalog_prices.usage_unit; store-catalog-aggregator carries it as CatalogPrice.meteredUnit (deliberately NOT folded into `usage`, whose includedQuantity:0 renders as "Unlimited" — the opposite of the truth for a pure per-unit price); storefront-catalog renders "per <unit>". The unit had lived only in a code comment saying "per SMS" while migration 357 priced sms per SEGMENT, so a three-segment reminder billed 9c against a card implying 3c and nothing compared the two. seedCatalogPrices refreshes usage_unit for METERED rows only: a licensed row's unit belongs to the operator (ops price editor) and a re-seed writing NULL over it would delete usage terms a human authored — covered by a real-PG no-clobber test.

Closed the arming landmine: the FIRST armed metered invoice would have billed every unit in a tenant's history. planMeteredInvoiceLines bills observed - billed, and `billed` comes from metered_invoice_watermarks, where a group with no row reads as ZERO billed. Founder decision 2026-08-05: forgo the backlog. Migration 360 adds single-row metered_billing_cutover (CHECK id = 'global'); invoice-generation.ts establishes it OUTSIDE the invoice transaction on the first armed sweep (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a second arming cannot move the boundary); readMeteredUsageBuckets gained an occurred_at >= since filter. WHY AN INSTANT AND NOT A SEEDED WATERMARK: a missing watermark row is also what a brand-new (product, unit, rate) group looks like, so treating absence as backlog would silently forgive a tenant's first-ever SMS a year from now - the third test is the one that would catch that mistake. FAIL-CLOSED: armed with no cutover recorded, `since` stays an unreachable future and nothing bills, because the alternative (fall back to the whole ledger) is exactly the catch-up invoice this change prevents, arriving through a door marked "the cutover write failed" - a missed night is recoverable, a retroactive invoice is not. UNARMED IS UNCHANGED: the full ledger is still reported as held, so the backlog stays visible even though it will never be billed. Proven on real Postgres 6/6 with a falsifying control (post-cutover usage IS billed, 7 units at 3c = 21c, while the 100 pre-cutover units are gone rather than deferred). Two existing suites now pin the boundary explicitly rather than inheriting wall-clock now(), which would have made their assertions depend on the day they ran.

Closed entitlement-lifecycle residuals (a)(c)(d). (a) A derived operator worklist (GET /cernia-ops/platform/entitlements/unsupported) rather than an alert emitter — a query catches failures nobody anticipated and self-heals when expires_at is set. (c) The cernia-ops UI, with the hashing tension answered honestly in the markup: the hashed matrix CANNOT have a one-click expire and should not, so the write affordance lives on the worklist, whose rows carry raw ids. Settled rule recorded — read-only aggregates hash, write worklists do not, because a hash cannot become a WHERE clause. (d) Downgrades narrow entitlements at period end via the registry minTier floor, failing OPEN on anything unresolvable because over-serving is the tolerated error and wrongly revoking is not. Best process note: the fourth falsifying control INITIALLY PASSED — the assertion was satisfied by the row data-testid rather than the cell — and two absence assertions were found vacuously true on an empty result. Both classes of false green were caught by the agent itself and fixed; that is the third time today a control has caught a test that proved nothing.

Enforced the telehealth-visits tier floor and grandfathered existing holders (founder decision: expiry at period end, never immediate revocation). The instructive part is that the one-line fix would have done NOTHING — the product is storefront:false and never reaches validateCart, so the real hole was the checkout.session.completed fan-out granting whatever the cart named with no tier check. The UI had been rendering it tier-locked for a floor the registry never had. Grandfather is a re-runnable reconcile pass rather than a migration (a migration is a second writer past the append-only history, and runs once where a floor is standing). The durable fix is a source-scanning test that fails any registry entry whose PROSE claims a tier restriction its body does not carry. Sweep found three more of the same class: compliance-evidence (included by nobody, fails closed), referral-pro (no gate at all), and billing-service checkout-cart (no floor whatsoever).

Corrected a stale clause on perunit-prices. It claimed the SMS storefront unit and the billed unit still disagreed (a 3-segment message billing 9c against an advertised 3c). Measured: the drift is closed AND guarded by catalog-seed.metered-unit-parity.test.ts, which reads both sides back from the database after migrations and seed rather than comparing constants, and passes 5/5. The residue is the PRICE decision, not a mismatch. Worth recording how this surfaced: the stale clause was used to build a founder question framed as a live billing defect, and the founder said "we have fixed this before" — which measurement confirmed. The punch list mis-stating its own residue is a recurring failure here, and it now costs a founder decision cycle rather than only an agent run.

Founder decision: publisher onboarding stays in the developer portal rather than being ported into apps/admin — publishing is a distinct persona, not another tenant-admin task. The bullet is deliberately NOT closed: it now owes a written exception in CLAUDE.md beside invariant 3. An invariant with an undocumented exception is one a future agent either "fixes" by undoing this, or cites as licence to put the next surface anywhere.

Closed metered-flush (c) and (f) and wired both. The airtime finding was worse than recorded — the carrier's CallDuration was not losing a race, it was being discarded by the markEnded guard, so no durable carrier figure existed at all. Carrier is now authoritative both directions (downward-only would have the platform eating airtime on a dropped media socket), and a correction crossing an invoice watermark records credit-note-required rather than relying on the invoicer, which would have silently skipped it. Email suppression is durable and sits INSIDE the metering decorator so a refused send is not billed. Residue: no operator surface for either, and no backfill — airtime already invoiced stays overbilled.

tracks.name: External Integrations & per-tenant config
tracks.description: Per-tenant credentials + vendor backends the voice agent talks to (Twilio for telephony, Deepgram for STT, ElevenLabs for TTS, OpenAI/Anthropic for LLM). Also covers self-serve tenant provisioning + per-tenant workflow customization. Without this layer every tenant shares the platform's trial credentials and can't customize the assistant.

stages.name: Tenant secrets — per-tenant credential storage
stages.rationale: Each tenant must paste their own Twilio/Deepgram/ElevenLabs/LLM credentials so calls bill to their accounts. Plaintext is encrypted at rest with envelope encryption (AES-256-GCM); the resolver falls back to platform-level env vars when no per-tenant override exists.

baseline.summary: No per-tenant credential storage. The voice agent's Twilio/Deepgram/ElevenLabs/OpenAI/Anthropic keys came from process.env only. Every tenant in a multi-tenant deploy would share the same vendor accounts — billing attribution impossible, key rotation per tenant impossible, white-glove onboarding meant editing the platform-level env.

current.summary: Shipped end-to-end. Migration 046_tenant_secrets (composite-PK (tenant_id, provider), opaque ciphertext column, JSONB metadata). TenantSecretResolver in @cernia/core with NoopSecretCipher (dev) + AesGcmSecretCipher (prod). apps/api boot now wires KyselyTenantSecretStore (secrets survive restart) + refuses to start in production when CERNIA_TENANT_SECRET_KEY/KID is unset or wrong length — TenantSecretBootError thrown loud. PUT/DELETE handlers emit structured tenant-secret.write/delete IAM audit rows. KMS rotation runbook (docs/operations/runbooks/tenant-secret-key-rotation.md) covers cadence, rehearsal in staging, multi-key decrypt window, re-encrypt job, and rollback.

history.note: Swapped apps/api boot from InMemoryTenantSecretStore → KyselyTenantSecretStore. Added prod-mode TenantSecretBootError refusing missing/short keys. Authored KMS rotation runbook with rehearse-in-staging + multi-key window + re-encrypt job.

stages.name: Twilio voice backend boot wiring
stages.rationale: @cernia/telephony ships a TwilioVoiceBackend + LiveKit/SIP backend. apps/api needs to instantiate one and wire it into the voice-call handler so an inbound call actually arrives at the dialog engine.

baseline.summary: packages/telephony has TwilioVoiceBackend + LiveKit/SIP backend with full unit coverage. apps/api/src/voice-call-handler.ts handles barge-in + recording-pause-on-PHI. NOT yet wired: the boot path doesn't construct a TwilioVoiceBackend instance and the /telephony/inbound webhook is stub-only.

current.summary: TwilioVoiceBackend fully wired. buildTwilioVoiceClient() native-fetch factory added to @cernia/telephony (no SDK dependency — uses Node 20+ fetch). Boot path in apps/api constructs TwilioVoiceBackend when CERNIA_TELEPHONY_BACKEND=twilio + TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID + TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN + CERNIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL are set; falls back to stub with structured log. 26 new tests cover create/fetch/update + auth header + idempotency. Typecheck + full telephony test suite clean.

history.note: LIVE OUTBOUND PSTN CALLS surfaced + closed TWO real telephony bugs that only a genuine call could expose (the inbound trial call could not reach the /voice path; outbound + a keypress past the trial preamble does). Setup: same cloudflared tunnel + operator trial Twilio account; destination +13029834679 added as a Verified Caller ID (trial accounts can only dial verified numbers); outbound placed via POST /telephony/outbound (real JWT → RBAC deriveOperation /telephony/outbound→TelephonyCall → caller-id allowlist assertOwnedByTenant(+12402444312) → real Twilio Calls API → CallSid → call.outbound.placed audit → call_sessions row → 200 — all proven live). BUG 1 (apps/api/src/telephony-routes.ts, POST /telephony/twilio/voice): the handler resolved the tenant from the To number — correct for INBOUND (To = our number) but WRONG for OUTBOUND, where Twilio fetches the TwiML *after* we placed the call and the tenant-owned leg is From (To is the external party). So every outbound TwiML callback resolved tenantId=null → call.unknown-number → no dialog (observed live: CallSid CA0f96c6… fetched /voice after a keypress but bailed to unknown-number). FIX: branch on body.Direction; for outbound-* resolve tenant from From, mark the existing outbound session answered, emit call.outbound.answered, return Connect/Stream TwiML (skip the inbound _dispatchInbound path). LIVE-VERIFIED on a fresh call (CallSid CA41d57c…): call.outbound.answered now fires with tenantId=22222222-… resolved from From, and the call_sessions row flips ringing→in-progress with answered_at set. BUG 2 (packages/telephony/src/backends/twilio-backend.ts placeOutboundCall): StatusCallbackEvent was sent COMMA-separated ('initiated,ringing,answered,completed'); Twilio's Calls API requires the call-progress event list to be SPACE-separated and parses a comma-joined value as one invalid token → subscribes to NO events → the StatusCallback never fires → outbound sessions never reach 'completed' (confirmed live: 0 /status POSTs for any of 3 outbound calls, while inbound /status worked because that comes from the phone NUMBER's own StatusCallback config, not this param). FIX: 'initiated ringing answered completed' (space-separated) + doc-comment corrected. ADR-0127: @cernia/api typecheck=0 + telephony-routes.test.ts 18/18 (added an outbound-direction regression test asserting tenant-from-From + call.outbound.answered + session direction stays outbound); @cernia/telephony typecheck=0 + twilio-backend.test.ts 26/26 (2 assertions updated to the space-separated form). The /voice fix is LIVE (apps/api hot-reloaded by tsx watch); the StatusCallbackEvent fix is unit-verified and goes live on the next @cernia/telephony rebuild + api restart. Secrets used as launch-time env overrides only; trial account = no BAA → synthetic/non-PHI calls only. UPDATE (live re-verify, same day): the BUG 2 comma→space change was INSUFFICIENT — Twilio rejected the space-joined value too, emitting notification 21626 'invalid statusCallbackEvents' on CallSid CA1bac94… (a live call surfaced this; unit tests never could). TRUE ROOT CAUSE: Twilio's Calls REST API requires StatusCallbackEvent as a REPEATED form param (StatusCallbackEvent=initiated&StatusCallbackEvent=ringing&…), not any single joined string. FINAL FIX in packages/telephony/src/backends/twilio-backend.ts buildTwilioVoiceClient.calls.create: split the whitespace event string and params.append() each event. LIVE-CONFIRMED on CallSid CAf4ebe5…: /status POSTs 1→5 (initiated/ringing/answered/completed all delivered), Twilio notifications now [] (21626 gone), audit chain call.outbound.placed→answered→ended (tenant 22222222), call_sessions row reached status=completed duration_seconds=4 — the outbound voice lifecycle now closes end-to-end on a genuine PSTN call. twilio-backend.test.ts 26/26 (added a getAll('StatusCallbackEvent') repeated-param assertion); @cernia/telephony typecheck=0. Also added a wiring cross-reference comment at the outbound-backend construction in apps/api/src/index.ts.

LIVE INBOUND PSTN CALL verified end-to-end through a public tunnel — the genuine-call half of the Wave-E telephony path that unit/synthetic tests could not exercise. Setup: cloudflared quick tunnel (https://sailing-multimedia-maple-nearly.trycloudflare.com) → local apps/api :8080 booted with CERNIA_TELEPHONY_BACKEND=twilio + the operator's real account (AC2ca625…, trial) + CERNIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=tunnel; the number +12402444312 (PN3eba5f6…) registered in tenant_phone_numbers (tenant 22222222-… purpose voice-agent) with its Twilio VoiceUrl + StatusCallback pointed at the tunnel via the Twilio REST API. RESULT: a real inbound call (CallSid CAed80803a93606fef5a64aac9edee9561, from +13029834679, status=completed, 13s) hit POST /telephony/twilio/status through the tunnel; our handler VALIDATED the Twilio HMAC-SHA1 signature against the reconstructed https URL (Host header preserved by cloudflared), emitted a call.ended audit (toNumberHash 067e8a95…d6ac93 — byte-identical to the hash of +12402444312, proving it was our number; status=completed, durationSeconds=13) and returned 204. Twilio's own Calls.json log corroborates the same CallSid/from/duration. This proves the live chain: real PSTN → Twilio → public tunnel → Fastify route → signature validation → audit → 204. The /voice (media) webhook did NOT fire on this inbound call — only /status did (log: 2 voice POSTs = both the synthetic signed test [valid→200+call_sessions row; bad-sig→403], 1 status POST = the real call) — because on a Twilio TRIAL account inbound calls play the mandatory ~13s trial greeting and the custom inbound VoiceUrl isn't proxied as on a paid account; NOT a handler defect (the /voice path is independently proven by the real-Twilio-signed synthetic webhook → 200 + persisted CAtuntest… session). REMAINING for live /voice media on a genuine inbound call: an UPGRADED (non-trial) Twilio account, and a signed Twilio BAA before any real patient audio is routed (trial = no BAA → synthetic/non-PHI only). Secrets used as launch-time env overrides only; never written to a committed file.

history.note: Deepgram STT VALIDATED live against the operator's real key — AND fixed a real bug that meant STT produced ZERO output in production. (1) BUG FIXED (apps/api/src/deepgram-ws-transport.ts): the ws 'message' handler gated on `typeof data === 'string'`, but the `ws` library delivers Deepgram's JSON TEXT frames as a Node Buffer (isBinary=false), so EVERY transcript/VAD/error message was silently dropped — STT never emitted a single transcript. The unit test gave false confidence because it called onJsonMessage() directly with a string, bypassing the ws delivery path. Fix: new handleSocketMessage(data, isBinary) decodes any non-binary frame to UTF-8 (Buffer | Buffer[] | ArrayBuffer | string); binary frames ignored. (2) Live proof: new apps/api/src/deepgram-stt.live.test.ts — a TTS→STT round trip in the Twilio telephony format (ElevenLabs Sarah → ulaw_8000 → DeepgramSttBackend encoding=mulaw/8000 over the real WS) — Deepgram transcribed 'the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' at 0.998 confidence. Diagnosed via direct WS probes that confirmed the full backend query (nova-2-medical + redact + no_retention, both finish modes) transcribes correctly, isolating the defect to the transport's frame-type guard. (3) Regression guard: 3 new unit tests exercise handleSocketMessage with a Buffer text frame / string / binary (the path the old test missed). Gated on ELEVENLABS_API_KEY + DEEPGRAM_API_KEY (skipIf). [onboardingfullprovisioner-retry-resolveexisting] ONBOARDING PROVISIONING IS NOW OBSERVABLE — CLOSED 2026-08-06. The bullet was real (only the line numbers had drifted; the ordering was as described): fhir.provision -> startTrial -> grants -> enqueueProvisioning, with the provisioning_runs row written LAST, so a failure in the first three steps left ZERO rows and the retry surface was blind. The $complete handler rethrows unknown errors to a 500 and the audit emitter is a fire-and-forget sink that only fires on success or denied, so nothing else recorded the attempt either. FIXED via a new apps/api/src/onboarding-provisioning-ledger.ts: one row per step, written BEFORE the step and advanced after; provision() is now a thin wrapper that parks the in-flight step on any throw and rethrows unchanged. No migration — it reuses provisioning_runs (289 + 297), so nothing collides with 364 — and no wiring line, since the ledger is built from the db the provisioner already holds. A SECOND DEFECT WAS FOUND BY CHECKING EACH STEP, and it is the more serious one: TrialLifecycleManager.startTrial THROWS TRIAL_ALREADY_ACTIVE when the admin already has a trial, so every retry that got past step 1 on the first attempt died at step 2 — steps 3 and 4 were unreachable FOREVER, which made the whole resolveExisting convergence story moot. Fixed with a narrow tolerance; any other trial error still aborts. FOUR DECISIONS ARE WRITTEN DOWN AT THE MODULE: (1) a ledger write that FAILS does not abort provisioning — that would convert a bookkeeping outage into the exact customer-facing failure the ledger exists to diagnose, and proceeding unrecorded is the status quo ante, so the worst case is no worse than today; (2) terminal state is needs-info, never failed, because the drain loop claims any pending row and promotes any failed one, so either would get the row claimed, found executor-less, and rewritten with last_error clobbered — and needs-info is also semantically right, since the password/PIN/EHR token are transient and a human must re-drive; (3) pre-tenant rows are filed under pending_onboarding_<sha256-32> rather than a guessed slug, because deriveSlugFromName maps every non-[a-z0-9] char to "-" so an underscore makes collision impossible — a guessed slug would have parked one practice's failed signup on another's status page; (4) the session id is a bearer capability, so grant_ref carries a digest. 8 new tests on real Postgres, gates 80/80, ratchet 371. WHAT REMAINS: (a) no reaper for orphaned pending_onboarding_* rows — erasure-cascade.ts deletes provisioning_runs BY tenant_id, so rows from signups that never produced a tenant belong to no tenant's erasure; they hold no PHI (session digest, stage, timestamps, platform text, 200-char error) but they accumulate; (b) a hard process kill leaves the row at running with a stale updated_at rather than parked — legible as "stuck in stage X since T", but there is no stale-running reaper; (c) the step-1 wedge (Tenant created, admin User not, so resolveExisting returns null and the conflict rethrows) is now VISIBLE but still not auto-recoverable; (d) listForTenant now returns 4 extra rows per onboarded tenant — every consumer was checked and only the admin U4 view reads it, iterating activeProductIds so they render nowhere, but any NEW consumer doing exact-match on that list must filter by productId.

[number-management-p4-portin] NUMBER MANAGEMENT IS SHIPPED (P4 port-in Cards 1-6, 2026-06-08; admin multi-number surface 2026-06-15). REASSIGN-BETWEEN-TENANTS SHIPPED 2026-08-07 and is MOUNTED — the previous release path really was release-and-re-buy, which loses the number: phone_number is globally UNIQUE with no tenant in the key (migration 030) and registerIdempotent actively THROWS when the surviving owner differs, so the code refused a move rather than merely lacking one. POST /cernia-ops/numbers/$reassign, OPERATOR-ONLY. Placed on the ops surface deliberately: every other route on /admin/numbers is tenant-scoped under billing.manage, but a reassign names TWO tenants and moves an asset across the boundary, so source-side authority alone lets a departing or compromised admin DONATE the practice's main line (a tenant admin's legitimate destructive ceiling is deactivating their own number, which is recoverable — giving it away is not), and destination-side authority is strictly worse, being a pull. The PRIMARY gate is the global RBAC hook — /cernia-ops/* is deliberately outside deriveOperation, so a non-operator falls to the deny-all catch-all no tenant RoleBinding covers — with the route's own requireSuperAdmin as defence in depth, proven by a control asserting that billing.manage PhoneNumber IS covered by a tenant admin's wildcard binding. WHAT MOVES, after sweeping every table with a phone column or Twilio SID beside a tenant_id: tenant_phone_numbers.tenant_id in place (a delete+insert would orphan PhoneNumber/{id} org refs), org_id -> NULL (it names a facility in the SOURCE's org tree), and the source's tenant_external_resources twilio number + SID iff they name this number — that last one load-bearing rather than hygiene, because a stale SID makes provision-tenant-external-resources short-circuit the source's replacement purchase FOREVER and makes voice-fallback-wiring PATCH Twilio config onto a number the destination now owns. RETURNING yields POST-update values, so the operator was handed a NULL SID — exactly no help with the carrier move — fixed to read-before-clear under FOR UPDATE; and one refusal test used from===to and passed on the same-tenant guard, staying green with the ownership check mutated out. [chargeback-statements-periodic-backstop] Chargeback statements HAVE A PERIODIC BACKSTOP as of 2026-08-06 (apps/api/src/chargeback-statement-backstop.ts, wired at index.ts). The gap was real and SHARPER than this bullet said: the webhook block is fire-and-forget by design — it runs AFTER the invoice is marked paid and AFTER the Stripe 200 is acked, so it must not reject the delivery — which means a pod rolling or a transient DB error in that window loses the statement permanently and Stripe will never redeliver. THE DESIGN POINT: the sweep resolves the tenant chargebackMethod FIRST and skips the none case without ever calling buildStatement, because none is the DEFAULT for every tenant with no pricing config — a naive gap-filler would have fabricated statements for nearly the whole fleet. A null from buildStatement (method set, no billable facilities) is a THIRD outcome, and flag-off reports disabled rather than a clean zero. Idempotent on the (tenant_id, source_invoice_id) UNIQUE index the webhook already uses, so the two producers cannot double-write. Bounded: a 35-day window (the config keeps NO history, so it applies CURRENT policy and an unbounded sweep would back-fill years after a policy flip) and a 200/run cap reporting truncated. 21 real-Postgres tests, every positive paired with a control. REMAINING, each genuinely separate: (a) a WHOLLY-LOST webhook delivery is still uncovered — the invoice is never marked paid locally either, so it is not a candidate, and POST /admin/billing/$reconcile reconciles SUBSCRIPTION status and the payment-method cache but NOT invoice status, so there is no repair path for paid-at-Stripe-open-locally; (b) cut-over tenants (billingCutoverShim.isCutOver) get nothing — the webhook forwards before the chargeback block and apps/billing-service has no chargeback producer at all, and whether this sweep repairs them depends on whether billing-service shares this Postgres, unverified; (c) no ops read surface, findings go to the log only; (d) historical policy is unknowable, so a tenant flipping none to even gets up to one cycle of retro-allocation.

[deepgram-noheal-local-remediation] DEEPGRAM NO-HEAL — clause (a) CLOSED 2026-08-07 and WIRED. The orphaned project could not be revoked because IDeepgramMgmtClient declared only createProject and createScopedKey. FOUNDER DECISION: add the delete, OPERATOR-ONLY — capability in, blast radius kept narrow BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by convention. THREE BARRIERS, weakest last. (1) The automated path's object HAS NO DELETE METHOD AT RUNTIME: buildDeepgramMgmtClient returns a literal with exactly two properties, and deletion lives on a different interface from a different factory, so casting does not help — a refactor would have to reach into another module and construct another object. (2) The provisioner's options type has no slot for a destroyer. (3) An authority argument the auto path cannot construct: a module-private unique symbol, un-nameable elsewhere AND checked at runtime, so forcing it through with `as never` throws before any HTTP call. Barrier 3 also carries the confirmation into the client boundary, so a future second caller that forgets to check still cannot delete the wrong project. Route guards: 400 on a missing id, 400 on a confirmation mismatch, 409 project-is-live checked ACROSS ALL TENANTS (an operator cannot take out tenant B by fat-fingering an id) with NO force override, 501 when unconfigured. Audited as deepgram.project.delete with the operator id; refusals recorded as deny. The type-level assertions cannot rot — the ratchet typechecks test files, so a @ts-expect-error that stops erroring raises the count (proven: adding the method to the interface moves it 371 -> 381). Runbook §4 is now §4a API-preferred + §4b console-fallback, with the header saying not to remove §4b because 4a depends on a third-party API that can be down. WHAT REMAINS: clause (b) — never exercised against a real Deepgram-provisioned tenant. The vendor is external-gated, so all evidence is an injected recording client; DEEPGRAM_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY must be set for the route to do anything but answer 501.

Self-serve signup — signup-phone SMS verification now has a FLIPPABLE provider (Twilio Verify | own-number OTP), and Twilio Verify is VERIFIED LIVE end-to-end (landed LOCALLY, held per push-on-signal). Problem: the only built SMS path was own-number Programmable Messaging, which needs an owned Twilio number + A2P 10DLC registration before US delivery works — so signup SMS couldn't actually be sent until A2P is approved. FIX: new apps/api/src/signup-phone-verifier.ts introduces a SignupPhoneVerifier seam with TWO providers — VerifySignupPhoneVerifier (Twilio Verify REST: /Verifications + /VerificationCheck; Twilio generates/sends/checks the code from its own managed sender, NO owned number or A2P needed — Twilio explicitly steers OTP use cases here) and OtpSignupPhoneVerifier (the existing own-number OtpService path, for when Cernia's A2P brand/campaign is approved). buildSignupPhoneVerifier() picks by env: TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID set → Verify, cleared → own-number. THE FLIP IS ONE ENV VAR. Both providers record the SAME consumed 'signup-phone' row in auth_verifications, so the flag-gated $complete/reserve-tenant gate (otpService.hasRecentVerification) is provider-agnostic — no gate change. Routes (apps/api/src/auth-verification-routes.ts) now call the verifier for the pre-auth /api/auth/signup/phone/{start,confirm} endpoints (authed MFA routes still use OtpService directly). Dev-safety: the Verify send honours the SAME COMMS_DEV_ALLOWLIST as the OTP senders (new exported isRecipientCommsAllowed in otp-senders.ts; gateByAllowlist refactored to use it, no behavior change). index.ts extracts otpStore, builds the verifier (allowSend=isRecipientCommsAllowed), passes it to the routes, and logs the active provider. LIVE PROOF: with a real Verify service (Cernia Health Signup, VA…) configured, POST /signup/phone/start → a REAL SMS arrived on the admin's personal mobile; POST /signup/phone/confirm with the texted code → {ok:true}; auth_verifications shows the signup-phone row consumed → hasRecentVerification=true. Four decisions recorded at the module (ledger-write failure must not abort provisioning; terminal state needs-info not failed, because the drain loop would reclaim a failed row and clobber last_error; pre-tenant rows keyed by hash not a guessed slug, which would have parked one practice's failed signup on another's status page; session id digested as a bearer capability). 8 tests on real Postgres, gates 80/80, ratchet 371. Shipped operator-only phone-number reassignment between tenants (POST /cernia-ops/numbers/$reassign, apps/api/src/cernia-ops-number-reassign-routes.ts + telephony-store.ts), wired at index.ts and boot-verified (Server listening; the route answers 401 not 404). Placed on the ops surface because a reassign is by construction cross-tenant — source-side billing.manage would let an admin donate the practice's main line. Moves the owner row, nulls org_id, and clears the source's Twilio SID (a stale SID would break the source's replacement purchase forever); leaves calls, transcripts and usage with the tenant that incurred them. Atomicity proven by forcing the second half to fail two different ways. Residue is carrier-side: no subaccount transfer exists, and the voice-fallback TwiML bin still points at the source practice.

Closed Deepgram clause (a): operator-only project deletion, wired. Containment is structural — the automated remediation path holds an object with no delete method at all, so it cannot reach deletion by cast or refactor; a module-private symbol checked at runtime is the third barrier. The live-project guard checks ALL tenants, so a mistyped id cannot destroy a different practice, and there is deliberately no force override. Still never exercised against a real Deepgram tenant — the vendor is external-gated.

Release 3 / T2 — self-serve API-key auth WIRED into the request path (the complete-but-unwired ApiKey system is now live). (1) Token-format reconciliation: apps/api/src/admin-api-key-routes.ts buildSecret() now mints the issuer's cernia_pk_<12-char base32 prefix>_<32-char base32 secret> format (was the divergent cernia_pk_<64 hex>, no separator, whole-secret hash) and stores secretPrefix=cernia_pk_<prefix> + secretHash=hashPassword(inlineSecret only), so a $generate-secret key now ROUND-TRIPS through DefaultApiKeyVerifier (proven by admin-api-key-routes.test.ts test 2). (2) Cross-tenant lookup: NEW apps/api/src/api-key-lookup.ts PgApiKeyLookup.byPrefix() queries the live `resources` table on the STORED generated column apikey_secret_prefix with NO tenant filter (the token is the sole credential; tenant is derived AFTER the match) — safe because secretPrefix has 60 bits of entropy + a platform-wide uniqueness constraint and ApiKey is a credential resource, NOT PHI (CLAUDE.md invariant 5). recordUsage() writes lastUsedAt by id, best-effort/non-fatal. (3) principalResolver branch: apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts PrincipalResolverDeps gains an optional apiKeyVerifier; a Bearer/cookie token starting with cernia_pk_ is verified as an API key (cross-tenant prefix lookup + constant-time scrypt verifyPassword + status/expiry gates), the tenant is read from the key's urn:cernia:tenant meta.tag, and the principal is built via the SAME resolvePrincipalFromClaims so RBAC/RoleBindings apply identically (authVia='api-key'). A cernia_pk_ token NEVER falls through to the JWT verifier: null verify → 401, no verifier wired → 401. The JWT Bearer path is byte-unchanged (regression test A4). (4) $revoke + $rotate: apps/api/src/admin-api-key-routes.ts adds tenant-admin-gated POST /admin/api-keys/:id/$revoke (status=revoked + revokedBy/revokedAt, idempotent, cross-tenant id → 404) and POST /admin/api-keys/:id/$rotate (mints a new verifiable secret for the same principal/name, revokes the old with reason='rotated', returns the new secret once with no-store headers). Boot wiring: apps/api/src/index.ts constructs DefaultApiKeyVerifier(PgApiKeyLookup(db)) injected into registerRbacHook so EVERY authed route honors API keys, and passes the tenant-scoped storage to adminApiKeyRoutes for revoke/rotate. Tests: NEW api-key-lookup.test.ts (6, real Postgres :5433 via createMigratedDatabaseFixture — cross-tenant byPrefix, unknown/soft-deleted→null, recordUsage), NEW admin-api-key-routes.test.ts (8 — format-reconciliation round-trip, revoke idempotent + revoked-key-no-longer-verifies, rotate, non-admin 403 / cross-tenant 404), + 6 API-key-branch cases in iam-route-guards.test.ts (seeded-RoleBinding authenticates with right roles, revoked→401, expired→401, JWT regression, no-verifier→401, unknown-prefix→401). Release 3 / T2 follow-up — three live-path bugs the T2 unit suite missed (it mocked RBAC + seeded the tenant tag) FIXED so self-serve API keys actually work end-to-end against the running stack. Bug A (RBAC fail-closed 403): deriveOperation (apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts) had NO mapping for /admin/api-keys/* custom-verb routes, so the global RBAC hook fell through to the {*,*} catch-all and 403'd a tenant-admin BEFORE the route's own isAdmin check ran. Added 4 mappings → write:ApiKey: $generate-secret, $issue, :id/$revoke, :id/$rotate. Bug B (UI-created keys never authenticate, 401): the admin UI creates ApiKeys by POSTing the resource, but storage scopes tenancy by COLUMN and does NOT stamp meta.tag urn:cernia:tenant, so the verifier failed closed ('API key is not tenant-scoped'). NEW server-side POST /admin/api-keys/$issue (apps/api/src/admin-api-key-routes.ts) issues via DefaultApiKeyIssuer, which stamps the tag from the AUTHED principal's tenantId (SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE — never client body); defaults the key principal to the caller so it inherits the caller's RoleBindings; tolerates empty/{} bodies; returns {secret, apiKey} once with no-store headers. Bug C (FHIR auth layer rejects api keys): T2 wired apiKeyVerifier into registerRbacHook ONLY, but @cernia/server's FHIR routes (GET /ApiKey, /Patient, …) have a SEPARATE auth preHandler (createAuthMiddleware → identityProvider.authenticate) that only knew JWTs — so an api key got 'Token malformed' (401) on any FHIR route even after passing the RBAC hook. FIXED by composing the FHIR-router identityProvider in apps/api/src/index.ts (step 6b): a cernia_pk_ bearer is verified as an api key (tenant from meta.tag, fail-closed if absent), any other token delegates UNCHANGED to the JWT provider; one shared DefaultApiKeyVerifier backs BOTH the FHIR layer and the RBAC hook. Each of the three bugs was reproduced (test fails) then fixed (test passes). Release 3 / T3 — tenant self-serve WEBHOOKS shipped by EXTENDING the existing SubscriptionEngine rest-hook engine (no second delivery path). A tenant-admin registers an HMAC-SIGNED FhirSubscription rest-hook and receives POSTs when matching resources are written. (1) Signing (security): packages/subscription/src/{types.ts,dispatcher.ts} gained an OPTIONAL rest-hook channel field `signingSecret` (additive — existing Workflow/Connection callers unaffected); when set, dispatchRestHook adds `X-Cernia-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, rawBody)>` over the EXACT bytes POSTed (body serialized ONCE so the tenant can recompute). (2) Secret storage — approach (a), REUSE the encrypted tenant-secret store: apps/api/src/webhook-secret.ts stores each webhook's secret in tenant_secrets (migration 046) under synthetic provider key `webhook:<subscriptionId>` via TenantSecretResolver (AES-256-GCM in prod, Noop in test); encrypted at rest, tenant-isolated by the (tenant_id,provider) PK, generated server-side, returned ONCE at registration with Cache-Control:no-store, NEVER written to the FhirSubscription body (so it cannot leak via a FHIR read). get() accepts ONLY a tenant-sourced row (never the platform-env fallback — that would be a forgeable shared secret). Rejected (b) HMAC(masterKey,subId): one compromise forges every tenant + no per-hook rotation. (3) Bootstrap (apps/api/src/subscription-bootstrap.ts): startup scan now also materialises active rest-hook FhirSubscriptions (criteria derived from filterBy/topic — bare resourceType matches every write of that type, the SAME criteria format Workflow triggers use), AND the onWrite hook (re)materialises a FhirSubscription on create/update + tears its handle down on off/entered-in-error, keyed by tenant::subId so there is never a duplicate. LOOP-AVOIDANCE: a FhirSubscription write is treated as CONFIG (re-materialise) and is NEVER fanned out as a deliverable match. (4) Routes (apps/api/src/webhook-routes.ts, tenant-admin gated + deriveOperation→FhirSubscription in iam-route-guards.ts): POST /admin/webhooks (server-authoritative tenant; pre-assigns id, stores secret BEFORE create fires onWrite so the materialised handle is SIGNED; returns {subscription,secret} once, 201, no-store), GET /admin/webhooks (lists own; never a secret), POST /admin/webhooks/:id/$test (synthetic signed Parameters ping through the SAME dispatcher), POST /admin/webhooks/:id/$disable (status=off + unmaterialise + secret removed). Tenant isolation: register/list/test/disable all scoped to the authed principal's tenant; deliveries fire only for the subscription's tenant (engine is per-tenant via onResourceWrite(tenantId,…)). MANDATORY LIVE TEST (apps/api/src/webhook-live-flow.test.ts — the T2-lesson acceptance bar): real node http receiver + real createServer + real PgStorageAdapter on :5433 + real engine bootstrap → register a Patient webhook → write a Patient via a REAL FHIR route → receiver gets EXACTLY ONE POST whose body is the Patient and whose X-Cernia-Signature equals an INDEPENDENTLY-computed sha256 HMAC; the secret is NOT readable via GET /FhirSubscription/:id; a Patient in a DIFFERENT tenant does NOT reach the receiver. Closed [webhook-registration-post-webhooks] as an INTENTIONAL DESIGN POSITION, not as work. The bullet was decision-gated because mapping it CONFLICTS with a documented rule: developer_portal is deliberately tierFeature:null in apps/api/src/product-registry.ts, and public-store-catalog-routes.ts states the rule explicitly — "tierFeature is null — add-ons are never bundled into a tier; they are bought." FOUNDER DECISION 2026-08-07: KEEP THE RULE. Webhook registration stays behind the purchased add-on rather than being bundled into a tier. This is closed rather than narrowed because there is no residual engineering work — the tier-inclusion mechanism already functions (store-catalog-aggregator grants any product whose non-null tierFeature is in the tier feature set), so bundling would have been a one-field change; the reason not to make it is commercial, and it has now been made. Recorded here so a future reader finds the DECISION rather than rediscovering the conflict and reopening it: the next agent to notice that webhook registration "should probably be included at growth" is looking at a settled question, and changing it means changing the add-ons-are-bought rule first, deliberately, not as a side effect.

history.note: PHI access-audit perf follow-up SHIPPED (PR #487) — the last open audit item. DefaultAuditQuerier.search previously loaded the whole tenant chain into memory + filtered in JS + parsed every JSONB snapshot. Now AppendOnlyStore gains searchPage(query): the PostgresAppendOnlyStore pushes filtering + pagination + count into real SQL (Kysely, fully parameterized — parameterized WHERE per provided filter actorUserId/targetId/actions-IN/resourceType/operation/inclusive-timeRange, a separate COUNT(*) for total, sequence_num ASC + limit+1 to detect nextCursor, and it OMITS before_state/after_state from the SELECT when includeSnapshots===false — a real bandwidth win, not post-filtering). DefaultAuditQuerier.search just validates + clamps + delegates to store.searchPage, so the observable contract is unchanged. The InMemoryAppendOnlyStore.searchPage moved the querier's old filter/cursor/slice logic in verbatim. Migration 294_audit_data_plane_fields.sql (packages/storage/src/migrations/294_audit_data_plane_fields.sql) adds nullable resource_type/operation columns + a (tenant_id, resource_type, timestamp) index to rbac_audit_events, additive only. @cernia/k4-rbac-audit-log (packages/k4-rbac-audit-log/src/{types.ts,postgres-append-store.ts}) grew optional resourceType/operation on RbacAuditEventInput/RbacAuditEvent — folded into the existing hash-chain payload (new events are tamper-evident over the extra context; old-shape events, which never had the keys, hash unchanged — proven by a mixed old/new-shape chain-verify test). New apps/api modules: phi-audit-scope.ts (PHI_AUDIT_RESOURCE_TYPES allowlist of 21 patient-compartment/clinical types + shouldAuditAccess() — denials always audited, allows only for PHI types), audit-write-buffer.ts (createAuditWriteBuffer — bounded sync FIFO, enqueue() never throws, drops-newest + counts past capacity, default cap 10k), rbac-audit-emitter.ts (createRbacAuditEmitter — the real IamAuditEmitter implementation for registerRbacHook's `audit?` seam in iam-route-guards.ts, previously wired as `undefined`; maps allow/deny decisions to RbacAuditEventInput, whole body try/catch-swallowed). Wired in apps/api/src/index.ts (section 7f, right before registerRbacHook): buffer + emitter constructed unconditionally (zero-cost when nothing consumes them); a `db`-gated background flusher (mirrors the existing `if (db)` PostgresAppendOnlyStore/exporter gate) drains the buffer on an unref'd 500ms interval and appends serially into the SAME tamper-evident table the audit-export route reads, with a one-shot append retry + count-only overflow/failure logging (no PHI in logs) and a best-effort onClose final flush. LOAD-BEARING PROPERTY VERIFIED: audit never blocks/slows/fails the request — enqueue is synchronous, does zero I/O, and cannot throw; all Postgres I/O happens only in the background flusher. Proven live: booted apps/api against real Postgres :5433 (CERNIA_DEV_LOGIN=1), POST + GET /Patient through the real RBAC hook, then `psql SELECT` on rbac_audit_events showed 2 real rows (access-granted/write and access-granted/read, resource_type=Patient) within ~1s, and DefaultChainVerifier.verify() against those live rows returned {allValid:true, totalEvents:2}. Real-Postgres integration test (apps/api/src/phi-audit-pipeline.integration.test.ts) proves all 5 required properties by name: (a) an allowed Patient read produces a tamper-evident row the chain verifier accepts, (b) overflow drops-and-counts without throwing, (c) a denied access (any resource type) logs access-denied, (d) an allowed non-PHI access logs nothing, (e) tenant isolation (each row's tenant_id, cross-tenant chains independent). remaining: [u7-residuals-all-l1] ORG SCOPING IS SHIPPED AND OPT-IN 2026-08-07. All three items this bullet carried are done. ENFORCEMENT IS PER-TENANT — the founder ruling of 2026-08-07, IMPLEMENTED HERE, so nothing on this bullet awaits a call. Not the platform flag: new table tenant_org_scope_mode (migration 367), matching the house pattern of small dedicated mode tables (tenant_isolation_mode 247, tenant_record_mode 254) rather than a generic settings blob — it is read on the authorisation path of EVERY authenticated request, so it must be a PK point lookup, and a PHI posture, a system-of-record choice and an access boundary are three independent decisions that should not share a row. CERNIA_ENFORCE_ORG_SCOPE survives as a THREE-STATE override, and the tenant row beats the middle state in both directions: '0' is a KILL SWITCH that turns scoping off even for opted-in tenants (one env change, no DB write across N tenants — a kill switch that needs a per-tenant write is not a kill switch); '1' is the default for tenants with NO row, which is why the existing org-scope suites still pass; unset is PRODUCTION TODAY, where the tenant row is the only thing that enables it. FAIL-SAFE DIRECTION: any error reading the setting resolves to NOT ENFORCING, and that failure is deliberately NOT cached. A failed lookup that silently enabled scoping would hide charts from clinicians, which is worse than the gap it closes. Fail-CLOSED on assignment resolution stays as it was — by that point the practice has said it wants separation. THE RESOURCE SPLIT is a DENY-LIST (org-scope-resource-policy.ts) and that choice is load-bearing. Scoped: Encounter, EpisodeOfCare, Composition, DocumentReference, ClinicalImpression, ServiceRequest, MedicationRequest, NutritionOrder, VisionPrescription. Practice-wide by decision: Patient/RelatedPerson (the founder ruling — a referral must still FIND the patient), allergies / immunizations / conditions / medication statements and observations / diagnostic reports (longitudinal safety data; hiding an allergy list from the covering facility is a hazard, not a win), Coverage, and Appointment/Schedule/Slot (a front desk that cannot see the other site's capacity cannot book the referral it was handed). WHY NOT AN ALLOW-LIST: this policy sits on the generic FHIR chokepoint, which also carries Organization (the tree the facility switcher is built from), Role/RoleBinding (what RBAC reads), terminology and billing — an allow-list that forgot one would not leak, it would BREAK THE PLATFORM for exactly the tenants who opted in, whereas a deny-list that forgets a clinical type leaves it as visible as today. Asymmetric failure modes; the safer one was taken. Admin surface at /admin/organizations/scope-policy — tenant-scoped self-serve per invariant 3, and it needs NO deriveOperation entry because it sits under the already-mapped /admin/organizations/ prefix, which a test asserts against the REAL deriveOperation + buildDefaultRoles rather than assuming, because a route that 403s everyone while its unit tests stay green has shipped here four times. ALSO DONE: l1 and l4 DELETED (40 files) after capturing their five unbuilt ideas in docs/design/org-model-unbuilt-semantics.md — cross-org consent, permission inheritance, org merge/split, shift handoff, SSO claim mapping. The note opens by saying there is no code to go back to, because the implementations were in-memory Map shims and restoring them would hand a future implementer the wrong substrate. Two findings from writing it: the l1 and l6 permission-inheritance designs DISAGREE on precedence (the note recommends l6's rule), and merge/split only ever moved org METADATA — re-pointing data was "the caller's responsibility" and there was no caller. l2 is RETAINED with its reason in a header: the IDN/facility model, Safe-Harbor suppression and the measure catalog exist nowhere else, but wiring it needs three tables, a measure-ingestion pipeline that does not exist, and a decision about whether Facility duplicates FHIR Location/Organization — doing it before deciding would recreate the exact parallel-implementation mistake that killed l1. WHAT REMAINS, both genuinely new: (i) NO cernia-ops CROSS-TENANT VIEW of which practices have opted in — per invariant 3 that is a half-ship, and it is a clean follow-up (aggregate counts only, no tenant PHI); (ii) THE CROSS-FACILITY REFERRAL HAND-OFF DOES NOT EXIST. A referral is a ServiceRequest, which is scoped, so one written at facility A is stamped to A and is not visible at B until re-attributed through $assign-resources. The PATIENT is findable either way — that is the safety property that was actually asked for — but the ORDER needs a deliberate hand-off, and today that is a manual operator action rather than a flow.

[orgscope-optin-regression-20260807] ORG-SCOPE OPT-IN SHIPPED A REGRESSION ON 2026-08-07 AND IT WAS REPORTED GREEN. Recorded because the way it escaped matters more than the defect. THE DEFECT: isOrgScopeEnforcedForTenant wrapped its settings read in `catch { return false }`, which flattened three situations into one confident answer — table absent (migration 367 not run), database unreadable, and healthy. The middle one was the problem. registerRbacHook has failed CLOSED on undeterminable org scope since Wave L (empty scope, null active org, an org-scope.resolve-failed audit row); the catch answered `false` before that contract could apply, so an unreachable database served an UNSCOPED read with no audit trail. A security control disabled by an error handler. Result: migrations 001-012 succeeded in vitest. The test then printed `[bisect 13/88] 013_audit_sharding.sql` and never printed 14/88 — i.e. migration 013 hung or the transition to 014 hung. The 180s testTimeout triggered after 218s wall-clock. Migration 013 contents (packages/storage/src/migrations/013_audit_sharding.sql): 6 ALTER TABLE statements on audit_log (ADD COLUMN shard_id NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, ADD CONSTRAINT CHECK shard_id >= 0, ADD COLUMN prev_shard_hash, UPDATE audit_log SET prev_shard_hash (no-op on empty table)) + 2 CREATE INDEX on audit_log + 4 ALTER TABLE resources ADD COLUMN ... GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED for SecurityFinding + 3 CREATE INDEX on resources. Standalone Node script applies all 88 migrations in ~600ms, so the issue is the vitest interaction with this specific multi-statement SQL file (whole file is one `sql.raw(text).execute(trx)` call). Next hypothesis to try: split migrations on statement boundaries before passing to sql.raw — if per-statement execution works in vitest where bulk does not, the fix is a runMigrations refactor. Bisect test (postgres-fixture-bisect.test.ts) deleted after the diagnostic; the finding is recorded inline in the remaining bullet so future agents can pick up from this point.

CIT harness Hypothesis C test: applied migrations 001-013 one SQL statement at a time inside vitest (each statement in its own sql.raw().execute(trx) call, all inside the same transaction). Hypothesis was that splitting on statement boundaries would unblock the hang isolated to migration 013 in Hypothesis B. Result: still hangs, BUT exposed a much earlier slow point — migration 010_phase2_tier3_terminology_context.sql statement #20 (ALTER TABLE resources ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS grp_actual TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS ...) took 8731ms (vs ~ms expected for an ALTER on an empty table), and the next statement(s) hung. Combined with Hypothesis B`s finding (whole-file 013 hangs, which also has many GENERATED-column ALTERs), the root cause class is narrowed to PostgreSQL `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED` column DDL under vitest`s forks worker — likely an interaction between pg-driver`s simple-query protocol, vitest`s stdio/IPC channel, and Postgres`s row-recomputation phase for the new generated column. Diagnostic tests deleted after the finding was recorded; next hypotheses listed for the next agent (extended query protocol; statement_timeout to convert hang to error; vitest pool=threads instead of forks; testcontainers Postgres).

[marketplace-fhir-seam-audited] MARKETPLACE FHIR SEAM — AUDITED 2026-08-06 AND THERE IS NO CROSS-TENANT READ. Proven in BOTH directions against real Postgres: tenant B reads the A patient id and gets 404 AND A reads its own and gets 200, same route, same storage, only the JWT claim differs. The enumerate test previously asserted only that the B searchset is empty, which a dead route would also satisfy, and now asserts it equals exactly the B patient. The cross-tenant 404 is asserted BYTE-IDENTICAL to a never-existed 404, so the seam cannot confirm another tenant ids exist while refusing to serve them. Attribution is pinned at the storage layer, so the 404 is provably the tenant predicate rather than an incidentally broken route. TWO REAL DEFECTS FIXED, neither needing a decision: (1) resourceType had NO shape check and GET /marketplace-platform/fhir/%3Cscript%3E/abc REACHED STORAGE (measured) — now 400 before storage, and the body never echoes the segment; the field is typed string on the sandbox RPC contract, i.e. arbitrary bytes from untrusted workflow code. (2) an unknown query parameter returned a 422 LISTING EVERY DECLARED SEARCH PARAMETER, so a probe loop over resourceTypes could map the whole search surface from error bodies — now echoes only the caller own names, capped at 10. THE BULLET WAS ALSO WRONG ON ONE POINT: count 500 is NOT caller-controlled — the route builds SearchOptions itself and the adapter discards _count/_offset/_page (a test asserts the store received count 500 given _count=100000). So that clause is is-500-right, not a security question. REMAINING: (a) the resourceType ALLOW-LIST is still inert by default (CERNIA_MARKETPLACE_FHIR_SCOPE unset resolves to any) and enabling it is a founder call — fresh evidence for why it was not guessed: 123 types are REGISTERED while the ResourceType union declares 57 MORE, so a guessed list would refuse reads that work today; (b) the id parameter is unconstrained, so within a tenant any id of a permitted type is readable by guessing — the route header claims ids come from the run-context envelope but NOTHING enforces that and the request carries no run id, so binding it needs a contract change on apps/marketplace-service; (c) offset is pinned to 0, so the seam cannot page past the first 500 of a type at all, a latent FUNCTIONAL bug nobody had noticed; (d) not exercised over the wire through the global RBAC hook with a real minted service JWT.
