The fix is a second config — tsconfig.typecheck.json, noEmit, same program plus the tests — so one file decides what is BUILT and the other what is CHECKED. `pnpm --filter @cernia/api typecheck:tests` runs scripts/typecheck-tests-ratchet.mjs. WHAT TURNING IT ON REVEALED, and why it is a ratchet: 567 pre-existing errors, invisible for as long as the exclusion has existed. 79 of them are the CONTRACT-DRIFT class this exists to catch (TS2420/TS2739/TS2741 — a double missing members of the interface it claims); the rest are largely noUncheckedIndexedAccess ergonomics on test arrays. Demanding 567 fixes before the protection turns on would mean it never turns on, so the ratchet pins both counts and fails on any INCREASE, and --update refuses to raise them. CONTRACT DRIFT IS NOW ZERO (was 79) and the ratchet pins it there, 2026-08-06. The 79 were ~12 root causes repeated across call sites, not 79 problems: RecordingExecutor missing resumeWorkflow/cancelExecution (24 errors, 3 files), call-session doubles missing findBySid/listByTenant (~19), RoleBinding fixtures missing grantedBy/grantedAt (~11), Role fixtures missing displayName/scope/status, InMemoryOtpStore missing findLatestConsumed, and singles. Missing members were added as THROWING stubs, never plausible return values — a double that quietly succeeds on a path the suite never meant to exercise turns a wrong call green, which is the class this check exists to surface. TWO OF THEM WERE REAL SIGNALS, not bookkeeping. tenant-rate-limit.test.ts declared a `scale` tier that IS NOT a SubscriptionTier and omitted `starter`, the tier a tenant lands on by DEFAULT — so every case rate-limited four tiers of which one did not exist and the commonest one was exercised by nothing. And the voice-call-handler STT double was missing hasBaa, so the BAA posture went unexercised there; fixed by spreading the real backend rather than inventing values. CORRECTION TO THIS BULLET: it said "NONE of it is in scribe files". That is true of the CONTRACT DRIFT subset (0 in scribe files, still true) and FALSE of the 567 backlog it reads as describing — 89 of them are in scribe test files, 30 in scribe-draft-routes.integration.test.ts alone. A reader would have skipped them. NARROWED 489 -> 430 on 2026-08-06, and the largest root cause was NOT ergonomics. Helper functions wrapping app.inject({...}) had no declared return type, so TypeScript resolved Fastify overloads to "void & Promise<Response> & Chain" — on which .statusCode and .json() do not exist. Declaring Promise<LightMyRequestResponse> fixed 59 across 7 files and is a STRENGTHENING: the helper now states what it returns. No casts, no assertions, and the 6 touched suites still pass 94/94. A MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING because the number was seductive: the first run reported 489 -> 7, which was an ARTIFACT. The import-insertion heuristic matched the opening "import {" of a multi-line import and inserted inside it; the resulting parse error made tsc BAIL before checking 135 other files. A 98% drop from one regex is not a result, it is a symptom. The real number is 430, and it was only found by distrusting the good one. WHAT IS LEFT: 430 errors, ratcheted, still deliberately not fixed by assertion. The remaining root causes are MEASURED and concentrated rather than a formless backlog: 39 possibly-undefined on test-array indexing, 16 InMemoryStorage vs OrgAdapterStorage, 16 StripeFetch, 16 FhirResource vs Record<string,unknown>, 15 kysely transaction variance, then a long tail across ~130 files. Each cluster is one double or one fixture repeated at many call sites, so the next pass is arithmetic rather than archaeology. The ratchet only ever goes down. RATCHET LOWERED 430 -> 400 (2026-08-06, second pass) and the method is the point: apps/api/src/test-support/defined.ts adds first()/at()/defined(), and `const x = arr[0]` became `first(arr, 'x')` across 4 files. THAT IS A STRENGTHENING RATHER THAN A SILENCING, which is the bar this ratchet exists to enforce: `arr[0]!` narrows AND KEEPS the failure, which then surfaces as "Cannot read properties of undefined" pointing at the assertion instead of at the cause. first() throws "expected meter calls[0] to exist, but the collection has 0 item(s)" — and in a test that drives an async pipeline and then inspects what it recorded, "the pipeline recorded NOTHING" is almost always the real failure, so `!` is precisely the annotation that hides it. 37/37 of the rewritten tests still pass. WHY IT STOPPED AT 400 rather than continuing: the remaining possibly-undefined errors are a LONG TAIL of varied shapes (inline indexing, Map.get, destructured optionals) that each need per-site judgement, not one more sweep. Continuing mechanically is how a strengthening turns into a silencing. ALSO FIXED: the baseline file's own _remainder field still read "The 430 that remain" AFTER the number moved — the same stale-summary pattern this session corrected on four status bullets. It now states the count once and carries the instruction to update it with the baseline.

[package-suites-red-main] PACKAGE SUITES ARE RED ON MAIN AND NOTHING SAYS SO — NEW 2026-08-06, surfaced by the CI-coverage sweep and the direct consequence of the bullet above: 11 of 329 package suites run at a merge-blocking tier, so the other 318 can be red indefinitely and are invisible. A local sweep, ultimately 324 of 324 suites, reported 26 red outside the CI set. TREAT THE NUMBER 25 AS UNRELIABLE AND THE FINDING AS REAL — the two must not be conflated. The sweep ran while six agents and the parent were hammering the same test Postgres AND while the schema snapshot and shared template database were being regenerated underneath it, which is exactly the condition that makes a real-PG suite fail spuriously. SPOT-CHECKED AFTERWARDS ON AN IDLE MACHINE: @cernia/o4-cost-tracking-budgets was listed RED and is GREEN (227/227) — so at least one entry is a contention artifact. Two others were confirmed genuinely red, and both are INDIVIDUAL TESTS rather than dead suites, which the phrase "25 red suites" overstates: @cernia/data-governance 1 failed / 247 (DeidentificationOrchestrator safe-harbor, reidentVaultDays — VaultExpiredError from an IN-MEMORY vault, so not a fixture artifact) and @cernia/speech 3 failed / 321 (DeepgramSttBackend endpointing expects 1000 and gets 1500; two barge-in cases in factory + round-trip). WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN: (a) a CLEAN re-measurement on an idle machine, one suite at a time, to replace the contended list with a trustworthy one — the sweep is cheap to repeat and its output is the work queue; (b) the confirmed failures above, unowned; (c) @cernia/developer declares `vitest run` with ZERO test files, so wiring it into CI would fail on "No test files found" — the fix is to write tests or drop the script, NOT --passWithNoTests, which converts "this package is untested" into a green tick; (d) the 281 suites the sweep measured green are NOT wired in, deliberately: a Windows-local pass is not a Linux-runner pass against a freshly migrated database, and adding 281 unverifiable filters to a workflow that cannot currently run is the blind addition that gets a job disabled. (e) SUPERSEDED WITHIN THE HOUR, and left visible because the shape of the mistake is the point. This clause said @cernia/integration-tests "WAS NEVER MEASURED AT ALL". It finished about twenty minutes after that was written and merged: 1 test file failed / 25 passed (26), exit 1, after 1,580 SECONDS — it runs on testcontainers, spinning up MinIO and Postgres, which is why it outlived two poll windows and read as dead. It was slow, not unmeasurable. The allow-list was regenerated from the complete sweep, its entry is now suite-red-when-last-measured, and the suite-not-measured reason has ZERO members and was dropped automatically — which the checker verifies, since it fails on an orphan reason. So the sweep is 324/324 with NOTHING unmeasured, and the tally is 281 green / 26 red (23 assertion + 3 database-fixture) / 0 unmeasured. THE RED COUNT REMAINS UNRELIABLE for the contention reason stated above — it moved 25 to 26 here, and o4-cost-tracking-budgets is still a known false positive within it. A timeout is not a measurement, and recording it as a third state was right; asserting the suite could not be measured was one step further than the evidence went. PARTIALLY MITIGATED THE SAME DAY: scripts/check-ci-test-coverage.mjs is now a PRE-PUSH GATE (scripts/install-hooks.mjs), so a package that gains a `test` script no CI job runs fails the push unless it is allow-listed with a reason. That stops the gap WIDENING; it does nothing about the suites already red, and it is enforcement of the exclusion list only — not of the suites themselves. It matters because GitHub Actions has been unable to run since 2026-07-29, making the pre-push hook the ONLY enforcement of anything right now.

[csrf-test-passes-alone] A CSRF TEST PASSES ALONE AND FAILS IN COMPANY — found 2026-08-06 at integration, PROVEN PRE-EXISTING rather than assumed. apps/api/src/cernia-ops-session-routes.test.ts case 5, "cookie-auth POST WITHOUT the CSRF header -> 403", is green when that file runs alone (11/11) and green across the whole `cernia-ops` glob (28 files / 278), but RED and DETERMINISTICALLY so when the run also includes `everything` and `billing-routes`. Reproduced twice on the working branch, then reproduced AGAIN on main at 1f94606c with the six-agent wave absent from the tree — so it is not a regression from that wave, and the checkout-and-rerun is the evidence rather than an inference from "our files look unrelated". WHY THIS SHAPE MATTERS MORE THAN THE ONE TEST: the assertion is that a cookie-authenticated POST without the CSRF header is REFUSED. A cross-file interaction that can flip that result to a pass-through is either (i) shared module-level state — a CSRF secret, a session store, or an app singleton — leaking between test files, in which case the test is measuring another file's state and proves nothing about the route, or (ii) a real ordering-dependent hole in the middleware registration. BOTH readings are bad, and the current one is worse than a red: the suite is GREEN in every command anyone actually runs, so a genuine CSRF regression would be invisible. NOT INVESTIGATED FURTHER here because it was found during an unrelated integration and chasing it would have stalled six merged changes; recorded rather than carried in someone's head. WHAT IS LEFT: bisect the glob to the exact partner file, then determine which of the two readings it is — the fix differs completely (isolate the shared state vs. fix the middleware). The repro is one command: cd apps/api && DB_PORT=5433 DB_PASSWORD=cernia npx vitest run --poolOptions.forks.singleFork cernia-ops everything billing-routes. Note this matters more than usual while GitHub Actions is down, since no scheduled full-suite run exists to catch it.

[migration-crossschema-guard-bug] MIGRATION 346 HAS A CROSS-SCHEMA GUARD BUG THAT MAKES THREE SUITES FAIL ON MAIN — found 2026-08-07 while building elsewhere, reproduced on UNMODIFIED main across three files the finder never touched. Its column guard queries information_schema.columns with NO table_schema predicate. createPostgresFixture gives each test file its OWN schema inside one shared database, so any SIBLING schema that happens to own a `provenance` table makes 346 believe the column already exists, skip its ALTER where it is actually needed, and 357 then dies. Symptom: "column provenance ... does not exist", 13 failed / 30 passed across metered-usage-producers, metered-invoice-lines and ratify-seeded-prices — and it is ORDER-DEPENDENT, so it comes and goes with which suites share a run. THE FIX IS ONE LINE (AND table_schema = current_schema()), but it edits a LANDED migration, which needs its own decision: amending 346 in place changes what already ran on every environment, whereas a new migration that re-applies the ALTER conditionally is additive and safer. WORTH FIXING SOON because it manufactures phantom red suites, and this repo has already spent agent runs proving a failure was not theirs.

[migration-drift-guard-already] SNAPSHOT REGENERATED 2026-08-07 — the guard is green and this bullet is now about what regenerating it EXPOSED. CORRECTION TO THIS BULLET, WHICH I WROTE THIS MORNING: it said the snapshot was stale by 48 migrations and "fails by 5". Measured: the DDL was stale by THREE (365 voice_airtime, 366 email_suppression, 367 tenant_org_scope_mode — exactly 4 tables, no table lost, verified by diffing CREATE TABLE sets before and after). What was 319-behind was the schema_migrations SEED ROW LIST, not the schema. Two different kinds of stale, and the bullet conflated them. WHY IT MATTERED ANYWAY: createMigratedDatabaseFixture builds its template from this snapshot, not from the migrations, so any suite using it tested a schema the platform no longer had. Regenerating fixed 8 red files outright (facility-switch-routes, iam-route-guards-org-scope, org-scope-enforcement, org-scope-tenant-optin, llm-audit-dangling-correlation, patient-erasure-ambiguous, repair-stranded-scribe-signs, scribe-coverage-routes) — 57 failing tests down to 42. A GENERATOR BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED IN THE PROCESS, and it is the more important half. scripts/generate-schema-snapshot.mjs shells docker with `shell: true`, which makes Node JOIN argv into one string WITHOUT quoting, so its `SELECT filename FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY filename;` was split on spaces — psql reported `extra command-line argument "filename" ignored`, returned nothing, and the caller read the empty result as "this database records no migrations". The script then wrote a snapshot with an EMPTY migration seed AND PRINTED ITS NORMAL SUCCESS LINE. Every fixture cloned from it would have reported itself un-migrated. Fixed with a shellQuote, and — the part that stops a recurrence — an empty result from a table that EXISTS is now FATAL. The old code had `if (applied.length > 0)` inside a bare catch, so "table absent" and "query broken" produced the same silent success. Same shape as the streaming-cost false alarm: a swallowed failure read as a state. REMAINING: the snapshot is regenerated by hand. Nothing recomputes it in CI, so it will drift again — the guard fails loudly and has evidently been tolerated for weeks. Worth a job that regenerates and opens a PR when the migration set changes.

[api-suite-measured-baseline] THE apps/api SUITE HAS A MEASURED BASELINE FOR THE FIRST TIME, 2026-08-07. 675 test files, 2188 suites, 8004 tests, 11.4 minutes against real Postgres + Redis. AT LEAST TWO TESTS ARE ORDER-DEPENDENT: cernia-ops-store-routes.test.ts and patient-erasure-executor.integration.test.ts were green in the first full run, red in the second, and PASS IN ISOLATION (39/39). CI BLIND SPOT FOUND AND HALF-CLOSED — this stage's own summary was false. It claimed comprehensive-tests.yml "runs unit + integration + Playwright + 3 audit scripts"; it never ran the unit suite of any app. The workflow's only test steps were `pnpm --filter @cernia/testing-real-services test` and `pnpm --filter @cernia/external-fakes test`. NO job ran `pnpm test` (= `pnpm -r test`) or `pnpm --filter @cernia/api test`, so ~570 test files under apps/api/src — INCLUDING THREE SECURITY/COMPLIANCE FORCING FUNCTIONS — were enforced by nothing. PROVEN CONSEQUENCE, not a theoretical one: apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.completeness.test.ts (the ADR-0140 forcing function, whose whole purpose is to block a release when a tenant-scoped table is unclassified) was sitting RED ON MAIN at commit 442931e9 with FOURTEEN unclassified tables, among them scribe_transcripts — a table whose own DDL comment (migration 311) reads "The full visit transcript. PHI — server-side system of record only." PHI survived tenant erasure and the gate that existed to catch exactly that had never been executed by CI. The other two unenforced gates were iam-route-guards.repo-coverage.test.ts and iam-route-guards.scribe-coverage.test.ts. CORRECTION TO THE OBVIOUS DIAGNOSIS (recorded so the next agent does not 'fix' the wrong file): root vitest.config.ts:24 omits `apps/*/src/**` from its `include`, which LOOKS like the cause and is NOT. That config only governs a bare `vitest` run at the repo root, which no script and no workflow invokes — the root `test` script is `pnpm -r test`, which recurses and runs apps/api under ITS OWN vitest.config.ts, and that one does include `src/**/*.test.ts`. Widening the root include would have enforced nothing new while re-running 1000+ app tests under a config lacking apps/api's setupFiles (./vitest.setup.ts) and its 30s/60s timeouts — i.e. it would convert an unused command into a mass-failing one. The include is now commented in place explaining why it stays as it is. FIX SHIPPED (option c — make the gates real today rather than block on a green full suite): new `test:gates` script in apps/api/package.json + new `gates` job "Forcing-function gates (@cernia/api)" in .github/workflows/comprehensive-tests.yml running `pnpm --filter @cernia/api test:gates`. The gates are pure static analysis over migration DDL / route declarations / the cascade constants — NO Postgres, NO build, 4.9s for all five files — so they get a fast standalone job instead of waiting on service containers. THE GATE LIST DEFENDS ITSELF: an explicit file list in a package script has the same rot mode as what it replaced (write a new gate, forget to register it, it runs nowhere, we are back here). So apps/api/src/gate-registration.test.ts enumerates gate-shaped files on disk (`*.completeness.test.ts` / `*-coverage.test.ts`, plus a GATE_EXTRAS list for pre-convention names) and fails naming any file missing from `test:gates`; it also fails on a stale entry naming a file that no longer exists, and it is itself in the list so it runs in the same job. FALSIFIED: dropping an unregistered zz-probe.completeness.test.ts into apps/api/src turned it red with "expected [ 'zz-probe.completeness.test.ts' ] to deeply equal []", then green on removal. VERIFICATION: `pnpm --filter @cernia/api test:gates` → 5 files / 32 tests passed in 4.86s.

CI NEVER BUILT A DEPENDENCY CLOSURE — every step that claimed to was selecting the opposite set. GitHub Actions returned from a multi-day spending-limit pause and four jobs in .github/workflows/comprehensive-tests.yml went red on every PR with TS2307: Cannot find module '@cernia/audit-posture' (also '@cernia/mapping', '@cernia/design-tokens', '@cernia/branding'). ROOT CAUSE 1 — pnpm's `...` is DIRECTIONAL and was written backwards in ten steps across seven workflows. '...pkg' = pkg + its DEPENDENTS; 'pkg...' = pkg + its DEPENDENCIES; '...^pkg' = dependents excluding pkg; 'pkg^...' = dependencies excluding pkg. MEASURED, not assumed: `pnpm --filter '...^@cernia/storage' exec pwd` lists apps/admin, apps/api, apps/cernia-ops and 50+ others, all of which depend ON storage; `pnpm --filter '@cernia/storage^...' exec pwd` lists audit-posture, config, core. So `--filter '...@cernia/api' build` selected Scope: 2 of 331 projects and built NONE of the 116 packages apps/api needs, and `--filter '...^@cernia/testing-real-services' build` selected Scope: 72 of 331 dependents while omitting @cernia/audit-posture, which packages/storage/src/adapter.ts imports in PRODUCTION source. Fixed in comprehensive-tests.yml (4 steps), openapi-diff.yml, owasp-zap-dast.yml, perf-regression.yml, playwright-browser-matrix.yml (2), voice-agent-evals.yml, voice-agent-eval-live.yml. ROOT CAUSE 2, only visible once the filter was right — six packages' tsconfig `references` disagreed with their own package.json dependencies, so a dependent that referenced them compiled THEIR sources with nothing to resolve against: packages/storage was still missing ../audit-posture (so @cernia/connectors, which references ../storage, failed even under the corrected filter — audit-posture was unordered and built in parallel with it), packages/connectors missing ../mapping, packages/server missing ../audit-posture + ../connectors, packages/finops and packages/notifications missing ../storage, packages/voice-agent missing ../speech. apps/* still have reference gaps but are build leaves — nothing references them and pnpm's topological order supplies their deps' dist — so they are flagged, not changed. ROOT CAUSE 3 — the `gates` job added 2026-07-29 had NO build step, and every @cernia/* resolves through dist/, so on a fresh checkout 5 of its 10 gate files never ran at all: vitest died with "Failed to resolve entry for package" on @cernia/rbac, @cernia/server (x2), @cernia/core and @cernia/scribe, taking BOTH ADR-0140 iam-route-guards coverage gates with them, and the job reported that as a single red step rather than as gates that never executed. It now runs `pnpm --filter '@cernia/api^...' build` first; timeout-minutes 10 to 25. REGRESSION GUARD: apps/api/src/ci-build-closure.completeness.test.ts scans .github/workflows and fails naming file+line if the leading-ellipsis form returns; registered in apps/api/package.json `test:gates` so gate-registration.test.ts keeps it there. VERIFICATION from a genuinely clean checkout — RED `pnpm --filter '...^@cernia/testing-real-services' build` reproduced byte-identically to the CI log including "Scope: 72 of 331"; GREEN `pnpm --filter '@cernia/testing-real-services^...' build` = Scope 5 of 331, all Done, then both CIT typechecks clean; GREEN `pnpm --filter '@cernia/api...' build` = 117 projects, apps/api build: Done, exit 0. TRAP RECORDED: *.tsbuildinfo lives NEXT TO tsconfig.json, not under dist/, so `rm -rf dist` alone leaves tsc --build reporting "Done" while emitting nothing — a false green that cost one repro cycle here. PR #770.

THE DRIFT GATE WAS READING A QUARTER OF THE API, AND ITS ONE RED WAS A PHANTOM. With #770/#771 landed, openapi-diff reached its check and reported 25 unrecorded routes plus one UNWAIVED BREAKING removal, GET /scribe/templates. The removal was not real. That route has been served continuously since c6b8ff0a and is registered today at apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts:1850. ROOT CAUSE — the gate's producer, scripts/export-openapi-spec.mjs, walks apps/api/src with a regex requiring `(` to follow the method name directly, so it cannot read any route carrying an explicit TypeScript generic. Commit 59e77ffb (#637) retyped the route from `fastify.get('/scribe/templates', …)` to `fastify.get<{ Querystring: … }>( '/scribe/templates',`; the route did not move, the scanner simply went blind to it, it dropped out of the export, and the diff engine reads 'in baseline, not in candidate' as a deleted endpoint. MEASURED on this commit: the old regex saw 259 route registrations, the fixed one sees 996 — 737 registrations, 74% of the API surface, were invisible to the drift gate, and a breaking change to any of them would have passed silently. TWO REASONS IT STAYED HIDDEN: (a) scripts/export-openapi-spec.test.mjs already carried the U11 regression lock asserting the baseline covers the FULL surface, and NO workflow ran it — it was dead from the day it was written; (b) the gate was not reaching its check at all. FIXED — exporter regex tolerates inline, multi-line and nested generics (scan fn exported as scanRouteSource for direct testing); baseline re-seeded 223 to 871 paths per docs/api-contracts/README.md §3.3; six scanner regression locks + a `baseline.length > 600` floor added; the test is now wired into .github/workflows/openapi-diff.yml BEFORE the export step. PROOF THE GATE CAN FAIL (all three reverted): renaming /scribe/templates gave 'BREAKING — 2 unwaived endpoint change(s)' exit 1; adding a generic to the untyped POST /voice/$verify-ingress gave 'No changes detected' exit 0, i.e. the original bug is dead; adding a scratch GET /voice/$scratch-probe gave 'Added (additive — 1)' exit 0. HONEST COUNT — comparing the real surface at the last baseline refresh (79c5f9a5, 2026-07-12) against HEAD with a working scanner: 113 routes ADDED, 0 removed. The reported '25' was just the subset written without a generic. Recorded in docs/api-changelog/2026-08-03-surface-added-since-july-baseline.md (additive) + 2026-08-03-openapi-scanner-blind-to-typed-routes.md (patch). SIDE FINDING FIXED — /dev/login was published in docs/api/openapi.json, which apps/api/src/openapi-routes.ts serves verbatim and UNAUTHENTICATED at GET /api/openapi.json, so anonymous callers were told a token-minting seam exists; `/dev` added to NON_PUBLIC_PREFIXES and the entry removed from the artifact. Three authorization findings on the newly-visible service seams filed in remaining[]. PR #772.

TWO GATES THAT WERE RED FOR REASONS UNRELATED TO THE CODE UNDER TEST. (1) MIGRATION NUMBERING — not two duplicates but FOUR: 289 (289_erx_refill_fulfillment + 289_provisioning_runs), 290 (290_referrals + 290_scheduled_workflows), 335 (335_invitations_tenant_id_text + 335_scribe_coding_pass_outcome) and 338 (338_llm_audit_reserved_resource + 338_scribe_consent_decision). In each pair the file with NO later dependent moved to the tail — 289→347, 290→348, 335→349, 338→350 — and the survivor stayed put because a later migration ALTERs what it created (297_provisioning_run_context, 306_referral_listing_handle, 337_scribe_coding_pass_backfill) or, for 338, because 339_scribe_audio_destruction implements the path it introduces. In all four pairs the mover also sorted FIRST alphabetically, so the survivor's position in the total order is unchanged. Renaming a shipped migration is NOT free — schema_migrations is keyed by filename, so a rename makes an applied migration look pending (observed: catalog_price_terms recorded as 339_* in one database and 341_* in the repo). packages/storage/src/migrate.ts now carries MIGRATION_RENAMES, an append-only old→new ledger; runMigrations rewrites the schema_migrations row instead of re-running the file, and assertRenameLedgerIsSound fails closed on a malformed entry. PROVEN on real Postgres: a FRESH database migrates 306 files / 292 tables with zero duplicate numbers and all eight movers' and survivors' DDL present; and a database rewound to the OLD filenames re-runs NOTHING (306→306 rows, the one-time relocation in 350 leaves its probe row untouched). RECURRENCE: scripts/check-erasure-classification.mjs — the existing zero-dependency pre-push hook, which already reads the whole migration corpus — gained checkMigrationNumbering (C0), so a duplicate cannot be pushed; migrate.test.ts now reports ALL collisions at once instead of aborting on the first, which is why three of these four were invisible. packages/storage 324/325 → 330/330. (2) OWASP ZAP DAST — the baseline job had NEVER run once since it landed 2026-05-26; every PR died at ~30s in `Initialize containers`. TWO stacked defects. The minio service cannot start under Actions (minio/minio needs `server /data` as its CMD and a services: entry has nowhere to put one); its own comment claimed the container would be "ignored if it fails", which is not a thing Actions does — a failed service container fails the job before checkout. Behind it, unreachable until now: softwaresecurityproject/zap-baseline and -full-scan are NOT published Docker repositories (404 — that namespace is gone); zap-baseline.py is a SCRIPT inside ghcr.io/zaproxy/zaproxy. Both fixed. NOTHING THAT WAS BEING CHECKED STOPPED BEING CHECKED: the minio service never came up in any run, S3_ENDPOINT/MINIO_ENDPOINT were never exported, so apps/api has always booted here on its in-memory object store and a passive HTTP scan is unaffected by the blob backend either way. The gate also stops lying by omission — a run that produces no report now says "SCAN DID NOT RUN — this is not a pass" in the PR comment and names what went unchecked, instead of failing with an empty comment as it had for 70 days. (3) Found in passing: apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.completeness.test.ts is RED on a pristine Windows checkout of main and GREEN in CI — core.autocrlf=true gives scripts/check-erasure-classification.mjs CRLF endings, which vitest's module transform cannot parse, and it reports SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token at the import line rather than at the .mjs. Root-caused to a missing root .gitattributes; `*.mjs text eol=lf` added (same remedy as packages/design-tokens/.gitattributes). apps/api test:gates 66/80-with-a-dead-file → 80/80. Also repaired a coupling the renumber exposed: llm-audit-dangling-correlation.integration.test.ts selected the migration to withhold with startsWith('338_'), which silently stopped matching and made the test claim the one-time relocation was broken; it now selects by the shared LLM_AUDIT_RESERVED_RESOURCE_MIGRATION constant.

ZAP: A THIRD STACKED DEFECT, VISIBLE ONLY BECAUSE THE FIRST TWO WERE FIXED — then GREEN. With the minio service removed and the image corrected, the job reached the scan for the first time in 70 days and died there: `Failed to load config file /zap/wrk/rules.tsv — Level MEDIUM is not a supported level: ['PASS','IGNORE','INFO','WARN','FAIL']`, after which ZAP EXITS WITHOUT SCANNING — no JSON, no HTML — and the summariser correctly returned exit 2. .zap/rules.tsv is a four-column repo format whose second column is a SEVERITY; zap-baseline.py requires an ACTION. It has never been loadable by ZAP, and docs/security/zap-baseline-config.md §1 asserted the opposite ("ZAP itself reads the first two columns") — corrected in place, along with the file's own header. `-c` is no longer passed, and that is the right shape rather than a workaround: .zap/rules.tsv is the SUMMARISER's allowlist and the summariser is the gate, so it needs ZAP to REPORT an allowlisted finding in order to list it under "Allowlisted (suppressed)" with its reviewer-signed reason — a ZAP-side IGNORE would delete it from the JSON before the gate saw it. No row asks for OFF, so nothing that was suppressed stops being suppressed; all five reviewer-signed rows still parse (verified against parseRulesTsv). PLAYWRIGHT E2E — THE RED WAS CONFIGURATION, NOT 3046 ROTTEN TESTS. Three defects, each of which alone made a green run impossible, none of which had ever been observed because the job was gated behind a failing `needs: [backend-integration]` and had literally never executed a spec until PR #770/#771. (1) FOUR FIFTHS OF THE RUN HAD NO BROWSER. tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts declares five projects (chromium-desktop, firefox-desktop, webkit-desktop, edge-desktop, chromium-mobile); the e2e job runs `playwright install --with-deps chromium` and then `playwright test` with no --project filter. MEASURED with --list on a clean worktree: 3046 total, 630 chromium-desktop, 604 firefox-desktop — i.e. ~1812 firefox/webkit/edge tests whose only possible outcome was "Executable doesn't exist". That is the arithmetic behind "Running 3046 tests". Cross-browser is the job of .github/workflows/playwright-browser-matrix.yml, which installs the right binary per matrix entry; .github/branch-protection-README.md already described this check as a "single-project smoke". It now pins --project=chromium-desktop. (2) THE BACKEND WAS NEVER STARTED. 108 of the 147 spec files read E2E_API_BASE (default http://localhost:8080), mint a tenant JWT with POST /dev/login and POST fixtures over HTTP before they touch a page — see tests/e2e/specs/wave-U-mips.spec.ts mintToken()/createReport() for the shape. The job built apps/api and ran its migrations and then never ran it, so every one of those specs died in its fixture helper on ECONNREFUSED. Only 8 specs carry a `test.skip(!process.env['E2E_API_BASE'])` guard; the other 100 fail loudly. Fixed with a "Boot apps/api on :8080" step modelled on perf-regression.yml + owasp-zap-dast.yml, CERNIA_DEV_LOGIN=1, and a PREFLIGHT step that POSTs /dev/login once and fails the shard with one legible line if no token comes back — a 200 from /health only proves something is listening. (3) VISUAL BASELINES ARE WINDOWS-ONLY. Every file under tests/e2e/screenshots/ ends -win32.png (e.g. status-full-chromium-win32.png, and 20 design-*-chromium-desktop-win32.png). Playwright appends the platform from process.platform at compare time, so on ubuntu-latest it looks for -linux.png, finds nothing, and fails all 28 toHaveScreenshot tests no matter what the UI looks like. All 10 call sites already sit inside tests tagged @visual, so the config now folds @visual into every project's grepInvert when CI runs off win32 — QUARANTINE, explicitly counted, with the docker recipe for generating Linux baselines in the config comment. Also quarantined: tests/e2e/specs/onboarding-installer.spec.ts (12 tests), which belongs to tests/e2e/installer.config.ts — it navigates to absolute http://localhost:3212 and only ever ran under the main config because `testDir: './specs'` matches every file in the folder; added to testIgnore. TOTAL DISABLED: 28 visual + 12 installer = 40 of 630 chromium-desktop tests, leaving 620 running as a real gate. STRUCTURE: the job is now a 4-way `--shard` matrix (fail-fast: false, so one shard's red does not hide the others) with a new `e2e-summary` job named exactly "Playwright E2E" so the required check in .github/branch-protection.yml keeps pointing at something. timeout-minutes 30 to 45 per shard — NOT a re-run of the raise-the-budget experiment that was already tried and reverted at 60 minutes (that experiment is what proved the suite was red rather than slow); ~14 of the old job's 30 minutes went to install + three builds before the first spec ran, and sharding duplicates that fixed cost into each shard instead of dividing it.

(a) THE ADMIN SHELL BECAME AUTH-GATED AND ~51 TESTS NEVER NOTICED. apps/admin/src/lib/auth-session.ts redirects a visitor with no `cernia.token` to the public web hub, so an unauthenticated `/` renders no <aside> at all. New tests/e2e/fixtures/admin-session.ts seeds the chrome-level session and says in its own header why a signature-less JWT is right for a rendering guard and wrong for anything that touches the API. (b) /dev/login GRANTS THE PRODUCTS THE PAYWALL TEST ASSERTS ARE ABSENT. entitlement-gating.spec.ts asserts PATCH /api/voice-agent/policy -> 402 for an unentitled tenant and its header claimed the tenant "never has a phone-agent grant"; measured 200, and product_entitlements showed five active rows created by the login itself. Verified on a live api: default login now writes 33 rows, grantProducts:false writes 0. Dev-only, behind isDevLoginEnabled(). (c) TESTS ASSERTING A UI THAT WAS DELETED. login.spec.ts (7) and two accessibility.spec.ts tests target the v1 paste-a-bearer-token form — input#token, label[for=token] reading "Bearer token". /login is now the real credential form (label[for=tenantId|email|password]) covered by auth-login.spec.ts. (d) BRAND AND MARKUP DRIFT. status/theme asserted a "FHIR" badge (the brand badge now reads "Health"), the literal class `border-r` (@cernia/ui SidebarShell uses the LOGICAL `border-e` so RTL works — asserting the physical property would now be asserting an RTL bug), and title "Cernia Admin" while a metadata export shipped and made it "Platform Status | Cernia Health Admin". One of those tests contained the sentence "If a metadata export is added ... this test should be updated"; it was added and nobody came back. (e) A REQUIRED FIELD THE FIXTURES NEVER SENT. wizard-orchestrator.ts made primaryAdminPhone mandatory (E.164, the admin's own mobile for SMS-OTP, distinct from the facility number); onboarding-complete-flow, phone-number-selection and number-port-in 422'd on every run. Five tests, one field. (f) TWO PLAIN TEST BUGS, one of which the compiler had already reported: schedule-import called page.setInputFiles(LOCATOR, ...) where the API takes a selector string — it is one of the standing `tsc --noEmit` errors under tests/e2e, and neither the spec nor the typecheck was gated, so both signals sat there; and multi-tenant-isolation read page.content() while the auth guard was navigating away ("Unable to retrieve content because the page is navigating"), now a plain HTTP GET, which is the stricter check anyway since PHI would leak from the wire. Its sibling assertion was rewritten to test the INVARIANT (no admin shell for an unauthenticated visitor) instead of the mechanism (a redirect to /login that no longer happens). RESULT: 485 collected, 450 pass, 22 skip, 3.5 min at 4 workers, against a live apps/api + built admin on a fresh database. Everything still disabled is counted in remaining[] and annotated at its own call site. CI worker count also corrected: `workers: "50%"` resolves to ONE on a 2-core runner (that is the "using 1 worker" in the log, and why shard 2 was still mid-suite at its 45-minute deadline); pinned to 2, with the line reporter added so a CI failure is legible as text rather than as a wall of F and T.

PLAYWRIGHT E2E, PART 3 — THE E2E ADMIN PORT IS NOT IN apps/api's CORS ALLOWLIST, AND A LOCAL ENV VAR HID IT. With the API booted and the specs fixed, the first real CI run still reported 36 failures in shard 1 alone — every one a UI assertion, every one "element(s) not found", while the API-only assertions in the very same files passed. The failure's own DOM snapshot gave it away: "Failed to load framework / Failed to fetch". That is a browser network refusal, not a missing element. ROOT CAUSE: packages/config/src/defaults.ts corsOriginsDefault allows localhost and 127.0.0.1 on ports 3000-3006. tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts boots the admin app on :3210 (chosen precisely to avoid colliding with a dev server on :3000). So every BROWSER-side fetch from a spec's page to apps/api is refused at preflight, while the same spec's node-side `request` fixture — which performs no preflight — sails through. That splits the suite exactly in half along the line the CI log showed. FALSIFIED BOTH WAYS on one build: with the 3000-3006 default, `OPTIONS /compliance/frameworks` with `Origin: http://localhost:3210` returns NO access-control-allow-origin header and compliance-flow is 6/6 RED; with CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3210 the preflight answers `access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:3210` and it is 6/6 GREEN. Fixed by setting CORS_ORIGINS on the e2e job. NOT '*' — packages/server forces credentials:false on a wildcard origin, which changes auth behaviour under test. HOW IT WAS NEARLY MISSED, recorded because the next agent will hit it: every local run up to this point had CORS_ORIGINS='*' exported into the shell, so the whole UI half of the suite was GREEN locally and RED in CI for a reason invisible in the diff. A local green obtained under an env var CI does not set is not a green. The proof that mattered was re-running with the CI allowlist and watching it go red. FINAL MEASURED BASELINE under CI-equivalent CORS: 477 collected, 449 pass, 22 skip, 6 fail — and all six failures are @visual tests, which are excluded on non-win32 CI because their baselines are -win32.png. 3.0 minutes at 4 workers.

The whole f5 suspend lifecycle is registered, wired to Postgres, and reachable by nobody. This is NOT a regression: they had been dead the whole time, invisible because they were registered through a dynamic app.route({method,url}) loop that the deriveOperation repo-coverage gate's static scan could not read. Making them literal is what let the gate see them, and they are recorded in ACCEPTED_UNMAPPED (apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.repo-coverage.test.ts) with that reasoning. The un-mapping is CORRECT as far as it goes — `tenantId` is a path param, so these are cross-tenant by construction and a canonical-verb mapping would reach a tenant admin through *:admin. The gap is the MISSING OPERATOR PATH, exactly the shape J11-F3 had for GET /api/o6/audit: either move the family under /cernia-ops/* (an API-contract change; they are now in docs/api-contracts/openapi-baseline.json) or give the global hook a platform-operator branch for a named non-/cernia-ops allowlist. [ambient-scribe-defect-register] Ambient scribe defect register — CLOSED 2026-08-05, and all three named residuals were REGISTER faults rather than code. D34, D20 and D43 were each verified fixed IN CODE with their own green suites (packages/speech batch-transcriber 24/24 incl. the empty/whitespace/ wrong-value control; apps/admin scribe-templates-view 47/47 with the loaded section spread first so a field the editor cannot render is carried, not dropped; o1-llm-gateway routing-cost-baa 8/8). WHY THEY READ AS OPEN — two mechanical faults in the document, both HIDING fixes rather than inventing them: (a) the §"proposed findings" table declared FIVE columns while sixteen of its rows carried SEVEN, and markdown renders only the header's width, so the Status, Fix and Proof cells of those rows WERE NOT RENDERED AT ALL — D34 and D43 showed "🔴 open" while their own rows carried "🟢 fixed (PR #712 / #714)"; the widths were broken in the first place by bare pipes inside code spans (a TS union `a | b` reads as a column break unless escaped). (b) D21, D22, D31 and D48 recorded their fixes with ✅, a marker outside the document's own declared status key, so every count anchored on 🟢 read them as open. Re-derived after repair: 47 distinct defects, 47 carrying a green marker, ZERO open — against a headline that had said "33 registered · 13 fixed · 20 open". Both classes are now gated in scripts/check-test-plan-consistency.mjs (checkTableShape + checkStatusMarkers), which reports 34 problems against the pre-repair document and none against the repaired one. The repair was proven lossless by comparing the multiset of defect-row cell contents before and after.

[ambient-scribe-j06-backfill] Ambient scribe / J06 backfill residual — MEASURED 2026-08-05 and there is no residue to find. The live read path was already fixed (see history): with migration 340's log present, a hand-removed entitlement row makes logIsConsistent reject the log and wasEntitledDuring answer "unknown" → "indeterminate", not "skipped-not-entitled". WHAT WAS LEFT was a DATA residue: rows migration 337 arm 2 already stamped on a database that ran it. Surveyed across every database carrying scribe data: scribe_w2_live has ZERO skipped-not-entitled rows; scribe_f18 has 32, and ZERO of them are contradictory (none has coding suggestions), so every one is consistent with a tenant that genuinely did not buy coding rather than with a mis-stamp. The stamping source is NOT recoverable from the row — 337 and $draft write the same value with no provenance column — so "no contradictory row" is the strongest statement available here, and it is the one that matters: the harmful arm is the contradictory one. Nothing to repair.

[perpatient-erasure-ambiguous-tables] PER-PATIENT ERASURE — THE AMBIGUOUS TABLES ARE NOW ENUMERATED (2026-08-06); what is left is 17 RULINGS, not a discovery. THE FINDING THAT UNBLOCKED THIS: the "14" were named NOWHERE — not in ADR 0155, not in patient-erasure-classification.ts, not in any test. The COUNT existed and the LIST did not, so "classify the 14" was never a hard task; it was an UNSTARTABLE one, and it sat here for two days looking like a decision problem. A number is not a worklist. Re-deriving mechanically does not reproduce 14 either: the only rule statable from the schema — in ADR_0140_CASCADE, not already classified, has >=1 JSON/JSONB column — yields 62. The original 14 was a human judgement about which payloads could plausibly carry patient data, and that judgement was never recorded. SHIPPED: apps/api/src/patient-erasure-ambiguous.ts enumerates all 62 with their JSON columns, tiered — 16 needs-ruling (a patient reference is PLAUSIBLE) and 46 no-patient-dimension (configuration, schema, policy, platform metadata) — each with the reason, including the negatives, because "we looked and the answer was no" is a finding and an empty list is not. It is a WORKLIST, NOT A CLASSIFICATION: the executor does not read it and a test asserts it never will, because an unanswered question consumed by the executor becomes a silent decision. THE LIST CANNOT GO STALE THE WAY "14" DID: patient-erasure-ambiguous.test.ts RE-DERIVES the candidate set on every run from the cascade + the classification + the committed schema snapshot and demands an exact match, so adding a cascade table with a JSONB column fails the build until someone tiers it. That is the forcing function ADR 0155 never had. CURRENT INVENTORY (2026-10-09): 66 JSON-payload candidates, 17 needs-ruling and 49 no-patient-dimension; auth_transient_state joins the open rulings because its ciphertext may hold a patient principal. THE 17 NEEDING A RULING, and the shortlist is the deliverable: event_outbox (undelivered domain events that name a patient), llm_traces + llm_trace_spans (the record of what was SENT to a provider), agent_memory_entries (an EMBEDDING derived from patient text — no string predicate will ever match it), support_tickets + support_ticket_comments (free text a human typed), schedule_import_jobs (the ERROR LOG echoes the rejected row, so a failed import KEEPS the patient name), bulk_export_jobs (the manifest may be a patient index), alerts + alert_in_app_feed + alert_dead_letters (dead-letter tables outlive their sources BY DESIGN, which makes them the likeliest place for a reference to survive an erasure), scheduled_workflows + workflow_drafts, report_definitions (a saved per-patient filter outlives the run), and migration_jobs + sync_runs (probably counts, but "probably" is what this removes). ALSO SURFACED BY THE DERIVATION: the committed schema snapshot is BEHIND the migrations — usage_cost_allocation (363) is in the cascade and absent from the snapshot. Pinned as a named exception rather than tolerated, so the next drift fails instead of silently widening. STILL TRUE, unchanged: a per-patient erasure is complete over what the platform can SEE, which is not the same as complete. Nothing here is classified and nothing is deleted.

THE PUNCH LIST CAN NO LONGER SILENTLY GO STALE, AND THE SCRIBE TEST PLAN CAN NO LONGER CONTRADICT ITSELF. (a) FORCING FUNCTION — scripts/check-status-freshness.mjs, wired into pre-push by scripts/install-hooks.mjs beside the ADR-0140 gate (NOT CI: Actions is failing on an account billing problem, so a CI-only gate would be inert on arrival). R5-F4 DIAGNOSED AND CLOSED AS NOT A PRODUCT DEFECT. "One load in FIVE of /admin/scribe/templates renders zero rows" is next dev's COLD ROUTE COMPILE racing a fixed-offset probe read. The experiment run 5 named was run verbatim (tests/e2e/w5-templates-load-probe.mjs): the original probe shape is preserved (domcontentloaded + a flat 3500ms + read, because a probe that waits for the row can never observe the phenomenon) and every load is ATTRIBUTED from its network trace — product-race requires the API response to have ARRIVED, CARRIED rows, and the DOM to still be empty a settle window later. RESULTS, 35 loads, four arms: next start 20/20 ok, API answering in 16-60ms; next dev, THREE cold starts x 5 loads, reproduced the exact run5 signature (rowPresent:false, keys:[], rows=0) on LOAD 1 in 2 of 3 runs — and in both the API call was NEVER ISSUED by the read (document itself did not arrive for 17.9s / 19.3s), which is stronger than latency: no component had mounted, so no response was being withheld. Cold run 3 is the discriminator — same code, same fixture, same minute — compile finished 18.0s, request 19.9s, response 20.2s, read 22.1s came AFTER, and it rendered. product-race classifications: 0 of 35. NO CODE WAS CHANGED: a speculative retry or loading-state change would have gone green while masking a real client-side race if one ever appeared, and apps/admin/src/lib/scribe-api.ts + scribe-degradation.ts are untouched. Residual stated: this machine compiled in ~19s vs run 5's 38.6s, which changes the magnitude, not the mechanism. Evidence w5-load-probe-start.json + w5-load-probe-dev.json + w5-load-probe-dev-cold{1,2,3}.json + w5-scribe-admin-ui-report.md §2. TWO STACK HAZARDS RECORDED THERE: (i) next dev and next start SHARE apps/admin/.next, so run side by side the production server answers 200 with a BLANK BODY — indistinguishable in a results file from the defect being investigated, and it produced a false 20-of-20-empty first pass; (ii) a path-only network filter matches BOTH <admin>/admin/scribe/templates and <api>/scribe/templates, which timed the HTML document and would have attributed a 19s page compile to a 20ms API.

D20 CONSEQUENCE (b) FIXED — the template editor no longer discards fields it cannot render. toApiSections rebuilt each section from a FIXED literal, so anything not in that literal was dropped on save into note_template_versions (a versioned, audit-snapshotted clinical artifact); `key` was merely the only such field in 2026-08, so D20's fix closed the measured harm and not the shape of it. apps/admin/src/app/admin/scribe/templates/scribe-templates-view.tsx: EditorSection gains source?: NoteTemplateSection (the section EXACTLY as loaded), toEditorSection carries it, and toApiSections spreads it FIRST and writes only the editor-owned fields over it — an editor that cannot show you a field has no business deleting it. A section the editor CREATED has no source and gains nothing spurious. EDITOR_OWNED_SECTION_FIELDS is exported and `satisfies readonly (keyof NoteTemplateSection)[]`, so the ownership boundary is readable and a new field must be added there deliberately before the editor starts writing it. The `delete section.required` is load-bearing now that the source is spread: without it, un-ticking the box on a section that arrived required:true would leave the spread's true in place and the control would silently do nothing. FOUR new cases in scribe-templates-view.test.tsx, all RED on github/main 38f4930c ("section field \"x-cernia-future-hint\" was dropped on save"), and written to fail on a field THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET: the fixture is typed Required<NoteTemplateSection> & Record<string, unknown> so the COMPILER demands a value for every declared field, and the assertion iterates Object.keys(fixture) rather than naming fields — add a field to the interface and the fixture stops typechecking until it is added, then the round-trip goes red unless it is preserved. An extra x-cernia-* member stands in for a field the type does not declare at all. Baselines by checking main's file out over the working copy, never git stash (refs/stash is repo-global across sibling worktrees). See w5-scribe-admin-ui-report.md §3.

Reconciled the scribe defect register against the code, and closed the two mechanical faults that had been hiding fixes. Asked to fix D34, D20 and D43, all three turned out to be already fixed in code and green; what was broken was the document. Repairs, in order of blast radius: bare pipes inside code spans escaped (6 rows) so cells stop splitting; short rows padded (9); the §"proposed findings" header widened from 5 to the 7-column schema §0.1 already uses, with its 5- and 6-cell rows remapped losslessly (11) — before this, sixteen rows rendered NOTHING past their fifth cell, which is precisely where Status/Fix/Proof live; D34 and D43 status cells flipped to 🟢 with their PR references; and the ✅ markers on D21, D22, D31 and D48 normalised onto the declared key. The register headline is re-derived from the rows: 47 registered · 47 fixed · 0 open (was 33 · 13 · 20). Losslessness was PROVEN, not asserted — the multiset of defect-row cell contents is identical before and after, the only delta being three pairs of fragments rejoined into the single cells they were always meant to be. Also struck a bullet that had itself gone stale: the "process gap" item claimed no forcing function existed for the status write and that §0.2 still read "not started"; scripts/check-status-freshness.mjs exists and §0.2 now reads "18 of 18 families run, 199/204" and is regenerable with --fix.

J06 backfill data residue measured, not assumed: zero contradictory rows across every database carrying scribe data. The 32 skipped-not-entitled rows in scribe_f18 all lack coding suggestions, so each is consistent with a tenant that did not buy coding rather than with a 337 mis-stamp. Recorded honestly: the stamping SOURCE is unrecoverable from the row (337 and $draft write the same value, no provenance column), so "no contradictory row" is the strongest available statement — and it is the one that matters, because the contradictory arm is the harmful one.

D20 residual bullet REMOVED as stale — measured, not assumed. It claimed apps/admin/src/app/admin/scribe/templates/scribe-templates-view.tsx "rebuilds each section from a FIXED field set (toEditorSection / toApiSections), so a future NoteTemplateSection field would still be silently dropped on edit". That is a description of the code this bullet outlived. toApiSections now spreads the loaded section FIRST — literally "...(s.source ?? {})" at scribe-templates-view.tsx:265 — and writes over it only the names in EDITOR_OWNED_SECTION_FIELDS, a const list tied to the type by "satisfies readonly (keyof NoteTemplateSection)[]" so a name that is not a section field stops compiling. EditorSection.source deliberately holds the WHOLE loaded object rather than a pre-filtered unknown-fields bag, and the code says why: filtering would need a list of known fields maintained in a SECOND place, and the field that gets forgotten in the second place is exactly the field the rule exists to protect. A section the editor CREATED has no source and so gains nothing spurious, and the explicit "delete" of the "required" key is load-bearing once the source is spread — without it, un-ticking the box on a section that arrived required:true would leave the spread true in place. So the SHAPE of the harm is closed, not merely the one measured instance ("key") that made D20 read as a one-field bug. Gated by apps/admin scribe-templates-view tests (47/47). Nothing to do; the bullet was describing its own replacement.

DEFECT REGISTER IS NOW COUNTABLE FROM ITSELF — the bullet asking for exactly this is closed, and it asked for the right thing. It said: "the register is not machine-readable and any count transcribed from it drifts. Re-derive by hand, or make the status column parseable, before quoting a number again." Made parseable. THE DERIVED ANSWER, which nobody has to type again: 61 rows across 4 defect tables, 48 UNIQUE defect ids, 48 fixed, 0 open, 0 conflicts. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, which is not quite what the bullet guessed: it described markers that "lead the cell" versus markers "mid-cell inside bold". The measured faults were (a) two of the four defect tables had NO Status column at all, so their sixteen rows could not be counted by any rule, and (b) ten rows in the F7/F17 table carried an em-dash in Status while their marker sat in Found-by or Proof. Every one of those ten did carry exactly one marker somewhere, so nothing was hiding an OPEN defect — checked before assuming, because "all green" would otherwise have been an assumption. THE TOOL: scripts/scribe-defect-register.mjs reads every defect table (first column id, at least one bare D-number row) and requires each Status cell to BEGIN with exactly one marker from the key. It rejects ambiguity rather than resolving it — two different markers in a cell is a failure, not a first-wins guess — and treats disagreement between tables about one id as a failure too. It deliberately does NOT read the check-mark as a status: that mark means an evidence CHANNEL closed, a claim about proof rather than about the defect, and one row read "CHANNEL CLOSED ... consequence (b) is NOT closed", which a tick-counting parse would have scored as done. Wired as pnpm check:defect-register + a CI step, gated by scripts/scribe-defect-register.test.mjs (15 tests, node --test) with a firing case AND a silent case for every check, plus two controls that mutating the REAL document turns the gate red — without them "0 problems" would also be what a parser finding no tables reports. ONE FINDING WAS MY OWN PARSER: its first version split on every pipe and "discovered" rows carrying 10 columns under a 7-column header. That was wrong — the escape is correct markdown and the document uses it correctly. The rule is recorded in the file so the convincing wrong version is not rediscovered. FOUND AND FIXED IN PASSING: scripts/check-test-plan-consistency.test.mjs was RED on main — its own synthetic fixture quoted "4 | 0 | not started" with bare pipes inside backticks, making that row 8 cells under a 6-column header, so the sibling gate correctly fired on the test fixture and the test failed asserting silence. A gate test breaking the rule its gate enforces. Escaped; 28/28 now. ALSO corrected in the document: D20 row still ended "consequence (b) ... is NOT closed", which measurement showed false (toApiSections spreads the loaded section first).

RENDER HALF CLOSED. The loader half carried the API's {error} code; nothing guaranteed a SCREEN turned it into something a clinician could act on, and answering that per surface would have produced N wordings for one condition. So: one map (apps/admin/src/lib/scribe-error-sentences.ts), 75 codes, and a gate that DERIVES the vocabulary instead of listing it — scribe-error-sentences.gate.test.ts scrapes apps/api/src/scribe-*.ts for error: literals AND every literal inside each errorCodeOf(...) call in scribe-api.ts. A refusal shipped without wording now fails the build. The gate also asserts the sentences are usable: none may contain its own code, an HTTP status, or be under 30 characters, and every not-configured code must name an ADMIN, because a clinician told only "not configured" retries forever. THE GATE CAUGHT TWO OF MY OWN ERRORS, which is the argument for deriving rather than listing. (a) An orphan check found brand-new-spelling in the map and not in the API: it is a FICTIONAL code invented inside a drift-gate test fixture, swept in because my first enumeration grepped scribe-*.ts including test files. (b) Reading only the first literal per errorCodeOf(...) call missed 25 codes living in ternary ARMS. THE RESOLVER ORDERING WAS ALSO WRONG FIRST, and a pre-existing test caught it: preferring the mapped sentence whenever a code was present DISCARDED server detail no generic wording carries — the coding-accept refusal arrives naming the actual ICD code ("...not supported by the note: I10..."). Order is now server message, then map, then fallback, with the client's own "... (NNN)" placeholder detected by shape so it loses to the map. Six views rewired to use the mapper as their FALLBACK, keeping site-specific arms (no-active-facility, template-version-conflict) that add context a generic sentence cannot. apps/admin 561/561, tsc clean.

PER-PATIENT ERASURE EXECUTOR BUILT AND ARMED (founder, 2026-08-06 — all three compliance decisions taken, plus an explicit build-and-arm over the dry-run option I recommended). (1) eRx / fax / financial are RETAINED and REPORTED with their authority (21 CFR 1311.305, 45 CFR 164.528, tax/invoice integrity) — ADR 0140 classified all three ERASE on a TENANT-TERMINATION argument that does not transfer to one patient, because the practice still exists and is still bound. Encoded as data in apps/api/src/patient-erasure-policy.ts with a sentence per family the requester can be shown verbatim, and reported EVEN AT ZERO ROWS — a retention nobody is told about is indistinguishable from an oversight. (2) A legal hold naming the patient REFUSES the request outright: nothing deleted, hold id and reason returned, HTTP 409 (the operator is authorised; the DATA is not erasable). This also closes the flagged-but-untracked gap that tenant-erasure-worker.ts consults legal_holds NOWHERE. (3) ARMED — applyPatientErasure executes for real and no env var quietly turns it into a no-op, because a destructive function that pretends to be destructive is worse than either honest option. The safety is STRUCTURAL: planPatientErasure is side-effect-free and is the whole answer to "what would this do" (every number a real COUNT(*) against the delete predicate); apply takes a PLAN, not a patient, so it cannot resolve; the route re-plans SERVER-SIDE so a client can never supply the resolved id sets (that would be handing the executor a list of rows to destroy); execute requires {"confirm": true}; and it is operator-only on /cernia-ops/*, matching the same 2026-08-06 decision that DECLINED admin:tenants:erase for tenant roles. THE ORDERING RULE IS NOW A PROPERTY OF THE TYPE, not of anyone's memory: resolve everything first, delete nothing until every id set is in hand. ADR 0155 warned that reusing the tenant cascade order deletes parents first and the second half then "deletes ZERO ROWS WHILE REPORTING SUCCESS". Asserted directly: resource_versions — whose only route to a patient runs through resources, deleted in the same run — is gone afterwards AND its reported count is non-zero. Both halves, because either alone is satisfied by a broken executor. A REAL DEFECT THE TESTS CAUGHT: tableExists was to_regclass('public.' || table), so under any schema not literally named public EVERY table read as absent — the executor would find nothing to erase, report a clean run, and delete none of the patient's data. Silent, and it looks exactly like a patient with no records. Now unqualified, resolving through search_path. The `resources` link columns are DISCOVERED from the live catalogue rather than computed from a naming rule (001 declares 13 generated columns, later migrations reach ~58; a computed name that does not exist is a crash mid-erasure, in the one operation where partial failure is worst), and the coverage HOLES are named in every response. 15/15 real-PG tests incl. cross-tenant and cross-patient blast-radius controls. ALSO MEASURED WHILE BUILDING: fax_transmissions has NO patient column — it is INDIRECT via referral_tasks.id, so any plan that assumed a direct predicate on it was wrong. ADR 0155 amended; routes at GET/POST /cernia-ops/platform/patient-erasure/{plan,execute}. NOT RUN AGAINST ANY DATA — there is no live environment in this repo — and the TENANT-level CERNIA_ERASURE_EXECUTE remains unarmed and untouched.

The "14 ambiguous erasure tables" turned out to be a COUNT WITHOUT A LIST — named in no ADR, no module and no test — which is why the task never started rather than never finished. Mechanical re-derivation yields 62, not 14, so the original number encoded an unrecorded human judgement. apps/api/src/patient-erasure-ambiguous.ts now enumerates all 62 with JSON columns and a per-table reason, tiered 16 needs-ruling / 46 no-patient-dimension, and patient-erasure-ambiguous.test.ts re-derives the set from the cascade + classification + schema snapshot on every run so it cannot drift. A test also asserts the executor never imports it — a worklist consumed as a classification turns an open question into a silent decision. Side finding: the schema snapshot is behind migration 363 (usage_cost_allocation), pinned as a named exception.

Schema snapshot regenerated and — the larger find — TEMPLATE INVALIDATION FIXED. The snapshot lagged by THREE migrations (362, 363, 364), not the one the drift gate named; 297 to 298 tables, every hunk in the diff attributed to a migration, zero delta on functions/triggers/sequences/ GENERATED columns. But regenerating the file alone would have changed NOTHING for any test on any machine: ensureMigratedTemplate() built cernia_test_template only if a database of that NAME was absent, with no freshness check, so a box that had ever built one never rebuilt. The template on this box held 315 seeded migrations — stale against even the OLD committed snapshot of 316 — and every suite cloning it was testing a schema matching no artifact in the repo, with nothing red because nothing compared them. FIX: the template is now named for the snapshot CONTENT HASH (cernia_test_template_<sha8>), so the existence check that already ran IS the freshness check — no hash to compare, no staleness to detect, nothing for a human to drop on their own machine or in CI. Superseded templates are swept best-effort, because a drop that fails while another worker is cloning must never fail a test run during CLEANUP. packages/testing-real-services/src/postgres-fixture.ts, 33/33. Also: the migration-drift-guard test WAS ALREADY RED (316 seeded vs 319 on disk) and now passes. NOTE the fixture billing semantics changed with migration 364 — four product_usage_pricing rows flipped seeded-default to operator-set, so snapshot-cloning tests now see them as BILLABLE; checked, no current test depends on the old value.

current.summary: 4 of 5 bullets shipped; 1 remains. The ADR/code authority split this stage flagged is resolved: ADR-0140 now carries the thirteen 2026-07-29 Scoped-IN entries plus billing_meter_report_watermarks with their per-table justifications, two non-existent table names in the retain table are corrected to the real ones, and the direct contradiction between the ADR ("the code is the operative list") and erasure-cascade.ts ("the AUTHORITY is the ADR") is settled in favour of code-operative / ADR-as-rationale-of-record, in both files. The 2026-07-29 batch is now proven to REMOVE SEEDED ROWS rather than to be valid SQL against a missing table. What remains is the arming decision itself.

remaining: [unchanged-20260806-perpatient-work] UNCHANGED BY THE 2026-08-06 PER-PATIENT WORK, and worth saying because the two are easy to confuse: the per-patient executor shipped ARMED that day, on its own operator-only routes, and it does not read this flag. CERNIA_ERASURE_EXECUTE remains UNARMED (single gate, apps/api/src/index.ts:6469, itself behind a positive CERNIA_ERASURE_INTERVAL_MS; no .env, deploy manifest, compose file or workflow sets it). The ADR-amendment precondition recorded here is DISCHARGED as of 2026-08-03 — the code no longer runs ahead of its own stated authority. Two things stand between here and arming, and neither is a code change: (a) prod-tenant-lifecycle remaining[] still carries the erase-vs-retain sign-off on the two genuine retain candidates (eRx under DEA/EPCS, fax_transmissions under HIPAA §164.528) — the argument for ERASE is now written at the entries in erasure-cascade.ts, but it is an engineering argument, not a compliance opinion; (b) arming a destructive irreversible cascade in production is an operator decision with a runbook and a rollback story, and belongs to a human. AMENDED 2026-08-04 (ADR 0155) — arming is UNCHANGED and still belongs to a human, but its SCOPE is now stated explicitly so nobody reads the per-patient work as having widened it: CERNIA_ERASURE_EXECUTE arms the TENANT-AGGREGATE cascade ONLY. ADR 0155 adds a per-patient erasure DESIGN and a machine-checked classification (apps/api/src/patient-erasure-classification.ts) and NO EXECUTOR — so nothing new becomes destructive when this flag is armed, and arming it does NOT give a patient a right-to-erasure path. When a per-patient executor is built it will need its OWN separate arming decision, its own runbook and its own rollback story; it must NOT be folded behind this flag, because the two instruments have different gates (the tenant retention floor is structurally inapplicable per-patient — a patient has no offboarding anchor) and different blast radii. THE PRE-ARMING FINDING RECORDED HERE IS CLOSED 2026-08-06. It said apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.ts never consults legal_holds while apps/api/src/cernia-ops-patient-erasure-routes.ts does, and that the "arguably covered by the retention floor" defence was an argument nobody had written down. The gate was built instead of the argument: computeHold now counts ACTIVE (released_at IS NULL) holds FIRST, ahead of both clocks, and returns the new ErasureHoldReason values legal-hold / legal-hold-unreadable. THREE DECISIONS ARE LOAD-BEARING. (1) ANY hold blocks, regardless of scope — a tenant-aggregate erasure destroys whatever a hold names however narrow it is, so scope-matching (isEventOnHold, which is the right question for ONE audit event) could only ever produce a false negative that deletes held data. (2) The registry is read DIRECTLY off opts.db rather than injected like every other dependency here, because a seam needs a default and "skip" leaves the bug reachable by omission — which is exactly how it survived this long. There is now no way to construct a worker that erases without asking. (3) UNREADABLE IS NOT ZERO: a throw means the registry could not answer, which is what a missing table, a permission failure or a dead connection all return, and none of them are evidence that no hold exists — so it HOLDS, under its own reason, because an operator reading a held job must be able to tell "a hold exists" from "the hold registry is broken". Same absent-vs-unknown rule the scribe audio probe already turns on. Gated by 7 new tests in tenant-erasure-worker.integration.test.ts (20/20 green on real Postgres), including a POSITIVE CONTROL that the identical job is DUE with no hold — without it the hold assertions would pass on a job held for an unrelated reason — plus a released hold and another tenant's hold that must NOT block, and an ARMED run proving rows survive rather than only that a reason was reported. Falsified by disabling the gate: 4 of the 7 fail, and the 3 that stay green are exactly the ones asserting the gate does nothing. WHAT REMAINS, and it is a property of resumable destruction rather than an oversight: like every other gate here, the check is skipped for in-flight `erasing` resumes, which are past the point of no return (re-holding a half-deleted tenant would strand it). A hold placed AFTER a job begins erasing does not stop it. Closing that needs a re-check inside the cascade loop, which is a larger change than this gate.

PHI SURVIVED TENANT ERASURE — FIXED. The ADR-0140 cascade (apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts) left FOURTEEN tenant-scoped tables classified neither for deletion nor for the retain-set, so a right-to-erasure run completed while leaving them intact. Seven of the fourteen carry clinical content: scribe_transcripts (migration 311 — "The full visit transcript. PHI — server-side system of record only"), scribe_transcript_words (per-word timings whose `text` reconstructs the transcript verbatim), scribe_live_transcripts (per-chunk in-visit snippets), scribe_after_visit_summaries, scribe_edit_diffs (before_text/after_text ARE the clinical note body), scribe_coding_suggestions (clinical rationale) and scribe_proposed_actions (payload + a verbatim transcript quote in source_span). CLASSIFICATION — 13 Scoped-IN (delete-all on tenant_id), 1 Scoped-OUT. Every one of the thirteen carries tenant_id DIRECTLY (it leads the PK on all of them), so none needs a join through scribe_sessions and all are plain delete-all; they are deliberately NOT flagged afterObjectPurge, because buildScribeAudioEraser (apps/api/src/scribe-retention-sweep.ts:121) enumerates ONLY scribe_sessions, so nothing new gates the object purge and the existing "exactly four deferred tables" assertion in erasure-cascade.test.ts still holds. The seven PHI tables above, plus: scribe_vocabulary, scribe_template_defaults and note_template_versions (tenant configuration, no retention obligation); scribe_coaching_events (non-PHI engagement telemetry); voice_cutover_state (migration 308 — routing flag, no PHI, same class as tenant_record_mode / tenant_isolation_mode which are already Scoped-IN); and event_outbox (migration 309 — a drain-and-discard DELIVERY QUEUE, not an audit anchor: it MIRRORS rbac_audit_events rows, and rbac_audit_events is itself retained, so the 6-year audit obligation is discharged by the original while the PHI-bearing copy goes). ON scribe_vocabulary specifically: migration 317 asserts "NOT PHI", but it is admin-typed free text and the migration's own description lists "clinician names" as expected content, so a tenant can put a person's name in it. Nothing turns on resolving that — it is tenant configuration with no retention obligation, so it is Scoped-IN whether or not any individual term is PHI, which is the only classification safe under both readings. THE ONE RETAIN-SET ADDITION, billing_meter_report_watermarks (migration 332, added the same day by PR #675), is deliberate and is NOT the retain-set being used as a dumping ground: it is PHI-free by construction (tenant id, period string, metric name, two integers) and it is retained as the INTEGRITY GUARD on records that are themselves retained. runMeteredFlushSweep still VISITS an erased tenant, because enumerateBillableTenants (apps/api/src/saas-subscription-store.ts:165) reads saas_subscriptions — in the retain-set — and the aggregate reads usage_rollups, also in the retain-set. Delete the watermark and the next nightly claim sees reported_total = 0 and re-reports the whole period's cumulative total to a formula=sum Stripe meter: precisely the ~15.5x double-report defect migration 332 was written to close, now aimed at a tenant who no longer exists to dispute the invoice. Its inputs outlive the tenant, so it must too. PROOF: the forcing function was watched RED FIRST at github/main 442931e9 ("expected [ …(14) ] to deeply equal []", listing all fourteen), then GREEN after classification. FALSIFIED: a scratch tenant-scoped table added to packages/storage/src/migrations turned it red naming zzz_scratch_falsify_probe, then green on removal — the gate genuinely detects a NEW omission. The cascade was then executed END TO END against real migrated Postgres (apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.integration.test.ts 8/8, including the armed "erases in-scope, preserves Scoped-OUT + sibling tenant" case), proving all eleven new DELETEs are valid SQL against the real schema rather than only well-formed constants. ADR-0140 amended, and the 2026-07-29 batch proven to actually delete. (1) THE ADR. docs/architecture/adrs/0140-right-to-erasure-scope.md gained the thirteen Scoped-IN rows from the 2026-07-29 classification (the seven PHI-bearing scribe tables, scribe_vocabulary / scribe_template_defaults / scribe_coaching_events, note_template_versions, event_outbox, voice_cutover_state) plus billing_meter_report_watermarks in Scoped-OUT, each carrying the per-table justification that had been living only in the constant. Two table names in the retain table were WRONG — `audit_events` and `jit_grants` name nothing; the real tables are `audit_log` and `jit_access_requests`, reconciled in code on 2026-07-14 and recorded in prose but left standing in the table a reader would actually look them up in. One malformed markdown row (scribe_audio_destructions, missing its closing pipe) fixed. (2) THE AUTHORITY CONTRADICTION, which is what let the drift happen. The ADR’s Alternative 4 said "the AUTHORITY is this ADR; the constant is generated from this list in code review" and erasure-cascade.ts’s header repeated it, while the ADR’s own Completeness-audit section said "the code is the operative list". Measured cost of the ambiguity: 167 erase-classified and 75 retain-classified tables in the constant with no counterpart in the markdown. Settled in both files: the constant is OPERATIVE (it is what the worker executes and what both gates reconcile against); the ADR is the RATIONALE OF RECORD for the curated set — every table whose classification was argued rather than derived. A rule requiring 250+ tables to be transcribed into markdown is a rule nobody followed. (3) THE TEST. apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.integration.test.ts seeded 13 tables, exactly one of them scribe (scribe_sessions), and the other 2026-07-29 tables were not in MINIMAL_DDL at all — so the worker’s PG-42P01 skip swallowed each DELETE and the cases asserted nothing. All 13 now exist in the DDL, are seeded for BOTH the erasing tenant and the sibling, and are asserted zero-then-one. Every PHI column carries a canary string, and a post-erasure sweep over information_schema searches EVERY text/varchar/json/jsonb column in the schema for it — asking the schema rather than asking the list, which is the shape of the defect J09-F1 found. 13/13 green against real Postgres on :5433.

NO CHANGE TO ARMING — CERNIA_ERASURE_EXECUTE remains UNARMED and this bullet stays OPEN, deliberately: arming a destructive irreversible cascade in production is an operator decision with a runbook and a rollback story and belongs to a human. Recorded here only because ADR 0155 (per-patient erasure scope) landed today and a reader could otherwise assume it widened the flag. It does not: ADR 0155 ships a DESIGN plus a classification constant and NO executor, so nothing new becomes destructive under this flag, and a future per-patient executor must get its own separate arming decision rather than riding this one (different gates — the tenant retention floor cannot apply to a patient, who has no offboarding anchor). Also surfaced for the pre-arming checklist: tenant-erasure-worker.ts does not consult legal_holds despite legal-hold-store.ts existing. Flagged, not fixed, and not verified as a defect in the tenant path.

Built the legal-hold gate the tenant-erasure cascade never had. apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.ts: new countActiveLegalHolds() reads legal_holds directly off opts.db (NOT a seam — a seam needs a default, and "skip" leaves the bug reachable by omission); computeHold checks it FIRST, ahead of the retention floor and grace clocks, because a legal hold is an external instrument that outranks internal policy and an operator told "retention-floor-pending" waits for a date whereas "legal-hold" needs counsel. Any active hold blocks regardless of scope; an unreadable registry holds under a DISTINCT reason rather than being folded into zero. 7 tests added (20/20 on real Postgres), mutation-proven: disabling the gate reds exactly 4, and the 3 survivors are the ones asserting non-blocking. Residue: in-flight `erasing` resumes still skip every gate, so a hold placed mid-erasure does not stop that job. NOTE the asymmetry that made this findable — the NEWER per-patient executor (cernia-ops-patient-erasure-routes.ts) checked holds correctly from the start; the older tenant-aggregate worker never did. The newer code being safer than the older is the opposite of where anyone looks.
