NARROWED 2026-08-03: `node scripts/check-erasure-classification.mjs` is now wired into a workflow — it runs as the FIRST step of the `gates` job in .github/workflows/comprehensive-tests.yml, ahead of `pnpm install`, since it is dependency-free and takes ~0.5s, so an unclassified table fails in seconds rather than after a 25-minute dependency build. It was previously in NO workflow at all. WHAT REMAINS is not a wiring problem: (a) GitHub Actions cannot run — the spending limit has been exhausted since 2026-07-29 and every check reports fail in ~5s without starting, so a gate in a workflow is a gate that never executes; (b) once CI returns, `gates` must be made a REQUIRED status check on branch protection, otherwise a red job is advisory; (c) the workflow's `paths-ignore: docs/**` means an ADR-only PR skips the whole file — harmless today because this gate reads migrations and erasure-cascade.ts rather than the ADR, but it is the reason an ADR amendment cannot be gated the same way.

[cascadecompleteness-audit-five-flagged] The cascade-completeness audit for the five flagged families is DONE (2026-08-03) and the outcome is narrower than the bullet assumed. Findings: (i) the provenance was misattributed — ADR 0143 flags none of these tables; it governs WHEN the cascade may run, not what it covers. (ii) There is no `auth_sessions` table; the real ones are `patient_auth_sessions` (migration 293) and `patient_credentials` (292). (iii) All seven tables across the five families — patient_credentials, patient_auth_sessions, fax_transmissions, erx_prescriptions, erx_refill_requests, pharmacy_status_events, scheduled_workflows — were ALREADY classified ERASE and none was unclassified, so both gates were green on them all along. What was actually missing was the deliberate rationale: six of the seven landed in the 2026-07-14 alphabetical bulk block with no justification comment, which is exactly the "by whichever list they happen to land in" condition. Each now carries one in apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts. WHAT REMAINS is a compliance sign-off, not code: two are genuine RETAIN candidates and the ERASE argument written at them is an engineering argument. eRx is a controlled-substance prescribing record (DEA §1311.305 EPCS audit trail; state boards commonly 2-7 years) and fax_transmissions is a disclosure record (HIPAA §164.528 accounting-of-disclosures, 6 years). The case for ERASE in both is that the obligation attaches to the AUDIT record — audit_log, Scoped-OUT, 6 years — and not to the operational row, and that retaining the row without the `resources` Composition it belongs to leaves an unusable fragment. Someone with a compliance opinion needs to agree before CERNIA_ERASURE_EXECUTE is armed; if they disagree, the change is to move the two entries to ADR_0140_SCOPED_OUT.

Same fixture, same real operator routes, fixed cascade (j09f1-green-verify.json): 193 tables cascaded, all three at 0 with attempted=true / rowsDeleted 27+3+3, control tenant t-j09f1-control unchanged AND still non-empty, and the platform tenant_id='' price rows intact. Residue is commercial only, NO PHI — a broken guarantee, not a disclosure. CLASSIFICATION = ERASE for all three, argued per-entry in apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts and amended into docs/architecture/adrs/0140-right-to-erasure-scope.md: the parent product_entitlements has been Scoped-IN since the 2026-07-14 audit; ADR-0140 already classified the identical shape (scribe_recording_consent_events — an append-only history whose current-state sibling is Scoped-IN); logIsConsistent() in entitlement-history-store.ts returns raw.length===0 when the live row is absent, so RETAINING the history manufactures a state the reader itself calls incoherent and degrades every later read to 'cannot determine'; and none of the three is a financial record of record — invoices / stripe_invoices / charge_history / revenue_events / billing_usage_events / revenue_contracts / saas_contracts carry that 7-year obligation, are all Scoped-OUT, and are untouched by this change (grant_ref is only a pointer into Stripe, whose own horizon ADR-0140 already defers to). TWO CLASS-LEVEL DEFECTS behind the instance: (1) the completeness gate NAMED product_entitlement_events and product_usage_pricing — it was red on github/main with both — and both shipped anyway, because test:gates is not wired into any pre-merge check and CI cannot run (see the new `remaining` bullet); (2) the gate's scanner read only CREATE TABLE bodies, so catalog_prices — which acquired tenant_id by ALTER TABLE in migration 341 — was structurally invisible to it and the gate stayed GREEN for it. The scanner now also reads ALTER TABLE ... ADD [COLUMN] <tenant-key>, pinned by its own assertion so a refactor cannot silently drop the pass, plus an assertion that these three stay in the ERASE list (moving one to SCOPED_OUT would re-open the leak with the gate still green). NEW HAZARD FOUND AND CLOSED: catalog_prices and product_usage_pricing are the first cascade tables to reserve tenant_id='' as a PLATFORM sentinel row that every practice on the fleet resolves against. Every cascade predicate is `<key> = <tenantId>`, so a job row with a blank tenant id would delete the whole fleet's price list, irreversibly, while reporting a perfectly ordinary erasure. runTenantErasureWorker now REFUSES a blank tenant id before any gate or count, including for in-flight 'erasing' rows; regression test in tenant-erasure-worker.integration.test.ts. J09'S OWN CHECK TIGHTENED (the finding's namesake): it asserted 'every SCRIBE table is zero' while ADR-0140 promises 'every TENANT-SCOPED table', and the defect lived exactly in that gap. New apps/api/scripts/erasure-residue-sweep.mts sweeps information_schema for every tenant-key-bearing table and reads the SAME constants the cascade executes from, so 'permitted to survive' cannot drift from 'actually retained'; run-journeys-c.mts J09-4 now asserts on it. Proven red-then-green independently of the journey via apps/api/scripts/j09f1-residue-sweep.mts (j09f1-sweep-red.json names all 3 leaks and permits the 6 retained; j09f1-sweep-green.json 0 leaks / 5 permitted), with a falsifying control — pointed at the never-erased tenant it lights up 9 tables, so it is not merely returning empty. Because it reads the LIVE schema it has no ALTER blind spot at all. PR #745's separate audio-destruction path is untouched and still does not go through the executor. VERIFICATION: test:gates 10 files / 69 tests green; tenant-erasure-worker.integration 9/9 against real Postgres on 127.0.0.1:5433; apps/api lint 63 problems = the stated baseline, 0 new; typecheck and build clean. Evidence: docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/j09f1-{red,green}-{seed,verify}.json + j09f1-sweep-{red,green}.json.

ADR-0140 RELEASE-BLOCKER MADE ENFORCEABLE (follow-up to PR #762, which fixed the symptom and said it had not fixed the rule). The rule 'a table that lacks a classification is a release-blocker' was not one: test:gates runs in no pre-merge check and GitHub Actions cannot run at all (spending limit exhausted since 2026-07-29 - every check on every PR reports fail in ~5s without starting), so a gate that was RED on github/main naming two unclassified tables let those PRs merge and a real dual-controlled erasure left 156 rows behind. CI-based enforcement was therefore rejected as worthless today. THREE LAYERS SHIPPED. (1) AUTHORING - the migration declares its own classification, MACHINE-READ: migrations numbered above 345 must carry `-- ADR-0140: <table> = ERASE | RETAIN | NOT-APPLICABLE` and it must AGREE with apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts. This closes the actual defect: migration 340's header stated its classification CORRECTLY in prose and the array never learned it - a truth written in a comment and not in code. Forward-only ratchet (DIRECTIVE_RATCHET_FROM=345, pinned by an assertion so it cannot drift upward silently). (2) PUSH - NEW scripts/check-erasure-classification.mjs: zero dependencies (node:fs + regex; no build, no node_modules, no DB), one parallel pass over the 305-file migration corpus, MEASURED 444-574 ms wall including node startup (sequential reads measured 1.8-4.3 s on this OneDrive working copy - parallelising the reads, not weakening the check, is what made it cheap). Installed on pre-push by NEW scripts/install-hooks.mjs (cross-platform; install-hooks.sh is now a wrapper) which the root postinstall runs, so `pnpm install` installs it; hooks are written to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`/hooks so ONE install covers all ~100 worktrees, and a checkout that predates the script skips cleanly. Chosen over folding into test:gates because the ADR-0127 checklist is per-PACKAGE and packages/storage/src/migrations is not apps/api - the migration author had no reason to run an apps/api suite, and did not. (3) EXECUTION, UNBYPASSABLE - auditCascadeClassification in apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.ts asks the LIVE information_schema (scoped to current_schemas(false), because every cascade op is an unqualified DELETE and search_path is exactly the set of schemas such a DELETE can reach) and HOLDS every job on the new 'cascade-classification-incomplete' reason, naming the tables in report.unclassifiedTables. Applies to in-flight 'erasing' RESUMES too, unlike the two-clock gate: the clocks answer WHEN and a resume is past that decision, classification answers WHAT and every remaining DELETE is still ahead. Fail-closed - an audit that THROWS holds identically. PROVEN TO BLOCK, not merely asserted: a real unclassified table created in the live fixture schema holds an ARMED run with zero rows deleted and the job still 'confirmed'; five synthetic migration corpora (apps/api/src/__fixtures__/adr0140/) show the script rejecting an unclassified table, an ALTER-added tenant key, a missing directive and a directive that disagrees with the code. PROVEN NOT TO OVER-BLOCK: a platform table with no tenant key and an already-classified table both pass, and the pre-existing worker suite is unchanged. A test drafted with `audit_events` as the 'already classified' table was itself caught by the new gate - audit_events is the ADR's ASPIRATIONAL name and no such table exists - which is the same prose-vs-schema drift this change is about. VERIFICATION (ADR-0127): test:gates 10 files / 77 tests green (was 69; the completeness test is rewritten as the anti-drift test for the script and also runs the script's own checks); tenant-erasure-worker.integration 13/13 against real Postgres on 127.0.0.1:5433; apps/api typecheck clean; apps/api lint 63 problems = the stated baseline, 0 new. HONEST LIMIT, stated in the ADR amendment and in the narrowed remaining bullet: layers 1-2 make an unclassified table hard to LAND but are bypassable (--no-verify; a clone that never installed the hook); only layer 3 makes one impossible to ACT ON. A pre-merge check returns with CI. Files: scripts/check-erasure-classification.mjs, scripts/install-hooks.mjs, scripts/install-hooks.sh, package.json, apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts, apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.ts, apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.completeness.test.ts, apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.integration.test.ts, apps/api/src/__fixtures__/adr0140/, docs/architecture/adrs/0140-right-to-erasure-scope.md.

The self-serve PASSWORD path stops stranding its founding admin. POST /onboarding/:id/reserve-tenant provisions the tenant EARLY with the __deferred__ sentinel, creating the admin status:‘invited’ with no credential — correct for the SOCIAL path, where the Google callback’s promoteInvitedAdmin finishes the job. On the password path there was no second act: $complete conflicted on the Tenant create, OnboardingFullProvisioner recovered the tenant through resolveExisting, ran its idempotent post-steps and returned 200 while the password on the request body was dropped on the floor. Active tenant, admin that cannot authenticate, and no invitations row either, because onboarding writes none. Measured live on five tenants 2026-07-31; apps/api/scripts/acceptance-clinician-role.mjs documents the shape as a reason to avoid the route, and apps/api/src/orphan-tenant-cleanup.ts describes the wreckage. FIX: FhirStorageTenantProvisioner.upgradeDeferredAdmin (apps/api/src/fhir-storage-tenant-provisioner.ts), called from the conflict-recovery branch of apps/api/src/onboarding-full-provisioner.ts. Chose "upgrade" over the alternative "stop calling reserve-tenant on the password path" because the latter is a client-side fix for a server-side hole: the route is not gated on isSocial (it branches to a password-path 409 for a missing email, so it plainly expects password callers), and today’s installer calling it only from the Google handler is a property of one client, not of the API. FAIL-SAFE: it refuses the sentinel and the empty string, so it can never activate a social-path admin; and it only ever touches a user who is BOTH status:‘invited’ AND credential-less, so a genuine retry-after-partial-failure whose admin already has a password is untouched — that is the property that makes it safe to call on every conflict recovery rather than only the first. It writes the CANONICAL User.passwordHash, the only field the built-in provider reads, which is the field the last defect in this area got wrong. Seam widened optionally (IFhirProvisioner.upgradeDeferredAdmin?) so the in-memory doubles across the suites are unchanged. 6 new unit cases, 22/22 in fhir-storage-tenant-provisioner.test.ts. ALSO in this change: the ADR-0140 classification gate joined a CI job for the first time, and the five-family cascade audit landed with per-table rationale — see the two narrowed remaining[] bullets.

Closed [l6-mounted-looks-almost] by DELETING the l6 /policies CRUD from apps/api/src/platform-policies-routes.ts. MEASURED FIRST, not inferred: every one of the 13 declared routes resolved to the catch-all {verb:'*', resourceType:'*'} and returned 403 — for a tenant-admin on their OWN tenant, for a tenant-admin naming another, AND for cernia-super-admin, because the platform-operator pass is scoped to /cernia-ops/*. Reachable by nobody while reading as shipped. DROPPED RATHER THAN MAPPED for two reasons. (1) NOTHING CONSUMES l6 DATA — InheritanceResolver, EffectivePolicyEngine, OverrideManager and PolicyValidator are imported nowhere under apps/, and no path reads l6_access_control_policies to make an access decision. Mapping would have shipped an "Access Control Policies" editor whose deny rules deny nothing, which in a HIPAA product is WORSE THAN A 404 because it invites an admin to believe a restriction is in force. The o4 precedent supports the distinction: /api/o4/cost was FIXED because a consumer was being misled; /policies has none. (2) THE STORE IS UNFIXABLE FROM THE ROUTE LAYER — get/update/delete carry NO tenant predicate at all (global policy id), insert took tenant_id and org_id off the REQUEST BODY (mint or re-parent into another tenant), listByOrg filters a caller-named org, migration 081 leaves tenant_id NULLABLE, and the table has no RLS anywhere in the repo. The old header claimed "No cross-tenant reads possible — the Postgres CHECKs + indexed WHERE clauses do the isolation": FALSE IN EVERY CLAUSE. The falsifying control demonstrated the live leak directly — restoring the routes made GET /policies?tenantId=t-cedar return t-cedar's policy row to a caller who is not t-cedar. THE PLUGIN STAYS REGISTERED: grace-suspend-routes.ts deliberately does NOT register /grace/policy/:tenantId because this file owns it (boot-route-dedup pins the split; both would crash boot on FST_ERR_DUPLICATED_ROUTE), and the F-5 policy rows are live input to the suspend lifecycle — unregistering would have deleted a live engine's only config surface. A NOTE ON THE TEST INSTRUCTION, because it was WRONG and the agent was right to refuse it: the brief demanded "assert 404, not 403". registerRbacHook installs an APP-LEVEL preHandler, which Fastify runs for the not-found path too — so a route that never existed ALSO returns 403, and a 404-based assertion would have passed on a route that was still there. Under the mutant, 8 tests still passed: all the real-hook 403 ones. A 403-only test is not evidence here. Three instruments were used instead — Fastify's own route table, an RBAC-disabled harness where removed paths give a true routing 404, and the real hook. RESIDUE, deliberately not fixed: the F-5 /grace/* and M-5 /trials/* survivors remain UNMAPPED and therefore still 403, and /grace/policy/:tenantId still takes the tenant from a path param — but that family spans grace-suspend-routes.ts, and half-fixing it would leave five lifecycle routes on the opposite tenancy model. Also stale and not touched: docs/api openapi baselines still carry /policies entries, apps/admin/policies/access-control/* is now dead (already unlinked from nav and already 403ing; now 404s), and apps/api/package.json still declares the l6 dependency.

current.summary: Cross-tenant aggregation runs and reconciles (fixed 2026-08-03, 2,570 cents across all three platform routes). The one open item is not a defect: whether the fleet-read /by-tenant should hash its tenant ids like its eight peers do. The factual errors around it are fixed — the "opaque UUIDs" claim is corrected everywhere it survived, and the duplicated hash helper now imports the canonical one.

remaining: [raw-tenantid-displayname-cross] OPS BOUNDARY — THE LAST TWO RAW-IDENTIFIER READS ARE CLOSED 2026-08-06, and the bullet was NOT stale: both files still emitted raw values, confirmed by reading them rather than trusting the claim. cernia-ops-entitlements-routes.ts returned tenantId + displayName per tenant, so one response was a roster of every Cernia customer and what each had bought; cernia-ops-routes.ts passed the aggregator snapshot straight through on /voice-agents/billing and /voice-agents/performance. assertNoPhi never objected because neither field is PATIENT data — which is exactly why nothing caught it. All three read aggregates now emit tenantHash and drop displayName entirely, with the three cernia-ops pages re-headed "Tenant (hashed)" (a bare hash under a "Tenant" header is worse than either). THE NON-OBVIOUS HALF: tenantStore.list() sorts by displayName, so shipping that row ORDER hands back the mapping the hash removes — anyone holding the customer list reads alphabetical position off the row index and re-labels every row. The matrix now re-sorts on the opaque key, and under the dev salt the two orders are exact reverses so the test genuinely falsifies. 268 cernia-ops tests (+9), gates 80/80, mutation-proven: re-adding the raw fields reds E07, removing the re-sort reds E08. Every hash test asserts on the SERIALISED BODY rather than a field name, with inclusion-first guards so an empty tenants[] cannot satisfy an exclusion. DELIBERATELY LEFT RAW, each with a reason: POST .../entitlements/expire (the operator NAMES the tenant — a hash cannot become a WHERE clause, and hashing only the response replaces a confirmation with a value the caller cannot check); GET /cernia-ops/tenants (rows link to the tenant detail page and it is the $impersonate entry point); $impersonate / $approve / $reject (audited actions on a caller-named path). TWO GENUINELY MIXED, FLAGGED NOT FORCED: (a) GET /voice-agents/rollout — the read IS the write's input, every toggle PATCHes the tenantId it read, so hashing breaks every switch; displayName was kept too, because with the id already raw, dropping the label only leaves an operator flipping a live phone agent for a practice identified by slug, where a wrong-row click changes what a real clinic does. The proper fix is an opaque handle the PATCH also accepts — a different change, not smuggled in here. (b) GET /voice-agents/numbers — resolving a DID to its practice IS the feature, so a hash cannot answer the only question the page exists to answer; if this must be de-identified the honest version is narrowing who can reach it, not blanking the field. ALSO OUTSTANDING: packages/cernia-ops/src/types.ts still documents "Tenant IDs ARE shown here" on the VoiceAgent*Snapshot types, now true only internally — the wire is de-identified but the doc comment is not, and that package was outside the change's writable set.

history.note: PROD-P11: @cernia/finops PostgresCostTracker + migration 067_finops_cost_ledger. PK (tenant_id, occurred_at, ledger_id BIGSERIAL); CHECK on provider + category + non-neg quantity/cost. PHI tripwire blocks MRN/DOB-shaped values + forbidden keys (patientId, mrn, dob). 16/16 tests green against real Postgres including cross-tenant rollup isolation. Commit 99fdddd2.

CORRECTION to the 2026-05-26 "complete". /cernia-ops/finops/{rollup,by-tenant,margin-per-tier} returned EMPTY WITH NO ERROR. PostgresCostTracker never implemented the cross-tenant capabilities the routes assumed — and, contrary to the reading in both the route comment and the bug report, it did NOT reject the wildcard: "*" is a non-empty string, so it satisfied the `tenantId is required` guard and was bound as a literal WHERE tenant_id = '*', matching no row and returning a well-formed ZERO rollup. Because nothing threw, the route's own cost-tracker-wildcard-not-supported fallback never fired — the failure was quieter than documented. /by-tenant and /margin-per-tier separately probed for listTenantIdsInWindow, did not find it, and substituted an empty tenant list. Measured live on a 2,570-cent / 2-tenant ledger: all three answered HTTP 200 with zeros and no warning field at all. FIX: packages/finops/src/cost-tracker.ts gains platformRollup() and listTenantIdsInWindow(), both sharing ONE private aggregate() with rollup() so the platform figure cannot drift from the per-tenant rows it is supposed to be the sum of; rollup() now REJECTS PLATFORM_WIDE_TENANT_SENTINEL by name, so a wildcard can never again be silently read as a tenant. apps/api/src/cernia-ops-finops-routes.ts returns 501 cost-aggregation-unsupported naming the missing capability instead of degrading to zeros / items:[] / all-tier-zero. An empty 200 from these routes now means the ledger really was empty. LIVE AFTER: rollup totalCents 2570; by-tenant t-cedar 1030 + t-lakeshore 1540 = 2570; margin-per-tier tenantCount 2 / totalCostCents 2570. WHY IT WAS GREEN THE WHOLE TIME: cernia-ops-finops-routes.test.ts injected a hand-written TestCostTracker that implemented BOTH capabilities production lacked — it honoured the "*" wildcard and had listTenantIdsInWindow — so every case passed against a double strictly more capable than the shipping class. Same failure as the bare-Fastify harness on /api/o6/audit, in the dependency direction instead of the middleware one. That double is deleted; the suite now injects the REAL PostgresCostTracker, with one deliberately-incapable double retained solely to prove the 501. Tests: @cernia/finops 136/136, cernia-ops-finops-routes 11/11 (R08-R11 new, pinning refused-vs-empty in both directions).

The "opaque UUIDs" claim corrected everywhere it survived, and the duplicated hash helper removed. The earlier 2026-08-03 defect fix corrected the justification in cernia-ops-finops-routes.ts’s header but left it standing in four other places, one of them RENDERED TO THE OPERATOR ("Tenant IDs are opaque UUIDs", apps/cernia-ops/src/app/cernia-ops/finops/page.tsx). Live tenant ids are practice-naming slugs. All four corrected; no patient identifier is involved on this surface either way, so the accurate statement is that a CUSTOMER-identifying value crosses the platform boundary — a different claim from the one being made. Separately, cernia-ops-finops-routes.ts carried its own byte-identical copy of hashTenantId while cernia-ops-auth.ts exported the canonical one seven other cross-tenant stores import; it now imports it, with the unsalted-sha256 weakness recorded at the function rather than only in a status file. The BEHAVIOUR is deliberately unchanged — see the narrowed remaining[] bullet, which now carries the evidence that makes the decision cheap: the drill-down the bullet was protecting has no production caller.

THE OPERATOR CONTRACT IS DECIDED AND THE RULE IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN (founder): read-only cross-tenant AGGREGATES hash, targeted operator-ACTION lookups emit raw. That is not a new convention — it is the one the codebase already followed across seventeen surfaces without stating. /by-tenant is a pure aggregate with no action affordance, so it now emits tenantHash; /tenant/:tenantId is a targeted lookup and stays raw. THE PREMISE THAT HAD BLOCKED THIS WAS FALSE OF THE SHIPPED PRODUCT, and the bullet already said so: fetchTenant has zero production callers and cost-by-tenant-table.tsx rendered the id as inert monospace text — a React key and a sort key, both of which a hash serves. THE HASH IS NOW SALTED, which was clause (c) and is the part that actually mattered. It was sha256(tenantId) over human-readable practice slugs; a dictionary inverts that in seconds, so "hashed" and "de-identified" were different claims and this file asserted the second. CERNIA_TENANT_HASH_SALT is required in production and THROWS when absent rather than falling back to the weak digest — a silent fallback would reproduce exactly the weakness being removed, in the only environment where it matters, and every hash would still look like a hash. Dev falls back to a fixed published constant. Nothing PERSISTS these hashes (measured: all twelve callers compute per request, including fax-transmission-store getPlatformSummary), so first-time salting is safe; ROTATING it is not, and the env doc says so. THE CONSUMER WAS UPDATED IN THE SAME CHANGE, which is the half that makes this shipped rather than half-shipped: TenantRollupItem.tenantId -> tenantHash in apps/cernia-ops, the table rewired, and the COLUMN HEADER changed from "Tenant ID" to "Tenant (hashed)" — a header claiming otherwise would be the same defect this surface already had once (a false justification about tenant ids rendered to an operator screen, corrected 2026-08-03). Asserted on the WIRE, not on a field name: 16-hex shape, no tenantId property, the raw slug absent from the whole body, distinct hashes per tenant (a hash collapsing every tenant would pass the other three), plus salt-changes-output / different-salts-differ / stable-for-same-input and both production-throw cases. apps/api/src/cernia-ops-finops-routes.test.ts 13/13.

Hashed the last two raw-identifier ops reads: /cernia-ops/platform/entitlements and the two voice-agent aggregates now emit tenantHash and drop displayName, with the three consuming pages re-headed "Tenant (hashed)". The load-bearing find was that hashing the FIELD is not enough — tenantStore.list() sorts by displayName, so the row order alone reconstructs the mapping; the matrix re-sorts on the opaque key and a test pins it (dev-salt order is the exact reverse). 268 cernia-ops tests, gates 80/80, both assertions mutation-proven. Write and caller-named surfaces left raw on purpose (a hash cannot become a WHERE clause); /voice-agents/rollout and /numbers flagged as genuinely mixed rather than forced — for rollout the read is the write's input, and for numbers resolving a DID to a practice is the whole feature. packages/cernia-ops/src/types.ts doc comments still claim tenant ids are shown, now true only internally — follow-up for a PR that owns that package.

stages.name: Search parameters return the rows they name
stages.rationale: A declared search parameter that builds a predicate no row can satisfy is a conformance defect that looks like a clean answer: HTTP 200, well-formed Bundle, total=0. Nothing downstream can tell it apart from 'this patient has no records', which is why it survived in production across $everything, bulk export, the EOB assembler and the pre-visit brief. This stage tracks the parameters whose SQL translation is known to be unable to match, by type.

current.summary: The guaranteed-empty class is CLOSED on both halves. References were fixed 2026-07-31/2026-08-03; the remaining 72 non-reference parameters (68 token, 3 string, 1 uri) are fixed 2026-08-03 — applyJsonbFallback now ORs its original containment probe with a SQL/JSONPath predicate for DOTTED expressions only, which is a strict superset and so provably cannot lose a row that matched before, and the token system|code branch no longer hard-codes a coding[] shape that a conformant Identifier never has. Single-segment expressions (~190 parameters, already correct) compile byte-identically. Proven red-then-green against real PostgreSQL: 16 of 19 cases in packages/storage/src/search-sql-containment.integration.test.ts fail against github/main and all 19 pass after — and the 3 that passed on the broken code are all EXCLUSION assertions, which is the point. The appointment-reminder job no longer depends on participant slot order. Open: compartment pagination (and a next link that loops), write-time reference validation, and the 225 unregistered columns now re-scoped as a perf question.

remaining: [five-arrayindexed-reference-columns] The five array-indexed reference COLUMNS (`appointment_patient`, `appointment_practitioner`, `provenance_target`, `encounter_practitioner`, `procedure_performer`) still exist and are still materialised on every write, now with NO reader: `packages/notifications/src/scheduled-jobs/postgres-appointment-reminder-store.ts` was the last one and was rewritten 2026-08-03 to LATERAL lookups that scan `participant[]` for the type being asked for (red-then-green on real Postgres: 2 new cases fail against `github/main`, 13/13 pass after). What remains is dead weight rather than a defect — five STORED generated columns plus their partial B-tree indexes, computed on every Appointment/Provenance/Encounter/Procedure write for nobody. Dropping them is a migration; the build-time drift gate already prevents anything registering them again, so leaving them costs write time and index space, not correctness.

[walkpatientcompendium-walkencountercompendium-page] COMPENDIUM PAGING — (b) closed 2026-08-06 (truncation moved into the Bundle body as a conforming search.mode:'outcome' entry, headers retained). (a) AND (c) CLOSED AT THE STORAGE LAYER 2026-08-07. (a) The adapter applied .limit().offset() with ORDER BY emitted only when a caller passed `sort` — one key, no tiebreak — so offset paging over tied lastUpdated silently SKIPPED AND REPEATED rows. Every search now carries a TOTAL ORDER (`id` appended as the final sort key, default last_updated ASC, id ASC), and searchPage() returns {bundle, nextCursor, hasMore} reading limit+1 rather than guessing from a full page. search()'s signature is untouched, so the ~6 structural storage-reader seams stay satisfied. The cursor is opaque, bound to tenant + resource type + a SHA-256 fingerprint of the query, and every mismatch THROWS; parameter values are hashed, never in the clear, because cursors ride in URLs. Ascending is argued rather than assumed: ascending can DUPLICATE under concurrent writes, descending silently OMITS. Proven on real Postgres with DELIBERATE ties (40 rows across 4 instants, page size 7 so boundaries land inside tie groups): full walk returns all 40 exactly once at two page sizes, while the pre-change SQL under an identical interleave SKIPS rows deterministically across 3 runs. A tenant-A cursor throws on tenant B. (c) The walker inferred truncation from a full page while the adapter already returned a real COUNT. THREE doubles (not two) set total to the page length, so they could never produce total > entry.length — the exact signal needed. The doubles were corrected FIRST and proven behaviour-neutral before the walker changed, which is the order that matters: using the count first would have tested a fiction. A patient with EXACTLY 1000 of a type is no longer wrongly told their chart is incomplete, and one with 12,000 is told how many are missing. WHAT REMAINS: (i) $everything resumability is STILL BLOCKED, and the reason has narrowed to a writable-set fact rather than a design one — the walker's ResourceGraphStorageReader seam declares only read/search, and the live implementation is OrgScopedStorageAdapter implementing ServerStorageAdapter in packages/server, so the walker cannot consume searchPage at all yet. THAT ALSO BLOCKS THE LARGER IN-REQUEST WIN: looping searchPage per type until exhausted would remove the per-type ceiling as a truncation cause entirely, bounded by the existing maxResources budget. Two files. (ii) The two original blockers are DEFERRED, not solved — the (resourceType, id) de-dupe set and pass 2's discovered-Encounter-id list are both O(emitted, up to 10,000) and cannot ride in a URL cursor. (iii) NO COVERING INDEX: (tenant_id, resource_type, last_updated, id) would make the cursor fast as well as correct, but a new migration breaks the migration-drift guard until the schema snapshot is regenerated — the cursor SORTS rather than index-scans today. (iv) `sort` + `cursor` together is REFUSED rather than implemented, because generic keyset over a nullable generated column silently drops NULL rows via row-comparison. (v) Untouched and worth tracking: _sort naming a parameter with no generated column is a silent no-op — a real drop-without-a-trace of the D48 family.

[declared-search-parameters-name] 227 declared search parameters name a `column` that is not in KNOWN_GENERATED_COLUMNS. Two named a column no migration creates and are fixed; the other 225 name columns that DO exist, so they fall through to the same clause they would have used with no column declared. RE-SCOPED 2026-08-03: this was worth reclaiming because falling through meant a guaranteed-empty containment probe. It no longer does — `applyJsonbFallback` now answers dotted expressions correctly via jsonpath — so registering these columns is a PERFORMANCE change (indexed equality instead of a GIN probe), not a correctness one. Measure before doing it: the perf comparison already recorded in KNOWN_GENERATED_COLUMNS found the jsonpath plan FASTER than the column plan on a live table (4.0ms vs 26.5ms for the same 191 rows), so the assumption that a registered column is the fast path is not safe to carry into this batch unmeasured.

[scribe-order-screen-runs] SCRIBE ORDER SCREEN CHART CEILING — CLOSED 2026-08-07. THE DEFECT: the loader walked the compendium for MedicationStatement / MedicationRequest / AllergyIntolerance / Condition and DISCARDED the walker summary, so a patient with more resources than the ceiling produced a PREFIX that both consumers treated as the whole record — findDuplicate returned undefined meaning "no duplicate" (FM7), and the same lists fed the DDI evaluator whose severity drives signAffordance. "No interaction found" was a claim about the first N resources wearing the clothes of a claim about the patient, and the screen looked IDENTICAL either way. NOT the Part 2 exclusion the loader documents: that drop is deliberate and legally required, this was an arbitrary technical ceiling nobody chose for a specific patient. TWO FOUNDER DECISIONS, both implemented. (1) 2026-08-06 — RAISE THE CEILING 400 -> 2000 (SCRIBE_ORDER_SCREEN_MAX_RESOURCES). 400 was never a clinical number, and the screen reads ALL matching resources rather than only active ones (the status filter runs AFTER the fetch), so a long-tenured chronic patient reached it on prescribing history alone. The ceiling is deliberately NOT removed: the walk is synchronous while a clinician waits, and an unbounded walk turns a pathological chart into a hung order screen. (2) 2026-08-07 — SURFACE A VISIBLE CAVEAT AND KEEP ONE-TAP SIGNING, rejecting the FM4 treatment of withholding the signature. The reasoning: raising the ceiling moved truncation from ROUTINE to RARE, and a warning that fires rarely is signal rather than furniture — the condition under which a caveat works and a refusal is disproportionate. THE COPY IS THE DELIVERABLE and is server-authored, rendered verbatim: it leads with scope ("PART of this patient's chart, not all of it"), REWRITES THE DANGEROUS PHRASE IN PLACE (read "none found" as "none found in the part that was read", never as "none"), names BOTH consumers so it cannot be filed as being about the DDI check alone, states the positive risk rather than only the epistemic gap, and ends in REVIEW rather than "do not sign" — with a test asserting it contains no refusal language, since one-tap is retained. The bold headline itself becomes "No interactions found IN THE PART OF THE CHART THAT WAS READ", so a clinician who reads only the bold line still gets the true claim. ATTACHMENT RULE, which is what keeps it signal: eRx draft always, contrast lab yes, PLAIN BLOOD DRAW NO (its duplicate check is deliberately passed an empty medication list and its interaction basis is not-applicable, so nothing it says depends on the chart), non-draft cards no. PHI: counts and FHIR resource TYPE names only, pinned by a test seeding sentinel strings and asserting none appear anywhere in the serialised caveat. THE FOUNDER DECISION IS ENCODED AS AN ASSERTION, NOT A COMMENT: across clear/moderate/high, truncated and untruncated runs must produce IDENTICAL signAffordance and severity, and evaluateOrderSignGate must still return ok on a caveated payload — so a later change cannot quietly turn this into the withhold option. ONE THING THE BULLET DID NOT MENTION AND THE WORK FOUND: scribe-draft-routes declared the clinical context as an inline literal, so the truncation flag survived to assembly ONLY BY STRUCTURAL ACCIDENT — invisible to the type checker and one narrowing edit from being dropped. Now annotated OrderPatientClinicalContext, with a falsifying control proving the guard has teeth. 38 order-proposal tests (was 31), 17 route tests (was 15), 99 admin tests (was 96), gates 80/80, ratchet 371. NOTHING REMAINS on this bullet. Not verified in a live browser — the surface is covered by a component test plus a real-Postgres route test that drives loader flag -> assembly -> JSONB -> GET /proposed-actions -> confirm.

[bulkexportroutes-authored-tested-never] bulkExportRoutes IS AUTHORED, TESTED, AND NEVER REGISTERED — found 2026-08-07. apps/api/src/bulk-export-routes.ts exists with tests and is not registered anywhere in apps/api/src/index.ts, so every route it declares 404s. THIS IS THE EXACT FAILURE THAT SWALLOWED $everything and, before that, POST /dev/checkout-grant: code that is green in its own suite and absent from the running server. WORSE THAN A MISSING FEATURE: it is ADVERTISED in docs/api-contracts/openapi-baseline.json, because that baseline is auto-discovered FROM SOURCE rather than from a live app — so the published contract promises routes that do not exist, and the drift gate cannot catch it since source and baseline agree. WHAT IS LEFT: register it (if bulk export is wanted) or delete it and regenerate the baseline (if it is not) — but not neither, because the current state tells a customer the endpoint is there. AND: the route-registration completeness gate should learn this shape. It currently verifies that every DECLARED route maps to a verb; it does not verify that every declared route is REGISTERED. That generalisation is the durable fix and would have caught all three instances.

history.note: Reference search parameters fixed at the translation layer. applyReferenceParam (packages/storage/src/search-sql.ts) no longer falls back to JSONB containment — it emits `body @? '$.<path> ? (@ == "<value>")'`, which matches the stored {reference: ...} shape and, in lax mode, any element of an array-valued path (AuditEvent.entity, DocumentReference.author) with no cardinality table to drift. @? rather than jsonb_path_exists() so the existing idx_resources_body_gin can serve it; the value is JSON.stringify-escaped into a BOUND parameter and never reaches SQL text. 63 single-valued reference columns that already existed and were already indexed were registered; 8 array-indexed ones deliberately were not, because a column reading `-> 0` answers only for the first element. DocumentReference added to PATIENT_LINK_PARAM_BY_TYPE (packages/core/src/compartment-link.ts) and PATIENT_COMPENDIUM_RESOURCE_TYPES (packages/fhir-graph/src/edge-catalog.ts) — it was in neither, so every patient's signed-note documents were unreachable through $everything by any route. New real-Postgres regression test packages/storage/src/search-sql-reference.integration.test.ts executes the clause and counts rows (5 of 7 cases fail on github/main); the pre-existing suites could not catch this because one asserts on compiled SQL and the other drives an in-memory storage double. Live evidence docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/finding32-red-github-main.json and finding32-green-fix.json, probe apps/api/scripts/everything-fix-probe.mjs. Closes journeys.json finding 32.

The half of finding 32 that PR #744 dismissed, plus the three follow-ups it deliberately left. (1) BARE PATIENT REFERENCES. The 2026-07-31 note said a scan of run2_b found zero bare subject references and concluded the hazard was latent; it scanned the two databases on the host that happen to have none. A census of all 299 databases (296 with a `resources` table, 64,310 resources) finds 108 bare rows in 13 databases — run2_c 3, run3_c 4, api_errors 19, scribe_f1 14, scribe_fix 14, scribe_e2e 13, and seven more — every one a `subject.reference` on Composition / DocumentReference / ServiceRequest, with `patient.reference`, participant and target clean everywhere. FIXED ON THE WRITE SIDE: `ScribeSessionStore.start` (apps/api/src/scribe-session-store.ts) canonicalises via the new `canonicalPatientReference` (packages/core/src/patient-reference.ts) before the INSERT. The store rather than the route, because `session.patientId` is read by FIVE writers that each drop it straight into a `.reference` — Composition.subject (scribe-draft-routes.ts), DocumentReference.subject twice (scribe-sign-routes.ts), and ServiceRequest.subject / Appointment.participant[0].actor / Task.for (index.ts ~4258-4420). D19 is NOT narrowed: the API still accepts both spellings and still answers 201 for "pt-123"; D19's own comment defers "normalising the STORED value" as a separate, migration-shaped change, and this is that change. Migration 344 repairs rows already written — tenant-scoped and fail-closed, rewriting a bare id only when exactly one non-deleted Patient with that id exists in the SAME tenant. Read-side acceptance deliberately NOT added: the reference is wrong in the record and not only in the index ($push-to-ehr transmits it to an EHR that cannot resolve it), and a bare value names no type, so accepting it on read would make `?subject=Practitioner/x` match the same row. LIVE RED→GREEN on database `barefix`, a template clone of run3_c, with port↔database pairing proven in both directions by a write before either probe (present in barefix, absent from run3_c): `$everything` for the J07 patient went total=4 / 3-of-7 own records to total=8 / 7-of-7. Isolation: patient B (same tenant) and tenant t-meridian were each SEEDED NON-EMPTY first — 2 records each, one canonical and one deliberately bare — and B's own bare record was invisible to B in RED (1/2) and visible in GREEN (2/2) while never appearing in A's compendium in either. Zero leaked in either direction; cross-tenant read still 404 not 403; undeclared parameter still 422; the token parameter still answers. Evidence: docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/barefix-{red,green}.json. (2) ARRAY-INDEXED REFERENCE COLUMNS — five, not four. `appointment_practitioner` also pins a slot (`participant -> 1`) and the 2026-07-31 census missed it by grepping for `-> 0`. It and `appointment_patient` are generated from the SAME declared expression, `participant.actor.reference`, so the schema was encoding a writer convention. All five removed from KNOWN_GENERATED_COLUMNS so `referencePathMatch` serves them, matching any element. The perf objection recorded on 2026-07-31 ("trades an indexed lookup for a GIN scan on a live path") does not survive measurement: on cernia_main the jsonpath plan runs 4.0 ms against the column's 26.5 ms for an identical 191-row answer, and neither is a scan, because `AdapterSearch` pins tenant_id + resource_type + deleted before any parameter clause. The claim that this breaks the voice reschedule flow TODAY is also not true: 295 Appointments across the host, 0 with a Patient participant at an index other than 0, 0 with a Practitioner at any index other than 1, 0 NULL `appointment_patient`. It is LATENT, and fixed because it costs nothing and is invisible when it fires, not because it is currently biting. Real-Postgres red→green in packages/storage/src/search-sql-array-reference.integration.test.ts — 3 red on github/main, and the 4 isolation controls green on both sides, which is the property a control should have. (3) COMPENDIUM TRUNCATION. `walkPatientCompendium` passed no `count` on all THREE passes (the tracked bullet named only pass 1) and `walkEncounterCompendium` on one more, so each took the adapter default of 20 while `summary.truncated` reported only the maxResources cap. Now `COMPARTMENT_PAGE_SIZE = 1000` on every compartment search, and a page returning exactly full sets `truncated`. packages/fhir-graph/src/walker-paging.test.ts is red 4-of-5 against github/main's walker; its double reproduces the adapter's real `Math.min(count ?? 20, 1000)`, which the existing walker.test.ts double does not — that is why 19 green tests missed this. (4) TWO PHANTOM COLUMNS. `practitioner_identifier` and `consent_date` confirmed absent from all 296 databases AND from every GENERATED ALWAYS clause in the migrations; the `column:` claims are dropped from apps/api/src/resources.ts. No behaviour change — an unregistered column was already ignored — but the registry stops asserting an index it does not have. (5) THE DRIFT GATE the 2026-07-31 note asked for. packages/storage/src/known-generated-columns.test.ts parses migrations/*.sql and fails on any registered column a migration does not create, or that pins an array slot, with an explicit allowlist for the 31 token/string columns where indexing coding[0] is deliberate. It goes red 3-of-5 the moment `appointment_patient` or `practitioner_identifier` is re-added. Deliberately parses the migration TEXT rather than booting a fixture: applying 303 migrations blows the 10s hook timeout and would make a correctness gate skippable whenever Postgres is down. The parser was validated against `information_schema` on the dev host first — identical answer, two independent derivations. (6) apps/api/scripts/search-param-census.mts replaces the prose census: 526 declared, 243 column-backed, 21 jsonpath, 190 correct containment, 72 guaranteed-empty — not 74, because `applyDateParam` uses `#>` extraction rather than containment and the 2 date parameters counted on 2026-07-31 were never broken. HARNESS TRAP WORTH KEEPING: `$everything` caches its Bundle for 30s keyed on (tenant, anchor, window, types, count, includeAuditTrail). The first GREEN run — 24s after RED, with identical parameters by design — was served the RED answer and reported the fix as having done nothing. barefix-probe.mjs now waits out the TTL. A harness that does not know about that cache produces a false negative indistinguishable from a failed fix.

The 72 non-reference guaranteed-empty parameters, and the reminder job’s participant-order assumption. (1) CONTAINMENT. applyJsonbFallback (packages/storage/src/search-sql.ts) built `body @> {"<first-segment>": value}` from a DOTTED expression, so `identifier.value` asked whether an ARRAY of Identifier objects equals a string — false by construction, exactly as for references, on 68 token + 3 string + 1 uri parameters. Fixed by OR-ing the original probe with `body @? '$.<segments> ? (...)'`: dotted only, so the ~190 correct single-segment parameters compile byte-identically, and a disjunction rather than a replacement so it is a strict SUPERSET — no per-parameter before/after measurement is needed to establish that nothing was lost, which is what made the earlier "blanket flip is not safe" objection blocking. String modifiers are carried through (like_regex with flag "i", metacharacters escaped) so a dotted string parameter still answers starts-with/contains rather than silently becoming equality. (2) system|code. The token branch built {key:[{coding:[{system,code}]}]} — right for a CodeableConcept, impossible for an Identifier, which spells its fields system/value and has no coding at all; that is the 17-type `identifier` family the bullet called "probably one fix". Now also OR-ed with a filter applied at the PARENT of the final segment, which derives the right shape from the expression instead of assuming the datatype. (3) EVIDENCE. packages/storage/src/search-sql-containment.integration.test.ts, 19 cases against real PostgreSQL on :5433, every exclusion paired with the inclusion proving the excluded row exists and is matchable. Red-then-green measured by checking out github/main’s search-sql.ts under the same tests: 16 failed, 3 passed — and all 3 that passed are exclusion-only assertions, the failure mode the file header warns about. 32/32 pre-existing compiled-SQL tests unchanged. (4) REMINDER JOB. postgres-appointment-reminder-store.ts read the patient from appointment_patient (participant[0]) and the provider display from participant->1; an HL7v2 SIU appointment (AIL before AIP, no patient participant) produced NO reminder — null patient ref, failed join, no phone, no email, silently. Both are now LATERAL scans of participant[] keyed on the referenced type. 3 new cases; 2 of them red against github/main, 13/13 green after. (5) PRE-VISIT BRIEF. GET /scribe/pre-visit-brief?patientId=Patient/<id> 404’d because the route required a bare local id while every other surface — and scribe_sessions.patient_id since the canonicalisation fix — uses the canonical spelling; now normalised in via the existing patientLocalId export, leaving a non-Patient reference untouched rather than reinterpreting it.

REFERENCE CONFORMANCE IS ENFORCED AT WRITE TIME. The bullet asked for the class fix and said it "needs its own measurement of what currently posts non-conformant references" first. Measured, then armed. packages/storage/src/validate-reference.ts walks a resource and rejects any Reference.reference that is not one of R4's forms (relative, absolute, #fragment, urn:uuid/oid — versioned suffixes allowed), wired into runResourceWriteValidation in adapter.ts so it covers POST /Composition, /Appointment and every other generic caller, not just the scribe path. THE MEASUREMENT SHAPED THE DESIGN. `reference` is NOT a FHIR-Reference-only property name: packages/catalog-clinvar-dbsnp stores dbSNP rows whose `reference` is a reference ALLELE ("ATT", "A", "C"). A validator keyed on the property name would call those malformed. So an object counts as a Reference only when EVERY own key is an R4 Reference element — a dbSNP row carries rsId/chromosome/alternate and is excluded by construction rather than by an exceptions list someone maintains. Those rows are not FhirResources and never reach the write path, but the shape is real and the guard is asserted with the allele as a named control, paired with the same string IN a Reference position, which IS rejected. THE OTHER HALF OF THE MEASUREMENT: armed and run, 585 tests across the write path itself (storage 370), the apps/api gates (80), the heaviest scribe writers (92) and other resource-writing suites (43) — ZERO rejections. Nothing in the exercised corpus posts a non-conformant reference, which is what makes a hard reject safe rather than a guess. 16 unit tests.

Founder decision: raised the scribe order-screen chart ceiling 400 -> 2000 (SCRIBE_ORDER_SCREEN_MAX_RESOURCES, apps/api/src/index.ts) after the truncation flag surfaced that the screen could not tell a complete chart from a partial one. Same change added the flag itself: OrderPatientClinicalContext.truncated/truncatedTypes populated from the walker summary the loader had been discarding, plus a PHI-free structured warn. The ceiling is kept, not removed — the walk is synchronous with a clinician waiting. Options considered and NOT taken yet, recorded so the sequencing is legible: a partial-screen caveat banner (only meaningful once truncation is rare, else it is warning fatigue) and FM4-style withholding of the signature (safest, but costs one-tap signing for exactly the highest-volume patients). The flag now measures crossing frequency, which is the input to that choice.

Moved the $everything truncation signal out of headers and into the Bundle body as a conforming search.mode:'outcome' entry (packages/core BundleOutcomeEntry + SearchsetBundle, packages/fhir-graph/src/truncation-outcome.ts, apps/api everything-routes.ts). Headers retained deliberately — dropping them would silently break any client built against them since the next-link removal. The obvious design (widening BundleEntry.resource) was rejected after MEASURING 21 cascading errors into index.ts: Bundle is StorageAdapter.search's return type and ~6 packages structurally depend on its narrowness. Best finding was self-inflicted and caught by the agent's own falsifying control — the union widening was DECORATIVE (narrowing it back failed nothing), and was made load-bearing by an idempotence guard that now yields TS2367. That is the failure mode this repo keeps meeting in a new costume: a change that looks like it does something because nothing proves it does not. Clauses (a) keyset pagination in packages/storage and (c) walker inferring truncation from a full page rather than the adapter's real COUNT remain open and untouched.

Closed the order-screen chart-truncation gap. The caveat is attached to the proposal the clinician acts on, server-authored and rendered verbatim, and it rewrites the dangerous phrase in place rather than adding a note beside it. signAffordance and severity are UNCHANGED by design — the founder chose caveat over FM4-style withholding, and that choice is now a test asserting truncated and untruncated runs are identical, so it cannot be quietly reversed. The work also found the flag was reaching assembly only by structural accident (an inline literal in scribe-draft-routes, invisible to the type checker); now annotated and guarded.

Closed compendium paging (a) and (c) at the storage layer. Every search now has a total order with `id` as tiebreak, and searchPage() issues an opaque tenant-bound cursor; proven on real Postgres with deliberate lastUpdated ties, with a control showing the old SQL skips rows deterministically. For (c) the agent corrected the three test doubles FIRST and proved that neutral before touching the walker — using the adapter's real COUNT while the doubles still reported page length would have tested a fiction. $everything resumability stays blocked, but the reason narrowed to two files outside the writable set rather than a design question.

tracks.name: Microservices Wave-2 — Interop-service extraction
tracks.description: First Wave-2 satellite: a new independently-deployable apps/interop-service (@cernia/interop-service, port 8093, own Postgres DB) — the protocol-speaking integration edge (HL7v2/MLLP, X12/EDI, CDA, NCPDP, connectors, mapping) extracted reuse-first from the monolith per the Wave-1 R4 assignment. Built 2026-07-21 per docs/plans/2026-07-21-001-refactor-microservices-wave2-interop-plan.md; closeout in docs/architecture/microservices-wave2-retrospective.md; governance in docs/architecture/adrs/0146-interop-service-extraction.md. PRs #572-577 + integration commits 8c0a443b, 4086bad5.

stages.name: Scaffold + own DB/RLS + outbox + service-identity (IU1-IU5)
stages.rationale: Governance ADR-0146 + a Wave-1-pattern scaffold: @cernia/server.createServer boot, net-new RLS-native operational tables, the stock event-backbone outbox, and the service-identity substrate. Reuse-first — IU2 is ~90% a copy of audit-service; the outbox and identity substrate lift as-is.

baseline.summary: No apps/interop-service. Interop rode generic FHIR RBAC in the monolith with no owned tables, no dedicated boot, no outbox, no service identity. Connection/ConnectionRun were FHIR resources indexed via STORED generated columns in packages/storage migration 005.

current.summary: IU1 ADR-0146 landed (canonicalization decided: x12-engine + catalog-hl7-v2-messages canonical; retire catalog-x12-edi-transactions + hl7v2). IU2 scaffold on @cernia/server, port 8093, DB interop_service, compose opt-in 'interop' profile — live boot proven (/healthz 200, /readyz 503 fail-closed), 7 tests. IU3 migration 001 = 7 RLS-native operational tables (composite (tenant_id,id) PK + FORCE RLS + per-tenant policy), 37 real-PG tests, cross-tenant read denied on all 7. IU4 stock PostgresOutboxStore bound to interop_outbox (bespoke store eliminated), 43 tests + PG crash-soak zero-lost/zero-double. IU5 service-identity verify + outbound KMS-signed client + per-tenant rate-limit, 25 tests.

history.note: IU1-IU5 merged (PRs #572-577). ADR-0146 + service-map cross-ref; scaffold apps/interop-service (port 8093, DB interop_service) with live boot; migration 001 (7 RLS-native operational tables, 37 real-PG tests); stock event-backbone outbox on interop_outbox (crash-soak zero-lost/double); service-identity verify+client+rate-limit (25 tests).

Two X12 and two HL7v2 implementations overlapped with no canonicalization. Surescripts client is a stub throwing NotImplementedError.

current.summary: IU6 format-engine registry executes ADR-0146 canonicalization (HL7v2->catalog-hl7-v2-messages, X12->x12-engine, CDA->catalog-hl7-cda-r2, NCPDP->catalog-ncpdp-telecom-d0) with construction-time drift guards rejecting retired packages; 14 tests incl. X12 270/271 round-trip via injected fetchImpl. IU7 mapping-runtime hosts @cernia/mapping (5 rungs), 10 tests + paramsToSlotSearch parity. stages.name: Monolith endpoints + service-side seam clients (IU10-IU14 + P3 reconcile)
stages.rationale: The seam inversion vs voice: interop WRITES mapped FHIR back to the monolith RecordGatewayRouter and READS config/secrets/patient-identity over service-identity-gated endpoints. RecordGateway stays monolith-side; SecretsResolverClient is a broker (no plaintext creds/PHI in the interop DB).

Service-side clients: IU11 ConnectionConfigClient (short-TTL cache+invalidate, 13 tests), IU12 SecretsResolverClient broker (no-persist structural, mTLS->KMS-grant handle, 9 tests), IU13 RecordWriteClient (inverse of voice reads) + PatientMatchClient (quarantine-on-unmatched, 13 tests), IU14 MappingExecutorClient (agent/workflow rung reads over the seam) + AuditEmitClient (hash-chained PHI-free events over the IU4 outbox, 27 tests). history.note: IU10-IU14 + P3 reconcile merged. Five monolith /interop-platform seam endpoints (one additive index.ts registration) + four service-side seam clients; broker non-persistence asserted; RecordGateway stays monolith-side. apps/api/src/interop-platform-routes.ts, apps/interop-service/src/platform-client/*.

SECURITY (task #157): the /interop-platform/secrets/$resolve broker keyed its never-plaintext rule on the caller-supplied req.body.kind, so OMITTING the field fell past the mtls-client-cert boundary into the plaintext arm. Fixed in apps/api/src/interop-platform-routes.ts via the new apps/api/src/platform-secret-broker-policy.ts: kind is REQUIRED and matched against INTEROP_SECRET_KINDS; the platform vendor providers (stripe/twilio/openai/anthropic) are hard-denied; only TENANT-provisioned secrets are brokered (no process.env fallback, which was a platform-environment read primitive for any interop-scoped token); and records/$write is constrained to INTEROP_WRITABLE_RESOURCE_TYPES. Red/green regression suite: apps/api/src/platform-secret-broker-policy.test.ts.

THE PDMP PATIENT HASH STOPPED READING AS DE-IDENTIFICATION WHILE BEING NONE. hashPatientIdentifier (apps/erx-service/src/safety/pdmp-query-logger.ts) derived sha256(tenantId + pepper + rawIdentifier) with the pepper defaulting to ''. pdmp_query_log.patient_hash is documented as un-relinkable 'without the raw identifier + pepper'; with an empty pepper the digest is a PUBLIC function of the identifier and the tenant id (which is not a secret), so anyone holding the table can confirm whether a given patient was queried by hashing candidates from an SSN range, a state MPI export or a breached roster. The variable was an OPS step recorded only in a Wave-3 retrospective and nothing checked it, so every deployment ran unsalted while the code read as protected. NEW apps/erx-service/src/safety/pdmp-hash-pepper.ts: resolvePdmpHashPepper (env, trimmed - a whitespace-only Kubernetes secret is not a secret), isDeployedEnvironment (the same generous dev line as scribe-audio-durability.ts, pinned by an env MATRIX test so the two hand-written copies cannot drift), and assertPdmpPatientHashPepper, which REFUSES TO BOOT. Called first in main(), before the pool and before anything can run a PDMP query. A MINIMUM LENGTH of 16, not merely non-empty: a four-character pepper is brute-forced in the same pass that enumerates identifiers, so 'set it to anything' would close the check and not the hole. NO OVERRIDE FLAG - a deployment setting ALLOW_UNSALTED_PATIENT_HASH=1 is a deployment publishing a public function of its patients' identifiers with a config key as its consent. The error names the consequence and the fix (openssl rand -hex 16) and NEVER prints the pepper - asserted by a test, because the message lands in a log aggregator. Rotation is explicitly NOT attempted: it re-keys every historical hash and breaks the audit correlation the column exists for, which is a migration with a design behind it, not a default to change here. EVIDENCE (BOTH arms, against the real main()): apps/erx-service/src/safety/pdmp-hash-pepper.boot.integration.test.ts - a production boot with no salt REJECTS; the SAME boot with a 32-hex salt reaches 'Server listening at http://127.0.0.1:<port>'; a 1-character salt also rejects, naming the length. Plus 30 unit tests including the falsifying control that the pepper actually changes the digest - without it every other assertion would still pass if the pepper stopped reaching sha256 entirely.

Closed [tu21-realws-fsm-suite]. Fixed delays replaced by condition polls (apps/telehealth-service/test/support/poll-until.ts); `retry` removed from BOTH real-WS suites (custom-signaling-host 1->0, boot-e2e 2->0). DROPPING THE RETRY EXPOSED A LIVE PRODUCTION BUG: ensureLocalSession did check-then-act across an await, so two peers whose WS upgrades landed within one DB round trip both built a LocalSession, the last won the map, and the first peer's registration landed in an object deliverLocal could never reach again. Nothing errored — the FSM reached negotiating, both participant slots bound, the durable row looked perfect — and one party silently received NOTHING for the life of the visit. Measured 34 of 80 overlapping handshakes losing a peer permanently; 0 of 250 after memoizing the in-flight build. Reviewed and accepted knowingly even though it is production code outside the agent's writable set: this.local.set runs synchronously immediately before the return, so there is no re-entry window when the .finally() clears the in-flight map. SECOND FALSE PREMISE CORRECTED, and it is the reason the retry survived: the 2026-08-03 fix recorded a "hookTimeout 180s / testTimeout 20s split", but it was passed as describe() options and vitest's TestOptions accepts neither key — both were silently dropped, the suite ran on the 5s/10s DEFAULTS, and retry:1 was doing all the work. Proven by a sabotaged run reporting "Test timed out in 5000ms". Hook budget moved to vitest.config.ts where the key exists. The poll has teeth: a committed case where the peer never connects fails in ~1s with a named error rather than hanging, and the race test self-classifies orphan-vs-slow so a loaded box cannot be misread as the bug. 5 clean runs plus 3 under concurrent load.

[surfaced-while-closing-auditservice] ⚠️ DEPLOY-ORDER HAZARD, READ FIRST: apps/api does NOT yet stamp the roleSnapshot claim, and it is the mint path for /auth/login, /dev/login, social auth, step-up, impersonation and the ops sandbox. DEPLOYING audit-service WITH GRACE OFF MAKES IT REFUSE EVERY MONOLITH-MINTED TOKEN. Ship order is: teach apps/api to stamp the claim FIRST, or set AUDIT_LEGACY_TOKEN_GRACE_UNTIL + _REASON with a real date. apps/api was outside the change's writable set, which is exactly why the grace window exists. CONSEQUENCE (2) IS CLOSED 2026-08-07 — a tenant that has CUSTOMISED a stored Role is now evaluated against that customisation rather than the code catalog. A roleSnapshot claim (packages/auth/src/role-snapshot.ts) rides INSIDE the signed JWT payload; the issuer resolves roles once at mint and stamps the flattened permission set, and audit-service evaluates that set through the same @cernia/rbac evaluate(), so verb implication and the wildcard exemptions are INHERITED rather than reimplemented. Proven on a real difference in BOTH directions over the wire against real Postgres: a narrowed auditor that lost {AuditEvent, export} gets 403 on POST /audit/export where the catalog gives 200 — and still 200 on /audit/events, so the 403 is the missing grant and not a dead credential — while a widened tenant-member that gained {AuditEvent, search} gets 200 where the catalog gives 403. CONSEQUENCE (1), THE REVOCATION LAG, IS NOT FIXED AND IS NOT CLAIMED TO BE. A grant revoked one second after a mint keeps working for the remaining life of that token. Stamping more into a bearer token does not make it a statement about the present. Two narrowings that are NOT a fix: maxSnapshotAgeSeconds (default 900) is audit-service's OWN ceiling on snapshot.at, enforced independently of exp, so the lag becomes min(issuer TTL, our ceiling) — a bound we control, which today refuses nothing exp would not but stops a longer-lived token silently extending a revoked grant here; and every decision event carries snapshotAgeSeconds + snapshotSource so the lag is graphable rather than theoretical. Closing it properly needs a revocation feed or a verify-time session lookup, which would put back the hot-path dependency on identity-service that this design was chosen to avoid. SECURITY POSTURE: the snapshot is inside the RS256 signature — verified by reading the mint path before adding to it, since JwtIssuer.sign strips reserved names and hands remaining private claims to Principal.claims. FAIL-CLOSED on missing / malformed / unsupported-version / subject-mismatch / tenant-mismatch / incomplete / stale / future-dated, each with its own reason code and NO implicit catalog fallback. The only fallback is legacyTokenGrace: OFF by default, requires an ISO deadline <= 30 days (the constructor throws otherwise) plus a non-empty reason, covers ONLY `missing` and never `malformed`, and labels every decision it permits. Tamper-proven: the SAME elevated snapshot properly signed returns 200 (a positive control, so the payload is not harmless), and spliced into an already-signed tenant-member token it returns 401 with decisions.length unchanged — the guard never ran. A snapshot supplied by header, query string or body is ignored in all three cases. TOKEN SIZE is bounded without truncating: `scope` declares which resource types the snapshot is authoritative for, and a consumer asked about a type outside it REFUSES rather than reading absence as "no grant"; over 128 perms / 6 KB the builder EMPTIES the list and sets incomplete:'overflow', which the consumer refuses. Measured 15 roles x 8 perms under budget. ALSO REMAINING: identity-service ships the RoleResolver PORT but boots with NO_ROLE_SNAPSHOT and a loud warning, because its own database (ADR-0145) holds idp connections, JIT/break-glass rows and an outbox — no Role rows. The choice was made non-optional in the type so it cannot compile away, and the integration test proves the wiring end to end through a real SAML ACS round-trip with a real customised role, but production still needs a resolver injected.

[clean-streaming-completion-lands] CORRECTION 2026-08-07 — THE HEADLINE ON THIS BULLET WAS FALSE, AND IT WAS MINE. It said "a clean streaming completion lands no durable cost row" and "streaming LLM traffic is not being costed", and that was reported to the founder as a live billing defect. IT WAS A FIXTURE SCHEMA GAP. The transport parity suite bootstrapped ONLY migration 001, so its o4_llm_cost_ledger lacked usd_micro_cents (003) and pricing_status / rate_source / unpriced_reason (004); every INSERT failed with SQLSTATE 42703 and makeCostLedgerSink's DEFAULT onError was () => {}, so the write failure was swallowed and read as "not costed". On a correctly-migrated database the clean completion path writes its row through the same seam the guardrail-block path uses. Every other cost-touching suite in the service bootstraps 001+003+004 and says so in a comment; this was the only one that did not. The bug was found by patching a logger into the silent seam, which named the cause in one run. FIXED AND NOW CLOSED: fixture corrected to match production, and the parity assertion STRENGTHENED rather than lowered — it now pins persisted token counts, model, provider, requestId and BOTH money columns. THE PRODUCTION DEFECT UNDERNEATH IS REAL AND IS ALSO FIXED: composition.ts wired the sink with no onError, so in production a TOTAL cost-recording outage produced no exception, no log and no metric — an empty ledger was indistinguishable from an idle service. The default is now a structured non-PHI log line, gated by a test that drops the column and asserts the 42703 is NAMED, plus a control proving a healthy write logs nothing. The service has no in-repo migration runner, so a deployment stopping at 002 fails in exactly this shape. THE STANDING usd_cents = 0 QUESTION IS ANSWERED, and it is NOT this bug (42703 means NO ROW, not a zero row). Traced off the persisted row: priceUsage(gpt-4o, 6, 6) = 0.000075 USD, so usd_cents = Math.round(0.000075 * 100) = 0 while usd_micro_cents = 7500. usd_cents IS THE LEGACY WHOLE-CENT COLUMN AND IS LOSSY BY CONSTRUCTION for any sub-cent call, which is nearly every LLM call — migration 003 exists precisely for this. The money is in usd_micro_cents and it is populated. ANYONE SETTING PER-NOTE PRICING OFF usd_cents WILL READ $0 AND BE WRONG; the read must be usd_micro_cents after branching on pricing_status. The parity test now pins usd_cents=0 AND usd_micro_cents>0 on the same row so this cannot be re-mis-concluded. WHAT REMAINS, a THIRD defect found while reconciling and deliberately not folded into the parity fix: the persisted verdict is pricing_status = NULL ('unknown'), not 'priced' — priceUsage returns the verdict and the fan-out's estimateCostUSD DROPS it. Amounts are correct so nothing is mispriced today, but a FinOps query filtering pricing_status='priced' returns ZERO streaming rows, and 'unknown' is exactly the state the read side widens from usd_cents. Documented at the assertion site.
