GET /api/o6/audit — the LLM-audit compliance surface PR #742 named as "the consumer that was being misled" — was reachable by NO principal: tokenless 401, tenant-admin 403, clinician 403, cernia-super-admin 403, every one of them "RBAC denied * on *", because deriveOperation had no /api/o6/* branch and the platform-operator pass is scoped to /cernia-ops/*. Pasted red on a booted API against real Postgres before any change. FIX, both halves in one change because either alone is a defect: mapped to {search, AuditEvent} in apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts (the SAME operation as GET /admin/audit, so the two audit surfaces cannot drift into different reachability), AND the tenant made server-authoritative from req.rbacClaims.tenantId — a mismatched ?tenantId= is now 403 cross-tenant-read-refused rather than honoured. That second half is the trap iam-route-guards.repo-coverage.test.ts explicitly warned "is primed to fire on the obvious fix"; the route left that pinned catch-all list only because it was defused. apps/api/src/llm-observability-routes.ts now takes a REQUIRED rbac dep plus an in-route requirePermission preHandler, so no future test can stand it up ungated — a bare Fastify() with no RBAC preHandler is exactly what hid this through 47 closures and two journey runs. WHO READS IT: the tenant, over its own data (tenant-admin + tenant-member from buildDefaultRoles, auditor from buildConfigurableRoles — measured against both shipped catalogs, not assumed). NOT the platform operator: a row carries user_id=Practitioner/<name>, a scribe session_id and a Composition id, none of which may cross the tenant boundary (CLAUDE.md invariant 5 / ADR 0026 §3), so cernia-super-admin is deliberately still 403 here. The operator half shipped alongside as a NEW cross-tenant surface, apps/api/src/cernia-ops-ai-observability-routes.ts (GET /cernia-ops/ai-observability/audit): tenant ids sha256-hashed, every row-level identifier reduced to a count, prompt/response hashes dropped, sendPhiSafe on the way out, and producedFraction as the fleet generalisation of the 42.1%-dangling metric PR #742 fixed. LIVE-PROVEN with real tokens on a booted API: tenant-admin 200 with its own 10 rows, tenant-member 200 own-tenant, a DIFFERENT tenant's admin 200 with only its own row and no trace of the first, ?tenantId= widening 403, operator 403 on the tenant route and 200 on the fleet view whose payload contains zero occurrences of any seeded tenant id, clinician name, session id or note id. Tests: llm-observability-audit.rbac.test.ts 13/13 (real global hook, real signed JWTs, real RoleBindings, real Postgres), cernia-ops-ai-observability-routes.test.ts 8/8.

AuditEvent carved out of the RBAC wildcard — the PHI-access trail is no longer a clinician surface. tenant-member (the CLINICAL role every tenant is provisioned with) held {"*",read}+{"*",search}, which reached search:AuditEvent, i.e. GET /admin/audit (the tamper-evident chain recording which patient record each user opened), GET /api/o6/audit, and the generic-REST GET /AuditEvent (a REAL registered resource type — apps/api/src/resources.ts auditEventDefinition). Any clinician in any practice could read who-looked-at-whom. MECHANISM (the founder decision was "carve AuditEvent out of the wildcard", NOT "replace the wildcard with an allow-list"): Permission is a pure allow-list with no effect:deny and no evaluator deny pass, so a carve-out could NOT be expressed in default-roles.ts at all — the exclusion had to land where the wildcard is interpreted. packages/rbac/src/permission-matcher.ts gained WILDCARD_EXEMPT_RESOURCE_TYPES={AuditEvent} and typeCovers returns false for a granted "*" against an exempt type; an explicitly-named grant still matches. STATUS-QUO PRESERVED for every other holder: packages/saas-platform/src/lifecycle/default-roles.ts tenant-admin +{AuditEvent,admin}, developer-api +{AuditEvent,read/search/write/delete} (customer API keys would otherwise have started 403ing in production), configurable-roles.ts auditor +{AuditEvent,read}+{AuditEvent,search} (it reached the trail ONLY via its wildcard, so without this the compliance role would have kept the signed export and lost the browse surface). Closed-set drift alarms updated in the same commit incl. a NEW one for TENANT_MEMBER_PERMISSIONS, which had none. LIVE ACCEPTANCE (apps/api/scripts/acceptance-auditevent-carveout.mjs, product-path credentials only — onboarding/login/invite/accept, never /dev/login): RED on unfixed code = tenant-member 200 with rows on both /admin/audit and GET /AuditEvent; GREEN = 403 on both, while tenant-admin 200-with-rows, auditor 200-with-rows, office-admin 403 unchanged, a second tenant still isolated, and tenant-member still searches Patient/Observation/Encounter/Condition/MedicationRequest/DocumentReference. EXISTING TENANTS: required a backfill and got one — Role rows are FHIR resources that a code change does not rewrite, so apps/api dev:backfill-role-catalog (ensure-tenant-roles.ts reconcile-if-drifted) must be run on every deployment; verified against pre-existing tenants.

apps/audit-service /audit/* got its RBAC verb check — it had NONE, and it is the only place HIPAA §164.528 disclosure accounting is mounted. MEASURED LIVE on two real processes (apps/api :8231 signing, audit-service :8232 verifying its JWKS key) against real Postgres `auditrbac`, credentials minted through onboarding→login→invite→accept→login: RED tenant-member GET /audit/events 200 with 3 PHI-access rows · GET /audit/disclosure-accounting 200 · office-admin 200 · auditor POST /audit/events 201 and POST /audit/legal-hold 201 (a read-only role writing the record it audits) · cernia-super-admin 200 with raw tenantId/actorUserId · tenant B's admin POST /audit/events {"event":{"tenantId":"<A>"}} → 201, and the forged row landed in TENANT A's chain at sequence_num 5 (CROSS-TENANT WRITE). GREEN all of those 403, controls unchanged (tenant-admin + auditor 200-with-rows, auditor export 200, tenant B admin sees only its own row). 28/28 both directions, apps/audit-service/scripts/acceptance-audit-service-rbac.mjs; artifacts docs/status/evidence/2026-08-03-audit-service-rbac-{RED,GREEN}.json. MECHANISM: apps/audit-service/src/audit-authz.ts evaluates through @cernia/rbac against the SAME catalog the monolith seeds tenants from — platformRoleCatalog MOVED from apps/api/src/ensure-tenant-roles.ts to @cernia/saas-platform/lifecycle/platform-role-catalog.ts so both surfaces share one definition (a second copy is how this hole opened). It therefore inherits WILDCARD_EXEMPT_RESOURCE_TYPES for free: the clinical role is denied here by the same line of code that denies it in the monolith. Route→verb map matches the monolith verbatim where the monolith has an opinion (POST /audit/export → export:AuditEvent, reads → search:AuditEvent); an UNMAPPED route is denied, so a route added tomorrow cannot inherit the old open default. NO BACKFILL REQUIRED — the catalog output is byte-identical across the move (platform-role-catalog.test.ts asserts it against the literal pre-move expression), and the decision reads the code catalog rather than stored rows; #768's dev:backfill-role-catalog remains the prerequisite for the auditor CLAIM to appear at login. TWO DEFECTS FOUND EN ROUTE, both fixed here: (1) packages/k4-rbac-audit-log/src/api-routes.ts makeAppendEventHandler spread the caller's event AFTER the server-derived actor fields, so tenantId/actorUserId/sourceIp/sessionId were all forgeable — the cross-tenant chain write above; (2) apps/audit-service/src/index.ts read AUDIT_JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_JWK only to decide whether to throw and then verified against a keypair minted in-process, so every token apps/api issued 401'd — in production too, with the key correctly provisioned.

CLOSED the `/api/o4/*` + `/api/o6/traces*` follow-up — the one this stage flagged as "reachable by nobody, ON PURPOSE", because each route resolved its tenant from a caller-supplied `?tenantId=` and mapping it would have handed any authenticated caller another tenant's LLM spend. Both halves landed together, as the bullet required. TENANT AUTHORITY: `tenantOf(req, fallback)` is DELETED from apps/api/src/llm-observability-routes.ts; all seven handlers resolve from `req.rbacClaims.tenantId`, refuse a caller-named tenant (query string or `:tenantId` path segment) with 403 cross-tenant-read-refused, and carry an in-route requirePermission preHandler over the REQUIRED deps.rbac. The three BY-ID reads needed a second mechanism the bullet had not spotted: `CostLedgerStore.getById` and `TraceStore.getTrace`/`getSpans` key by a GLOBAL id and take no tenant argument, so those handlers post-filter on the fetched row and answer 404 — not 403 — leaving a neighbour id indistinguishable from a nonexistent one; `/spans` fetches its parent trace first because `getSpans(id)` alone had no tenant to check. MAPPING (apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts): cost + budgets onto BillingAccount, the same operation as GET /admin/billing/usage, so the `billing` role is not locked out by a synthetic type only `*:admin` covers; traces onto a synthetic LlmTrace, deliberately NOT AuditEvent, since traces are model/latency/token metadata while prompt and completion content stay behind /api/o6/audit. New apps/api/src/llm-observability-tenant-authority.test.ts drives the REAL RBAC hook with real signed JWTs over a real two-tenant Postgres fixture; iam-route-guards.repo-coverage.test.ts and llm-observability-audit.rbac.test.ts had their "still unmapped" controls inverted to "mapped, and NOT onto AuditEvent".

Closed consequence (2) of the audit-service authz gap: a signed roleSnapshot claim inside the JWT means a tenant's CUSTOMISED Role is honoured instead of the code catalog, proven in both directions over the wire (a narrowed role loses export, a widened one gains search). Consequence (1), revocation lag, is explicitly NOT fixed — a snapshot inside a bearer token cannot be a statement about the present — and the module headers say so including "do not read the paragraph above as saying otherwise". Two narrowings that are not fixes: our own independent staleness ceiling, and snapshot age on every decision event so the lag is graphable. Fail-closed on eight distinct malformations with per-reason codes; the only fallback is an off-by-default, date-bounded, missing-only grace window. Tamper test passes (same snapshot signed = 200, spliced = 401, guard never ran). DEPLOY-ORDER HAZARD recorded at the top of the bullet: apps/api does not stamp the claim yet, so shipping audit-service with grace off refuses every monolith-minted token.

CORRECTED a bullet I wrote and reported as a live billing defect. "Streaming traffic is not being costed" was a FIXTURE gap — the parity suite bootstrapped only migration 001, the INSERT failed 42703, and the cost sink's no-op default onError swallowed it. Production was fine. The agent said so plainly rather than letting its fix inherit a claim it had not earned, which is the behaviour worth keeping. Three real things came out of it: the sink now LOGS its failures (in production a total cost-recording outage was silent), the standing usd_cents=0 puzzle is answered (legacy whole-cent column, lossy by construction; read usd_micro_cents), and a third defect is newly recorded (the pricing verdict is dropped, so pricing_status is NULL not 'priced'). LESSON, third time this week: a claim asserting a NEGATIVE from a silent failure is weaker evidence than it reads as.

SECURITY FIX (KU6 seam) — the marketplace platform seam had an UNGATED PHI read. apps/api/src/marketplace-platform-routes.ts carries a hosted entitlement gate whose 402 branch fires only when an `entitlementChecker` is injected, and the boot (apps/api/src/index.ts, the marketplacePlatformRoutes registration) injected only `entitlementReader` — which feeds endpoint (c) alone. The 402 branch was therefore DEAD in production, and GET /marketplace-platform/fhir/{resourceType} + /{resourceType}/{id} — an ANY-resourceType tenant-scoped read — served PHI to a tenant whose `marketplace` entitlement had lapsed. The theory that KU9 covered it does not hold: KU9 gates the marketplace-service's OWN publish/checkout/execute routes, not this seam. FIX: the boot now injects `entitlementChecker: productEntitlementChecker` (matching interop AW-3 / erx EU11), and the plugin exempts ONLY the entitlement read-back (c) — gating an entitlement QUERY on that entitlement is circular and would turn its documented SoR-404 → service-fallback into a 402 for exactly the tenants the fallback exists for; that route carries no PHI (tenant id + product slug). The exemption compares a $-normalized path so a percent-encoded %24read caller cannot land on the wrong branch. RED/GREEN in apps/api/src/marketplace-platform-routes.test.ts: a lapsed tenant now gets 402 on both the single-resource and the searchset back-read and on the secret broker, an entitled tenant still gets 200, and (c) still answers 404 (not 402) for a lapsed tenant in both the literal and percent-encoded forms. A source assertion pins the boot wiring so the dead-branch regression cannot return silently.

[crossservice-followup-bu7-single] CROSS-SERVICE FOLLOW-UP (BU7) — the SINGLE tracking bullet for the usage-PRODUCER gap (the platform-seams and ops-activation-closeout copies were merged here 2026-08-03). The metering plane is a durable sink whose idempotency layers guard a pipe its producers must feed. PRODUCER 1 of 4 NOW EMITS: marketplace-service writes the frozen five-key envelope on the `usage` stream in the same txn as the sandbox_usage_events row (apps/marketplace-service/src/outbox.ts writeSandboxUsageEventWith + sandbox-usage-store.ts; real-PG proven in sandbox-usage-emit.integration.test.ts). (a) ml-ai-service NOW EMITS AND IS BILLING-LIVE — 2026-08-06. The bullet's own pointer was WRONG and is corrected here: the emit site is NOT platform-client/audit-emit.ts:283, which is a hash-chained audit emitter with its own idempotency memo; it is PostgresCostLedgerStore.record() in ai/cost/cost-ledger-store.ts, the only place that already holds the caller's tenant-scoped PoolClient and can therefore be ATOMIC with the ledger row. Emits ml.inference.usage on the usage class, quantity in TOKENS not money (the frozen contract says quantity is a count, and the spend already lives on that row at micro-cent precision). Unpriced calls still emit — the tokens were consumed — and zero-token records do not, because the consumer rejects quantity <= 0. WIRED AT BOOT in apps/ml-ai-service/src/index.ts, not only in tests: without that line the producer is green in the suite and dead in production, which is the precise failure this bullet exists to prevent. (b) voice-service EMITS BUT HAS NO CALL SITE — built 2026-08-06, NOT YET BILLING. Read this clause carefully before treating voice usage as covered. voice.minute.usage, the envelope, VOICE_MINUTE_METER_ID and src/usage/voice-minute-usage-store.ts all exist, are atomic against a new domain table (migration apps/voice-service/migrations/011_voice_minute_usage.sql — the SERVICE's own lineage 001-010, not the monolith's 364), RLS-proven and exported. The table is load-bearing rather than gold-plating: atomicity needs a domain row to be atomic WITH, and voice-service had none, since call_sessions is carved but no code in the service writes it. NOTHING INSIDE voice-service ENDS A CALL: the BFF call-session route is a deliberate 501 in DEFERRED_ROUTES (asserted at voice-agent-actions-bff.test.ts:309, parity row tracked in docs/status/pipecat-parity.json) and the monolith owns the live lifecycle via packages/telephony. So a voice minute is still not metered end-to-end. Closing it means either changing that documented 501 contract or wiring the monolith caller — a deliberate stop, not an oversight. ONE THING ALREADY RIGHT FOR WHEN IT LANDS: the idempotency key is `voice-call:<callSid>`, DELIBERATELY IDENTICAL to the monolith's apps/api/src/voice-minute-usage.ts, so if both producers ever report the same call the metering buffer collapses them instead of double-billing. (c) the monolith voice-budget path REMAINS OPEN and untouched — packages/billing/src/voice-budget/tracker.ts VoiceBudgetTracker.record persists budget consumption with no outbox wired at the apps/api voice-call-handler call site. HONEST TALLY: 2 of 4 producers are billing-live (marketplace, ml-ai); 1 is built but uncalled (voice); 1 is untouched (monolith voice-budget). RELATED, AND CLOSED SERVER-SIDE 2026-08-06: /ai/workflow-gen existed only as a marketplace client call. It was worse than a 404 — MLAI_AI_INBOUND_ROUTE_FAMILIES did not list it, so the MU5 guard rejected it as route-family-not-granted. POST /ai/workflow-gen/$generate now mounts in ml-ai-service against the in-process o1 gateway, with a test that reads the marketplace client's frozen path constant OUT OF ITS OWN SOURCE and asserts equality, so the two ends cannot drift silently. STILL PENDING on the client side: MARKETPLACE_OUTBOUND_ROUTE_FAMILIES in apps/marketplace-service/src/service-identity-client.ts is still ['/marketplace-platform','/api/entitlements'] and needs /ai/workflow-gen plus a PlatformClient pointed at the ml-ai base URL before the seam is live end to end.

tracks.name: Design System — Clinical Calm

stages.name: Stage 2 — Live tenant theming (BrandStyle)
stages.rationale: A tenant's confirmed brand color recolors the patient/admin/web surfaces at runtime via BrandStyle (@cernia/branding), always routed through the WCAG contrast auto-guard (deriveBrandVars). Never applies to cernia-ops (R19). A confirm-marker gate (KTD5) prevents surprise retroactive recolor of pre-existing stored colors.

baseline.summary: BrandStyle built, tested, contrast-guarded, XSS-safe, and exported from @cernia/branding — but rendered in NO app layout, so the white-label promise (Wave-H completion / F2 / AE2) was unmet despite the code existing. No brand-color confirm marker existed anywhere.

current.summary: Code complete: the brand_color_confirmed_at marker is wired end-to-end and BrandStyle is mounted in admin/patient/web (NOT cernia-ops, R19), fail-closed so pre-existing/unconfirmed colors emit nothing. The two gates before a LIVE per-tenant recolor are both external to the theming work: the SSR resolver cannot be wired to the tenant-brand API as it stands (that route is authenticated; anonymous SSR has no credential — see remaining[0] for the unblocker), and browser acceptance needs a seeded stack.

remaining: [blocked-blocker-apps-wiring] BLOCKED, and the blocker is not in the apps. Wiring each app's configureDefaultResolver to the tenant-brand API is what this bullet asks for, and GET /tenants/:id/brand CANNOT SERVE IT: apps/api/src/tenant-brand-routes.ts:210-246 requires an authenticated principal bound to that tenant (401 unauthenticated, 403 cross-tenant, per ADR 0126's anti-enumeration posture). SSR brand resolution runs on the ANONYMOUS request — the login page is the surface a per-tenant recolor most needs to reach — so there is no credential to present. Confirmed unwired: configureDefaultResolver has zero non-test callers repo-wide, resolveBrand soft-falls-back to DEFAULT_CERNIA_BRAND on every request (packages/branding/src/ssr/resolve-brand.ts:355-360), and BrandStyle therefore renders nothing in admin/patient/web even though it is correctly mounted in all three. UNBLOCKER: a deliberate decision to expose an UNAUTHENTICATED brand-only read — resolvable by host/subdomain rather than by tenant id, returning colour + logo + brandColorConfirmedAt and nothing else. That discloses which tenant slugs exist and what they look like, which is exactly what the 403-not-404 posture on this route was chosen to prevent, so it is a security tradeoff to be made explicitly and not a wiring task.

[liveacceptance-adr0127-original-intent] Live-acceptance (ADR-0127 by original intent): browser-verified tenant recolor of a seeded confirmed-brand tenant on patient/admin/web + default-brand visual-regression-unchanged screenshot — needs a running seeded stack.

history.note: (U11/T1) tenant theming made real: wired a server-authoritative brand_color_confirmed_at marker end-to-end — migration 310 (nullable, no backfill = fail-closed) + TenantBrand.brandColorConfirmedAt + KyselyTenantBrandStore + tenant-brand-routes (PUT stamps now() on a color save; sanitiseTenantBrand drops any client-forged marker; toResponse surfaces it) + cernia-schema-snapshot.sql for real-PG tests — and mounted <BrandStyle primaryColor confirmed> inside <BrandProvider> in apps/{admin,patient,web} layouts (NOT cernia-ops, R19). Fail-closed: unconfirmed/pre-existing colors emit no style tag (no deploy-day surprise recolor, KTD5). Admin branding page shows the AE2 'adjusted for contrast (WCAG AA)' + 'save to confirm' activation notices. Fixed admin tailwind hsl(var()) -> var() so the mounted vars recolor admin; deleted the superseded cernia-theme.css placeholder. Tests: core 821, branding 106 (brand-style 10), storage tenant-brand-store 25, api tenant-brand-routes 30 (incl. forgery-dropped). Status stays 'partial' because a LIVE recolor also needs the pre-existing SSR resolver lookup wired + a seeded-stack browser proof.

Investigated the SSR-resolver bullet rather than half-wiring it, and found it is not implementable as written. GET /tenants/:id/brand is authenticated (apps/api/src/tenant-brand-routes.ts, authorize() — 401 unauthenticated, 403 cross-tenant under ADR 0126 anti-enumeration). SSR brand resolution happens on the anonymous request, which is the whole point of a per-tenant recolor: the login page. So "wire configureDefaultResolver to the tenant-brand API" cannot be done without first deciding to expose an unauthenticated brand-only read keyed on host, which discloses tenant existence — the exact thing the 403-not-404 choice on that route protects. Bullet narrowed to name the unblocker instead of leaving it looking like unstarted wiring. Confirmed while there: zero non-test callers of configureDefaultResolver, resolveBrand soft-falling back everywhere, BrandStyle correctly mounted in admin/patient/web and correctly absent from cernia-ops.

tracks.name: Specialty Taxonomy Unification
tracks.description: One specialty vocabulary across the platform, three orthogonal axes, NUCC-anchored (docs/prds/specialty-taxonomy-unification.md). Five disjoint lists had drifted apart because they described different kinds of thing: onboarding (9 values conflating specialty + org type + care setting), scribe (11 template tags), k5-specialty-role-templates (25 RBAC keys), voice-agent (75 patient-speech phrases) and catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos (83 orphaned NUCC codes). packages/specialty-taxonomy is now the canonical source; consumers migrate one at a time, each keeping its current behaviour.

stages.name: Stage 1 — Canonical taxonomy package (consumed by nobody)
stages.rationale: PRD Rollout step 1: ship the vocabulary as a pure addition — 42 clinical specialties + 3 escape hatches, 8 org types, 8 CMS-POS-anchored care settings, one merged alias table (clinical free text + patient speech + NUCC codes, longest-alias-first), a conservative resolver that returns undefined rather than guessing, and the legacy mapping tables. A leaf package with zero @cernia dependencies so every consumer can import it without a cycle.

baseline.summary: Five disjoint specialty vocabularies, no shared definition, no shared alias table. A tenant onboarded as `dental` still got the SOAP note default because nothing joined onboarding's value to scribe's tags.

current.summary: packages/specialty-taxonomy ships the full surface (specialties, org types, care settings, aliases, NUCC codes, resolver, ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP / SCRIBE_TAG_MAP / K5_MAP, version stamps). Retroactively tracked — Stage 1 landed without a status entry.

history.note: Stage 1 shipped as commit fefa5c67 (PR #648) but left NO production-readiness entry — this track is the retroactive record, added by Stage 2B. packages/specialty-taxonomy/src/{specialties,org-types,care-settings,aliases,nucc-codes,resolver,legacy-maps,version,types,index}.ts. Data corrections carried in the package (upstream untouched): 367500000X is the CRNA; 363LP2300X is NP Primary Care; 207N00000X is dermatology; scribe's alias table had pointed rheumatology's 207RR0500X at cardiology.

stages.name: Stage 2 — Consumers migrate one at a time, behaviour unchanged
stages.rationale: PRD Rollout step 2: each consumer imports the shared vocabulary and deletes its local one, KEEPING its current behaviour. What unifies is the vocabulary definition and the alias table; each consumer's legacy output strings survive at its own edge via the mapping tables, because those strings are matched against persisted data and live tenant records. No user-visible change in this stage.

history.note: Stage 2C — the two orphaned specialty-adjacent vocabularies are resolved, and they got DIFFERENT answers because they are different things. (1) packages/catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos: DELETED src/nucc-taxonomy.ts + src/nucc-taxonomy.test.ts, buildPractitionerWithTaxonomy and the NUCC_SYSTEM/NPI_SYSTEM/FhirPractitioner/FhirHumanName/FhirIdentifier scaffolding in src/fhir-builders.ts, the NuccTaxonomyCode and PractitionerInput types in src/types.ts, their barrel exports in src/index.ts, and the NUCC sections of README.md. The package survives as what its NAME says — CPT modifiers + Place of Service + pricing engine + Claim/Encounter builders. The decision rested on a measured diff, not an assumption: of the catalog's 82 unique codes (the tracked bullet said 83), 65 were ALREADY in the taxonomy, and the 17 that were not are suppliers, facility subtypes and provider roles rather than practice specialties. Because the taxonomy's R3 test fails on any code no SPECIALTY or ORG_TYPE references, folding those 17 would have BROKEN the package that is supposed to be frozen — the invariant made folding illegal, not just pointless. And the file was not inert: 7 of the 65 shared codes were mislabelled upstream (PRD R4's three, plus 1223P0700X, which is Prosthodontics and not Pediatric Dentistry), while getTaxonomyBySpecialty/searchTaxonomy formed a second specialty-resolution API that resolved 'Dermatology' to the dermatopathology code — a live trap for the next developer who imported it. (2) packages/catalog-abms-credentialing: KEPT, neither folded nor deleted. It carries no NUCC code, slug, alias or resolution function, so it never was a sixth specialty vocabulary and does not violate R1; board -> certification -> subspecialty is credentialing (what an individual is certified for), a different shape from the taxonomy's practice axis, and folding it in would have corrupted that model to avoid a deletion. Deletion was rejected on measurement rather than sentiment: 60 of the repo's 70 catalog-* packages have zero workspace consumers, so 'no consumer' singles this one out only by accident of which package the PRD happened to name, and the data behind it is real — 24 boards, 114 subspecialty relationships, 52 state/territory licences, working DEA check-digit and NPI Luhn validators with algorithmic tests. It did, however, FAIL tsc --build on baseline (credentialing-workflow.ts(304,5) TS2322, a stateResults literal widening status to string); preserving a package for a future consumer is only honest if it compiles, so that one-line cast is fixed. NO migration, no slug/tier/alias/legacy-map change, and the only edit inside packages/specialty-taxonomy is a comment: nucc-codes.ts's R4 note used to say fixing the upstream labels was 'a later stage's job' and pointed at a file that no longer exists. Verification, same-tree baseline vs after: @cernia/specialty-taxonomy 78 tests pass (unchanged), @cernia/catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos 146 -> 106 tests pass across 4 -> 3 files (40 removed with the deleted nucc-taxonomy suite and the 5 buildPractitionerWithTaxonomy cases, zero failures, no surviving assertion edited), @cernia/catalog-abms-credentialing typecheck+build now clean where the baseline FAILED, @cernia/api typecheck clean at 0 errors (it never imported either package, so there is no path for this change to reach it), and pnpm -r --no-bail --filter './packages/**' build goes from 4 failures to 2 (302 packages build clean). Baseline failures were r-mobile-ios-foundation, catalog-abms-credentialing, connectors and p1c-ml-model-registry; catalog-abms-credentialing is fixed here and connectors was a first-run ordering artifact that clears once the workspace has been built once. The 2 survivors are pre-existing, unrelated and carried forward. ZERO new failures — specialty-taxonomy, catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos, catalog-abms-credentialing and connectors all report 'build: Done'.

Stage 1b — the last hand-written specialty list is gone, at the TYPE level. Four consumers still spelled their literal union out by hand (packages/scribe/src/specialty-match.ts ScribeLegacyTag, apps/admin/src/lib/clinician-specialty.ts SpecialtyTag, packages/k5-specialty-role-templates/src/types.ts Specialty, packages/onboarding/src/types.ts Specialty) because the three tables in packages/specialty-taxonomy/src/legacy-maps.ts were ANNOTATED Readonly<Record<string, ...>>, which erases the keys — Object.freeze was never the culprit, the annotation was. The maps are now declared with `satisfies` instead (ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP additionally goes through a mapped type over keyof typeof ONBOARDING_LEGACY_ENTRIES so its VALUES stay pinned to OnboardingLegacyMapping and an entry with specialties: [] does not infer never[] for Stage 3). Each union is now `keyof typeof <MAP>`, so a specialty list declared outside the taxonomy package is unrepresentable rather than merely test-caught — the PRD constraint is enforced by tsc. PROOF, and the failure mode that matters: each of the four consumer sources carries a @ts-expect-error negative type test asserting that `not-a-specialty` is rejected; if the keys ever erase back to `string` the union collapses to `string`, every other check still passes, and the now-unused directive fails the build. Falsified deliberately by re-annotating the maps: scribe src/specialty-match.ts(103,1), k5 src/types.ts(89,1), onboarding src/types.ts(407,1) and admin src/lib/clinician-specialty.ts(58,1) all reported TS2578 Unused @ts-expect-error directive. dental-restorative (PRD R13, the only key mapped to undefined) is a REQUIRED property of type `undefined`, so it survives keyof and Object.keys — asserted by a positive type test in scribe + admin and re-verified at runtime through matchSpecialtyTag. ZERO RUNTIME CHANGE, proven by diffing the emitted dist JS before/after: the only non-comment delta in any of the four files is ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP becoming an alias binding to the identical frozen object (Object.freeze moved onto a private ONBOARDING_LEGACY_ENTRIES const). Key ORDER untouched, so SPECIALTY_TAGS / ALL_SPECIALTIES / LEGACY_SPECIALTIES and the admin Specialty <select> render identically. One drift-guard test DELETED as tautological: onboarding types.test.ts "every legacy value is assignable to the Specialty union" — its body was `const all: readonly Specialty[] = LEGACY_SPECIALTIES`, an assignment that could never fail because LEGACY_SPECIALTIES is DECLARED readonly Specialty[], and vitest does not typecheck, so the "compile-time half of the lock" it advertised was never executed by anything; its only real assertion, toHaveLength(9), is subsumed by the byte-identical-to-pre-migration test beside it. Every other drift-guard test is KEPT and its stale comment corrected: they assert runtime VALUES and ORDER, which Object.keys erases to string[] and which the type system therefore still cannot see. Verification: @cernia/specialty-taxonomy build + 78 tests, @cernia/scribe typecheck/build + 302 tests, @cernia/k5-specialty-role-templates typecheck + 256 tests (incl. real-Postgres store), @cernia/onboarding typecheck + 182 tests, @cernia/api typecheck clean, @cernia/admin typecheck clean + 1761 tests. No assertion edited anywhere.

Stage 2B — three consumers migrated, zero output strings changed. (1) packages/voice-agent/src/practitioner-directory.ts: the 75-phrase SPECIALTY_TAXONOMY literal is DELETED; matchSpecialty now delegates to matchSpecialtyText and maps the canonical slug back to today's FHIR PractitionerRole.code via LEGACY_CODE_BY_SLUG (+ LEGACY_CODE_BY_ALIAS for the two folded slugs, since obstetrics-gynecology must answer 'obstetrics' for "obstetrician" and 'gynecology' for "gynecologist"); a slug with no legacy code returns null, so the emitted vocabulary cannot grow. SPECIALTY_TAXONOMY survives as a DERIVED view over TEXT_ALIASES. Regression found and fixed by the equivalence proof: the shared package marks "ent"/"gp"/"gyno"/"er doctor" exact-only (they are substrings of "dentist"/"urgent care"/"other doctor"), which silently broke "the ENT" and "the gyno" — the most natural phone phrasings; matchShortTokenAlias restores them with WORD-BOUNDARY matching, run only after the resolver declines, so longest-alias-first still wins. New proof: packages/voice-agent/src/practitioner-directory.legacy-equivalence.test.ts pins all 75 pre-migration phrases bare AND padded into an utterance. (2) packages/k5-specialty-role-templates/src/types.ts: ALL_SPECIALTIES derived from K5_MAP keys — 25 RBAC keys unchanged and in the same order, so no role template can be orphaned. (3) packages/onboarding/src/types.ts: LEGACY_SPECIALTIES derived from ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP keys and wired into validateUseCase in wizard-orchestrator.ts; the `Specialty` type name is deliberately NOT renamed because apps/installer's use-case wizard page imports it by name. Persisted shapes, step schemas and UseCaseStepData.specialty are byte-identical.

Stage 2A — scribe + admin migrated, completing the package-consumer set. packages/scribe/src/specialty-match.ts: the private 37-entry ALIASES table is DELETED; SPECIALTY_TAGS derives from Object.keys(SCRIBE_TAG_MAP); matchSpecialtyTag is now exact-tag self-match -> matchSpecialty() -> inverted SCRIBE_TAG_MAP, with the exact-tag check FIRST because SCRIBE_TAG_MAP deliberately maps dental-restorative to undefined (PRD R13: a procedure type, not a specialty) yet the tag must still round-trip. apps/admin/src/lib/clinician-specialty.ts drops its hand-copied duplicate and depends on the dependency-free leaf package directly — no transpilePackages entry needed, it resolves from dist. apps/api/src/scribe-clinician-specialty.ts unchanged (verified, not cosmetically touched). Behaviour measured two ways: an 820-string corpus sweep plus a reverse sweep of all 34 keys of the deleted table. 33 inputs NEWLY resolve that previously returned undefined (patient-speech phrases such as "heart doctor" and "skin doctor" plus 14 NUCC subspecialty codes) — pure broadening, and safe in one direction only: the shared resolver can turn undefined into a correct specialty, never into a wrong one. Four families changed rather than broadened; see the two PRODUCT DECISION / BUG FIX bullets in `remaining`. Regression locks packages/scribe/src/specialty-match.test.ts and apps/admin/src/lib/clinician-specialty.test.ts both pass with no assertion edited.

CLOSURE PASS — 5 remaining bullets to 2, and three of the five were closed by work that had ALREADY LANDED. (1) The catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos bullet described its own completion: verified on main that packages/catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos/src/ no longer contains nucc-taxonomy.ts or its test (the directory holds only cpt-modifiers, pos-codes, pricing-engine, fhir-builders, types, index), so the rival 82-code specialty vocabulary and its second resolution API (getTaxonomyBySpecialty / searchTaxonomy) are gone — commit f4fddc01 / PR #663. Moved to history rather than left on a punch list it had stopped describing. (2) Same for the catalog-abms-credentialing bullet: verified the package is present and intact (24 boards, state-licence and DEA/NPI validators, src/credentialing-workflow.ts carrying the TS2322 fix), and that it holds no NUCC code, slug, alias table or resolver — it is credentialing data, not a specialty vocabulary, so KEPT-AS-IS was the decision and there is nothing outstanding. Same commit. (3) The accepted-narrowing bullet and the mapping-bug-fix bullet were asking for the SAME evidence — a live check against real tenant data — so they are MERGED into one, keeping the sharper statement of what is actually owed (a live $draft by a clinician who carries one of the affected specialties, i.e. the chain-order tier) and dropping ~4.5 KB of narrative that recorded already-paid debts. The voice-agent LEGACY_CODE_BY_SLUG bridge stays open and was re-verified present at packages/voice-agent/src/practitioner-directory.ts.

LIVE $draft closes the mapping/narrowing bullet. A real clinician record carrying each specialty created a real session against a booted apps/api (:8181, DB scribe_spec from the committed snapshot), and the resolver was read back from scribe_sessions rather than from a response body. All four families the bullet named resolved through the specialty tier: 207RR0500X->system-rheumatology (was cardiology), 1223P0221X->system-dentistry (was the pediatrics medical template), 207PT0002X->system-emergency-medicine and 2080P0006X->system-hospital-medicine (were general-pediatrics), 101YM0800X->system-psychotherapy (was psychiatry). One session went the whole way: POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$draft returned 201 in 14s over a live Anthropic call per section, producing Composition/4ab257e2-6b42-4770-9ab5-14393b8dbf79 titled "Rheumatology (Inflammatory Arthritis / Consult) note" with extension scribe-template=system-rheumatology@v1 and the session at status=drafted. Three of its ten sections came back EMPTY because the transcript covered none of extra-articular involvement, a general exam, or a DAS28 score - the model left them blank rather than inventing rheumatology-shaped sentences. TWO CONTROLS carry the result: (1) the CHAIN ORDER, which is the risk the bullet actually named - with a personal default set, the SAME rheumatology-carrying clinician resolved to system-soap with source=personal, so the specialty tier is consulted and yields to the tier above it; (2) an unaliased title ("Interpretive Dance Therapy") also landed on system-soap but with source=FALLBACK, so source=specialty on the five green rows is a real claim and not a value the resolver stamps unconditionally. NOTE ON THE PROVIDER: OpenAI was unusable - a direct call returned 429 billing_not_active ("Your account is not active") - so the run used Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. Evidence, including the verbatim draft response and the session rows re-read from the database: docs/status/evidence/scribe-specialty-live-draft/.

stages.name: Stages 3-5 — Tenant projection, resolution tier, specialty templates
stages.rationale: PRD Rollout steps 3-5. Stage 3 splits onboarding's conflated 9-value field onto the three axes and migrates existing tenants with a DISMISSIBLE confirm prompt (R15/R16 — no tenant is blocked, and a tenant with no specialty behaves exactly as today). Stage 4 adds the resolution tier + relevance filter behind a per-tenant flag, with 'show all' shipping WITH the filter, never after it. Stage 5 ships specialty note templates in tier order.

baseline.summary: No tenant carries specialty/org-type/care-setting on the new axes; no confirm prompt; no relevance filter; templates limited to scribe's original tags.

current.summary: STAGE 4 IS COMPLETE — the headline defect R10 is closed. A dental tenant whose clinician carries no Practitioner.qualification and whose practice set no default now drafts on the DENTISTRY template instead of SOAP, because apps/api/src/note-template-store.ts resolveForClinician gained two rungs below the clinician-specialty match: `tenant-specialty` (the practice's own declared specialty, R10) and `care-setting` (R11's (*, care_setting) rung — the SNF round note without a fictional snf-internal-medicine specialty). Both read tenant_specialty_profiles (migration 328) through an INJECTED store, so a caller that injects none cannot change behaviour at all, which is R15's regression guard by construction rather than by inspection. GET /scribe/templates now orders by tenant relevance with the full library shipped in the SAME response under `hidden` (R8/R9 — one action, no second round trip) plus ?all=true for the flat pre-Stage-4 list; tenant-authored templates and SOAP are never filtered. The per-tenant gate is now a REAL COLUMN (migration 329, 2026-07-29): scribe_tenant_config.specialty_relevance_enabled, tri-state so NULL keeps the pre-329 derived answer (a settled profile: needs_confirm = FALSE), TRUE forces it on and FALSE turns it off even for a confirmed profile — the state the derived gate could not express. The same migration widened the template_source CHECK so `tenant-specialty` and `care-setting` PERSIST as themselves instead of being flattened onto `specialty`, and the recorder chip names them apart. The admin Specialty picker gap Stage 5 opened is closed: it now offers every template-bearing specialty and persists the CANONICAL SLUG, with existing legacy-tag values deliberately NOT migrated. The stage stays `partial` only because the Stage-5 template tail and the four Stage-3/GA follow-ups below remain open. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30: test family F2 (docs/testing/scribe-e2e-test-plan.md section 5) executed all EIGHT rungs of resolveForClinician over real HTTP — 15/15 — asserting the PERSISTED scribe_sessions.template_source by direct Postgres query, with a decoy default on the tier above wherever one is possible so no rung passed by elimination. The two Stage-4 rungs this stage shipped are confirmed live and distinctly: F2-07 landed 'tenant-specialty'/system-dentistry (exactly one declared specialty, relevanceEnabled:true, clinician with no qualification) and F2-08 landed 'care-setting'/system-geriatrics (TWO declared specialties, so R10 correctly abstains and R11's care-setting rung answers) — migration 329's widened CHECK is therefore proven to persist the two tiers separately rather than flattening both to 'specialty'. Evidence docs/status/evidence/scribe-e2e/f2-results.json + f2-summary.md. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30 (F13 + F16, the two whole-surface sweeps): every one of the 43 derived /scribe/* route/method pairs is REACHABLE by a real ["clinician","tenant-admin"] token through the real global RBAC hook (F16 43/43) — so the class of defect that once left ten scribe routes 403ing every real caller is measured absent rather than assumed absent, and the measurement carries its own falsifying control (the same classifier denies tenant-member on 26/26 mutating pairs and office-admin on 40/43). Cross-tenant isolation holds on 42 of 43 (F13): tenant B, with its own token and its own entitlement, is refused on every id-bearing route using tenant A's ids, the shared-by-name patient probe returns only its own, and tenant A's rows are byte-identical after the sweep. The one hole is D19 — POST /scribe/sessions never resolves patientId, so a session can be opened on another tenant's patient id (referential, not a PHI read; see the remaining bullet). F16 also surfaced D18 (a malformed template section is an unhandled 500, not a 400). Evidence docs/status/evidence/scribe-e2e/f13-f16-results.json + f13-f16-summary.md.

remaining: [antepartum-built-verified-20260806] ANTEPARTUM — BUILT AND VERIFIED 2026-08-06 (PRs #826, #831). The record has a home, it is linked in the nav, its LOINC codes have been checked against the register rather than merely flagged, and the single remaining item is stated in the last clause of this bullet — READ THAT rather than this sentence, which has already been wrong twice today for summarising a residue that kept changing underneath it. SETTLED (founder decision 2026-07-29, docs/decisions/2026-07-29-scribe-observation-write-boundary.md): the scribe NEVER writes FHIR Observations; vitals ingestion stays device-only, and the transcript-extraction design the investigation had converged on is declined, not deferred. ENFORCED as of 2026-08-03 (apps/api/src/scribe-observation-write-boundary.test.ts): the device-only decision now fails the build if any scribe module constructs an Observation. It was previously unenforced in the strongest sense — assertScribeSignGate (packages/storage/src/scribe-sign-guard.ts) returns early for every resourceType other than Composition, so a scribe-written Observation would have passed ZERO gates. The scan covers all 61 production scribe sources across apps/api/src/scribe-*.ts and packages/scribe/src, separates WRITES from the legitimate READS that exist today (the pre-visit-brief compendium walk), and carries a falsifying control on both halves. THE OPEN PRODUCT QUESTION IS ANSWERED (founder, 2026-08-06): device-only bars PATIENT self-logging and bars the SCRIBE — it does not bar a clinician. A clinician-facing manual-entry surface is permitted. The strict reading was offered explicitly, with its consequence stated (antepartum becomes unbuildable and should be closed as declined), and was not taken; so was a named-exceptions list. The general allowance was chosen, which matches the sibling-project rule this was copied from — applying it as "nobody may type a vital" was a transcription error, not a decision. Recorded as an amendment in docs/decisions/2026-07-29-scribe-observation-write-boundary.md. NOTHING ENFORCED WAS WEAKENED: the scribe still never writes an Observation (the build gate is unchanged), patients still cannot self-log, and there is still no antepartum template. The gate header now states its scope explicitly, because a future reader would otherwise read it as barring all manual entry — and the manual-entry surface must NOT be placed under scribe-*, since a measurement inferred from a transcript is a different claim from one a clinician typed. BOTH PIECES ARE NOW BUILT (2026-08-06), so nothing on this bullet is blocked on a decision OR on an unwritten primitive. (a) THE CLINICIAN MANUAL-ENTRY SURFACE: POST /clinical/observations, apps/api/src/clinical-manual-observation.ts + clinical-flowsheet-routes.ts. It is NOT the generic POST /Observation, and that was MEASURED before it was decided: the generic FHIR REST surface already accepts it and derives (write, Observation), but a bare Observation records NO PROVENANCE, so a hand-typed measurement and a device reading become indistinguishable in the chart forever — which is the entire substance of the ruling. The route writes the Observation and its Provenance AS ONE ACT. It is also not the device webhook, whose HMAC envelope IS the claim that a device produced the value (and which, measured, does not produce FHIR Observations at all — it writes vital_readings, migration 073, so the two are different records rather than competing implementations). Not under scribe-*; that build gate is unchanged. THE FAILURE IT REFUSES TO HIDE: if the Observation lands and the Provenance does not, the chart holds an UNQUALIFIED measurement created by the mechanism meant to qualify it. No cross-resource transaction exists at that seam, so it answers 500 with the orphaned id rather than 201 — a 201 there is the outcome nobody investigates. (b) THE FLOWSHEET PIVOT: apps/api/src/observation-flowsheet.ts + GET /clinical/flowsheet + /admin/clinical/flowsheet. Nothing new is queried — it reshapes rows that already exist, exactly as this bullet predicted. The pivot answers a question the raw rows do not (WHICH COLUMN a measurement belongs to) and every answer can be wrong silently, so: Encounter wins when there is one; otherwise a 6h time window (calendar-day bucketing was rejected — a visit straddling midnight splits in two and a patient seen twice in one day collapses into one); an inferred column is LABELLED, because rendering it like a recorded visit asserts a structure the data does not contain; two readings of one code at one visit COLLIDE and the displaced one is NAMED, because a repeat blood pressure is the first reading of a hypertensive workup; and a code with no data still gets a row, because "we never measured fundal height" is a finding. A UI DECISION MADE RATHER THAN DEFERRED: the flowsheet is a PAGE, not a tab on the patient chart — it grows a column per visit and a tab would force horizontal scrolling inside a card from the first trimester. Reachable by link, so folding it in later is a route change. On screen, an UNMARKED cell does not read as "device": the marker absence also covers a provenance lookup that failed, so it says nothing rather than asserting the stronger thing. 55 tests (pivot 15, builders 19, routes 12, view 11 minus overlap); RBAC mapped onto the canonical Observation verbs so no new grant was needed; gates 80/80. THE CODES WERE THEN CHECKED (2026-08-06, same day) AND THE CHECK EARNED ITS KEEP — one of the three was WRONG. 11881-0 CONFIRMED: the LOINC record is "Uterus Fundal height TAPE MEASURE", and the method is what confirms it rather than the name — a tape measure is exactly the act being recorded. 55283-6 CONFIRMED and it answers the note's actual worry: it is "Fetal Heart rate" with Component "Heart rate", System "^Fetus", Property NRat, Scale Qn, Class H&P.HX, ACTIVE, and METHOD: NONE — the general method-agnostic concept, not one of the method-specific variants (11633-5 reactivity by US, 89692-8 a 10-minute mean), which is right for a flowsheet that does not record how the rate was obtained. 11875-2 REFUTED: it is "Fetal position US" — a DIFFERENT observation (position, not presentation) by a DIFFERENT method (ultrasound, not the palpation an antepartum visit uses). Wrong on BOTH axes, which is precisely why it survived a plausibility read, and precisely the silent mis-file the needs-clinical-review marker existed to catch. FETAL PRESENTATION IS THEREFORE NOT SHIPPED AT ALL, rather than shipped with a downgraded flag: a wrong code in a dropdown a clinician can select is worse than an absent one, because it files silently and reads as data forever after. The refusal is recorded IN CODE as ANTEPARTUM_UNRESOLVED_CODES (apps/api/src/clinical-manual-observation.ts) carrying the rejected code, what it actually means, the two candidates that are closer with why NEITHER is adoptable (11877-8 "Fetal presentation US" — right concept, still asserts ultrasound; 73761-9 — a birth-certificate field about presentation AT BIRTH, not a serial antepartum observation), and what would settle it. A search on 2026-08-06 did not locate a method-less variant; the LOINC Antepartum record panel 57082-0 is the next place to look. unreviewedAntepartumCodes() is now EMPTY, and a test pins that this is NOT the same as "nothing outstanding" — it is empty because the unsettled one was removed. THE NAV LINK IS DONE: /admin/clinical/flowsheet is in the sidebar (id clinical-flowsheet, apps/admin/src/lib/nav-model.ts), ungated because both routes are RBAC-gated server-side onto the canonical Observation verbs with no entitlement check. nav-model.test.ts pins the LINK rather than the page, because the page already had tests and the link is what was missing. WHAT IS STILL LEFT, and it is now ONE thing rather than four: NO LIVE CLINICAL USE, and the fetal-presentation code needs either a method-less LOINC concept or a clinical decision to accept 11877-8 and record only ultrasound-determined presentation. The pivot is code-agnostic, so a practice that settles it can pass the code to GET /clinical/flowsheet?codes=... without a code change.

[scribe-audio-reference-residual] SCRIBE AUDIO REFERENCE — residual only (ADR 0153/0154, narrowed again 2026-08-04 by migration 355). WHAT IS LEFT: (a) CLOSED 2026-08-05 — the HEAD-only probe exists. IChunkStore gained `statAssembled` (apps/api/src/scribe-chunk-store.ts), implemented as a real S3 HeadObjectCommand and derived from readAssembled in memory so the two can never disagree about whether a session has audio; probeScribeAudioBytes now uses it, so proving an assembled object absent no longer transfers a whole visit's recording per session per pass. That transfer cost was the stated reason this sweep is operator-driven rather than scheduled, so the blocker to running it on a timer is removed — SCHEDULED 2026-08-05 (scheduleScribeAudioRefSurvey + surveyScribeAudioRefsOnce in apps/api/src/scribe-audio-durability.ts, wired at apps/api/src/index.ts; CERNIA_SCRIBE_AUDIO_SURVEY_INTERVAL_MS, hourly by default, 0 disables, a garbage value disables rather than silently reverting to the default). It SURVEYS and can never execute: the scheduler takes no execute argument and no env var reaches one. That is the load-bearing part rather than caution — absent means the store answered and had nothing, which is EXACTLY what a bucket/prefix/region misconfiguration returns, cleanly, so it never reaches the unknown arm. An executing timer would turn one config typo into thousands of irreversible rows each asserting a specific patient recording is gone, and would be self-confirming because the next tick finds nothing to do after the first erased the evidence. Writing stays a per-tenant decision a human makes with the survey in front of them. A new wholesale-absence log action fires when every candidate probed absent and none was present, naming the misconfiguration explanation rather than leaving an operator to infer it from a count. Gated by apps/api/src/scribe-audio-survey-schedule.integration.test.ts (11 tests, real Postgres) whose central assertion is the ABSENCE of a write, paired with a positive control that the identical state DOES write under execute:true - without it the no-write assertion would pass on a function that did nothing - plus controls that one surviving object suppresses the warning and an empty sweep does not trigger it. ALSO FIXED: probeScribeAudioBytes carried a docstring still claiming the seam exposed no HEAD and that the probe downloaded each object, contradicting its own body twenty lines below since #812. Proven by a store double that RECORDS its commands (apps/api/src/scribe-audio-head-probe.test.ts, 9 tests): a probe issues HeadObjectCommand and NO GetObjectCommand, with a falsifying control that it still answers `present` when the bytes are there. The load-bearing arm is absent-vs-unreachable: an unreachable store THROWS so the reconciler records `unknown`, because `null` means absent and the reconciler writes destruction rows off absent — a store that swallowed an outage would convert downtime into a permanent record that a patient's audio was gone. (b) CLOSED 2026-08-05 — the Provenance is still not rewritten, and now it does not have to be. buildSignProvenance keeps the audio ref verbatim (ADR 0153/0154: a Provenance records what the signer ACTUALLY USED, and editing it when the audio is later destroyed would falsify the audit trail). What was missing was the SECOND question — what does that reference point at today, and if nothing, was that a decision or a loss. GET /scribe/sessions/:id/audio-state answers it beside the resource: refAtSign plus one of five states (never-recorded / destroyed / present / absent / unknown), each with a sentence. The distinctions are the point: `destroyed` carries completedAt and the reason and is only claimed for a COMPLETED destruction over audio that existed (an ordered-but-unconfirmed row, or a nothing-to-destroy row under migration 351, is NOT a destruction); `absent` with no destruction record is an unexplained LOSS and says so; `unknown` is an unreachable store and is never folded into absence. A recorded destruction wins over a probe that still finds bytes, and the contradiction is surfaced as a WARNING rather than hidden. apps/api/src/scribe-audio-ref-state.ts + the route in scribe-audio-routes.ts (12 tests). parseScribeAudioRef lets a reader holding ONLY the Provenance recover the session id from either ref scheme; the parsed tenant is explicitly informational — the route is session-keyed and takes the tenant from the CLAIM, because a ref-keyed lookup would have turned a compliance convenience into a cross-tenant probe (ADR 0004). The presence probe is the HEAD-only statAssembled, so answering the question does not download a visit. NOT CLAIMED: no UI consumes this route yet. (c) NARROWED 2026-08-06 — rows ordered BEFORE 2026-08-04 NO LONGER CLAIM a measurement they never took. scribeAudioDestructionStatus gained a fourth value, destroyed-unverified, for a completed destruction whose pre-order presence is NULL, and GET /scribe/sessions/:id/audio-state carries verified:false plus a sentence saying the removal of bytes is an assumption rather than a finding. THE SAFETY PREDICATE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WEAKENED: scribeAudioWasDestroyed still answers true for those rows, because two callers use it to WITHHOLD — the transcript seek route would otherwise hand a reviewer a timestamp into audio a patient may have withdrawn consent over, and the ref-state surface would relabel every legacy destruction as an unexplained LOSS. Both measured before changing it; both pinned in scribe-audio-destruction-unverified.test.ts (13 tests). ADR 0154 amended. Nothing is backfilled, because any value chosen would be the invention this avoids. WHAT REMAINS of this clause: a ref nulled before migration 355 by anything other than the reconciler is unexplainable, permanently — no environment or backfill changes that, The superseded wording is in history[] rather than trailing here, so this bullet ends on what is actually left: a ref nulled before migration 355 by anything other than the reconciler is unexplainable, permanently. No environment change and no backfill fixes that, because any value chosen would be the invention this whole clause exists to avoid.

history.note: J04 CONSENT-DECLINE SEAM — A PATIENT'S REFUSAL TO BE RECORDED IS NOW A RECORDABLE FACT. Consent was the PRESENCE OF A ROW (migration 305), so a patient who refused and a visit nobody ever asked about were the same database state: the product could honour a refusal but never PROVE it had. Measured live on github/main 47d679f5 it was worse than unmodelled — POST /scribe/sessions/:id/consent {decision:'declined'} answered 201 and recorded an AFFIRMATIVE, after which audio was accepted (202), the audio object assembled (200), the audio downloadable (200) and the transcript readable (200) on the refused session; a second clinician's bodyless POST also returned 200 and the note then drafted. Migration 338 adds decision (granted|declined|revoked) + decided_by/decided_at + revoked_at/revoked_by to scribe_recording_consents (attested_by/attested_at nullable: a decline never had an attestation; a revocation KEEPS them beside revoked_at because those two together are the only evidence the audio already captured was captured lawfully) plus an append-only scribe_recording_consent_events table so a change of mind cannot erase the refusal. hasConsent() is now true ONLY for decision='granted', so all 17 consent-gated route guards close on declined AND revoked with no route change — the sweep was RE-PROVED on both states after the change (17/17 → 403 consent-required, zero artifacts) alongside the never-asked control and the consented control. POST /consent now takes {decision} and 400s anything unrecognised (a bodyless post still means granted — the shipped recorder contract); POST /$revoke-consent is the withdrawal; GET /consent is the audit read. Consent decisions are OWNER-gated like $cancel. A declined session is the new terminal status 'declined' instead of sitting in the clinician's list as 'recording' with a live Record button, and getDraft propagates the API's own 403 reason instead of flattening every 403 to 'forbidden' — the clause J04 actually failed on, re-measured first (PR #723 had not reached it). Live BROKEN→FIXED evidence with the same runner, DB and fixtures: docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/j04-consent-broken.json (3/12) vs j04-consent-fixed.json (13/13), summary + 4 browser screenshots in j04-consent-summary.md.

F8-06b: after $amend a re-sign is 409 already-signed and the note is STILL 'amended' in the database, never reverted to 'final'. Artifacts were COUNTED, not statuses — a status-only assertion passes on the unfixed code too, which is exactly how D1 shipped. NEW P0 DEFECT D14 (open, from case F8-04b which was NOT in the plan): the KTD5 storage guard covers 'final' but NOT 'amended'. packages/storage/src/scribe-sign-guard.ts:58 returns early unless status === 'final', while the route gate treats final AND amended as post-signature states (isSignedStatus, packages/scribe/src/sign-gate.ts:33). So POST /Composition with {status:'amended', meta.tag=[scribe-note]} is 201 CREATED AND PERSISTED — a signed legal record minted outside the clinician sign action, bypassing the owner check, the clinician-role check, AE1 consent, the Provenance and the DocumentReference. The lesson is sharper than the bug: D1's OWN FIX on 2026-07-29 widened this predicate at the route layer and did not mirror it onto the storage layer, and packages/storage/src/scribe-sign-guard.test.ts has never contained the word 'amended', so nothing failed. When a predicate is duplicated across two enforcement layers, widening one is a defect in the other. NOT FIXED HERE — this change is the harness and the red. D4 HALF-REPRODUCED, HALF WITHDRAWN (F8-04): a 'final' scribe-tagged Composition over HTTP → 500 with a FHIR OperationOutcome severity=fatal code=exception where a 403 belongs, so the status-mapping half is real and now has a baseline. The INVARIANT HELD (0 rows persisted, confirmed independently by a manual probe) and the guard is correctly SCOPED — the untagged-'final' control is accepted 201, which is what makes the 500 attributable to the scribe guard rather than to a generally broken POST /Composition. BUT D4's 'leaking the exception message' claim is NOT reproducible on current code: diagnostics is a generic 'An unexpected error occurred.'. That half of the defect row is withdrawn, which narrows the fix to error-code mapping and removes the information-disclosure argument for prioritising it. The first three all 400 BEFORE the gate under test, so each would have made a case fail (or pass) for a reason unrelated to what it asserts. The port/DB pairing was PROVED not assumed — a throwaway tenant's /dev/login on :8153 wrote 18 rows to scribe_f1 and 0 to scribe_e2e. That check is not ceremonial here: apps/api/.env names DB_NAME=scribe_e2e, so a failed env override would have run every consent assertion against the wrong database and still looked green. The env now lives in ONE file that both the boot script and the runner source, and the runner writes the stack into the artifact from its own process.env, so §0.3 cannot claim a stack the API did not boot with. THREE TEST-SIDE BUGS ARE RECORDED IN §7 because each impersonated a product finding, and all three are the same failure mode — an assertion wrong in a direction that looks like a defect: (1) a sentinel string containing a literal NUL byte used as a SQL LIKE parameter, which Postgres rejects with SQLSTATE 22021 and which surfaced mid-F3-05 as a stack trace that read like a product crash; (2) `count === 1` on Provenances, which FAILS ON CORRECT CODE since a signed note carries three — reported as F8-01/F8-02/F8-06 failures on the first run; (3) a falsifying CONTROL sharing a title prefix with its SUBJECT, so F8-04 counted the control it was supposed to exclude and the artifact said persistedFinalRows=1, reading like a KTD5 breach that had not happened. The lesson kept in the plan: a control and its subject must never share a matching prefix, and an invariant should be reported as its own field rather than folded into a pass/fail boolean.

D1 (P0 clinical-record defect) CLOSED — `POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$sign` could sign an ALREADY-SIGNED session. apps/api/src/scribe-sign-routes.ts passed a hard-coded `currentStatus:'preliminary'` into assertSignAllowed, which made packages/scribe/src/sign-gate.ts's `post-sign-immutable` branch unreachable from the ONLY route that can mint a `final` note; the sole other guard (`409 no-draft`) fires on a null composition_ref, which a signed session does not have. A second call therefore re-wrote the Composition, minted a SECOND DocumentReference, wrote a SECOND Provenance and RE-FIRED the EHR write-back — a duplicate signed legal note in the patient's chart AND a duplicate document pushed into the practice's EHR. FIX: the route now READS the Composition before the gate and passes its real status. The Composition was judged the authoritative signature record over scribe_sessions.status, because the session row is a mirror the route updates LAST and can therefore lag a note that is already `final` — exactly the partial-failure shape in which the duplicate is minted. BEHAVIOUR: an already-`final` note whose session is `signed` REPLAYS the existing result (200 + `alreadySigned:true`, nothing written), because at the HTTP layer a retry of a lost 200 is indistinguishable from a deliberate re-sign and rejecting would strand a note the clinician believes is unsigned; a note that has moved PAST its signature is refused `409 already-signed` — 409 not 403 because the caller is fully authorised and it is the RESOURCE STATE that forbids the transition, consistent with $amend / $push-to-ehr (`409 not-signed`) and PUT /draft (`409 post-sign-immutable`). A SECOND, UNREPORTED defect surfaced while fixing: sign-gate's immutability branch tested only `final`, so re-signing an `amended` note — the state $amend leaves composition_ref pointing at — passed the gate and would have REVERTED a legally amended note to `final` plus minted another document. Generalized to isSignedStatus() (`final`|`amended`), which also stops a signed note being reverted to a draft. PROOF: apps/api/src/scribe-sign-routes.integration.test.ts describe `D1 — repeat $sign never duplicates the signed record` counts ARTIFACTS rather than status codes (Composition writes, DocumentReferences, Provenances, EHR pushes) and was watched RED on main — "expected [ { …(5) }, { …(5) } ] to have a length of 1 but got 2" — alongside a red `409` assertion for the amended case; plus 5 new sign-gate unit tests (red first) and a real sign→$amend chain test proving the legitimate post-sign path still works. That suite also now bootstraps migration 316 so the EHR write-back count is real, narrowing D8 for this file. VERIFIED: @cernia/scribe 371/371, all 44 apps/api scribe suites 495/495, @cernia/api typecheck + build clean; the one lint error on scribe-sign-routes.ts (`require-await` on scribeSignRoutes) is carry-forward, proven present on baseline via `git stash push` of that single file.

Migration 329's tri-state flag became SELF-SERVE: apps/admin/src/app/admin/settings/practice-profile/page.tsx now renders the control a tenant admin was missing, so flipping specialty-relevance no longer requires an operator with direct API access. Shipped as a THREE-option select (testid `relevance-enabled`), deliberately NOT a checkbox: `scribe_tenant_config.specialty_relevance_enabled` is tri-state and the third state is not a polite 'off' — it is 'never chose', which TRACKS the practice profile (on once needs_confirm clears, off while it has not) and is the state every tenant is in today. A checkbox would have to render it as one of the two explicit answers, misreporting what the tenant is actually getting and deleting the only route back to it once touched. The page also states which way the default currently resolves for THIS tenant (testid `relevance-default-explainer`), read off the saved profile rather than guessed, so an admin does not have to experiment on live notes to find out. WIRE CONTRACT, and the subtle part: the unset state is carried by ABSENCE, not by a null — the server omits `relevanceEnabled` entirely for a tenant that never chose (R15: an unset tenant's response is byte-identical to pre-329). So the client types it `relevanceEnabled?: boolean` and NOT `boolean | null`, and the save OMITS the key when the admin did not move the control (server reads absent as 'leave it alone') while sending an explicit `null` when they return it to the default (server reads null as 'clear the choice'). Those are three distinct instructions and apps/admin/.../practice-profile-api.ts builds the PUT body key-by-key rather than letting JSON.stringify erase an undefined, so the distinction does not rest on implicit behaviour. ANTI-SILENT-FAILURE: the control renders from the SERVER's echo after a save, never the optimistic local pick, and an 'unsaved' marker (testid `relevance-unsaved`) stays lit whenever the draft diverges from stored — so a failed write cannot leave the switch standing there showing a value that never landed. No new API route and no new deriveOperation mapping: GET/PUT /admin/practice-profile were already mapped to read|write TenantSpecialtyProfile in apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts. Tests: apps/admin/src/app/admin/settings/practice-profile/page.test.tsx +10 (25 total) pinning all three states in both directions, the omit-vs-null distinction, the failed-save marker, and server-echo-wins. RBAC completeness gate generalised from /scribe/* to the WHOLE API, and the blast radius it exposed measured and partly closed. NEW: apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.repo-coverage.test.ts. It walks every `<instance>.<method>(` call in all 623 non-test modules under apps/api/src -- skipping a generic argument list, resolving a `${CONST}` template prefix against the file's own string constants -- and finds 972 route declarations across 253 files. It then subtracts the FIVE places registerRbacHook authorises OUTSIDE the RBAC model (the unauth allow-list INCLUDING buildApp's boot-time extension of it, TEST_MODE_DISABLE_RBAC, the service-identity branch, the self-introspection pass, the platform-operator pass) and fails on any remaining route that lands on the deny-all catch-all, OR that is mapped onto a verb no default role grants. THE SCRAPER IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART, so it is guarded rather than trusted: a >900 route floor, a >200 file floor, eight named routes from unrelated families each exercising a different registration style, and an EXACT list of the one declaration it cannot resolve statically (observability-middleware.ts's config-driven Prometheus scrape path -- its default GET /metrics is scraped from index.ts anyway). Reading only the module-level permitAllForUnauthenticatedRoutes would have reported four boot-exempt families as broken, so the boot extension is scraped from index.ts too, with an assertion that the block was found. THE FINDING: 172 tenant-facing routes across ~49 modules had NO mapping and were 403ing before their handler -- the same defect as billing-write, the developer portal and the ten scribe routes, at 17x the scale. 101 were mapped here in 27 families whose route-file headers name apps/admin or the clinic UI as the consumer (email templates, schedule import, telehealth visits, RPM clinic reads, voice budget, ML pipeline + drift, LLM gateway, billing alert queue, usage thresholds, marketplace entitlements, revenue recognition, surveys, setup tasks, MEDD, tenant secrets/brand assets/custom-domain/SMTP, the remaining /admin/billing surface, workflow+bot $run, cross-org report, referral fax log, voice ingress). Verb rule applied per route and stated in the code: collection GET -> search, item GET -> read, mutating POST/PUT/PATCH -> write, DELETE -> delete, and a POST that is PURE COMPUTE over caller-supplied input -> read, because mapping a read as a write would lock tenant-member (which holds only *:read / *:search) out of something it should see. The block is APPENDED AT THE END of the if-chain deliberately: every path in it previously resolved to the catch-all, so it cannot swallow an earlier branch -- and the neighbours it sits beside are asserted to still resolve unchanged. /cernia-ops/* is EXCLUDED, with the inversion documented in the test: there an unmapped path is the CORRECT deny for a non-operator, and mapping one would make the hook log an ALLOW and demote the real decision to the handler's requireSuperAdmin (the allow-then-deny bug this repo already shipped and fixed on isolation-posture-summary). A dedicated test locks that exclusion in both directions so it cannot be tidied away. FALSIFIED BEFORE SHIPPING, twice: deleting the /admin/setup-tasks mapping turns the gate red naming `GET /admin/setup-tasks`, and re-pointing that same mapping at a custom verb turns the unbound-verb check red naming the same route. (The first version of the scribe gate asserted deriveOperation(...) === undefined, which nothing ever returns, so it passed while reporting nothing -- not repeated.) WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED is in the two exactly-asserted lists and in `remaining`: 71 routes stay unmapped with a per-family reason, and 13 stay mapped-but-unbound because closing them means widening default-roles.ts, which was out of scope. Stage 4 — the resolution tier + the relevance filter. THE HEADLINE (PRD R10): a dental tenant with no clinician qualification and no defaults anywhere now resolves system-dentistry, not SOAP. That is the defect the whole programme exists for, and apps/api/src/scribe-specialty-relevance.integration.test.ts "R10 — THE HEADLINE" is the assertion that says so, against real Postgres. (1) apps/api/src/note-template-store.ts — resolveForClinician gains two rungs BELOW the clinician-specialty match and above SOAP: `tenant-specialty` (R10) and `care-setting` (R11). TemplateResolutionSource is widened with both; every pre-existing value is untouched. The profile store is an INJECTED, OPTIONAL dependency (NoteTemplateStoreOptions.specialtyProfiles) — a store constructed without it cannot execute either rung, so R15's regression guard holds by construction, and the test proves it by running the same inputs through a Stage-4 store and a pre-Stage-4 store and comparing tier for tier. The profile read happens at the BOTTOM of the chain, so the common paths (a saved default, a recognised credential) cost no extra query, and it is fail-soft: a missing table degrades to the old chain rather than aborting a capture. (2) apps/api/src/scribe-template-relevance.ts — ONE module owns "what does this tenant practice, and what follows from that", so the tier and the picker can never disagree about a tenant. THE MULTI-SPECIALTY DECISION lives here: the tenant rung fires only when the tenant declared EXACTLY ONE specialty. A tenant with two or more has told us its clinicians are not all one thing (R2 made that representable on purpose), and picking one for a clinician we cannot identify is a coin flip whose losing side is a cardiology note on a nephrology visit — strictly worse than SOAP, which is generic and reads as generic. Cardinality is measured on the DECLARED set, not on the subset that happens to carry a template, so [cardiology, nephrology] abstains too: ambiguity is a property of what the practice said, not of our library's coverage. Abstaining does not strand the tenant — the care-setting rung still runs. (3) packages/scribe/src/care-setting-templates.ts — the (*, care_setting) map, TOTAL over CareSettingSlug by `satisfies` so a care setting added upstream is a compile error until somebody decides what it drafts with. skilled-nursing -> system-geriatrics (the 4Ms note IS the SNF round document: functional status, cognition, mobility/falls, deprescribing, what-matters); hospice, ED, inpatient and urgent-care map to their obvious documents; office / telehealth / home are DELIBERATELY undefined — office shapes nothing, telehealth is a modality not a document shape, and home has no shipped template, so guessing would be the wrong-specialty defect the PRD forbids. ORDERING CALL, recorded as an assertion rather than left implicit: an INTERNIST in a SNF still gets the internal-medicine note, because (specialty, *) outranks (*, care_setting) in the PRD's own chain and Stage 4 places both new rungs below the clinician-specialty match. The PRD's prose ("an internist working in a SNF gets the SNF-shaped note") reads the other way and the two cannot both hold; flipping the order is a one-line change if the setting should dominate. (4) GET /scribe/templates (apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts) — relevance ordering with the reveal SHIPPING IN THE SAME RESPONSE: `items` leads with the tenant's specialties, then the care-setting template, then tenant-authored rows, then SOAP; `hidden` carries the rest of the system library so "Show all specialties" is a client-side concat, not a second query; `?all=true` returns the flat pre-Stage-4 list. Tenant-authored templates and SOAP are never hidden. A tenant with no profile, or with the gate off, gets the original list in the original order with NEITHER new field present — byte-identical over the wire, which is what makes R15 checkable by a client. (5) THE PER-TENANT GATE is derived, not a column: ON iff a profile row exists AND needs_confirm is FALSE. A migrated guess the tenant has not seen is not consent, and no row at all is off. This is PRD rollout step 4 ("enable for new tenants first, then existing ones once the prompt has run") expressed against data that already exists, because a flag column is a migration and Stage 4's scope excluded one — see `remaining` for the DDL still owed and why the persisted template_source is narrowed to `specialty` for now. The gate is injectable at both call sites so a column-backed reader drops in without touching the logic. (6) apps/admin/src/lib/clinician-specialty.ts — the picker gap Stage 5 opened is closed. Options derive from SPECIALTIES[].templateId, so all 24 template-bearing specialties are selectable (the fourteen Stage-5 templates were previously unreachable from the admin UI entirely), plus dental-restorative, which is derived from SCRIBE_TAG_MAP as the one legacy tag with a template and no canonical slug (R13). It PERSISTS THE CANONICAL SLUG; existing legacy values are NOT migrated and specialtySelectOptions(current) keeps a stored legacy tag selected so an edit form cannot blank it. (7) Carry-forward fixed in passing: apps/api typecheck was RED on baseline with 2 pre-existing errors in Stage 3's backfill (indexing ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP's nine literal keys with a runtime string). Fixed with a local widening that can MISS, typed to say so — the map's literal keys are load-bearing upstream and must not be widened there.
