R16 PLATFORM HALF — the operator-facing fleet view of the specialty-migration audit. Stage 3 shipped the tenant-facing half only; per CLAUDE.md a feature that surfaces in apps/admin but not apps/cernia-ops is half-shipped, and 'which tenants did we auto-map, from what, and how many are still unconfirmed' was unanswerable without SQL. (1) apps/api/src/specialty-migration-fleet-store.ts — a SEPARATE platform-scoped module, deliberately NOT a cross-tenant method on tenant-specialty-profile-store.ts: that store's tenant scoping is a safety property, and a getAllTenants() sitting beside get(tenantId) is how it gets lost. One FULL OUTER JOIN of tenant_specialty_profiles (328) to tenant_summary (062) — full outer because neither side is authoritative: a freshly provisioned tenant can have a profile before the nightly roster refresh, and an un-backfilled tenant has a roster row and no profile. Either LEFT JOIN silently drops exactly the population the view exists to surface. Totals, worklist and rollup are all derived from that one row set so they cannot disagree. (2) The from->to ROLLUP is the point, not the flat list: per legacy value it shows what ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP decided, how many tenants are still on that guess, and every target a human CORRECTED to with a count. mapLikelyWrong fires when >= CORRECTION_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD (2) tenants converge on the SAME target that DISAGREES with the map — agreement, not volume, because two tenants correcting one value to two different answers means the legacy value was ambiguous (which the map may already record via needsConfirm), not that the decision was wrong. A 'correction' that lands on the map's own answer is marked agreesWithMap and confirms the decision instead of counting against it. (3) THE WORKLIST INCLUDES TENANTS WITH NO PROFILE ROW, with reason 'no-profile'. Unmapped is not confirmed; dropping them would make the worklist look finished. totals.unresolved = needsConfirm + withoutProfile. (4) apps/api/src/specialty-migration-fleet-routes.ts — GET /cernia-ops/platform/specialty-migration, requireSuperAdmin + sendPhiSafe, READ-ONLY (an operator changes a tenant profile via the audited $impersonate flow, never a fleet view; CLAUDE.md invariant 6). (5) deriveOperation: the route is DELIBERATELY LEFT UNMAPPED and iam-route-guards.ts now documents why, because 'always register the route' is the correct reflex for a TENANT-scoped path and the wrong one here. /cernia-ops/* is authorised for its intended caller by the platform-operator pass, which runs BEFORE rbacEvaluate; mapping the path onto any synthetic type a tenant-admin's {'*','admin'} covers would make the hook log an allow and demote the real decision to a handler check — the audit-misleading allow-then-deny already found and fixed on /cernia-ops/isolation-posture-summary. specialty-migration-fleet-routes.deriveoperation.test.ts pins the catch-all, proves against real buildDefaultRoles output that no default tenant role covers it, carries /admin/practice-profile as the control that keeps the negative assertions honest, and then proves the thing that actually matters end to end through the REAL registerRbacHook: a tenant-admin with a real signed JWT and a real {'*','admin'} RoleBinding gets 403 AT THE HOOK ('RBAC denied' diagnostics, handler never runs), while a cernia-super-admin token with no RoleBinding at all passes and gets 200. (6) apps/cernia-ops/src/app/cernia-ops/platform/specialty-migration — @cernia/ui primitives, semantic tokens, lucide icons, cookie-session fetchOpsJson like every sibling fleet view; the map-likely-wrong signal is a banner naming the legacy value rather than a flag to spot in a table. Axes render as SLUGS, not prose labels: this is an audit of a mapping, so the stored value is the thing to show, and the map's own rationale arrives as mapNote. (7) PHI: the payload is tenant id + tenant display name + taxonomy slugs + counts + full ISO instants. Those slugs describe the PRACTICE, never a patient — which is why migration 328 records the table as carrying no PHI and Stage 3 classified it erase-on-tenant with no independent retention obligation. confirmed_by is NOT selected: a named individual inside the tenant that a mapping audit does not need. Timestamps are full ISO instants because assertNoPhi reads a bare YYYY-MM-DD as DOB-shaped and would 500 the route. PROOF: 9 route/store tests against real Postgres :5433 (from->to, correction rollup, the map-is-wrong signal AND its negative control, the no-profile worklist member, totals reconciliation, 401/403, zero-PHI payload), 7 deriveOperation/RBAC-gate tests, 9 cernia-ops page tests. FINDING: the dev database has no human-corrected tenant, so the mapLikelyWrong signal is proven by seeded fixtures only and says nothing yet about ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP's nine real decisions -- the backfill has still not been run against any live database (separate bullet above).

Stage 5 — 14 specialty note templates shipped in evidence-led tier order (packages/scribe/src/specialty-templates.ts, library 11 -> 25). Each carries the standard it is grounded in as a code comment directly above it, so R12 is checkable without guessing. TIER 1, the two gaps that close the Stage-2 narrowing: system-emergency-medicine (AMA CPT 2023 E/M revision + ACEP 2023 guidance — the ED visit level is MDM-only, so the MDM section is `required` and must carry differential, data reviewed and risk; deliberately NOT the urgent-care shape, it adds a chronological ED course, reassessment and a justified disposition, asserted by test) and system-psychotherapy (CPT 90832/90834/90837 + 45 CFR 164.501, which EXCLUDES modality, frequency, session times, diagnosis, functional status, treatment plan and progress from the privileged 'psychotherapy notes' definition — the template documents ONLY that excluded set, i.e. a progress note for the designated record set and never a privileged note; no access-control mechanism implied or implemented, out of scope). TIER 2: system-hospital-medicine (CPT 99231-99233 as revised 2023 + SHM Core Competencies; inpatient progress-note shape, interval events first, A/P by problem, running discharge planning), system-obstetrics-gynecology (ACOG well-woman visit + chaperone documentation + cervical screening intervals; the AMBULATORY GYNECOLOGIC shape chosen deliberately and documented in-file — the ACOG antepartum record is a serial flowsheet and is NOT merged in), system-physical-therapy (CPT 97161-97163, whose four graded evaluation elements are the section list, + CMS timed-code minutes), system-hospice-palliative-medicine (NCP Clinical Practice Guidelines for Quality Palliative Care 4th ed. domains + Medicare hospice CoP 42 CFR 418.54/418.56). TIER 3 ambulatory coverage: system-gastroenterology (ACG/AGA alarm features + ACG CRC surveillance interval), system-endocrinology (ADA Standards of Care incl. CGM time-in-range + the annual complication-screening set), system-neurology (AAN exam domains + localization-first reasoning), system-ophthalmology (AAO Preferred Practice Pattern element order), system-otolaryngology (AAO-HNS CPGs keyed to otoscopy/laryngoscopy/audiometry), system-oncology (AJCC stage + NCI CTCAE grading + ECOG performance status), system-podiatry (ADA comprehensive diabetic foot exam + Wagner/UT wound classification), system-geriatrics (IHI Age-Friendly 4Ms + AGS Beers + CMS Annual Wellness Visit elements). Radiology, pathology and anesthesiology deliberately skipped (the taxonomy records they have no ambient encounter) as are the three escape hatches — asserted by test so none can acquire a template by accident. R14: every new section sets omitIfEmpty explicitly, so no conditional section can render an empty header; R13: no procedure type entered the specialty enum. TAXONOMY: templateId set on those 14 slugs in packages/specialty-taxonomy/src/specialties.ts (24 pointers now) — the only field edited in the otherwise frozen package. REACHABILITY, the load-bearing part: the new templates are tagged with their CANONICAL slug (inventing a 12th legacy tag would re-create the package-local vocabulary Stage 2 deleted), and the legacy matchSpecialtyTag can never return a slug, so packages/scribe/src/specialty-match.ts gained matchTemplateSpecialty() = legacy tag if one exists, else the canonical slug when SPECIALTIES[].templateId is set (DERIVED from the taxonomy, never hand-listed, so a future template becomes reachable the moment the pointer lands). matchSpecialtyFromCandidates — the one function apps/api/src/scribe-clinician-specialty.ts calls, whose result is handed straight to resolveDefaultTemplate and never persisted — now resolves template keys, while matchSpecialtyTag keeps its 11-value persisted wire vocabulary byte-identical for the callers that WRITE it. Stage 3 — tenant specialty projection + migration + confirm prompt. (1) packages/storage/src/migrations/328_tenant_specialty_profile.sql: one row per tenant, tenant_id PK (mirrors 055_tenant_customizations), org_type single / specialties TEXT[] SET-valued / care_setting single, needs_confirm + confirmed_at + confirmed_by, source ('migration'|'onboarding'|'admin') + legacy_value for R16, a GIN index on specialties, partial indexes for the R16 audit query and the confirm worklist, and a CHECK forbidding needs_confirm = TRUE alongside a non-null confirmed_at. Note what that CHECK deliberately does NOT require: needs_confirm = FALSE does not imply a stamp, because the three values the mapping was confident about (dental / physical-therapy / hospice) land settled WITHOUT anyone being asked. Requiring a timestamp there would have the database assert that a human confirmed something no human ever saw, and would leave R16 unable to separate "we were sure" from "they told us" — which is exactly what `source` exists to record. Slugs are validated in the APPLICATION layer, not by a CHECK, because the taxonomy tracks NUCC's twice-yearly releases and a CHECK would turn every vocabulary addition into a migration. (2) apps/api/src/tenant-specialty-profile-store.ts — InMemory + Postgres implementations. get() returns null for 'never derived', which is load-bearing: Stage 4 must be able to tell that from a real answer, so the store never fabricates a default. seed() is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, which buys idempotence and confirmation-preservation in one SQL clause instead of a read-then-write race. confirm() PRESERVES legacy_value so R16 survives a tenant correcting our guess. validateProfile() is the only slug gate (PRD R5) and collapses duplicates because the axis is a SET. (3) apps/api/src/tenant-specialty-profile-routes.ts — GET/PUT /admin/practice-profile. The tenant comes from rbacClaims only; the path carries no tenant id, so there is no cross-tenant addressing surface at all, and a smuggled body tenantId is ignored rather than validated (proven by test). confirmedBy is server-derived and cannot be forged. (4) apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts — BOTH verbs added to deriveOperation as read/write on the synthetic TenantSpecialtyProfile type. Without this the global hook falls through to the catch-all {verb:'*', resourceType:'*'}, which no binding covers, and 403s a legitimate tenant-admin BEFORE the handler runs — invisible to route tests that stub rbacClaims. tenant-specialty-profile-routes.integration.test.ts therefore asserts deriveOperation directly AND that a real buildDefaultRoles('tenant-admin') covers the result, with an unmapped-sibling control proving the assertion has teeth. FINDING: office-admin is NOT covered — {'*','admin'} belongs to tenant-admin alone, while office-admin is a scoped front-desk allow-list (Appointment/Patient/Task/Invoice/Communication) — so this route's isAdmin deliberately OMITS office-admin instead of copying the scribe predicate, which advertises an access path the hook denies. tenant-member CAN read (so a clinician sees the banner) but cannot write. (5) apps/api/src/backfill-tenant-specialty-profiles.ts — a SCRIPT, not a migration, for two reasons: the decision table is TypeScript (ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP; re-expressing those nine decisions as a SQL CASE would create exactly the second source of truth this PRD exists to kill), and it must stay re-runnable after the migration ledger has moved on, since tenants keep arriving. LEFT JOIN from tenants so a tenant with no persisted session (provisioned before migration 281 made the wizard durable) is still backfilled rather than dropped; DISTINCT ON takes the newest session per tenant for retried provisions; needsConfirm comes from the MAP and is never re-decided; care_setting is seeded from the org type's defaultCareSetting so R11's (*, care_setting) rung has something to match for a migrated tenant. (6) apps/api/src/onboarding-full-provisioner.ts — an optional specialtyProfileStore seam writes the SAME derivation at wizard completion with source 'onboarding', so a new tenant does not wait for a backfill run. Best-effort: it never blocks a tenant going live. The wizard UI, its step schemas and UseCaseStepData are UNCHANGED. (7) apps/admin/src/app/admin/settings/practice-profile/{page.tsx,practice-profile-api.ts} — single-select org type, MULTI-select specialties (R2 in the UI: 'multi-specialty' appears nowhere as an option; ticking two boxes IS a multi-specialty group), optional care setting, escape hatches included under 'Other' so the picker cannot dead-end, and a DISMISSIBLE confirm banner that explains what was guessed and from what using the map's own note. Grouping labels come from SPECIALTY_GROUPINGS rather than a local table, so no vocabulary is re-declared. Visible success AND visible error on save; a save attempted with no org type says why rather than silently doing nothing. (8) apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts — tenant_specialty_profiles classified into ADR_0140_CASCADE as delete-all on tenant_id. The ADR-0140 completeness test is a forcing function that goes red on any unclassified tenant-scoped table, and it caught this one. Classified as ERASE rather than retained: the row describes what a PRACTICE does and where, never who it treats, so it carries no independent retention obligation — the same class as tenant_customizations and tenant_facility_profile. PROOF: 20 store tests + 14 backfill tests + 16 route tests against real Postgres :5433, plus 5 provisioner tests and 15 admin page tests. The backfill test runs the backfill THREE times, confirming a profile between runs, and asserts that run 2 writes only the newcomer while the confirmed row keeps its source / confirmedBy / confirmedAt / axes and does NOT revert to the multi-specialty guess. RESOLUTION IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED — apps/api/src/note-template-store.ts is untouched, which is PRD R15's regression guard: a tenant with no profile behaves exactly as it did before this stage.

RBAC gap closed (PR #656, 6350dcdb). Ten registered /scribe/* routes had no deriveOperation mapping and 403'd at the deny-all catch-all before their handlers: pre-visit brief, session audio, evidence-span, $coverage, coaching-event, proposed-actions + its confirm/dismiss verbs, template $restore, and both em-config verbs -- essentially every scribe feature shipped 2026-07-28. Added the eleven mappings (all STANDARD verbs, since `admin` does not imply custom verbs) plus a registration-completeness test that reads the declared routes off the source and fails on any unmapped path, so a new scribe route is red the moment it is written rather than 403ing silently. Two bugs found while writing that test, either of which would have shipped a test proving nothing: deriveOperation's signature is (method, url) not (url, method), and it never returns undefined -- an unmatched path returns the catch-all pair, so an `=== undefined` check would have reported zero unmapped routes forever. Also corrected: $coverage is a GET despite its $ prefix; mapping it as a write would have locked clinicians out under tenant-member's read-only binding. Falsified by deleting the audio mapping and confirming the test goes red naming that route.

END-TO-END ACCEPTANCE RUN, unattended. Chrome with --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture feeding a 162s two-voice dental consultation synthesised from Windows SAPI (tests/e2e/fixtures/) drove the REAL capture path: getUserMedia -> MediaRecorder -> 3 chunked uploads -> Deepgram -> a diarised transcript -> $draft. PROVEN END TO END, against a real database and a real browser rather than fixtures: (1) R10 — a dental tenant whose ONLY signal is a backfilled specialty profile resolved to system-dentistry over HTTP, and the drafted note carries periodontal probing depths, tooth-level charting and a staged treatment plan, none of which the 4-section SOAP note could hold; (2) the backfill ran against a real DB for the first time (created=1, then created=0 skipped=1 — idempotent); (3) every route mapped in PR #656 is reachable with a real principal in a real browser — $coverage 200, transcript 200, coaching-event 202, chunks 202, $finalize-upload 200 — so the ten-route 403 class is closed by observation, not by assertion; (4) the HIL gate held: all 7 proposed actions came back status 'proposed'. TWO GATES INITIALLY MISREAD AS DEFECTS, both the product being correct: 'clinician-role-required' (a tenant-admin cannot read a patient transcript or draft a note — correct) and 'consent-required' (AE1: no consent, no mic, and the server rejects chunks regardless). Diagnosing them required reading the actual error bodies; three prior hypotheses (pro-tier entitlement, missing RoleBinding, missing role in the default catalog) were all wrong. One real defect found and fixed en route: /dev/checkout-grant mounted under CERNIA_DEV_LOGIN=1 but was never added to the unauthenticated allow-list beside /dev/login, so it 403'd at the deny-all catch-all in the one mode it exists for. Note the repo-wide RBAC gate lists that route as acceptable on the reasoning '404s unless dev-login is on' — which is false; it 403s. One extraction-accuracy defect found, tracked in `remaining`.

RETRACTION + controlled model A/B. The 2026-07-29 'F4 follow-up extraction accuracy' finding reported earlier today (invented '3 months' interval, 'two weeks' migrating from the rinse duration into an appointment) was an ARTEFACT OF THE HARNESS, not a product defect, and is withdrawn. The harness recorded 75s of a 162s consultation, so the entire back half of the visit — the periodontics referral, the six-week follow-up, the chlorhexidine instruction — was never captured. Both models were being graded on content they had never been given; the 'invented' intervals were invented from an empty prompt, which is a different and much less alarming thing than misreading a stated one. Root cause: a hardcoded 75_000ms record window. Fixed by deriving the duration from the WAV header (WAV_SECONDS + 12s tail), because a fixed number cannot know how long a fixture is, and the parts of a consultation clinicians care about — what happens next — live at the END, exactly where a truncation lands. WITH THE FULL 2272-char transcript, on identical input: ollama/qwen and anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 BOTH extract the six-week follow-up, the periodontics referral and the two-week chlorhexidine course correctly. Sonnet is marginally richer clinically (specifies 0.12% concentration); qwen is fully adequate for this task, which matters for the self-hosted no-BAA posture — there is no accuracy argument here for sending PHI to a third party. Both duplicate every action identically, which is what identified the duplication as OURS. METHOD NOTE: two earlier attempts at this A/B were invalid and were caught before being reported — a re-draft returned the stale rows from the previous model unchanged, and clearing the rows first produced zero. Byte-identical output from two different models was the tell.

$DRAFT IN-FLIGHT CLAIM (migration 330) + orphan cleanup. The F4 residual is closed. `$draft` had no concurrency claim, so two overlapping calls both ran transcript -> per-section LLM drafting -> coding -> follow-up -> order -> write a Composition -> set composition_ref; last writer won on the ref and the loser’s note survived in `resources` at status `preliminary`, referenced by nothing. Measured in scribe_harness: 10 Compositions, 7 sessions, 4 with a composition_ref, 6 orphans. The partial guard that existed was shaped right and scoped wrong — migration 291’s route set status `transcribing` before STT so a concurrent GET saw the in-flight state, but ONLY when no transcript existed yet; once one was persisted the second call skipped that branch and raced into the expensive phase. Migration 330 extends the same idea over the whole operation: packages/storage/src/migrations/330_scribe_draft_claim.sql adds scribe_sessions.drafting_claimed_at (the claim AND its fencing token) + drafting_prior_status, and widens the status CHECK with `drafting`. apps/api/src/scribe-session-store.ts claimDraft() is a single conditional UPDATE (WHERE drafting_claimed_at IS NULL OR < staleBefore ... RETURNING *) — a read-then-write would be the same race one level up. The claim rides the TIMESTAMP, not `status`, because the draft path legitimately moves `status` to `transcribing` while holding it. apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts takes the claim before template resolution, answers 409 `draft-in-progress` (retryable, nothing written) to the loser, releases explicitly before EVERY reply so an immediate retry is not 409’d, and releases again in a `finally` so a THROWN draft frees it rather than waiting out the timeout. Release RESTORES the status captured at claim time (an `uploaded` session that fails to draft lands back on `uploaded`), mirroring the contract the `transcribing` branch already had. Stale window: 10 minutes (DEFAULT_DRAFT_CLAIM_TTL_MS, overridable via deps.draftClaimTtlMs) — crash recovery only, sized an order of magnitude above the ~15-30s harness pipeline and several times the worst realistic draft (one LLM call per template section plus the coding/ follow-up/order passes), so it never fires on a draft that is merely slow. apps/api/src/scribe-draft-inflight-claim.integration.test.ts proves it against real Postgres: two concurrent $draft calls give one 201 + one 409 and EXACTLY ONE Composition (red before the fix at 201/201), a sequential redraft still succeeds, a thrown draft restores `uploaded` and is immediately re-draftable, a stale claim is reclaimable while a live one blocks, release is fenced on the claim token, and the claim is tenant-scoped. Cleanup for the orphans already written: apps/api/src/purge-orphan-scribe-compositions.ts (runnable script, not a migration — the decision logic is TypeScript). It matches only SCRIBE-TAGGED, `preliminary`, unreferenced Compositions, is tenant-scoped, idempotent, DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT and REFUSES to execute without an explicit single --tenant (there is no cross-tenant delete). It removes the resources row + its resource_versions history and KEEPS the audit Provenance — the PHI goes, the record of the write stays. A "has no Provenance" safety predicate was written and then removed: the storage adapter mints a CREATE Provenance for every write, so it matched all 10 harness Compositions and would have made the purge a permanent no-op. TENANT ERASURE ALREADY REACHES ORPHANS — apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts entries 0/1 delete `resources` + `resource_versions` delete-all BY tenant_id, not by walking from the session, so an unreferenced Composition is erased with the tenant; locked in by a new assertion in erasure-cascade.test.ts. Migration 330 was added to the BOOTSTRAP_SQL of all 26 integration fixtures that touch scribe_sessions, and `drafting` was threaded into the analytics in-progress set (apps/api/src/scribe-analytics-store.ts) and the admin status union + actionsFor (apps/admin/src/lib/scribe-api.ts) so a mid-draft session is not counted nowhere and not offered a Draft button that would only earn a 409.

SCRIBE P1 TRIO CLOSED (D2 + D3 + D9 of docs/testing/scribe-e2e-test-plan.md §0.1), one red-then-green each. (1) D2 — POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$cancel had NO ownership check at all while iam-route-guards.ts maps it to a bare write:ScribeSession that any *:admin satisfies, so any tenant-admin or second clinician could end a colleague's in-flight recording mid-consultation. apps/api/src/scribe-session-routes.ts now gates on the session owner and answers 403 {error:'forbidden',code:'not-session-owner'}, the same signature its PATCH sibling already used. DELIBERATELY NO ADMIN CARVE-OUT: the plausible 'admin tidies a stuck recording row' need loses to the asymmetry — a wrong cancel is unrecoverable through the API (no route writes status back off 'cancelled'; PATCH only moves template_id) and $coverage evicts its cache on a terminal status, while a stuck row blocks nothing (start() is a plain INSERT with no open-session predicate, the $draft claim self-heals on draftClaimTtlMs, usageByTemplate already excludes a null composition_ref). A real ops need must arrive as its own audited $force-cancel. Chunks + assembled audio survive a cancel untouched (scribe-chunk-routes.ts gates on neither status nor owner) — the capture is interrupted, not erased. (2) D3 — CERNIA_SCRIBE_STT=deepgram (a VALID id in the streaming SttBackendId union, and the obvious thing a human types) crashed the whole API at boot with 'unknown batch backend "deepgram"'; resolveScribeProviders validates that var for emptiness only. Rejecting the value is right and failing FAST is right (a lazy throw would fail after a clinician had already recorded a visit), so the fix is the message: packages/speech/src/batch-transcriber.ts now names the variable, the rejected value, the full valid batch set, and the streaming/batch mix-up itself via STREAMING_ONLY_BACKEND_HINTS (deepgram -> deepgram-prerecorded; whisper -> no batch equivalent, the scribe's option is the self-hosted whisper-selfhost) plus the reminder that CERNIA_SCRIBE_STT and CERNIA_SPEECH_STT are separate variables. (3) D9 — $coverage re-resolved the template with `undefined` for the facility (apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts) while $draft threads activeOrgOf(req) on BOTH of its re-resolution paths, so a tenant with a facility default coached the clinician against the PRACTICE template while the note drafted from the FACILITY one — prompted for sections the note would not contain, silent about sections it would. One-argument fix. Tests: apps/api/src/scribe-session-routes.integration.test.ts (D2, red 'expected 200 to be 403'; green also asserts a tenant-admin is refused, cross-tenant is 404, owner still cancels), packages/speech/src/batch-transcriber.test.ts (D3, 4 message-content cases, red on the old bare message), apps/api/src/scribe-coverage-routes.integration.test.ts (D9, red "expected [ 'practice-only' ] to deeply equal [ 'facility-only' ]"; green compares $coverage's returned section keys against the templateId $draft stamps, runs with CERNIA_ENFORCE_ORG_SCOPE=1 and gates its activeOrgId stamp on isOrgScopeEnforced() exactly as iam-route-guards.ts does — the facility tier is dead without the flag and the test would otherwise pass vacuously, so it asserts the flag is armed). Verification: @cernia/speech build clean, speech suite 288 passed / 3 pre-existing failures identical to baseline (factory, round-trip, deepgram-stt endpointing), @cernia/api typecheck + build clean after rebuilding the dep closure, all 43 apps/api scribe test files green (490/490), lint deltas nil (6 speech + 4 api errors byte-identical to baseline).

AE1 RECORDING CONSENT ON THE WRITE PATH — P0 compliance defect D5 CLOSED (docs/testing/scribe-e2e-test-plan.md §0.1). Consent was enforced at exactly seven read/ingest sites and at NONE of the write path. The gap was justified in code by a FALSE comment (apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts:137-141) asserting "a transcript can only exist WITH consent" because consent gates chunk ingest — but `$draft` short-circuits on an already-persisted scribe_transcripts row and never consults the chunk store, and that row can arrive with no chunk upload at all. REPRODUCED FIRST, as a test: seeding scribe_transcripts directly with zero consent rows, the chain $draft (201, Composition preliminary) -> $after-visit-summary (201) -> $sign (200, Composition `final`, session `signed`) -> EHR push (1 DocumentReference) completed end to end — a legal record minted and patient PHI sent to a third-party EHR with no consent attestation anywhere. FIXED by enforcing the SAME ScribeConsentStore seam independently at each route: $draft, PUT /draft, PUT /coding, $after-visit-summary + GET/PUT after-visit-summary, proposed-actions/:paid/confirm (apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts), $sign + $push-to-ehr (apps/api/src/scribe-sign-routes.ts, new optional `consent` dep), $finalize-upload (apps/api/src/scribe-chunk-routes.ts) — all 403 {error:'consent-required'}, matching the existing signature. WIRED in apps/api/src/index.ts (scribeSignRoutes registration) — without that line the gate is inert, which is how D5 shipped. The inventory UNDERCOUNTED: PUT /coding, GET/PUT after-visit-summary and proposed-actions/:paid/confirm were also unguarded; the last one signs and TRANSMITS a real eRx to a pharmacy off an unconsented recording. TWO routes deliberately left ungated with the reason recorded in-file: $amend (apps/api/src/scribe-amend-routes.ts header — it requires session.status==='signed' and $sign now refuses without consent, so a signed note is itself the evidence; gating it would also block a legally-required correction after the erasure cascade deletes scribe_recording_consents) and proposed-actions/:paid/dismiss (creates nothing, transmits nothing, returns no narrative). The false comment is replaced with the actual mechanism. PROOF: apps/api/src/scribe-consent-enforcement.integration.test.ts 9/9 on real Postgres :5433 (exploit watched failing first, then refused at $draft with nothing downstream minted; happy path draft->PUT draft->AVS->sign->push still completes; cross-tenant consent does not unlock). Whole scribe suite 491/491 across 43 files; @cernia/api typecheck clean; lint 15 errors before and after (no new).

SCRIBE E2E TEST FAMILY F2 (TEMPLATE RESOLUTION) EXECUTED LIVE — 15/15, and ALL EIGHT resolution rungs are proven live rather than assumed. New runner apps/api/scripts/run-scribe-f2.mts forces resolveForClinician (apps/api/src/note-template-store.ts) onto each rung deliberately — personal / assigned / visit-type / facility / practice / clinician-specialty / tenant-specialty / care-setting / SOAP fallback — over real HTTP with real minted tokens through the real global RBAC hook, and asserts the persisted scribe_sessions.template_source by querying Postgres DIRECTLY (the data channel) rather than trusting the API's echo. That column is what the review UI shows the clinician as 'why this template', so a dead rung is invisible until a dentist gets a generic SOAP note. TWO DESIGN RULES MADE THE GREEN MEAN SOMETHING. (a) A DECOY DEFAULT ON THE TIER ABOVE: every case that can have one configures a default on a rung above the one under test, pointing at a DIFFERENT template, so a pass proves the rung under test WON rather than that it was the only row present (F2-03 and F2-04 both carry a practice-default decoy). (b) ONE TENANT PER RUNG: the tiers are ordered, so a stray default anywhere above makes a case vacuous. A VACUOUS PASS WAS CAUGHT BY ASSERTING THE SOURCE, NOT THE TEMPLATE: F2-10 (Dr. Silva, radiology to SOAP fallback, the deliberate control) initially resolved system-soap with template_source='practice', because apps/api/scripts/seed-scribe-fixtures.mts wrote a tenant-wide __tenant__ to system-soap default for tenants B/C/D. The template id looked exactly right and the rung the case exists to test never ran; the same row also shadowed F2-11/F2-12. Section 2 asks for a practice default in Tenant A ONLY, so the seed now writes none for B/C/D (reasoning recorded at the branch) and the runner deletes any the F1 run left behind. SCRIBE D12 (P1) + D13 (P2) FIXED — red-then-green on both the unit and the live ⚙️ channel; F1 re-run 12/12 with F1-02 now 402ing all 43 route/method pairs. (1) D12 — THE PAYWALL. Two scribe route families shipped WITHOUT the base ambient-scribe entitlement gate. GET /scribe/analytics had no requireEntitlement at all, so a tenant holding no scribe product was answered 200 WITH THE FULL PAID AGGREGATE while its sibling GET /scribe/sessions 402d in the same breath; its only gate was an in-route tenant-admin check, and role is not payment — every tenant has an admin. GET /scribe/pre-visit-brief was gated on ambient-scribe-pro ONLY, so a tenant that had bought nothing got 403 tier-denied: told its TIER was too low for a product it did not own. FIX: an optional requireEntitlement dep plus a plugin-scoped preHandler hook in apps/api/src/scribe-analytics-routes.ts and apps/api/src/scribe-pre-visit-brief-routes.ts (the scribeVocabularyRoutes pattern — the hook is scoped to each plugin encapsulation context so it gates only its own family), with requireAmbientScribe passed at both registrations in apps/api/src/index.ts. ORDERING WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: createRequireProduct orders itself 401 then 404 unknown-product then 402, and the brief pro check is IN-ROUTE, so a preHandler necessarily lands first — which is what lets the two signatures coexist (402 product-not-entitled for owns-nothing, 403 tier-denied for base-but-not-pro). They are deliberately NOT collapsed: F1-02 asserts the first and F1-05 the second, and they are different facts about the customer. Consequence worth knowing: on analytics, payment now precedes the in-route admin check, so an un-entitled non-admin gets 402 rather than 403 — the actionable answer. (2) D13 — OBSERVABILITY, NOT BEHAVIOUR. A pro tenant whose coding pass failed 100% of the time was byte-identical over HTTP to a base tenant that never bought coding ($draft 201 with no coding key, then GET /coding 404 coding-not-found), so a paying practice could get no diagnostic coding for months with nothing to look at, and F1-06 could not tell a correct tier skip from a silent failure. The fail-soft swallow is CORRECT and is unchanged — a note must still arrive — and the status codes are unchanged, so no client breaks and the review UI still hides the card. FIX: a ScribeCodingPassStatus discriminator (ready, failed, skipped-not-entitled, not-drafted, unavailable) on the $draft 201 and on GET /coding (the 404, plus the 200 for symmetry). DESIGN CHOICE — DERIVED FROM ALREADY-PERSISTED STATE, NO MIGRATION: 'attempted' is exactly 'pro-entitled AND a draft exists', because the coding pass runs unconditionally when entitled and always persists a row on completion (even when the model legitimately returns zero diagnoses) — so entitled + a Composition + no row can only mean the pass failed. That needs no column and no backfill AND it retro-classifies the sessions that had ALREADY failed, which a new column could not. 'unavailable' is kept distinct from 'skipped-not-entitled' on purpose: labelling an unwired deployment 'not entitled' would be a lie about what the customer bought — the same conflation D13 is about. Visible to BOTH parties: the practice on its own API responses (it is their paid feature failing), the operator via the pre-existing non-PHI scribeCoding log marker. No PHI either way — product/config facts only. (3) WHY THE OLD TESTS COULD NOT CATCH D13: apps/api/src/scribe-coding-routes.integration.test.ts already had a base-tier case AND a fail-soft case — in two separate describe blocks with two separate Fastify apps, so nothing ever compared them. The new suite puts a failing-pro, a working-pro and a base tenant in ONE app via a per-tenant codingClientFor and asserts the discrimination directly: first that the status codes, the error body and the absent coding key are all IDENTICAL, then that codingStatus differs. On main that test cannot be written to pass — both sides read undefined, so even the not.toBe comparison fails. (4) RED WAS OBSERVED, not inferred: the source files were stashed and the new suites re-run against main's handlers. D12 red = expected 200 to be 402 (analytics), expected 403 to be 402 (brief), expected 403 not to be 403 (the two-denials case). D13 red = expected undefined to be failed, four times. Green: scribe-entitlement-gates.integration.test.ts 8/8, scribe-coding-pass-status.integration.test.ts 5/5, full scribe surface 533/533 across 47 files, tsc --noEmit clean, lint unchanged against a git stash -u baseline (13 pre-existing errors in the touched files, same rules, only line numbers shifted). Both suites carry falsifying controls — an ENTITLED admin must still get 200 from analytics, and a WORKING pro pass must report ready — without which a gate that denied everybody, or a status that said failed to everybody, would also look green. (5) TWO PROCESS CORRECTIONS FOUND WHILE DOING THIS. The obvious re-run command (--out f1-results.json) would have OVERWRITTEN the only record of D12 red, i.e. the 200-with-paid-aggregate; the green run is written to f1-results-2026-07-30-post-d12-d13.json and the 2026-07-29 artifact is preserved. And the runner discriminate() reduces every response to a whitelist of keys, so codingStatus was absent from the evidence artifact even though the API was returning it — the ⚙️ evidence would have understated the fix as unchanged. codingStatus is now in that list; any future discriminator must be added there too. (6) A LIMIT OF THE ⚙️ CHANNEL, recorded: on 2026-07-29 Tenant B pro coding pass failed twice on the local 8B model (which is how D13 was found); on this re-run it succeeded first try. The live channel CANNOT summon the failed state on demand, so D13 proof is necessarily a forced-throw in-process case and F1-06 live assertion covers only the skipped-not-entitled side. Separately, Tenant B $draft intermittently exceeds the undici 300s header timeout (TypeError: fetch failed at the F1-08 $draft call) — a pre-existing local-model latency characteristic unrelated to these fixes, but it makes the runner flaky at F1-08 and cost multiple full runs; a per-request timeout/retry on the runner api() helper is owed.

SCRIBE TEST FAMILY F4 (CAPTURE) EXECUTED ON THE REAL CAPTURE CHANNEL — 5/6, and the biggest hole in the scribe's coverage is closed. F4-06 is the case that did not exist in any form CI could run: a real Chromium fed a 162 s synthetic dental consultation into getUserMedia, MediaRecorder chunked it at 30 s, SIX chunks uploaded (measured median inter-chunk gap 30,036 ms — cadence, not just count, so a single end-of-visit burst cannot pass), $finalize-upload assembled the audio, REAL batch STT (deepgram-prerecorded) transcribed it, $draft wrote the note on the DENTISTRY template and the review screen signed it. Verified in POSTGRES, not from the API echo: Composition status='final', 1 DocumentReference, 1 scribe-sign Provenance (3 total = draft + edit + sign), session 'signed', template_id='system-dentistry' via template_source='specialty', 8/8 dentistry headings and ZERO SOAP headings, all 8 sections non-empty. STT was proven to have RUN rather than merely been configured: the persisted transcript is not the stub string, is 2272 chars, is speaker-diarized, and contains 8/8 clinical terms from the fixture's verbatim script. This matters because with CERNIA_SCRIBE_STT=stub a canned string is returned for ANY audio, so a completely broken capture path would still yield a signed dentistry note and a green test — the runner therefore reports F4-06 BLOCKED, never passed, if run behind the stub. The audio fixture did not exist and was generated from tests/e2e/fixtures/make-consult-audio.ps1 (5,185,646 bytes ~ 162.1 s, 24 turns, two SAPI voices); because the script is embedded in the generator it doubles as exact ground truth. TWO OF THE SIX PLANNED EXPECTATIONS WERE WRONG, in opposite directions, and both are corrected in the plan with the originals quoted. (a) F4-01's 'every scribe call under 400' is UNACHIEVABLE on correct code for the base-tier capture tenant: the recorder and review screens poll $coverage (pro-gated, 403), transcript (404 until the first chunk is transcribed), coding (404, pro-only) and after-visit-summary (404, empty state), all fail-soft by design (R16). 14 of 73 calls were >=400 and every one was correct. The PRE-EXISTING harness asserted this literal condition, so it would exit 1 on a perfectly healthy run. Replaced with: zero >=400 on the capture WRITE path (consent/chunks/$finalize-upload/$draft/$sign) plus a justified allowlist, so a genuinely new 403 still fails — deleting the assertion was the tempting wrong answer, since 403s on real routes are the class of defect the capture channel exists to catch. (b) F4-04's 'duplicate chunk index -> 400' DEMANDED A REGRESSION: re-POSTing the same index at the same size is a documented idempotent no-op (202) because a lost ack means the client re-sends (packages/scribe/src/chunk-session.ts:47); only a duplicate index at a DIFFERENT size is chunk-conflict. Corrected to assert both, with the idempotent replay as the control. NEW DEFECT D17 (P2) from F4-03 — the 10 MiB per-chunk cap cannot fire through its own route (413 + FHIR OperationOutcome, not 400 chunk-rejected); see its own remaining bullet. NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING: the first capture attempt rendered 'SOAP / Practice default' on the recorder for the dentist — indistinguishable from the flagship defect this family exists to detect — while the resolver was behaving correctly. The cause was a stale t-cedar/__tenant__ -> system-soap row that a REUSED scribe_f1 still carried (test-plan §6). Preflight now deletes it and the runner ASSERTS the capture session is stamped system-dentistry before recording, aborting rather than reporting a product defect. The template verdict was then FALSIFIED deliberately (--falsify reinstates that row): same dentist, same predicate, note returns [Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan], predicate false — so F4-06 discriminates rather than describing whatever the stack happens to do. STACK (recorded into the artifact from the runner's own process.env, via the same apps/api/scripts/f4-env.sh the API booted with): API c4219ac3 on :8163, admin :3210, Postgres :5433/scribe_f1 with the port-to-DB pairing asserted inside the runner before any case (18 rows for a throwaway tenant, 0 elsewhere; a zero count aborts). Note the LLM substitution: 192.168.1.164:11434 was DOWN and BOTH qwen3-vl blobs in the local Ollama cache are CORRUPT ('unable to load model'), and OPENAI_API_KEY is live but billing_not_active, so the draft ran on local qwen2.5:7b-instruct — F4's note quality is therefore NOT comparable with F1/F2's.

SCRIBE TEST FAMILIES F13 (CROSS-TENANT ISOLATION) + F16 (RBAC PER ROUTE) EXECUTED ON THE REAL-HTTP CHANNEL — F16 43/43, F13 42/43, two new defects. These are the two WHOLE-SURFACE sweeps, and F16 is the family that would have caught the incident that motivated the whole plan: ten /scribe/* routes once shipped 403ing every real caller while all their unit tests were green, because a route test stubs rbacClaims and never traverses the hook that denies them. THE ROUTE LIST STOPPED BEING A HAND-WRITTEN CLAIM. New apps/api/scripts/derive-scribe-routes.mts derives the inventory from the scribe-*-routes.ts files; the runner cross-checks it against SCRIBE_ROUTES in run-scribe-f1.mts with a route-SHAPED comparison (a :param matches any one segment, because the hand list carries concrete values like Ozempic and pa-1 where the source carries params, and a naive string compare reports four false disagreements). Both say 43 and they agree pair-for-pair, so F1s correction of the plans 41 is now independently confirmed rather than re-asserted. Building the deriver REPRODUCED the original miscount: with a six-line lookahead it found 40, dropping PUT .../coding, PUT .../after-visit-summary and PUT /scribe/templates/:id — each behind a fastify.put<{...}>( generic spanning ten-plus lines. The fix is to bound the lookahead by the NEXT registration, not by a line count. F16 — 43/43 REACHABLE, and the falsifying control is what makes that mean anything: a classifier that could never return denied would report every route reachable, which is the exact shape of the original incident. admin.reachable comes from the SAME isRbacForbidden call that denies tenant-member on 26 of 26 mutating pairs and office-admin on 40 of 43, so it demonstrably fires. TWO REFINEMENTS THE RUN FORCED. (1) The prediction is now a CHECK, not a restatement: iam-route-guards.scribe-coverage.test.ts proves MAPPING (no declared /scribe/* path left unmapped) but its STANDARD_VERBS set is a hand-written CLAIM about default-roles.ts and would stay green if the tenant-admin wildcard grant vanished tomorrow. The runner computes the expected outcome from the real deriveOperation + buildDefaultRoles + permissionCoversOperation (the same matcher the hook uses) and compares it to the live result: 0 mismatches / 43. (2) deriveOperation returns NO null — an unmatched url falls through to {verb:'*',resourceType:'*'}, the catch-all no binding covers, which IS the fail-closed deny that made those ten routes 403 everybody. Unmapped therefore has to be detected as the catch-all; a null check would report zero unmapped routes no matter what. Measured: none of the 43 sits on it. A BRIEF EXPECTATION THAT WAS WRONG, checked rather than assumed: office-admin is NOT denied on all 43. OFFICE_ADMIN_PERMISSIONS holds (Appointment, read) and (Patient, read), and GET /scribe/schedule / GET /scribe/patient-search map to exactly those, so both answer a front-desk token 200 — correct by design and not an escalation, since the same reads are already theirs on the generic FHIR surface. The third, GET /scribe/pre-visit-brief, also passes the HOOK on (Patient, read) and is refused IN-ROUTE with 403 clinician-role-required. Worth recording as its own fact: the RBAC mapping alone does not defend the paid clinical brief; a route-level gate does. F13 — 42/43, and the one failure is a WRITE. Tenant B (t-lakeshore, its OWN token and its OWN base+pro entitlement, so nothing it gets back can be an entitlement refusal masquerading as isolation) was refused on 25 session-scoped pairs, 4 template-by-id pairs and the patient-scoped brief using tenant A's ids; the sharpest probe — GET /scribe/patient-search?q=Avery, the shared-by-NAME patient section 2 deliberately plants in both tenants — returned only Bs own; and a direct Postgres read shows tenant As row state BYTE-IDENTICAL after the whole sweep (session status, template version + archived, vocabulary row, consent row, E/M config, total session count), so no 404 was hiding a mutation. D19 (P2, NEW): POST /scribe/sessions never resolves patientId. apps/api/src/scribe-session-routes.ts:157 checks typeof patientId === 'string' and nothing else, so tenant B opens a scribe session on tenant A's patient id (201, row persisted in t-lakeshore, verified against the resources row still owned by t-northside), on an id that exists in no tenant (201), and on "not-a-reference-at-all" (201). session.patientId then becomes Composition.subject AND DocumentReference.subject at $sign (scribe-sign-routes.ts:307 + :411), so a tenant can mint a signed legal record subjected to another tenant's patient identifier, and $push-to-ehr would transmit it. BLAST RADIUS STATED HONESTLY: REFERENTIAL, not a PHI read — the Patient resource is never fetched on any scribe path and GET /scribe/pre-visit-brief for the same id correctly 404s — with the escalation condition written down (the moment any consumer resolves session.patientId without the tenant filter, this is a disclosure). The sharpest framing is internal: the SAME handler validates visitType against a closed set specifically so a typo cannot mint a phantom key, and says so in a comment. The PHI subject of the note gets none of that. THE ATTRIBUTION D19 FORCED, which matters more than the defect: GET /scribe/sessions in tenant B does return pt-t-northside-local — but as the patientId of a row BELONGING TO B, planted by D19s own earlier POST. Flagging that as a second isolation breach would have double-counted one defect and misdescribed it as a tenant-filter failure. SCRIBE AUDIO DURABILITY + THE PRE-354 STRANDED-SIGN SWEEP (migration 355). Two gaps closed, both the same failure written twice: a clinical artifact changes state and the row that should explain it says nothing. (1) A DEPLOYMENT THAT CANNOT PERSIST CLINICAL AUDIO NO LONGER BOOTS. apps/api/src/scribe-audio-durability.ts assertScribeAudioDurable throws at the composition root (apps/api/src/index.ts, beside buildScribeChunkStoreFromEnv) when CERNIA_ENV names a non-dev environment (or NODE_ENV=production) and no SCRIBE_AUDIO_BUCKET + endpoint are set. A per-request 503 on POST /chunks was written first and rejected: it is LATER (the visit is already recorded before the system admits it cannot store it) and NARROWER (the same misconfiguration breaks $finalize-upload, the draft's audio read, the retention sweep and every destruction, so a gate on one route leaves the rest of the surface lying). There is deliberately NO override flag. Dev is exempt and is made HONEST instead: a boot pass reconciles every memory:// ref left by a previous process. The gate reads the env through a MIRROR of buildScribeChunkStoreFromEnv's contract, and the mirror is not left as a comment — the test drives an env matrix and asserts the mirror says "ephemeral" for exactly the inputs on which the builder returns an InMemoryChunkStore. (2) BYTES THAT WENT AWAY WITHOUT AN ORDER ARE NOW RECONCILED, NOT SILENT. Migration 355 adds two reasons to scribe_audio_destructions — process-restart (an ephemeral store lost them at process exit) and object-missing (a durable store no longer holds the object our row names, e.g. an out-of-band lifecycle rule). reconcileScribeAudioRefs probes the store and, for a ref whose bytes are PROVED absent, writes the row and clears the ref in ONE transaction. These rows carry audio_present_at_order=FALSE — MEASURED, not assumed — so they derive to nothing-to-destroy, NEVER destroyed: this system did not destroy those bytes and must not claim it did (the same class of false statement migration 351 removed). Absence has to be proved: a probe that throws, or that finds bytes, records nothing; a session that already has a destruction row is skipped entirely, because overwriting a PENDING withdrawal would turn "we were told to delete this and have not managed to" into "there was never anything here". 339's outcome invariant ("an outcome implies at least one attempt") had to be RESTATED rather than satisfied: a reconciliation attempts no delete, so attempts=0, and writing attempts=1 to fit the old CHECK would have been exactly the lie the table exists to prevent — the constraint now names the one honest exception. (3) THE PRE-354 STRANDED-SIGN SWEEP. apps/api/src/repair-stranded-scribe-signs.ts enumerates by EVIDENCE (a final, scribe-tagged Composition whose DocumentReference and/or signing Provenance is absent from `resources`) and mints exactly what is missing. It can do what the ROUTE cannot: 354's header records that nothing FINDS the DocumentReference, because it points at its Composition through content.attachment.url, not a declared FHIR search parameter — from SQL that is a JSONB path, so absence is proved rather than assumed, and that proof is the script's entire licence to write. The Provenance predicate is narrow on purpose (activity.text='scribe-sign'): the storage adapter mints a CREATE Provenance for EVERY write, so a bare target-match would find one for every note ever drafted and the sweep would never repair a missing signature record. The reconstructed Provenance KEEPS that activity (one the sweep cannot see is one it would mint again next run) and carries a repair:stranded-sign-sweep entity so the record says it was reconstructed. sign_started_at is NOT borrowed — migration 355 adds sign_repaired_at/sign_repaired_by and widens 354's CHECK from "a ref needs the sign marker" to "a ref needs a RECORDED EVENT that produced it", so sign_started_at keeps meaning exactly what 354 says and a repaired row stays distinguishable from a witnessed one forever. Excluded, each for its own reason: post-354 rows (their own $sign resumes them), cancelled/declined sessions (a patient's refusal is not a row a batch job flips to signed), revoked consent (a repair is at most as permitted as the act it completes), preliminary and amended Compositions. Safety follows purge-orphan-scribe-compositions.ts exactly: dry-run default, --execute requires --tenant, no cross-tenant write form exists, ids and counts only. It deliberately does NOT push to the EHR. LIVE EVIDENCE, not just green tests. Audio-durability probe asks HEAD instead of GET. IChunkStore gained `statAssembled`; the S3 store implements it with HeadObjectCommand (accepting NotFound, NoSuchKey and a bare 404 as ABSENT, rethrowing everything else), the in-memory store derives it from readAssembled so the two share one notion of "present", and probeScribeAudioBytes calls it. Previously the probe downloaded the entire recording to read its length and discarded it — a full visit's audio per dangling session, per pass, which is why the reconciliation sweep was operator-driven and limit-bounded. It is also a PHI property: a timer that materialised recordings across a tenant is a different exposure surface from one that reads content lengths. The method is REQUIRED on the interface, not optional, so a future store cannot quietly fall back to downloading. Scheduling the sweep remains a separate change.

A stale audio reference in a sign Provenance is now explainable WITHOUT rewriting the Provenance. The resource keeps the ref it was signed with — that is the audit-trail rule and it is unchanged — and GET /scribe/sessions/:id/audio-state answers what the ref points at today. Five states, not two: never-recorded, destroyed (with completedAt + reason), present, absent, unknown. `absent` with no destruction record is reported as an unexplained loss rather than laundered into a policy outcome, and an unreachable store is `unknown`, never absence. A recorded destruction outranks a bytes probe — a record is a decision with an author and a time, a probe is an observation that can be wrong — but a probe finding bytes after a recorded destruction is surfaced as a WARNING. Two design points worth keeping: the route is SESSION-keyed with the tenant from the claim (a ref-keyed lookup would have been a cross-tenant probe), and the resolver REQUIRES a probe argument because an earlier draft defaulted a missing probe to `present`, i.e. reported audio intact on the strength of nobody looking. Caught by review, not by a test, and now covered by one.

Closed (e) — the practice can now see its OWN outstanding recording deletions. The cross-tenant operator view (PR #79x) answers "is the FLEET honouring withdrawals?" in hashed, aggregate terms and deliberately carries no session ids, so it cannot answer the question the PRACTICE owes its patient: "you asked us to delete YOUR recording — did we?". Under HIPAA the practice is the covered entity, so that answer has to exist inside the tenant. GET /admin/scribe/audio-destructions (apps/api/src/scribe-audio-destructions-admin-routes.ts) + the /admin/scribe-destructions page. FOUNDER DECISION 2026-08-05: TENANT-ADMIN ONLY, and the RBAC verb is what enforces it — the route maps to {verb:"admin", resourceType:"ScribeSession"}, and `admin` is granted ONLY by TENANT_ADMIN_PERMISSIONS's `*:admin`; `read` would have admitted tenant-member via its `*:read`. This is a compliance register, not a clinical one, so it is gated on the practice owner rather than on session ownership. The mapping went in WITH the route, and the repo-coverage gate was PROVEN to see it (disabling the mapping turns that gate red naming this exact path — it is not passing blindly). DERIVATION IS SHARED, NOT REBUILT: scribeAudioDestructionsDue() gained an optional tenantId filter applied in SQL before the limit, so the tenant view and the retry driver cannot disagree about what is outstanding, and a small practice cannot be pushed out of its own page by a noisy neighbour. Proven on real Postgres 7/7 with INCLUSION ASSERTED BEFORE EXCLUSION (the isolation test seeds work in both tenants, proves the caller sees their own row, then proves the neighbour's is absent, then re-queries as the neighbour to prove their row was real) plus an explicit assertion that patient_id, the object key and the string "patientId" never reach the wire. THE CRASH WINDOW IS A DISTINCT STATE on this surface: a withdrawal with no order row renders "Never attempted", not "0 attempts". UI honesty rules match the register's: an UNKNOWN age renders the word "Unknown" (never "0h", never "just now") and, on a withdrawal specifically, counts as CRITICAL rather than calm; an empty register states "nothing outstanding" with the instant it was true at, because a blank table is indistinguishable from a page that failed to load; `truncated` is surfaced as "every number here is a lower bound". Deliberately read-only — a "retry now" button would let a practice mask an object-store outage by hammering it.

CLOSED the coding aggregate's last stated imprecision — the aggregate and the per-note read now give the same answer. The aggregate counted every NULL coding_pass_status as `indeterminate`, while the per-note read resolves many of them by replaying the entitlement history across the note's draft bracket; aggregate `failed` was therefore a LOWER bound and `indeterminate` an UPPER bound. THE RECORDED REASON FOR LEAVING IT OPEN WAS WRONG: it said closing it meant "one history replay per row". The history is keyed by (tenant, product) and the window is applied by a PURE FOLD afterwards, so N notes cost ONE read plus N in-memory evaluations. PostgresEntitlementHistoryStore.resolverFor() is that read; wasEntitledDuring() now delegates to it, so the fold exists exactly ONCE and the two surfaces agree by construction rather than by review. The SQL re-implementation — the other obvious way to close this — was rejected precisely because it would have created the second definition of "entitled" that module's header forbids, and it would have drifted from the live gate. Verdict→bucket mapping is inferCodingPassStatus's verbatim: entitled⇒failed, not-entitled⇒skipped-not-entitled, unknown⇒indeterminate. A STRADDLED window still resolves to unknown and STAYS indeterminate. New `codingIndeterminateResolution` block reports unrecorded/resolvedToFailed/resolvedToSkipped/unresolved/attempted/truncated, with `unresolved` RE-DERIVED from the population so the four numbers cannot fail to add up; `attempted:false` means the old bounds still apply and says so rather than leaving a reader to infer it from three zeros. Bounded at CODING_RESOLUTION_SCAN_LIMIT=5000 with a deterministic page and a `truncated` flag. The admin card's hint is now DERIVED: repeating the old "at least the number above and at most that plus this" caveat after resolution would UNDERSTATE the failure count an operator is looking at, and three distinct worlds (older API / ran-and-decided-nothing / resolved) are worded apart. Proven 6/6 on real Postgres with the pre-change store as the control on every arm, parity asserted against wasEntitledDuring itself rather than a typed-in number, and the failure RATE shown to move (0 of 1 attempt → 2 of 3) so this is not a cosmetic field. 20/20 on the view.
